utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Hey, good to see you again! How is college life treating you?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Pretty good, doctor! Finals are stressful but managing. Thank you for fitting me in today.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Of course, of course. So you are here for pre-operative clearance before your hernia repair scheduled in 2025, correct?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, the surgeon asked me to get cleared. I am a little nervous honestly.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: That is understandable. Tell me, are you having any body aches lately, or any tingling anywhere?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Umm, yes doctor, I do get body aches in my bones every other day, and there is a bit of tingling in my rectum area once a day or so.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Hmm, that tingling near the rectum is worth noting before the surgery. Any nausea or vomiting after every meal?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Ahh, yes actually, I have been feeling a bit of nausea after every meal for the past couple of weeks.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Okay. Any recent birds contact or exposure to someone at school who was sick?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, my roommate keeps birds as pets, and there was definitely someone at school down with a bad infection last month.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I see. Do you drink beer or any alcohol? Be honest with me, you know I do not judge.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Honestly doctor, I do have beer 2 drinks a week, sometimes more around exam time. And recreational drugs once in a while.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Alright, and what about recreational drugs — anything specific? And do you smoke?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Just cannabis occasionally, nothing heavy. And no, I don't smoke cigarettes.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Good. Any family history of high cholesterol or heart problems?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: I don't think so, doctor. No one in my family has had cholesterol issues as far as I know. My dad had something with his bones but nothing serious.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Have you had a bronchoscopy or any lung investigations done recently, given the bird exposure?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Don't think so, doctor. I had some basic blood work done but nothing like a bronchoscopy.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Given your birds exposure, the body aches, nausea, and tingling near the rectum, I am suspecting a psittacosis infection — that is a bacterial illness from bird contact. We will need to confirm this before clearing you for surgery.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Oh my, I had no idea doctor. So will this delay my hernia repair surgery?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: It may, yes. We need to treat the infection first and also monitor your cholesterol levels and get a bronchoscopy to rule out any lung involvement. The alcohol use is also something that affects anesthesia, so we need to address that too.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: For now, I am prescribing Tylenol for your body aches and fever, and a low dose of lorazepam to help with your anxiety around the surgery — but please do not mix that with beer or recreational drugs, that is very important.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Understood doctor, I will be careful. Should I stop the beer completely then?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Yes, please stop all alcohol and recreational drugs at least two weeks before surgery. Lorazepam and alcohol together can cause serious respiratory depression. And do not take Tylenol beyond the recommended dose since alcohol can make it toxic for your liver.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Thank you so much doctor, always feel better after talking to you. I will follow everything you said and come back after the tests.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Good morning, welcome back. Please sit down, how are you feeling today after the discharge?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Good morning doctor. Umm, I am mildly better but still feeling nauseous often and there is some gas trouble in my stomach also.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I see. Are you itching anywhere or having any rash on the skin?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: The rash on my arms has gone down mostly, but my mouth feels dry and slightly swollen inside constantly, doctor.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any pain or stiffness in your knee or any other joint?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Ahh, yes doctor, my right knee is paining three times a week, especially after I come back from the construction site.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Do you have a history of tuberculosis or osteoporosis? I see something was noted in your discharge summary.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, I had tuberculosis back in 2022, and the doctor had told me about early osteoporosis also a month ago when I did the bone scan.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Were you prescribed any medicines at discharge? Are you currently taking them all?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: They gave me albuterol inhaler for the breathing, doctor. But I am also taking some herbal medicine that my neighbour suggested for the swelling.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Please do not mix herbal medicine with your albuterol without asking me — it can cause a bad reaction, especially with your allergy history.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Have you been exposed to birds or any animal at home or at the worksite recently?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Umm, yes doctor, there are birds — pigeons — near our worksite. I have been working there for 20 years almost.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Do you go to the gym or do any heavy physical activity? And do you take any opioids for pain?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: I do go to the gym on weekends doctor. And I have been taking opioids socially — not regularly — but for 20 years on and off.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Are you having any breathlessness or cough when exposed to dust or the birds?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, cough starts often and my chest feels tight whenever I am near those areas. Also I am fasting for religious reasons since last week, so eating very less.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Based on your birds exposure, the breathlessness, cough, rash, and swelling in the mouth, this looks like hypersensitivity pneumonitis with an allergic reaction — triggered largely by bird droppings and dust at the site.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, is this serious? Will my knee pain and the gas also get better with treatment?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Yes, once we control the allergic response and you stay away from birds and heavy dust, most symptoms including the gas and knee discomfort should ease. Fasting can worsen the feeling nauseous so please sip water constantly.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I am prescribing cetirizine for the itching and swelling, pantoprazole for the gas and feeling nauseous, and continue your albuterol inhaler as needed. Stop the herbal medicine immediately.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Should I take anything for my knee pain doctor? It is mild but bothering me at work.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Given your osteoporosis, I will add calcium carbonate and vitamin D3 supplements. For the knee pain, apply a diclofenac gel locally — do not take oral pain tablets with your current medicines.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: We need to do a follow-up AST test to check your liver since you have been taking opioids, and also a BP check today before you leave.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Okay doctor, I will get those done. Should I avoid the gym on weekends for now? And the feeling nauseous is mild only after I eat something, not otherwise.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Hello, please come in and have a seat. How are you doing today?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, I am not feeling well at all. I work night shifts in an IT company and this morning I woke up with a very radiating pain starting from my neck going all the way to my head.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I see. Is this headache gets worse when you move your neck, or is it constant throughout the day?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: It gets worse when I sit at my desk. And sometimes I feel dizziness also. I was actually discharged from hospital last week — I had gone in for irregular periods and white discharge.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Okay, I see your discharge papers here. They did a urine culture and some other tests. Were any other investigations done during that admission?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, they did T3 levels and also a pulmonary function test. The reports just came in and I brought them today.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Good. Let me look at these reports. But first, tell me more about your periods — are they irregular for how long?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Umm, for about six months now. I also have weight gain, some acne on my neck, and hair thinning. I was very worried.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any international travel recently? And do you work near any chemical fumes or heavy equipment at your night shift facility?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes, I had international travel to Singapore three months back for a project. And at our office, there is a server room — sometimes I feel breathlessness when I am inside for long hours.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Noted. Does your facility use any industrial cooling chemicals or have you been exposed to any dust or chemical fumes in that server room environment?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Ahh, I am not sure doctor, but there is a lot of chemical fumes from the cooling units. My colleagues also complain of coughing and eye irritation.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: That is important. Do you smoke or drink? And are you doing any gym or exercise currently?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: I used to smoke — two packs a day — but I stopped last year. I do go to the gym for 30 minutes daily in the morning before my shift starts. No alcohol at all.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Good that you have quit. Now, the pulmonary function test results show some mild obstruction. Are you using any inhaler currently?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: No doctor, nobody prescribed me any inhaler. The hospital said they would wait for results. Also, my neck stiffness and tingling in my head area is becoming very uncomfortable at night.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any numbness going down your shoulders or arms? Any nausea or vomiting with these episodes?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Uh, yes doctor, the tingling is radiating into my shoulders sometimes. No vomiting, but mild nausea is there.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Looking at everything together — the irregular periods, acne, hair thinning, weight gain, and your T3 report — this is a case of PCOS with possible associated thyroid dysfunction. The neck and head symptoms suggest cervical radiculopathy, likely from your posture at night shifts.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, can the night shift work and the server room chemical fumes make all these things worse? I am very worried about my breathlessness also.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Absolutely. Prolonged chemical fumes exposure combined with your previous smoking history can aggravate your lungs. The pulmonary function test confirms mild airway obstruction. You must request a transfer away from the server room area and inform your occupational health department.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: For the breathlessness and airway issue, I am prescribing a inhaler — use it twice a day. For the tingling and pain in your neck and head, I am starting you on gabapentin at a low dose at night, and you will also need metformin for the PCOS management.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, should I stop the gym? I go for 30 minutes daily but the headache gets worse after exercise this morning itself.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Do not stop the gym entirely, but avoid any neck strain exercises until reviewed. The gabapentin may cause drowsiness initially, so take it only at night. Also, the urine culture shows a mild infection — complete the full course of antibiotics from the hospital. Repeat your T3 in four weeks.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Thank you so much doctor, I feel much better knowing what is happening. I will follow everything you said.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Hello, please come in and have a seat. No need to be nervous at all.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Thank you doctor, umm, I am just a bit anxious. I have been having wheezing and sneezing every few days and I do not know what is happening.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Okay, tell me more. Is there any cold, runny nose, or itching along with this wheezing?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Right, doctor, there is itching near my toes and sometimes my breast area also feels very sharp pain periodically.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any known insect bites recently or exposure to dust or chemicals? Do you work near any mine site?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Ahh, no doctor, I am an office worker only. No mine exposure. But there were insect bites on my toes about two weeks back.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Does the wheezing gets better on its own or does it stay continuously?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: It gets better after some time, doctor. But the cold feeling in my toes, that is cold to touch and stays continuously.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any similar wheezing or breathlessness episodes in childhood? Any childhood illness I should know about?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Umm, yeah doctor, I had some childhood illness in childhood involving breathing problems they told me. And I had appendectomy done in 2022.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Alright. Any swelling noticed near the spleen side, that is left side of your abdomen? Any rash on skin?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: I am not sure about the spleen side, doctor, but sometimes there is bloating in the abdomen. Denied any rash as such.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Do you caffeine — coffee or energy drinks — how often?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, I have been taking caffeine heavily, 3 times a week at least, and this habit has been going on for 10 years now.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Are you currently on any medicines? Any self-medication you have been doing for this wheezing?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Ahh, yes doctor, I started using some eye drops on my own thinking it was allergy. And I was told by a chemist to take furosemide for the swelling in my toes. I also read about heparin online for circulation.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Please stop the furosemide and heparin immediately — do not self-medicate with these, they are serious drugs and can cause bleeding and other complications. The eye drops are also not appropriate here.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: I am sorry doctor, I panicked. The wheezing was scaring me and I just tried whatever I could find.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Understood. Have you had any blood tests done? Was any AST or liver function checked recently, especially after that appendectomy in 2022?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yeah, doctor, a AST was done sometime back but I do not have the report with me right now. No other tests were done.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Based on everything — the wheezing, sneezing, itching, insect bites history, and the childhood illness — this looks like allergic rhinitis with possible urticaria reaction triggered by the bites.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Urticaria, doctor? Is that serious? And why is my breast area paining very sharp?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: The very sharp breast pain needs further evaluation. For now I am prescribing cetirizine tablet once at night for the allergic rhinitis and montelukast for the wheezing. Also a topical antihistamine cream for your toes.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Please reduce your caffeine intake — it can worsen wheezing and palpitations. Avoid insect bites by using repellent, and do not start any OTC medicines without asking me first.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Right, doctor, I will follow everything. Should I come back for that AST report and any other tests?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Good afternoon, please sit down. What brings you in today?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, I am feeling very tired and dizzy since last month. Two days ago I felt so weak I nearly fell at the construction site.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I see. Any headache or breathlessness also? And is your neck or abdomen giving any trouble?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, headache is there frequently. My neck feels stiff sometimes and the abdomen is also feeling a little uneasy.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any swelling or paining in your foot? Does the foot feel warm?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Umm, yes doctor, my right foot is warm and swelling is also there. It is worse with movement so I am trying not to walk much.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any history of bleeding disorders in your family or yourself? Any anaemia diagnosed before?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Ahh, my mother had some bleeding disorders doctor, they told us long back. For me, anaemia was detected last month but I did not take treatment properly.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: What about factory or chemical exposure at work? Have you been near any sick person with tuberculosis recently?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, my site is near a small factory and there was one colleague who had tuberculosis — he was a sick person and I was working close to him before the tests.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Do you drink alcohol or smoke? How often?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Uh, I smoke two packs a day doctor. And for drinking I am an occasional drinker, only on weekends. I also take a lot of tea, almost five-six cups a day.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Have you done any CT scan or complete blood count recently? Any medicines you are currently taking?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, I did a CT scan two days ago from outside but I did not read the report properly. I was given montelukast for some breathing problem before and azithromycin also last time for cough.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Did you have fever, night sweats, or weight loss in recent weeks?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, night sweats are there and I have lost some weight also. Fever comes and goes frequently in the evening.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Looking at your exposure to that sick person with tuberculosis, your weight loss, night sweats, and the CT scan findings, this appears to be a case of pulmonary tuberculosis combined with severe iron deficiency anaemia. The foot swelling is likely a nutritional complication.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, that is very serious. What treatment should I take? And what about my headache and neck stiffness?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I am prescribing tenofovir as part of your antiviral cover, azithromycin to continue for the respiratory infection, and montelukast to help with your breathing. We will also add iron supplements and folic acid for your anaemia. Anti-tuberculosis therapy will be started separately after confirming the sputum culture.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Your tea habit is reducing iron absorption — please avoid tea within one hour of taking iron supplements. Also, smoking two packs a day is making your breathlessness much worse, you must stop immediately.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Okay doctor, but I want to make sure I understood — what tests are still pending and what should I avoid?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: We will do a chest X-ray, sputum AFB smear, serum ferritin, and repeat complete blood count. Avoid heavy lifting at the construction site and rest your foot as the warm swelling needs to settle.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Now tell me back — which medicines did I give you and what food or drink should you avoid near your tablet time?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, you gave tenofovir, azithromycin, montelukast, and iron supplements with folic acid. I should not take tea near tablet time, should not smoke, and must rest my foot and not do heavy work.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Very good, you have understood correctly. Come back in one week with your sputum AFB smear and serum ferritin reports. If your headache worsens or neck becomes very stiff, come immediately — do not wait.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Good afternoon, please come in and have a seat. How are you doing today?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Good afternoon doctor. I am 67 years old and my family doctor has referred me to you. I have been feeling very unwell since some time ago — honestly it started after I recovered from COVID in 2021.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I see. Tell me what symptoms are troubling you the most — any fatigue, breathlessness, or tingling anywhere?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, the tingling is there in my hands and feet — it happens often. And fatigue also — I get tired very quickly, even with small activity.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any chest pain or palpitations? What about shortness of breath when climbing stairs?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Umm, chest pain — no, not really. But palpitations — yes, once in a while they come. Shortness of breath on chest exertion is there once in a while also.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any headache, dizziness, or brain fog — difficulty concentrating or remembering things?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Ahh yes, this brain fog is very much there doctor. I forget things, cannot concentrate properly. Dizziness is hardly ever but headache comes often.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Do you have any existing conditions — any hypertension or diabetes history? Any past surgeries?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, I have hypertension for 20 years. I also had cholecystectomy — gallbladder removal — time ago. And I have one drug allergy — to sulfa drugs.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Good that you mentioned the drug allergy — very important. Are you currently on any medicines for your hypertension?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: I am taking amlodipine and losartan for blood pressure. My BP is reasonably controlled doctor.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any exposure to crowded places or pollution regularly? Any recent mosquito bite history — I ask because fatigue and tingling can sometimes point to vector-borne illness also.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, I go to the market — definitely some crowded places exposure and pollution also. Mosquito bite — yes, we have many mosquitoes in our area. But no fever or rash recently.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: You mentioned caring for a sick family member — is that adding stress? Are you getting proper sleep?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, my wife is unwell — she has diabetes and knee joint problems. I am managing her also. I have insomnia because of this — sleep is very poor often.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Understood, that is a lot of burden. Any muscle weakness or joint pain? Any cough or loss of smell lingering still?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Muscle weakness — yes, especially in my legs. Loss of smell was there right after COVID but it has mostly come back now. Cough is hardly ever now. Joint pain — no, not much.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Has any blood work been done recently — like complete blood count, vitamin B12 level, or thyroid function test?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: My family doctor did some blood work — complete blood count was done. He said mild anaemia is there. Vitamin B12 was low also. But no ultrasound or advanced tests since my cholecystectomy.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Based on everything you have told me, this is a clear picture of post-COVID syndrome — also called long COVID — presenting with peripheral neuropathy causing the tingling, chronic fatigue, brain fog, and insomnia. The low Vitamin B12 is contributing significantly to the muscle weakness and tingling in your hands and feet.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I am prescribing Mecobalamin 1500 mcg once daily for the tingling and nerve support, multivitamin supplement, and low-dose aspirin 75 mg. For insomnia, start melatonin 3 mg at bedtime — avoiding stronger sleep medicines given your hypertension and your drug allergy history.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Please avoid crowded places as much as possible and wear a mask in pollution. Do not overstrain — fatigue will worsen if you push too hard. Your BP must be monitored every week at home.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: We will order a repeat blood work including Vitamin B12, thyroid function test, and nerve conduction study. I also want an ultrasound of your abdomen — since you had cholecystectomy, let us rule out any post-surgical changes. If the fatigue is not improving in six weeks, we may need to consider laparoscopy evaluation also.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Thank you so much doctor, I feel more clear now about what is happening. I will follow everything you have said.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Come in, come in. Please sit down. How are you doing today?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, I am not doing well at all. My knee is paining extremely painful... and I also have been feeling very tired and yellow looking just started this week.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Okay, what brings you here today — is it a refill visit or something new coming up?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Umm, mainly refill, doctor. I am on metformin and levothyroxine since 2023. But I delayed coming — I was caught up with college exams for weeks.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Alright. You mentioned knee pain — which knee is it, and is the area warm or swollen?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Right knee, doctor. It is warm to touch and feels thick inside. I have had this pain several times this month but I kept ignoring it.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Is there any jaundice — any yellowing of your eyes or skin?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, my friends noticed my eyes are a bit yellow. I also feel very pale. Could it be anemia?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Possibly. Are you having any fatigue, breathlessness, or dizziness along with the pallor?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Ahh, yes doctor, dizziness especially when I stand up fast. And fatigue is there several times during the day. I also had jaundice once last summer too.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I see. Any pollen or dust exposure recently? Sometimes allergic reactions can worsen systemic conditions.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Umm, the college campus has a lot of pollen these days doctor, I sneeze a lot. Could that be connected to the jaundice?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Not directly, but let us not ignore it. Now tell me — have you had any check-up done recently for your diabetes and thyroid?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: No doctor, I did a check-up back in 2023 only. Since then no tests done. I also have high cholesterol — the doctor had mentioned it then. And my mother had a mammogram done recently and they said there is family risk so I should watch out.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Okay, good you mentioned that family history. Do you exercise or follow any diet for the cholesterol?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: I go for jogging 3 times a week doctor, but diet is very bad — hostel food, lot of fried things. I also skip meals during exam time.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Based on what you are telling me, you have active anemia, possible jaundice recurrence, and knee pain that looks like joint inflammation — likely worsened by your poorly controlled diabetes and hypothyroidism.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, why does thyroid problem cause all this? I thought it just causes weight gain.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Uncontrolled hypothyroidism can cause anemia, joint pain, fatigue, and even affect your liver slightly, which explains the jaundice picture. Your high cholesterol also goes up when thyroid is low.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I am continuing your metformin and increasing the dose of levothyroxine. I am also adding iron supplement for the anemia, atorvastatin for cholesterol, and diclofenac gel for the knee.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, any side effects of atorvastatin? And can I continue jogging with this knee pain?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Avoid jogging for now — rest the knee for at least two weeks. Atorvastatin can rarely cause muscle pain, especially in the legs, so tell me immediately if you feel muscle weakness. Also avoid pollen exposure as much as possible.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: We will do a complete blood count, liver function test, thyroid stimulating hormone, HbA1c, and lipid profile today. Please do not delay like this again — missing medications for weeks is very risky for your sugar and thyroid.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, I also wanted to say — I feel knee pain is extremely painful in the knee joint area in the mornings mainly. Should I do any scan?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Yes, let us also add a X-ray knee today. If it is showing joint swelling, we may need a rheumatoid factor test also. Come back in two weeks with all reports and we will review everything thoroughly.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Good morning, please come in and sit down comfortably.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Good morning doctor. Umm, I am a homemaker but I also do part-time work at a construction site nearby, handling materials and such.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I see. What has brought you here today? What is the main problem?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, two days ago I had some kind of incident at the site and after that incident I am having headache and dizziness every few days. Also my arm is feeling numb on one side.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Can you describe the headache? Is it shooting type, or more like a dull ache?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, it is shooting type, starting from the back of my neck and going up to the forehead. Very bad it is.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any numbness or tingling in the fingers or toes? And do you have any shoulder pain also?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes, the numbness is there in the right hand fingers, and yes, shoulder pain on the right side is also bothering me since last week.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: At the construction site, are you exposed to any chemicals or fumes? Do you come near dogs or animals there?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Ahh, yes doctor, there are chemicals used for waterproofing and paint work. And there are stray dogs that roam around the site, I am there daily near them only.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Have you taken anti-rabies vaccination? Any previous vaccination history for rabies or tetanus?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Umm, I had vaccination done years back, but I am not sure which one exactly. Also doctor, I had knee replacement done two years ago and hip replacement also three years back.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Understood. Do you have sugar problem or blood pressure issue?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, I have diabetes and I am on medicines but my sugar is not coming under control at all. I also have urine problem — burning and frequent urination is there.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: What medicines are you currently taking? And do you smoke or drink alcohol?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor I am a social smoker, since college only, so roughly for 20 years. I take warfarin for my heart valve problem and also azithromycin was given recently for some chest infection.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Has any doctor done MRI brain or nerve conduction study before for this numbness?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: No doctor, nothing like that was done. Only blood sugar test and HbA1c were done last month. The HbA1c was very high, around 10.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Based on your uncontrolled diabetes, the numbness in your fingers, shooting headache, and dizziness, this looks like diabetic peripheral neuropathy combined with possible cervical radiculopathy from the site injury.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, what should I do now? And the urine problem and shoulder pain — are they also related?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: The urine problem may be a urinary tract infection which is common with uncontrolled diabetes. The shoulder pain at the right shoulder needs a shoulder X-ray to rule out any injury from the site. We will also order a urine culture and MRI brain.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I am prescribing gabapentin for your nerve pain and numbness. Continue your warfarin as before but we need to check your INR since azithromycin can interact with it.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, should I stop going to the construction site now? And the stray dogs there, is it dangerous?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Please avoid chemicals and heavy work at the site until your shoulder pain and dizziness settle. Regarding the dogs, since your vaccination history is unclear, kindly take anti-rabies shots as a precaution. Also, your smoking will worsen the nerve damage, so please try to stop.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Understood doctor. I will follow all this. One more thing — I am having sleep disturbance also every few days because of the headache at night, so that is also troubling me.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: The gabapentin should help with both the nerve pain and sleep disturbance. Come back after one week with the MRI brain report, urine culture, INR, and HbA1c results so we can reassess your treatment plan.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Arjun! Good to see you again, yaar. How are things going?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor saab, all good on the surface! But you know, I keep coming back to you for a reason.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Ha ha, fair enough. So tell me, how is the recovery going after the surgeries? Any new complaints?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Umm, the cholecystectomy site is clear now, no issues there. But the hernia repair from last summer — sometimes I feel a mild pull when I lift heavy at the gym.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Okay, good to hear the cholecystectomy site has healed well. That pulling sensation near the hernia repair site — is it often or only on heavy days?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Ahh, it happens multiple times a day on training days, doctor. I have been pushing weights again since last month. Also I have been getting this headache often — like almost countless times some weeks.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: This headache — is it on one side or all over the head? Any blurring of vision or nausea with it?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: It is mostly at the back of the head, doctor, throbbing type. Nah, no blurring or nausea. But it comes in the morning mostly.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Tell me about your sugar readings. You were on metformin — are the levels under control now?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Ugh, that is the issue doctor. I check every morning and the fasting sugar is still going up — since last three weeks it has been above 200. I am continuing metformin as prescribed.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: And what about your diet? You were supposed to cut down junk. Are you still eating fast food?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Ahh doctor, I am trying but honestly the fast food is still there — post-workout I grab something quick. And yes, I know you will scold me — I also started vaping again.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Arjun, seriously! How often are you vaping? And are you working in any environment with chemicals or have you been around a sick person recently?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: The vaping is every morning and sometimes post-gym too. About chemicals — the gym recently started using some strong cleaning agents, so maybe. And a teammate had viral fever — he is basically a sick person I trained with.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Okay. Any sore throat, cough, or shortness of breath — especially from that chemicals exposure at the gym?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Nah, no cough as such. But my throat feels dry and scratchy — chronic thing doctor, probably the vaping.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Right, so that dry scratchy throat is chronic pharyngeal irritation from vaping. And those morning headaches with fasting sugar above 200 — this is uncontrolled hyperglycemia causing vascular tension, Arjun.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: So the headache is from the sugar? I doubt it is something more serious, right doctor?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: The headache is most likely from the uncontrolled hyperglycemia. To rule out other causes we will do a HbA1c, fasting blood glucose, and a blood pressure check today. We also need to revisit your hernia repair site with an ultrasound abdomen given that pulling.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Should I continue metformin alone or do you think we need to add something, doctor?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: We are upgrading your regimen, Arjun. I am adding glimepiride 1 mg with dinner, and we will start sitagliptin 50 mg once daily. Continue metformin 500 mg twice daily as before. For the headache, take paracetamol 500 mg as needed for now.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Okay doctor. And for the gym — can I continue lifting or should I rest the abdomen more?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: No heavy abdomen loading — no deadlifts or weighted squats until the ultrasound abdomen report is clear. The vaping must stop completely — it is worsening your chronic pharyngeal irritation and affecting your blood sugar control. Cut the fast food too — your sugar will never settle otherwise.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Understood doctor. I will get the HbA1c and ultrasound abdomen done this week and come back.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Good. Come back in two weeks with the reports. Watch the fasting sugar every morning and note it down — I want to see the trend. Take care of yourself, Arjun — you are young, the body will respond well if you cooperate!

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Come in, please sit down. How are you doing today?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, I am a fisherman, I am working near the sea only. I came because you called me for the reports.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Yes, your blood sugar reports came and also the other test results. But first tell me, how are you feeling? Any new complaints?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, that passing urine thing is still there — I mean frequent urination — it is happening constantly, even every night I am waking up. I cannot sleep properly.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Okay. And you had come earlier mentioning some irregular periods and white discharge also, right? Is that still going on?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Umm, yes doctor, that white discharge is there for three months now. Periods also not coming properly for two years. I am not knowing what the problem is exactly.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Is the discharge slightly painful or any itching in that area?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Ahh, yes doctor, it is slightly painful sometimes near the lower abdomen. Itching also a little bit.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Do you drink contaminated water near the fishing area or eat contaminated food sometimes? Any international travel recently?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, we are drinking whatever water is available near the boats. Clean water we are not always getting. Travel outside India? No, I am not going anywhere.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Okay. Last week you had that fever episode — do you think you may have had dengue? Any body ache or rash at that time?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, last week fever was very bad. Body was paining a lot. Someone in the village said it may be dengue only. Rash also came on the arms.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: We had checked your heart rate during that visit — it was fast. And for your stomach complaints earlier, endoscopy and colonoscopy were advised. Did you get those done?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: The endoscopy I did, doctor. Colonoscopy I could not do, very costly it is. Heart rate test also was done that day you told.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Now coming to your sugar reports — your HbA1c is still very high. Despite the medicines prescribed earlier, the blood sugar is truely not under control. This is a serious matter.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, I am taking the medicines, whatever was prescribed. But I am not knowing the names properly. Sugar problem is there for two years now.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Looking at your reports and all your symptoms — the irregular periods, white discharge, weight gain, and uncontrolled sugar — this is a case of PCOS, that is polycystic ovary syndrome, combined with poorly controlled diabetes.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, this PCOS — what is that? I am not understanding these big words.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: It is a problem in your ovaries — small fluid-filled sacs form there, and it disturbs your hormones, causing irregular periods and discharge. Sugar problem also makes it worse.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I am prescribing metformin at a higher dose for the sugar, and adding combined oral contraceptive pill to regulate your periods. For the discharge, take fluconazole tablet.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, any side effects from these medicines? And what about my food and the water I am drinking at the fishing area?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Avoid contaminated water completely — boil or filter it always. Contaminated food from outside also avoid. Metformin can cause nausea initially but it will settle.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Also, do walking exercise at least 30 minutes daily — it will help control sugar and also help with PCOS. We need to check your fasting blood sugar and pelvic ultrasound next.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, I will try the walking. That frequent urination at night — will it reduce after this treatment? It is every night happening, very disturbing.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Once your blood sugar comes under control with metformin, the frequent urination will definitely reduce. Come back in one month with the fasting blood sugar and pelvic ultrasound reports.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Hello, come in, come in. Sit down please. You must be the young lady whose reports came in today?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, I came with my mother. She is waiting outside. We were very worried about the reports.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Alright, let us go through everything carefully. Tell me, how long has this cough and breathlessness been going on?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, the cough has been there from long time, maybe six to seven months. But the breathlessness and wheezing became very bad for a week only.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: And apart from the wheezing, have you noticed anything like puffy eyes in the mornings, or swelling anywhere on the fingers?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, my fingers look a little swollen and my puffy eyes are there every morning. My mother also noticed it. I thought it was just tiredness.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I see. Any redness or pain near the ears or around the temple area? Any headache?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Umm, there is some thin rash near my temple and sometimes near the ears also. Headache is there occasionally.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Have you had any irregular periods? How long has that been going on?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, irregular periods are there from long time. It comes every other day it feels like — sometimes very light, sometimes it skips. I was too shy to mention before.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: That is okay, you must tell me everything. Any history of knee replacement or any surgery in the family, or are you yourself on any long-term medicines?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: My grandmother had knee replacement doctor, but I myself have no surgery. I am not on any medicine regularly. We cannot afford much doctor, money is very tight for us.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Understood. Has anyone at home been smoking? Any dust or sun exposure for long hours?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: My father does smoking doctor, a pack a day at home only. And I travel to school in open vehicle, so yes, dust is there daily. Sun exposure is also a lot because we live in open area.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any hepatitis or jaundice history? Any skin rash that comes and goes often?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Not aware of any hepatitis doctor. But the skin rash on my face comes often, I thought it was just pimples. Never checked for it properly.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Now let me show you the reports. The ultrasonography shows mild fluid around the lungs, the ECG shows some changes in rhythm, and the Echo shows early pericardial involvement. These findings are very important.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, what does all this mean? Is it something very serious? We are already struggling so much with money.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I understand your worry. Looking at everything — the butterfly rash on your face, puffy eyes, irregular periods, swollen fingers, wheezing, the ECG and Echo findings, and the sun exposure history — this is a case of Systemic Lupus Erythematosus, what we call SLE. It is an autoimmune condition and needs careful management.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Ahh, doctor — lupus? I have heard that word but never thought it could happen to me. Why did this happen?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: SLE can be triggered by prolonged sun exposure, genetic factors, and stress. Your breathlessness and wheezing are because of lung involvement, which the ultrasonography confirmed. The irregular periods and puffy eyes are also part of the same picture.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I am starting you on hydroxychloroquine for the autoimmune part, low-dose prednisolone for the inflammation, and I am also adding probiotics to protect your gut while you are on steroids. We will also do a repeat ECG in two weeks.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, these medicines — are they very costly? We really cannot spend too much. And what about the cough and wheezing, any separate medicine for that?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I will prescribe the generic versions, they are much cheaper. For the wheezing I will add a salbutamol inhaler. Most importantly — strictly avoid sun exposure, cover your temple and face when going out, and please ask your father to stop smoking indoors as passive smoke is worsening your breathlessness. Do not miss any dose of hydroxychloroquine.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: I will tell my father doctor. Thank you so much for explaining everything clearly. I will come for the follow-up ECG and also the repeat Echo as you said.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Come in, come in. Please sit down. What has brought you here today?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor saab, my child is very sick. He has been having fever and loose motion since 2024, I mean, this started some months back but now it has become very bad since last three days.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Okay, let me examine the child. How old is the boy? And has there been any vomiting also along with the loose motion?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: He is seven years old doctor. Yes, vomiting is also there, intermittently only. He passed motion four to five times today, it is very watery.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Is there any stiffness in the neck? Any rash on the body? These things we always need to check in a child with high fever.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Umm, neck stiffness I did not notice doctor. No rash also. He is just very weak and not eating anything since yesterday.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Good. No neck stiffness is reassuring — that rules out something more dangerous. The fever is high grade and the loose motion is watery, which together point to an acute gut infection. Now, let me ask — have you recently taken the child to any village or crowded area?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, we went to my wife's village two weeks back. Very congested area, open drainage everywhere. And there was a lot of pollution also, some factory nearby was burning waste.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: That is very important history. Contaminated water and pollution in such areas are very common triggers for gut infections in children. The child likely picked up a bacterial or viral infection there. Did the child drink water from a hand pump or open well?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, hand pump water was there. We used to boil it but in the village we did not do that properly.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Understood. Now, is there any abdominal pain? And any blood or mucus in the stool? Also, check — is he passing any urine or has it gone down significantly?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Stomach pain is there doctor, he is holding his stomach and crying. Urine is also less, I noticed since this morning. No blood in stool as far as I can see.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Reduced urine output with loose motion and vomiting means the child is getting dehydrated. This is the danger sign we watch for. We must replace fluids urgently. Let me also examine his abdomen and check for tenderness.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, can this also be because of gastritis? Someone in the village told me he has gastritis only, nothing serious.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: No no, this is not simple gastritis. Based on the travel history, the contaminated water, the watery loose motion and fever, this is acute infective gastroenteritis, most likely bacterial. It can become serious if dehydration is not managed quickly.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, I am a daily-wage worker, I cannot afford too many tests. Please guide us simply. Also, I want to ask — this child has had stomach troubles long time, does he also have sugar problem?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Regarding sugar problem — that is rare in children his age but I understand your concern. For now let us focus on this acute illness. We will do a stool routine examination and a basic blood test — just CBC and blood glucose to check the sugar point you raised. Nothing very expensive.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Thank you doctor, you are very kind. We were very scared coming here.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Do not worry, the child is in good hands. I am prescribing ORS sachets — give one sachet dissolved in clean water every time after loose motion. Also starting zinc syrup once daily for fourteen days, and paracetamol syrup for the fever. Since the stool looks bacterial, I am adding azithromycin syrup for five days.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, anything we should be careful about at home? And he was having this stomach trouble intermittently even before — should I worry about that?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Yes, important things — only give boiled and cooled water, stop any outside food, watch for signs like sunken eyes, very dry lips, or no urine for more than six hours — if these happen, come immediately to emergency. Regarding the intermittent stomach troubles, that could be worm infestation or mild gastritis — we will address that once he recovers.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, one more thing — I myself have had acidity and gastritis for a long time. I used to take some tablet from the chemist but it is gone better on its own now. Should I do any test?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: For your own gastritis, if the acidity comes back or you get pain in the upper abdomen, come in separately. We can do a H. pylori test which is not very costly. Given your work with pollution exposure and irregular eating habits, it is worth checking.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, eating is very irregular, no fixed time. Work is in the sun the whole day also.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: That irregular eating is a big contributor to gastritis. For the child, come back after three days with the stool report and CBC result. If fever does not come down or loose motion increases, come same day — do not wait. Take care.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Good morning, please have a seat. I see this is for insurance documentation purposes today.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, my factory is asking for a full medical report. I am seven months pregnant also, so wanted everything checked.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Alright. Let us start from the beginning. How have you been feeling? Any complaints since morning?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, I have been having this BP problem few weeks now, and headache is there non-stop. Also swelling in my wrist since yesterday.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Is the swelling in the wrist dry or is there any fluid feeling? Does the headache gets better with rest?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: The swelling is dry only doctor, no fluid. The headache is intermittent, it gets better sometimes when I lie down.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Before this pregnancy, did you have irregular periods or any BP problem earlier also?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, I had irregular periods for a long time. And anemia was also detected two years back. The doctor gave me iron tablets that time.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any blurred vision, nausea, or vomiting happening? How many times?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Umm, nausea I had countless times in the early months but it is less frequent now. Blurred vision is present also, started since yesterday.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Do you work on the factory floor directly? Any chemical fume or heavy metal dust exposure? How do you commute — do you use public transport?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, I work near the chemical fume area packing section. And I travel by public transport daily — very crowded buses. Since morning I was standing in the bus for almost one hour.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I see. Do you drink alcohol? Any smoking?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, I stopped the alcohol. I was drinking since I was young but once pregnancy was confirmed I stopped fully. I am a social smoker only, social smoker since college days.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Good that you stopped alcohol. Have you done any tests recently? Any urine protein test or blood pressure monitoring done?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Ahh, blood pressure monitoring was done at the government hospital. They said reading was high but I did not do urine protein test doctor. I also did hemoglobin test — it was low, around nine point two.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any chest pain or shortness of breath? Any abdominal pain in the upper abdomen?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Shortness of breath is there since morning doctor. Chest pain — I doubt it, it is more like heaviness. Upper abdomen is also paining a little.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Based on everything — the high BP problem, blurred vision, swelling in the wrist, upper abdominal pain, and your anemia background — this is looking like preeclampsia. This is a serious pregnancy complication and needs urgent attention.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, is it very dangerous? The headache is intermittent only, it is not non-stop all the time.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Even intermittent symptoms with this pattern are risky in pregnancy. You must avoid all chemical fume exposure at the factory and stop using crowded public transport immediately. No more long standing.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I am prescribing labetalol for your BP problem, calcium tablets for pregnancy support, and you must restart iron and folic acid tablets for the anemia. Take labetalol twice daily as I am writing.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, my irregular periods history — will that affect the baby also? And will the swelling in wrist go on its own?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: The irregular periods history is noted in your record. The swelling in wrist — right now it may gets better with rest and elevation, but once we control the BP problem it should reduce. We will do urine protein test, complete blood count, and liver function test today for documentation also.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Thank you doctor. I will do all tests today itself and bring the reports for the insurance file.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Arre, Ramesh bhai! Long time. How are the children? That eldest son of yours, did he get the job he was applying for?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Haha, doctor sahib, yes he got it finally! Thank God. And your family is fine? Heard your daughter passed her exams with top marks!

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Yes yes, she did very well. Okay, enough of that — now let us talk about you. You are looking a bit tired, and I have your lab reports here from last month.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, honestly I have been not able to sleep worse at night it is, and the teeth pain is also coming more often lately. I am running the stall from morning to midnight so stress is also there.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Okay, okay. And the piles complaint you had — is that still troubling you? Any bleeding from the bottom?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, continuously it is there. Severe pain when I sit for long hours at the stall. And that hernia on the groin side, it is bulging out several times a day when I lift the heavy vessels.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Alright. Tell me about the medicines you are taking — I know you are going to three or four different doctors also, no?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, one doctor gave me tramadol for the teeth pain, and another doctor started simvastatin for cholesterol. That abscess on the back was drained in 2020 — that doctor also gave some tablets but I stopped those.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: You have diabetes since long, right? And you had COVID also — when was that?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Diabetes is there for many years, and COVID I had in 2020 only, same time as the abscess surgery. Also doctor, that time family member was sick in the house so it spread to me also I think.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Okay. Any history of osteoporosis or bone weakness? And any family history of heart disease?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: The bone problem — yes, they told me osteoporosis is there. And heart disease, umm, my father had it but I myself — negative, no chest issue for me yet. As a teenager I had some murmur they said but nothing since.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Do you chew tobacco? I have asked you before also. And what about that weed habit your friend mentioned?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Ahh doctor, chewing tobacco I am doing for 30 years, I know it is bad. Weed I take occasionally only, nothing regular. And gym I was doing for 20 years but stopped two years back because of the hernia.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Okay. Now let us go through your reports. The urine culture came back with some bacterial growth — nothing alarming but needs treatment. The thyroid test shows your TSH is elevated, which could explain the not able to sleep and fatigue you are feeling.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, thyroid — I have heard of it but what does that mean for me? And that PET scan the other doctor referred — did the report come?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: The PET scan report confirms what I was suspecting — you have hypothyroidism, and there is also early evidence of rectal inflammation from the long-standing piles. The hernia at the groin is an inguinal type and will need surgical repair soon.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, I was worried about the piles because the bleeding is there several times in a week. And the teeth pain — umm, it is severe at night especially, worse at night than daytime.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: For the hypothyroidism, I am starting you on levothyroxine — take it empty stomach every morning. For the urinary infection from the urine culture result, I am prescribing nitrofurantoin for one week. Continue the simvastatin but stop the tramadol from that other doctor — it is not safe with your diabetes medicines.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, that simvastatin — can I take it with the new levothyroxine? And should I be worried about the heart disease risk with all this cholesterol?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Yes, there is a gap of at least four hours needed between levothyroxine and simvastatin — take one in morning, one at night. The chewing tobacco you must stop completely — it is worsening the teeth problem and increasing heart disease risk also. With osteoporosis plus diabetes, the weed also must stop — it affects bone density.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, I understand. That chewing tobacco for 30 years — I have tried to stop but it is difficult when you are standing at the stall the whole day. The not able to sleep is making everything worse, I feel like it is continuously bothering me now.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I understand it is hard with your work stress. For the hernia surgery and piles surgery — both need to be scheduled within two months. No heavy lifting at the stall until then. The not able to sleep should improve once the hypothyroidism is under control with levothyroxine.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: For the teeth pain doctor, should I see a dentist? That pain is more often lately and without the tramadol I am not sure how to manage. What test should I do for that?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Yes, definitely go to a dentist — the long-term chewing tobacco use for 30 years has damaged the teeth and gums. I will refer you for a dental X-ray and oral examination. Come back in three weeks after starting the new medicines — we will repeat the thyroid test to see if levels are improving. Take care, Ramesh bhai.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Hello, come in, please sit. What is your name?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Sunita, doctor. I came last month also, you gave me some tablets.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Okay Sunita, so you are here for refill of your medicines? How are you feeling now, any new tiredness or dizziness?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, body is very weak-like, for three months I am feeling like this only. Head is also going round-round multiple times a day.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Is there any paining in the lower back or calf area also?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Ahh yes doctor, lower back is paining daily, and the calf part here — it is cramping sporadically, not every time.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Does the calf feel warm to touch when it is cramping?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Umm, yes doctor, it is feeling warm also sometimes. I thought it is because of walking only.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Okay. Are you eating properly? Any loss of appetite or nausea?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, food is not going properly. I am eating very less, after meals also stomach is feeling full and uncomfortable.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Are you living near any factory or road construction? Any lead exposure from paint or old pipes at home?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, our building is old type only, pipes also old. And husband is smoking every day inside the house, so secondhand smoke is there.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Do you yourself smoke or drink alcohol?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Denied, doctor, I never do all that. I quit even chewing tobacco two years back only.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Good. Were you taking the iron tablets and folic acid I gave last time? Were you taking them every day?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Umm, doctor, sometimes I forget. Not every day I took. Maybe never properly like full course I finished.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Sunita, I think your main problem is iron deficiency anaemia and vitamin B12 deficiency. That is why weakness, dizziness, and cramping in the calf are happening. We also need to check your kidney function because of the lower back pain.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, kidney problem also is there? What to do now?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Do not worry, I am ordering some blood tests today — KFT to check kidney and also EKG because of the cramping and fatigue. We will also check your haemoglobin and serum B12 levels again.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, one more thing — lower back pain is cramping type and for three months it is not going. Is that kidney only?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: It could be from muscle weakness due to anaemia itself, or kidney-related, so the KFT will tell us. Also, because of your blood pressure history, I want to continue enalapril — please do not stop it.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, enalapril I was taking, but tablets for anaemia also please give again, I will take properly this time.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Yes, I am prescribing ferrous sulphate tablet every day after meals, vitamin B12 injection once a week for one month, and folic acid tablet daily. Take all of these without skipping.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Also Sunita, please ask your husband to stop smoking inside the house — secondhand smoke is making your breathlessness worse. And if old pipes are there, get drinking water checked for lead contamination.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Okay doctor, I will tell him. Thank you so much, I will come back after test results.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Welcome back. How are you feeling today after the hospital stay?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Umm, doctor, I am better than before but still having headache and some dizziness sporadically. The numbness in my hip side is also still there.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I see. How long were you having these symptoms before you finally came in? You had mentioned waiting quite a while.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Ahh, doctor, I was ignoring it for many weeks. The headache was intense but I thought it would go on its own. The numbness started six months ago actually.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: That is quite delayed. Do you have any history of hypertension? And any past surgeries I should know about?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, I have hypertension for last three years. I also had appendectomy done long back, and there is stone in the GB also which doctor said to monitor.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Okay. Is the dizziness watery, meaning like the room is spinning around you, or just a lightheaded feeling?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: More like spinning only, doctor. Sometimes when I get up from bed it feels very bad. And my head feels heavy after that.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Are you living in a rural area? Any exposure to dust or asbestos in the house or nearby construction?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes, we live in a rural area. There is lot of dust around. My husband works near old buildings so there may be asbestos also, I am not fully sure.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Understood. What about your physical activity level and screen time? Do you spend long hours on mobile or TV?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Umm, physical activity is very less, doctor. And screen time is quite a lot — I watch TV after meals for a long time and mobile also at night. Maybe 1 hour daily on mobile at least.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: What medicines were you sent home with from the hospital? Are you taking them regularly?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: They gave me hydrochlorothiazide for the blood pressure and entecavir also. And one cough syrup for the cough I had. I am taking them but sometimes I forget the morning dose.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Based on your history, the spinning dizziness, numbness in the hip area, and delayed onset since six months ago, this looks like vertebrobasilar insufficiency with peripheral neuropathy, likely worsened by uncontrolled hypertension.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, this is serious? Will the numbness go away fully?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: It can improve with proper treatment and lifestyle changes. You must not miss your hydrochlorothiazide dose — your blood pressure being high is the main culprit here. We will also order a MRI brain and nerve conduction study to assess the neuropathy extent.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I am continuing hydrochlorothiazide and entecavir as before. I am also adding methylcobalamin tablets for the numbness and betahistine for the dizziness. The cough syrup you can stop now if the cough has settled.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Should I stop screen time completely? And is there anything I must avoid with the stone in the GB?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Reduce screen time as much as possible, especially at night — it worsens headache and dizziness. For stone in the GB, avoid fatty and oily food. Also get a repeat ultrasound abdomen in one month to recheck the stone size.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Also, because you live in a rural area with dust exposure, please keep windows closed in the morning and wear a mask if going outside near any construction with possible asbestos. This can aggravate respiratory symptoms.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, what about physical activity? Should I start walking or something? I have been sitting at home since hospitalisation.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Yes, start gentle walking — 1 hour daily is the target but begin slowly with fifteen minutes only. Do not sit for long after eating; a short walk after meals is very helpful for blood pressure and also for the stone in the GB management.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Now, I want to do teach-back. Can you tell me in your own words — which medicines you are taking, and when you must come back to me urgently if something happens?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Ahh, so I take hydrochlorothiazide for blood pressure, entecavir, methylcobalamin for numbness, and betahistine for dizziness. I should come urgently if headache becomes very intense or numbness spreads beyond my hip. And I need to do MRI brain and nerve conduction study soon.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Very good, you have understood everything correctly. Follow-up in two weeks — take care and do not delay coming in next time.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Good morning. Please sit down comfortably.
