utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Morning doctor.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: So this is a routine screening for your bus driving license, correct? Any complaints since morning or in general?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Nothing big doctor. Just a small cyst on my forehead that is there few weeks now.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Okay, I can see that cyst on your forehead. Is it paining or growing in size?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: No pain. Just sitting there continuously, not growing.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any headache or dizziness? Any nausea every morning?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Umm, headache is there every morning when I wake up. I thought it was just tiredness from driving.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: How much alcohol are you taking? Be honest, it is confidential.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Ahh, doctor I drink twice a day. Morning and night. Used to drink even more earlier.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: And smoking? Do you currently smoke?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, 10 cigarettes a day now. Earlier it was a pack a day when I was doing night routes.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any caffeine — meaning tea or coffee — how much are you taking to stay awake on long routes?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Four to five cups of strong tea, doctor. Every trip.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any past history of epilepsy or asthma? Any international travel recently or pets at home?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Asthma was there in childhood doctor, no epilepsy. No international travel. We have a dog at home, so pets are there.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Are you currently taking any medicines? Like for cholesterol or any infection?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Uh, one tablet for cholesterol — doctor at my village gave it. I think it is simvastatin. And I finished a course of ciprofloxacin last month for some stomach infection.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Alright. I will now check your blood pressure and order a liver function test and complete blood count. The morning headache combined with daily alcohol is concerning.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Is it something serious doctor?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Based on what you told me — the morning headache, twice a day alcohol, and elevated blood pressure I am reading now — this looks like alcohol dependence with hypertension. The cyst on your forehead is likely a simple sebaceous cyst, not dangerous.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Okay doctor. So what do I take?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I am prescribing thiamine tablets for the alcohol effect on your nerves, and amlodipine 5 mg twice a day for your hypertension. Continue your simvastatin as before.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Regarding your driving license — no alcohol at all before driving, that is mandatory. Reduce caffeine intake also, it raises blood pressure. And cut down smoking gradually from 10 cigarettes a day to zero.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Okay doctor, understood. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Good morning, please come in and sit down comfortably.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Good morning doctor, thank you. My employer sent me for this health check-up.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Alright. Any complaints you want to tell me first, or shall we go through the screening form together?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, since yesterday my left side of the hand is swollen and paining. Also my knee is giving stiffness once in a while.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Okay, and have you noticed any puffiness on the face or swelling on the legs also?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, both legs are swollen for six months. In the morning it is worse and by evening it is slightly reduced.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any breathlessness, decreased urine output, or frothy urine happening?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Umm, frothy urine is there rarely doctor. Breathlessness is no as such, but tiredness is there all the time.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Were any blood tests or ultrasound done before? And what medicines are you currently taking?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, ultrasound was done six months back only. The report said some kidney shrinkage. I was on furosemide for the swelling but I stopped it on my own and took some local tablet my neighbour gave.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: You stopped furosemide on your own? Why did you do that? And what local tablet was it?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Ahh, I was feeling dizziness after taking it doctor. The neighbour gave gabapentin saying it will help the knee pain also. I do not know the full name.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I see. Any exposure to cats at home, or do you work near a factory or in a place with dust?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, the house where I work has three cats. And before this job I was in a factory for two years, lots of dust was there. I used to cough a lot then.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Okay. Do you run or do any physical activity? And any cocaine use or other substance use I should know about?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, I do running 30 minutes daily in the morning. Cocaine I used to take for six months some years back but I stopped completely now. No alcohol or smoking.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Alright, let me summarise what I am seeing — bilateral leg swelling, frothy urine, known kidney shrinkage on previous ultrasound, past cocaine use, and dust exposure — this is consistent with chronic kidney disease with possible nephrotic syndrome. The self-stopping of furosemide has likely worsened the fluid retention.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, is it very serious? Will my kidney fail completely?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: It is a serious situation but manageable if we act now. I am ordering a fresh ultrasound of the kidney, serum creatinine, urine protein creatinine ratio, and a complete blood count today. The left side swelling on your hand also needs examination — it may be fluid accumulation or a joint problem.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, should I restart furosemide? And is the gabapentin safe to continue for my knee?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Yes, restart furosemide 40 mg once daily after food — do not stop it again without asking me. For the knee stiffness, gabapentin is not the right choice as it can stress the kidney further. I will prescribe paracetamol 500 mg for pain as it is safer for your kidney.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Please avoid dust exposure as much as possible, and wear a mask when around the cats. Cat allergens can worsen kidney inflammation in some patients. Also, running 30 minutes daily is fine but avoid any strenuous activity that causes excessive sweating as it can worsen dehydration with furosemide.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, any diet restrictions? And the swelling on knee is there once in a while, should I use any support?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Reduce salt intake strictly — no extra salt on food, no packaged items. For the knee, a simple compression bandage when it is paining will help. Monitor the hand swelling — if it spreads to the left side of the body further, come immediately.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Thank you so much doctor, I will follow everything you said and come back after the test reports.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Come in, come in. Please sit down, take a breath.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, I am a daily-wage worker and I have been having heavy bleeding every night for the past few days, and a week ago it just got very cold and I was feeling faint around noon.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Okay, tell me — are your periods regular, or have they been off for a long time?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: They have been irregular from long time doctor. I have gone to a local informal doctor before but he just gave some powder and sent me home. The bleeding is happening all the time now.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any discharge also? Or pain in the both sides of your lower abdomen?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Present, doctor — yes, there is some whitish discharge and the pain on both sides is dull and dragging. Also I have these dark circles under my eyes now.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: How many times have you passed heavy clots — was it countless times or only at certain hours?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Umm, countless times doctor, especially around noon and then again at night. I am soaking through pads very quickly.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any history of hepatitis or any liver trouble before?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Present, doctor — they found hepatitis a week ago when I went to a government hospital but I did not continue treatment. I was also told I have gallstones on the right side of my abdomen.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Do you tobacco in any form? And do you swimming regularly, or any outdoor travel recently?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: I do chew tobacco doctor, a pack a day almost. And yes, I had travel to a village last month — there were many mosquitoes. I also had a mosquito bite that got swollen on my arm.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any swimming in open water or ponds during that travel?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Ahh, present doctor, I did wade through the pond water once. And my husband has been giving me alprazolam that some neighbour suggested for my anxiety and sleeplessness.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Are you also a known diabetic? Any one given you insulin before?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: That informal doctor gave me insulin injection once saying my sugar was high. I do not know the exact reading. The dark circles started after that only.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Let me summarise what I am seeing — you have irregular periods and heavy bleeding with discharge, pain in both sides, known hepatitis left untreated, gallstones, unsupervised alprazolam and insulin use, and a recent mosquito bite after travel. I am also noting dark circles and general weakness.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Based on the clinical picture, this looks like PCOS with secondary anaemia, possible pelvic inflammatory disease, and we need to rule out malaria given your mosquito bite and travel history.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, the quack also told me something about PCOS but I did not understand. Is that why the bleeding happens every night?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Yes, PCOS causes irregular bleeding and when left untreated from long time, it worsens. You must stop the alprazolam immediately — that was not appropriate, and please do not take unsupervised insulin.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Do you have any previous USG report or blood test results with you?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: I have an old USG report showing the gallstones, that is all doctor. Nothing else was done.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I will order an ESR and complete blood count for the anaemia, a repeat USG report for the pelvis and gallstones, and a colonoscopy may be needed if the bleeding does not settle. Malaria rapid test also today.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: For now I am prescribing tranexamic acid to control the heavy bleeding, iron supplements for anaemia and dark circles, and metformin for PCOS management — we will monitor your sugar properly before restarting any insulin.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Please stop chewing tobacco — a pack a day is very harmful with hepatitis and gallstones. Avoid swimming in open ponds, avoid self-medicating, and come back with all ESR and USG report results within three days.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Good afternoon. Please sit. What brings you here today — are you seeking a second opinion?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, other doctor I went to, he say some things but I not understand properly. My son he is having fever and loose motion about a week now.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I see. How old is your son and how many times is the loose motion happening? Is it every day?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: He is seven years. Yes, every day it is coming, several times also. And fever also coming several times in day.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Is there any vomiting? Any pain in the belly or near the navel area?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Umm, yes doctor, he is holding his belly like this and crying. Near navel area mostly he is saying it is paining. No vomiting but feeling like vomiting sometimes.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Is the fever cold and shivering type, or just continuous warm feeling?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: It is cold type doctor, he shiver and then fever going up. Also his joints he is saying they are paining.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Has he been in contact with any sick person recently? Any prolonged sun exposure also?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Ahh, yes doctor, his school friend was sick last week — so sick person contact is there. Sun exposure also, he is playing outside every day in afternoon.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any childhood illness before this — any big sickness as a teenager or earlier?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor he is only seven, so no childhood illness big before. But I myself had typhoid as a teenager. My wife she had malaria also 2-3 years back.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Based on the fever pattern, loose motion, belly pain near navel area, and the contact with a sick person, this looks like a case of acute gastroenteritis with possible viral fever. We must rule out typhoid also.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, what test we should do? Other doctor not tell us any test properly.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: We will do a USG of the abdomen to check the belly, and also blood tests for typhoid. Then follow-up in three days and if eye redness continues we will do an eye exam also.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Okay doctor, thank you. You are explaining very nicely, other doctor was very fast only.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I am prescribing oral rehydration solution to be given after every meal, paracetamol syrup for the fever, and zinc tablets for every day for ten days to help with the loose motion.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, I also want to ask — I myself am having heartburn after every meal 2-3 years now. And also weight gain is happening.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I see. Do you drink alcohol? How often?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Ahh doctor, I am truck driver, so I drink alcohol 3 times a week. My wife she is scolding me only but what to do.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: The heartburn and weight gain combined with regular alcohol intake is concerning. Any pain in joints or swelling in belly for yourself?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: No swelling doctor, but joints yes, little stiffness in morning time. The heartburn it is cold liquid feeling coming up in throat.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: That sounds like acid reflux. The alcohol is worsening your heartburn and contributing to your weight gain. I strongly advise reducing your alcohol intake.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: For your acid reflux, I am prescribing pantoprazole once in morning before food and antacid syrup to be taken after every meal.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Okay doctor, I will try to reduce drinking. And for son I will do USG today itself and come for follow-up as you said. Thank you doctor.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Hello, come in. So this is your post-surgery review visit, correct?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, I had the past surgery in 2024, the appendix removal one. I wanted to ask you about some other things also, doctor.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: We will get to everything, don't worry. First tell me, are you having any fatigue or weakness since the operation?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Ahh yes doctor, I am feeling weakness constantly. And sometimes my hands and feet are going cold, even in normal temperature.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any shortness of breath or dizziness also? And is there any palpitations feeling in the chest?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, the dizziness is there, yes. Sometimes I feel a squeezing kind of tightness in the chest also. But actually I wanted to ask, I have been taking some herbal leaf juice every morning — is that okay?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: We will come to that in a moment. Tell me first — are you eating properly after the past surgery? Any loss of appetite?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Umm, not eating too well doctor. My appetite is not anymore like before. I am eating very light things only — just rice and some soup mostly.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Have you been exposed to any fumes at work or living in crowded places? I am asking because your breathlessness needs to be assessed properly.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: I work in a small workshop, so yes doctor, there are fumes sometimes. And I stay in a hostel which is quite a crowded place honestly.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Okay. Have you done any blood tests recently? Like a complete blood count or serum iron levels after the operation?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: I did a complete blood count last month, doctor. The report showed low haemoglobin — around 9 grams. No other tests I did after that.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: And you mentioned herbal juice — what exactly? And are you on any medicines? Any iron supplements or vitamin tablets prescribed before?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: No doctor, not anymore taking those vitamin tablets. I stopped them two weeks back. The herbal juice is just some neem leaf juice I am drinking every morning. Also — doctor, I am also taking escitalopram for anxiety, 10 mg, prescribed by psychiatrist.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Okay, noted about the escitalopram. Regarding the squeezing sensation in the chest — any cardiac issues were suspected? Was heart disease ruled out?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, ruled out already. The cardiologist did an ECG and echocardiography in 2024 before my surgery, all was normal he said.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Alright. Based on your low haemoglobin, the cold extremities, constant fatigue, and poor diet after the operation, you are having iron deficiency anaemia with likely nutritional deficiency as well.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, can this iron deficiency anaemia cause the squeezing feeling in my chest also? That is scaring me a lot.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Yes, when haemoglobin is this low, the heart works harder and you can feel palpitations and squeezing sensation. Since cardiac cause is already ruled out, correcting the anaemia will help this constantly bothering you.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I am prescribing ferrous sulphate 200 mg tablets twice daily after food, vitamin C 500 mg once daily to help absorption, and multivitamin capsules once daily. Please continue escitalopram as advised by your psychiatrist.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, should I stop the neem leaf juice I am taking every morning? And any food I should be having more?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Yes, please stop that neem juice for now — it can interfere with iron absorption. Increase your intake of fumes-free, green leafy vegetables, lentils, and eggs. Avoid tea right after meals as it blocks iron absorption also.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: We should also do a serum iron, serum ferritin, and vitamin B12 level today, along with a repeat complete blood count after four weeks of treatment.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, the weakness in my legs — will that go away once the anaemia is treated? It is constantly there and making it hard to work in the workshop.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Yes, once your haemoglobin improves over the next four to six weeks, the weakness in your legs and the cold feeling in hands and feet will reduce significantly. Also try to reduce your time near fumes at the workshop — that will help your recovery also.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Hello there! Come in, come in. And who is this young one?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Good morning doctor. I am his mother. He is Arjun, he is eight years old. We came for his yearly check-up.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Very good. So Arjun, how are you feeling today? Any pain or tiredness troubling you?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Umm, uh-huh, some palpitations are there doctor, and my chest sometimes feels funny. It has been going on for almost a month now.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: How often do these palpitations happen?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: They come every other day, doctor. Sometimes several times in one day also.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: What does the feeling in the chest feel like? Is it very sharp, or dull, or fluttering?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: It is very sharp, doctor, like a sudden jolt. He also has some skin infection on the upper back that is long time not healing.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Let me see that skin infection. Is it warm to touch? Is there any discharge from it?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes, it is warm to touch. The discharge is watery, not thick. No bleeding though.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Has he been exposed to anyone unwell recently? Any someone at school with similar skin infection?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Uh-huh, yes doctor, there was someone at school last month who had rashes all over.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any known allergies? Any food allergy in particular?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: He has food allergy to peanuts, doctor. And general allergies to dust also. Family history of TB on my husband's side — his grandfather had it, it is chronic in the family, they say.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Does he do any physical activity or running regularly? And any drinking of sodas or sugary things?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Uh-huh, he does running and physical activity every day in school. And yes, he drinks sodas and sugary drinks also every day. I have been telling him to stop.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any medicines he is currently taking? And has he done any tests recently like fasting sugar or stool test?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: He is on dexamethasone for his skin infection that another doctor gave. The stool test was denied by him last time so we never did it. No fasting sugar done. The hydrochlorothiazide and clopidogrel are for his grandfather, not him — I just keep them in the same bag, sorry doctor.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: No problem. Any weakness in the upper back or numbness in the arms? I want to consider ordering an EMG if needed.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: He denied any numbness, doctor. But weakness in the upper back — yes, he complains sometimes, mostly after running.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Okay. Based on everything, the skin infection looks like a bacterial skin abscess with watery discharge, likely spread from someone at school. The palpitations and chest discomfort need monitoring — possibly supraventricular tachycardia given the family background of TB and cardiac stress.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I am stopping the dexamethasone — that is not right for a bacterial infection. Instead, I am prescribing a proper antibiotic course. We will also keep the clopidogrel and hydrochlorothiazide in mind for his grandfather only, of course.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Let us order a fasting sugar given the every day sugar drink intake, and an EMG for the upper back weakness. The stool test must also be done this time — no skipping.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Please avoid any running or heavy physical activity until the palpitations are investigated. The skin infection on the upper back should be kept dry and covered. Stop all sugary drinking also, given the fasting sugar concern.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Thank you so much doctor, we will do all the tests and come back.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Arjun! Good to see you up and about. How is your mother doing? She had called me last week, quite worried about you.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: She is fine doctor, thank you. She has been fussing over me non-stop since the hospital discharge. You know how she is.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Ha, that is what mothers do. So tell me, how are you feeling now after coming home? Any new complaints since discharge?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, last night I had this headache again, very sharp pain on the head. And this morning also I felt dizziness when I got up from bed.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Okay, okay. Is the headache comes and goes type, or is it there all the time?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: It comes and goes, doctor. But this morning it was happening multiple times a day. Very disturbing it was.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any numbness or tingling? Especially in the wrist or fingers area — you had mentioned that in hospital also.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Umm, yes doctor, the wrist is still giving problem. Sometimes there is numbness going up to the arm. It is quite sharp pain at times.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Alright. Now I also see in your hospital file that they found fatty liver on the ultrasound. Did you know about this before, or is it a new finding?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Ahh, they told me in hospital only doctor. I had no idea. Is it very serious? They used big words and I got confused.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Fatty liver simply means extra fat is getting deposited in your liver. It is not an emergency right now, but we must take it seriously and manage it. Think of it like fat slowly building up where it should not be.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Oh okay, I understand now. Doctor, also when I was younger I had some breathing problem and they told my family I had COPD. But since I stopped smoking I feel much better on that side.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Good that you mentioned COPD. Are you still smoking? And any drinking habits?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Smoking is not anymore, doctor. I used to be a social smoker in college only. Drinking I am an occasional drinker, maybe once a month with friends.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Good on the smoking. But even occasional alcohol can worsen fatty liver, so I would strongly advise you to stop that completely. Your liver needs rest right now.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, in the hospital they also mentioned something about a fistula. I did not understand what that means at all. Is it related to my current problem?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: A fistula is basically an abnormal connection between two body parts that should not be connected. In your case it was noted as a separate finding. It is not directly causing your headache or dizziness, but we need to monitor it separately.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: One more thing — did you do any international travel in the months before this episode started? Sometimes certain infections are picked up that way.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor! I had done international travel to Thailand for a college trip about three months back. Could that be the cause?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: That is very helpful information. Looking at everything — your headache, dizziness, numbness in the wrist and arm, the travel history, and your hospital reports — this appears to be a case of viral encephalitis with peripheral nerve involvement. The fatty liver is a separate metabolic finding.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Viral en... what doctor? Is it very dangerous? Should I be scared?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Do not panic. It simply means a virus caused some swelling inside your brain, and your body is now recovering. We will do a MRI brain and a nerve conduction study for the wrist numbness, and also a liver function test to track the fatty liver.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I am prescribing acyclovir tablets for the viral infection, betahistine for the dizziness, and vitamin B12 supplements to help with the numbness in your wrist. For the headache, take paracetamol as needed, no strong pain-killers.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Okay doctor, I will take all medicines. Anything else I should be careful about? Like for college and all?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Rest is very important — no late nights, no alcohol, no travel for now. Eat light food for the fatty liver. If the headache becomes sharp pain again multiple times a day, come immediately. We will review after the MRI brain report comes.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Come in, come in — I am running a bit behind today, so let us get started quickly.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Of course doctor, no problem. I was discharged two days back and they asked me to follow up with you.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Yes, I have your discharge notes here. Tell me, any chest pain, shortness of breath, or dizziness since discharge?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: No doctor, nothing like that. But I am getting this dull headache that comes and goes — it has been there over a year now.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Is the headache on one side? Any nausea or light sensitivity with it?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Umm, yes, sometimes on one side. My upper back is also paining all the time, and I feel some numbness in my toes.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: The one-sided dull headache with that pattern — that is likely migraine. The numbness in your toes is unlikely to be unrelated — it may be peripheral neuropathy from your diabetes.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Ahh doctor, I have had diabetes and thyroid problem for many years. And high cholesterol also. I was also told years back I had jaundice.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Okay. During your hospital stay, did they do a CT scan or EKG?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, they did CT scan of my chest and an EKG. They also mentioned doing a bone marrow biopsy if the blood counts did not improve.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any recent family member was sick at home? Any infection exposure before the admission?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, family member was sick — my wife had fever and cough about two weeks before I got admitted.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: And in the hospital they had you on dexamethasone and heparin? Were you given Tylenol for the headache as well?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, they gave me dexamethasone and heparin injections, and Tylenol for the pain. I felt a bit better but the headache is still there.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Are you taking any herbal or alternative remedies at home alongside your regular medicines?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Uh, yes doctor — I take some herbal liver tonic for my jaundice history and an herbal cholesterol supplement. I thought they are natural so no harm.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I would advise you to stop those herbal supplements for now — some of them interfere with your heparin levels and can affect liver function, especially with your past jaundice.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Understood doctor, I will stop them.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Good. Do you exercise or do any physical activity regularly?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, I have been doing swimming for 30 years. Even now I try to go every other day but the upper back pain is making it difficult.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: That is good habit, keep up the swimming once you are more stable. The upper back pain and numbness in the toes — we need your HbA1c and thyroid function test done this week so we can adjust your diabetes and thyroid medications properly.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, for this migraine and the upper back pain — should I continue taking Tylenol at home?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: For the migraine, I am prescribing sumatriptan — take it at the first sign of the attack. For the upper back pain, continue Tylenol as needed, and I am adding gabapentin at a low dose for the neuropathy in your toes. Also continue your statin for high cholesterol.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Thank you doctor. One more thing — my blood sugar has been fluctuating all the time since the past month.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: That is why the HbA1c is important right now. Get the lipid profile and liver function test done as well, given the jaundice history and herbal use. Come back in one week with all reports and we will fine-tune everything.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Arjun! Long time no see, yaar. How is your wife and the kids? Still in that same apartment in Koramangala?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: All fine, doctor! Kids are doing great. Wife got promoted actually. And yes, same apartment only. You know how it is.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Ha, good good! And you? Still doing those night shifts at the IT company? Must be exhausting.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, still night shifts. Umm, actually that is why I came. I have this small rash on my forearm and chest. Nothing serious, I think. Also some itching.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Small rash only or is there swelling also? Let me see. And when did this start — 10-15 days back or earlier?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Ahh, yes, 10-15 days it has been there. The itching is worse at night, which is when I am working. The rash looks a bit ring-shaped in some places. I just thought it was the AC or something.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Ring-shaped rash — that is a classic sign. Any discharge or blistering on the skin? And does the itching happen rarely or more like monthly even before this episode?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: No discharge, no blistering as such. But the itching — I think I used to get it monthly in a mild way, but I ignored it. Now it became severe so I came.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: You are working from around what time? And does the itching hit you around noon when you are trying to sleep, or during the shift?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Mostly when I am sleeping in the afternoon, yes, around noon. The room gets very hot, I sweat a lot, and then the itching starts badly. The heat definitely makes it worse I feel.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Yes, heat and sweating are big triggers for fungal infection. Tell me, are you walking or doing any exercise? And are you still on cigarettes?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Walking I do on weekends only, doctor. Cigarettes — yes, I smoke 10 cigarettes a day. I know, I know. And caffeine is very high — three four coffees per shift minimum.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Office is an open workspace? Any colleagues who cigarettes near you — any secondhand smoke or smoke exposure in the break area?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, the break area is terrible. Everyone smokes there, so secondhand smoke is a lot. Earlier I used to smoke a pack a day but I cut down at least.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Good that you cut down. Now, any past medical issues — I remember you had some anxiety disorder and you went for hip replacement a year ago, correct? Any other previous operation?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, the anxiety disorder is still there, managed. The hip replacement was a year ago, recovering well. And I had a previous operation for appendix about five years back. That is all.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Good. Are you on any medicines currently — the lorazepam for anxiety still, or omeprazole for any gastric trouble? Any inhaler use?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes, I take lorazepam rarely now, only when anxiety is bad. Omeprazole I was taking for some gastric issue but I stopped. Inhaler — no, I never needed that.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Alright. I want to do a throat swab to rule out any fungal spread to the upper tract, and also considering your history post hip replacement, I want a spinal tap to rule out any deep-seated fungal infection risk — is that okay with you?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Umm, spinal tap sounds scary doctor. Is it really necessary? The rash is just on the skin na?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I understand your concern. Looking at the ring-shaped pattern, the forearm and chest involvement, and the sweating from heat — this is clearly dermatophyte fungal infection, what we call ringworm. The spinal tap I am suggesting only because of the post hip replacement status — immunological caution only, not panic.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Okay doctor, understood. Also I forgot to mention — I have burning sensation on the skin sometimes when I sweat. And my scalp also has some flaking 10-15 days now.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Yes, scalp flaking also points to fungal. I am prescribing a clotrimazole cream for the forearm and chest rash, fluconazole 150mg tablet once a week for four weeks, and a ketoconazole shampoo for the scalp. Also restart omeprazole since fluconazole can cause gastric irritation.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Most importantly — reduce that caffeine intake, keep the skin dry after sweating, avoid tight clothes in the heat, and please get away from that secondhand smoke break area. Smoking 10 cigarettes a day is also lowering your immunity and slowing recovery.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Okay doctor, I will follow all this. Should I do the throat swab today itself? And when to come back for follow up?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Yes, do the throat swab today from the lab downstairs. Come back in two weeks — if the rash is not reducing or itching is still severe, we will go ahead with the spinal tap also. And try to at least do that walking more than just on weekends — immunity needs it, yaar.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Welcome back. Good to see you up and about after the hospitalisation. How are you feeling today?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Thank you doctor. Honestly, I am still not fully okay. I am having puffy eyes in the morning and I am not able to sleep properly. The night shifts are not helping at all.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I see. Tell me about the stomach pain and acidity — are those still continuing after you were discharged?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, the acidity is there once a day, mostly after dinner. And there is gas also, it feels heavy and constant in the stomach.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Have you noticed any blood in stool? Any change in colour of the stool?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Umm, actually yes doctor — taking it seriously now because I saw blood in stool three days ago. It scared me quite a bit.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: That is important. Was there any nausea or vomiting along with that?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: There was some nausea, but no vomiting as such. My appetite has also reduced a lot since last week.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Are you taking any pain medicines on your own? Any acetaminophen or other over-the-counter tablets?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, I was taking acetaminophen regularly for the knee pain — almost once a day for the past month. I did not think it would cause any problem.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Ah, that is very likely contributing. Now tell me about your past history — I see you had a knee replacement. Any other surgeries or illnesses?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes, the knee replacement was done two years back. Also I have hypothyroidism which I am managing with tablets.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Do you smoke or use any tobacco? What about alcohol?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Ahh, I used to smoke about 5 cigarettes per day but I have reduced now. I drink socially — around 2 drinks a week, though during project deadlines it goes up to 3 beers a day sometimes.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any recent exposure to cats, insect bites, or crowded places? I am asking because of the puffy eyes you mentioned.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: We did adopt a cat at home last month. And yes, I was at a conference in a hall full of people — quite crowded places. No major insect bites that I remember.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Let me do a quick check-up — I will check your pulse and abdomen also. Any pain near the ovaries region for you? And any breathlessness or lung related complaints?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: No, nothing near the ovaries. And absent any lung issue as such — no cough or breathlessness, doctor.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Your pulse is normal. On pressing the upper abdomen there is some tenderness. I will order a stool occult blood test and upper GI endoscopy to check the stomach lining properly.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, so what exactly is going on? Is it something serious from the blood in stool?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Based on your history of regular acetaminophen use, alcohol intake, and night shift stress, this looks like a case of peptic ulcer disease with gastritis. The blood in stool suggests the stomach lining is irritated and possibly ulcerated.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Oh that sounds worrying. What should I avoid, doctor? And is the puffy eyes connected?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: The puffy eyes are likely an allergic reaction from the cat exposure — avoid keeping the cat in your bedroom. Also stop acetaminophen immediately and reduce the alcohol. No spicy food, no late-night eating, and try to regulate your sleep even with the night shifts.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I am prescribing pantoprazole 40 mg before breakfast, sucralfate suspension after meals, and domperidone for the nausea and gas. For the puffy eyes, take cetirizine at night. Please stop the acetaminophen completely.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Okay doctor, I will follow everything you said. Thank you so much for explaining everything clearly.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Hello, come in, come in. Please sit down comfortably. What is your name, son?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: I am Rohan, doctor. I am 16 years old. My parents sent me here for some surgery clearance check.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Alright Rohan, before we do the pre-operative clearance, I need to understand your general health. What is bothering you these days? Any pain or discomfort anywhere?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, umm, I have been having shoulder pain on the lower part of my shoulder and also some heaviness near the spleen area and navel area. It is very uncomfortable, doctor.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Okay, that is quite a few areas. Is this shoulder pain sharp or more like a dull ache? And since when?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: It started this morning very suddenly, but the heaviness near the spleen side has been there for a couple of days now. It is paining constantly, not going away at all.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I see. Any nausea, vomiting, or fever along with this? And have you had any bleeding or loose motion?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Ahh, no fever doctor, but I did have nausea a few times since 10-15 days. And my stomach feels bloated too.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Rohan, I want to ask you something and I need you to be honest with me, okay? Do you drink alcohol? There is no judgment here.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Umm, doctor please don't tell my parents, but yes, I have been drinking. My friends started it and I got into it. I have been doing it for 10 years... uh wait no, I mean, I know I am only 16, I started very young, maybe 3 years.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I understand, Rohan. It takes courage to share that. Do you also use tobacco in any form? And are you doing any running or physical exercise regularly?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: I did try tobacco a couple of times, doctor. And yes, I do running for school sports. But lately the shoulder pain and navel area heaviness is stopping me from exercising.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Have you had any recent hospital visit or exposure to birds or any animals? And any past fracture or surgery?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, I had a fracture in my left arm two years back, that is why surgery is planned now. And there was one hospital visit last month for chest pain but they said nothing serious. We also have birds at home, pigeons actually.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Okay. Are you taking any medicines on your own for this pain? Any painkillers from the pharmacy without prescription?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Ahh, yes doctor. I have been taking ibuprofen and sometimes antacid tablets on my own. I did not tell anyone. The ibuprofen helps a few times but then the pain comes back near my navel area constantly.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I see. Any yellowing of your eyes or skin? Any weight loss recently?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Umm, my mother did say my eyes looked a little yellow couple of days ago. And I have lost some weight I think, my clothes feel loose. There is also itching on my skin sometimes.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Rohan, based on what you are telling me, we need to do a few tests urgently. I am ordering a liver function test, complete blood count, abdominal ultrasound, and a chest X-ray also, given your history of chest pain.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, is this serious? Why would my spleen be hurting and why the yellowing? I am really scared now.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Rohan, I want to be honest with you gently. The combination of jaundice, the heaviness near the spleen, nausea, and your alcohol use is pointing strongly towards alcoholic hepatitis with possible early liver damage. The ibuprofen you are self-taking is also making the stomach lining worse.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, will I be able to have the surgery for my fracture repair? And what should I do now? I am very worried, I do not want my parents to be upset.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: The surgery for the fracture will have to be postponed until your liver function stabilizes — surgery under liver damage conditions is very risky. You must stop all alcohol immediately and stop the self-medication with ibuprofen completely. Your parents will need to know, but I will speak to them kindly alongside you.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: For now I am prescribing ursodeoxycholic acid tablets to support liver function, pantoprazole for your stomach lining, and multivitamin syrup with zinc supplements to help with your weight loss and nutritional deficit. Absolutely no ibuprofen or any NSAIDs from here on.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Thank you doctor for not being harsh. I will follow everything. I just hope the shoulder pain and the navel area pain also get better soon. I promise I will stop alcohol and tobacco completely.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Very good attitude, Rohan. You must also rest completely, stop running or any strenuous exercise until your liver function test reports come back normal. Avoid any birds contact at home as respiratory infections can worsen your recovery. Come back in 10-15 days for repeat blood work and we will reassess the surgery plan.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Good morning, congratulations on the new baby. Please sit, I am little behind schedule today so let us get straight to your reports.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Thank you doctor. Actually I am quite worried. Since the delivery I am having yellowing of eyes and feeling very fatigued also.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Okay, noted. Any bloating or discomfort in the intestine area — like stomach feeling heavy or gassy?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, the bloating is very bad, it comes every few days and I also feel a dull ache near my chest sometimes.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any pain radiating to the spine or back? Any nausea or vomiting?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Umm, slight back pain near the spine, yes. Nausea is also there, especially in the mornings. Vomiting — no, not at all.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any history of diabetes or heart problems like bypass surgery?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, I have diabetes and my father had bypass surgery. I myself have no heart operation but I used to take aspirin for some time over a year ago.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Are you currently on aspirin or any other medication like synthroid for thyroid?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Ahh, I stopped aspirin post-op after my C-section. And yes, I am on synthroid for my thyroid — been on it over a year now.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any animal hair exposure at home? Any pet dogs or cats?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, we have a cat at home so animal hair is everywhere. My itching on skin has been worsening also in this season.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Let me look at your lab reports. Did you get your thyroid test, EKG, and liver function test done?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, all done. I also got the lumbar puncture done as the neurologist had advised for my headaches.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Okay. Your liver function test shows elevated bilirubin and raised liver enzymes. Your thyroid test shows TSH is slightly off too, so synthroid dose may need adjustment.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, what does all this mean? Is the yellowing connected to the bloating in the intestine?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Yes, this is a case of jaundice along with fatty liver. The diabetes is likely contributing to the fatty liver, and post-delivery hormonal changes are worsening it further.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Is the seasonal change making it worse doctor? I feel the bloating and itching worse in this cold weather particularly.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Yes, seasonal dryness and the animal hair at home can aggravate itching and also put stress on the intestine through allergic pathways. The bloating every few days fits this picture.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I am prescribing ursodeoxycholic acid for fatty liver, and cetirizine for the itching. Take cetirizine after meals. I will also revise your synthroid dose based on the thyroid test.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Should I stop aspirin completely? And is breastfeeding okay with these medicines?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Yes, do not restart aspirin right now as it can worsen liver inflammation. Cetirizine is safe for breastfeeding but take it after meals only to avoid gastric irritation. Avoid the cat in the feeding room if possible.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, should I repeat the EKG also? And the lumbar puncture report — the neurologist said wait for your opinion.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: The EKG looked normal, no concerns there. The lumbar puncture report shows no infection. Your headaches are likely tension-type related to the fatigue post-delivery. Focus on rest and hydration.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Thank you so much doctor, I will follow everything carefully.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Come in, come in. You look a bit pale today — what happened?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, I came in just now from the gym, and I am feeling dizzy and breathless. My gums have been bleeding nonstop for the past hour. It is scaring me honestly.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Okay, let me check. Any fatigue, pallor, or palpitations also? You do sports regularly, right?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes, I play football and do heavy weight training daily. The fatigue has been there on and off but the gum bleeding from the gums is new and the dizziness is worse than usual.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any joint pain, rashes on the skin, or hair fall lately?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: The hair fall is there once in a while, but I attributed it to the gym stress. Joint pain is hardly ever there. No rashes.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Do you take any supplements or medicines at home? Any cough syrup or over-the-counter stuff recently?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes, I was taking a cough syrup last week for a viral. I also take synthroid for my hypothyroidism — been on it for 30 years almost, since childhood diagnosis.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Okay. Any pets at home? And seasonal changes — does all this worsen in winter or summer?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes, we have two dogs at home, so pets are there. And honestly, every winter my fatigue and breathlessness get significantly worse. I thought it was just the cold weather affecting my performance.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Do you smoke or consume cannabis?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: I take cannabis socially at parties, not regularly. I do not smoke cigarettes at all.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Have you done any blood work recently? Any complete blood count or serum ferritin done before?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: I had a CBC done three months ago and my haemoglobin was borderline low — around 10.5 — but my trainer said it is fine for endurance athletes. I did not follow up.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any tingling or numbness in the hands or feet? Any mouth ulcers or soreness around the tongue?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Umm, yes actually — some tingling in the fingers once in a while post-workout. And my tongue has been feeling smooth and sore for a few weeks. I did not connect it.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Putting it all together — the gum bleeding, fatigue, pallor, smooth tongue, tingling in the fingers, and that low haemoglobin — this looks like combined iron deficiency anaemia with vitamin C deficiency, possibly early scurvy. The seasonal worsening fits as well.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Scurvy? I thought that was an old sailor disease, doctor. How is that possible when I eat well and do sports?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: High-intensity athletes actually have higher vitamin C turnover. The pets are not causing it, but combined with seasonal low fruit intake and the stress of heavy training, your stores depleted. The cough syrup has nothing to do with it, but some syrups do affect platelet function mildly.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I am prescribing ferrous sulfate 200 mg twice daily with food, vitamin C 500 mg twice daily — this will also help iron absorption — and folic acid 5 mg once daily. We will hold heparin for now as there is active gum bleeding and we do not want to thin the blood further.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Can I continue my workouts? And should I stop the synthroid or take it at a different time with these new medicines?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Take synthroid first thing in the morning on empty stomach as usual, and give a gap of at least two hours before the ferrous sulfate — iron interferes with thyroid absorption. Reduce gym intensity for the next two weeks at least, no heavy lifting while the dizziness and bleeding are active.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I want you to get a serum ferritin, vitamin C level, CBC, and TSH done today itself. Also cut down the cannabis — it is not helping your breathlessness or lung capacity with sport.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: How long before I start feeling better, doctor? And the gums — will the bleeding stop soon?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: The gum bleeding from the gums should reduce within one week once vitamin C kicks in. The anaemia will take six to eight weeks to correct fully. Come back in four weeks with the reports and we will recheck your haemoglobin. Do not skip the synthroid and increase citrus fruits and green vegetables in your diet starting today.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Hello, welcome back. Please sit down comfortably.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Thank you doctor. I was referred back from the higher centre. I have been having back pain and whole body pain for quite some time now, it is nonstop.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Okay. Where exactly is the pain? Is it all over the whole body or is it concentrated somewhere specific like the ovaries region?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Mostly whole body doctor, but sometimes lower back too. And I also get gastritis around noon after eating.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Do you have any cough or fever? Is the cough productive?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Not really, the cough is not much. Umm, but when it does come it is productive, with some phlegm.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Have you had any international travel recently, or any tick bite? The higher centre flagged this for immunological workup.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, we went abroad last summer. And I think I got a tick bite while we were hiking there. I did not think it was serious at the time.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any history of anemia or TB in the family or in yourself?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: My mother has anemia. As for me, yes, I had low hemoglobin detected two years back. No TB though.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I see from your referral notes that a throat swab and ECG were done at the higher centre. Were any other tests done there?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: They did some blood work and a ANA test also doctor. The ECG was okay they said, but the ANA test came back a little unusual.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Hmm okay. What about your vaccination history? Are all your vaccines up to date?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Umm, I think so doctor. I have my vaccination card at home. I missed one or two maybe because we were travelling.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I also heard you consulted a local healer before coming here. What did he give you for the back pain and whole body pain?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Uh, he gave some herbal tablets and told me to rest. I know doctor, my parents said I should have come here first only. He said it was just fatigue.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Are you walking or doing any exercise? And please be honest — do you smoke?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: I do go for walking 30 minutes daily. As for smoking, look, I sometimes try it with friends, maybe two packs a day is too much but it is once in a while only.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Based on the ANA test result, the tick bite history, and your ongoing whole body pain with the joint swelling, this looks like a case of Lyme disease with possible autoimmune overlap. We need to confirm further.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Lyme disease doctor? Is it very serious? What will happen now?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Do not worry, we caught it. I will order a Lyme serology and a repeat complete blood count to check for anemia. The gastritis around noon is likely from the herbal tablets that local healer gave you — we will address that too.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I am prescribing heparin carefully given the clotting markers from the higher centre report, and amlodipine for the elevated blood pressure we noted today. We will also start an antibiotic course after the throat swab culture result comes.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, is the smoking making things worse? And what about the ovaries pain I mentioned, is it related?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Yes, smoking absolutely worsens autoimmune conditions and inflammation throughout the whole body. The ovaries discomfort may be secondary to the immune response — we will do a pelvic ultrasound to rule out any structural issues. Please stop consulting local healers and avoid smoking completely.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Okay doctor, I will stop. Thank you so much for explaining everything clearly.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Come in, come in. Welcome back. Please sit down.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Thank you, doctor.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: So, it has been quite a while since your last visit. What has been going on? You can tell me, do not be shy.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Umm, doctor, I am having numbness in my hands three days ago it started, and also feeling very tired continuously.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Okay. Is the numbness on both sides, and is the skin in that area feeling warm to touch?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yeah, doctor, a little warm it is feeling. Both hands are affected.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any swelling near the lymph nodes — for example, in the neck or armpit area? And any changes near the breast?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Ahh, no doctor, nothing like that near breast or lymph nodes. Father told me to mention that I also get headache occasionally.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: We first diagnosed the thyroid problem and high cholesterol back in 2021, correct? That was the time we started treatment. Why did you stop coming for follow-ups?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Umm, we shifted to another city six months ago doctor, so we could not come. Sorry.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Understood. Were you continuing levothyroxine regularly at least? And were the iron supplements also taken as advised?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yeah, I was taking levothyroxine but the iron supplements I stopped after some time doctor. Father also gave me diazepam once when I was very anxious, but I did not take it again.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Okay. Any past illness — like measles or any major infection as a child?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yeah, doctor, I had measles when I was very small. No other big illness.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Good. Now I need to ask about lifestyle habits. Any drugs or recreational drugs ever tried? Like cocaine?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: No doctor, chronic nothing like that I have never taken. Not even cocaine. I am a student only.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: That is good. Any heavy sun exposure during school hours, or dust at home or school?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Uh, yes doctor, there is a lot of dust at school. And sun exposure is also there during games period occasionally.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Based on everything, this child has hypothyroidism which is a chronic condition, along with peripheral neuropathy likely contributing to the numbness, and the fatigue points to low iron deficiency as well. We also need to recheck the high cholesterol.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: We will need to run a PT INR and a vitamin B12 level today to understand the numbness better and check for any clotting issues.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, will I need to take many medicines? The numbness is worrying me a lot.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Do not worry. I am prescribing levothyroxine to continue as before, restarting the iron supplements properly this time, and I am also adding vitamin B12 tablets to address the numbness. Please do not take diazepam without prescription again.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Avoid sun exposure during peak afternoon hours and wear a mask if dust is heavy at school. No drugs or recreational drugs of any kind — these can worsen the thyroid problem and cholesterol.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, how long will this numbness take to go away?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Once the vitamin B12 and PT INR results come, we will have a clearer picture. If hypothyroidism is well-controlled, the numbness should improve gradually. Please do not miss follow-ups again — this is a chronic condition needing regular monitoring.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Good morning. Please have a seat. I see this is a documentation visit for insurance purposes.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yeah, but I have been feeling off also. puffy eyes in January, then drowsy all the time.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Noted. Any dark circles under the eyes? Any swelling near the abdomen?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yeah, dark circles are there. Abdomen feels bloated sometimes.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: How often are you feeling drowsy? Is the fatigue bothering you at gym also?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: It happens once a week badly. At other times also, I have crashed after training countless times.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: You mentioned gym. How frequently are you training? Do you drink alcohol?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Training 3 times a week. Alcohol, yes, was heavy before. Now less.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: When you say before — how much alcohol were you consuming? And do you smoke?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: I am a social smoker. Alcohol was daily for a few years. I have cut down now.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any international travel recently? Some of these symptoms — puffy eyes, fatigue — can follow infections picked up abroad.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, I went overseas for a competition in January. That is when the puffy eyes started.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any pain near the kidney area or lower back? Any burning in urine?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Mild ache near the kidney side, yes. No burning in urine.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: What about your knee? Any pain or swelling in the knee with all this training?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Left knee has been paining for a while. Dull ache mostly, no swelling.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Have you done any imaging for the knee? Any MRI or X-ray done?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Only a basic X-ray. Doctor had mentioned fluoroscopy but I never got it done.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Looking at the overall picture — puffy eyes, dark circles, kidney area discomfort, and your history of heavy alcohol use — this looks like early nephrotic syndrome with possible hepatic involvement. The knee issue is likely overuse injury.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Okay. Is it serious?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: We need to investigate properly. I am ordering fluoroscopy for the knee, kidney function test, liver function test, and urine protein test. Alcohol must stop completely.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: I also have high cholesterol and hypertension — already on some medicines from before.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Which medicines are you currently on? Are you taking atorvastatin and metoprolol?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, atorvastatin and metoprolol both. Taking them daily.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Good, continue both. I am adding furosemide for the puffiness and vitamin B complex for the fatigue and dark circles. Come back once all reports are ready and we will update your insurance documentation accordingly.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Come in, come in. No need to be nervous, just relax and sit down.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Thank you doctor. Umm, I have been having headache and dizziness frequently these days. It got very bad a week ago and I got scared.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Okay. Is there any numbness or tingling anywhere — in the hands or feet?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, there is numbness on my left arm, especially after that incident. It is very frightening for me.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I understand. Is the headache throbbing or pressure-like? And which part of the head is affected?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Ahh, it is more like pressure-like doctor, mostly at the back of the head. Sometimes the whole head is paining.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: You are here for your quarterly review. Are you taking your losartan regularly? Last time I told you not to miss doses.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Umm, doctor I am sorry. I was missing doses, maybe two or three times a week. I know it is bad but sometimes I forget. And I was taking Advil on my own for the headache.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Taking Advil on your own is not a good idea at all. Have you had any vomiting or blurring of vision with these headache episodes?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: No vomiting, but my eyes do feel a little blurring of vision sometimes. Also my stomach is burning a lot, like GERD type feeling after food.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: This GERD — is it happening frequently? And do you smoke or have any sleep habits that are disturbed?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, the GERD is almost frequently, especially after meals. And my sleep habits are very poor, I sleep only three to four hours. I also smoke, around 5 cigarettes a day and I have been doing this for 10 years.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: That is a lot of smoking over 10 years. Any pollution exposure at your workplace? Or any exposure to birds at home?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Ahh, yes doctor, I work near a construction site so there is lot of pollution. And we keep birds at home — pigeons and parrots actually.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Okay. Any breathlessness or cough that has developed recently?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Umm, yes doctor, cough is there a little, dry type. But main problem is the dizziness and headache.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Were you ever put on prednisone before for any inflammation or lung condition?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: No doctor, never. I have hypertension which you diagnosed before, and I was told to watch my blood pressure, that is all.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Looking at everything — the missed losartan doses, the numbness in the left arm, the pressure-like headache at the back of the head, and the dizziness — this is a case of uncontrolled hypertension with possible hypertensive encephalopathy. The GERD is likely aggravated by the Advil you were self-medicating with.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, it is sounding very serious. Will I be okay? What tests are needed now?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Yes, we need to act quickly. We will do a MRI brain and a fluoroscopy to rule out any swallowing issue related to your GERD. Also a blood pressure monitoring over twenty-four hours is needed.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I am increasing your losartan dose and adding a short course of prednisone for the inflammation. Please stop Advil completely — it is worsening your GERD and can raise your blood pressure further.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Okay doctor. What should I do about my sleep habits and the smoking? And is the birds exposure a problem?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Yes, the birds at home can trigger hypersensitivity pneumonitis, so please keep distance. Stop smoking immediately — 5 cigarettes a day for 10 years is already causing damage.
