Improve your sleep habits, try to get at least seven hours, and avoid pollution exposure with a good mask at the worksite.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Thank you so much doctor, I will follow everything properly this time, I promise.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Arre, Rajesh! Long time. How is the family? Kids doing well in school?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Haha, yes doctor, all fine. Elder one just got into engineering college. Wife is well also.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Wonderful news! And you? Still going for your morning runs? I know how seriously you take your fitness.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Actually doctor, that is why I came. I have not been able to do my running properly for two years now. Something is not right with me.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Tell me, what is happening? Any headache or feeling dizzy?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, the dizziness is there continuously. And headache also — it is mildly uncomfortable but many times in a day. I ignored it for weeks thinking it will go.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Hmm, constantly dizzy, that is concerning. Any numbness in both sides of the body, or tingling in the hands or feet?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Umm, yes actually. numbness on both sides of my face — it feels cold, like blood is not flowing. It is present almost every morning.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any recent international travel? Or exposure to sick contacts? And do you have any history of kidney stones or other chronic conditions?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, I had international travel to Dubai and London about three months back for work. And yes, kidney stones — I had surgery pre-operative assessment done two years ago for that. No other big history.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Okay. Are you on any medicines currently? Any OTC medicine you have been taking for the headache?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Ahh, I was taking OTC medicine from the medical shop — some painkiller — but it is not helping much. I also take lisinopril for blood pressure and multivitamins since I was young, it is my habit.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Good that you mentioned lisinopril. And your sleep habits? Are you sleeping well? Any insomnia?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: My sleep habits are disturbed doctor. I wake up many times at night because of the headache. It is very troublesome.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Now let me go over your lab reports. The nasal swab result came back — did you get any other tests done before coming today?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Only the nasal swab you had ordered last week doctor. And the blood pressure reading at the chemist showed it was mildly uncomfortable range — around 145 over 90.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any nasal congestion or facial pain? Any fever — is it present or absent?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Fever is absent doctor, but yes, nasal congestion is there for two years also, on and off. I thought it is just allergy.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Rajesh, seeing your nasal swab result and these symptoms together — the dizziness, numbness, nasal congestion — this is a case of sinusitis which has become active and is now affecting your neurological balance. The headache and dizziness are coming from the sinus pressure building up.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, can the sinusitis really cause so much dizziness and numbness on both sides? I was very worried it is something serious in the brain.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Yes, sinusitis pressure near the nasal passages can refer to facial numbness and cause dizziness — especially when it is constantly inflamed. But I also want a MRI brain done to rule out any central cause, just to be safe.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I am prescribing a nasal corticosteroid spray — use it twice daily. Also starting you on amoxicillin-clavulanate for ten days. Continue your lisinopril and multivitamins, but stop the OTC medicine painkiller — it can affect your kidney stones history.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Okay doctor. Any special diet changes? And can I resume my running?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Avoid cold air and dust during your running for now — wear a mask outdoors. Fix your sleep habits first, that is important for recovery. And please do not delay further — for two years you have been carrying this. We also need a sinus CT scan to check the extent of sinusitis.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Understood doctor. I will do the MRI brain and sinus CT scan this week itself. And I will stop the OTC medicine from today. Thank you for checking everything so thoroughly.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Good morning, please come in and sit down. How can I help you today?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Good morning doctor. I am pregnant, around six months along, and I have been having stomach pain and acidity for quite some time now. My mother-in-law said I should come and get checked properly.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Okay, let us go through everything carefully. Where exactly is the pain — is it in the lower abdomen or higher up near the ribcage?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Mostly near the ribcage area, doctor. It feels like a burning sensation going up into the throat also.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Is there any nausea or vomiting along with this?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Confirmed, doctor. Nausea is there every morning and sometimes even after eating. My family says I look very pale nowadays.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any gas trouble or bloating?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, gas trouble is very bad. Bloating is there once in a while, but the acidity is almost constant. My mother-in-law noticed I am burping a lot after meals.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Have you recently travelled anywhere? Any dust exposure or been near a construction site?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, we visited my husband's village last month. There was a lot of dust and a big construction site right next to the house. Also I got a mosquito bite or two there, so I was a little worried also.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: No fever or chills after that trip? Any loose motion?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Never used to have fever before but after the trip there was a mild fever for two days. Loose motion was there for about three days but it has stopped now.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Do you have any past history of gastric ulcer or gastritis? Any such problems before pregnancy?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, two years ago I was diagnosed with gastritis. I took some medicines for it and it was fine after that.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Are you taking any stress? Also, have you been self-medicating — any antacids or anything from the chemist on your own?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, stress is there because of the pregnancy and the travel. I was taking antacid syrup from the medical shop for the last week, but I was not sure if it was safe. My mother-in-law said stress is making everything worse.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any heartburn when lying down at night? And is there any swelling in the legs or feet?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, heartburn is very bad at night when I lie down. Swelling in the feet is there once in a while by evening time.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Have you done your routine antenatal blood tests and urine routine examination? Also, has your obstetric ultrasound been done recently?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: The obstetric ultrasound was done last month, baby is fine doctor. But the urine routine examination was not done recently. My hemoglobin test showed anemia — it was 9.5 grams.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I see. Based on everything, this is a case of gastroesophageal reflux disease, commonly known as GERD, which is very common in pregnancy as the growing uterus pushes up on the stomach. The gastritis history is also contributing. The anemia needs to be addressed too.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I am prescribing pantoprazole 40 mg once daily before breakfast, and sucralfate suspension after meals three times a day — both are safe in pregnancy. For the anemia, continue your ferrous sulfate and folic acid tablets as before. Do not take over-the-counter antacid syrup on your own without asking me.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Avoid spicy and oily food completely. Do not lie down immediately after eating — wait at least one hour. Keep your head elevated when sleeping. Reduce stress as much as possible, it directly worsens acidity. Also avoid any further dust exposure since you are pregnant.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I am ordering a fresh urine routine examination and a stool routine test to rule out any infection from the travel. Also get your blood pressure checked regularly given the swelling in the feet. Come back in two weeks or earlier if the pain near the ribcage worsens.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Thank you so much doctor, I will follow everything you said. My mother-in-law will be relieved to hear the baby is fine.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Hello, come in, come in. Please have a seat. I see this is a referral visit — what brings you here today?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, I am a 15-year-old girl. My periods have been extremely painful and irregular since the last six months, and I also have this discharge that is bothering me all the time.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Okay. Is the pain in the lower abdomen or anywhere near the epigastric region also?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Mostly lower abdomen doctor, but sometimes it goes up near the epigastric area and feels unbearable. I read online it could be PCOS or even endometriosis.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any acne on the face or back? Any unusual hair fall or weight gain?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Present, yes doctor — lots of acne on my face and there is also hair fall three times a week I notice big clumps in the shower. The internet said these are classic PCOS signs.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any tenderness or swelling in the breast area? And is the discharge warm or foul-smelling?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Umm, the breast area is slightly sore, yes. And the discharge — it is warm and yellowish. Doctor, I also developed a skin infection on my thigh last month and it has not fully gone.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Was that skin infection after a mosquito bite or any other pesticides contact? Do you live near farmland?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Ahh, I think there was a mosquito bite first, then it got infected. We do live near fields so pesticides exposure is possible, but I am not aware of any direct contact.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any history of food allergy? And are you currently on any medicines — like OTC medicine or cough syrup for anything?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes, I have a food allergy to shellfish. And I was taking some OTC medicine for sinusitis two weeks back. Also a cough syrup my mother gave me when I had a cold.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Was the sinusitis also accompanied by facial pain or nasal discharge? And how often?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes, doctor, facial pain and blocked nose — it keeps coming back three times a week when weather changes. I read sinusitis can trigger hormonal issues, is that true?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: That connection is not so straightforward. Now tell me — do you alcohol drink or smoke at all?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: I drink alcohol occasionally, like 2 drinks a week at parties. I don't think so that it is causing my period problems, but maybe?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: It definitely contributes. Have you done any tests earlier — a USG report or albumin level check? And when was your last weight check?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: My family doctor did a USG report three months ago and said ovaries looked bulky. Weight check was done then too — I had gained 6 kg. No albumin test was done.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Based on the bulky ovaries on USG report, the acne, hair fall, irregular periods, and weight gain, this is a case of PCOS — Polycystic Ovarian Syndrome. The skin infection and discharge are secondary concerns we will address separately.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, I also read that warfarin can sometimes affect periods — my aunt takes it. Could that be a reason? And can PCOS happen during pregnancy also?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Warfarin affects bleeding patterns but you are not on it, so it is not relevant here. Regarding during pregnancy — PCOS is a pre-existing hormonal condition, it does not newly develop during pregnancy, though it can complicate one.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I am prescribing combined oral contraceptive pill to regulate your cycle and reduce acne, along with metformin 500 mg for insulin resistance. For the skin infection, I will add topical clindamycin to apply on the thigh area.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Please stop the alcohol completely while on metformin — it can cause serious side effects. Also avoid self-medicating with any OTC medicine without asking me first, especially given your food allergy history.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Okay doctor. And what about the sinusitis — should I continue the cough syrup? And do I need another USG report soon?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Stop the cough syrup for now. I will refer you to an ENT for the recurring sinusitis. Yes, repeat USG report, albumin, and a full hormonal panel in four weeks, and come back for weight check monthly so we can track your progress properly.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Good morning, please come in and sit. You look a little distressed today.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, I am having stomach pain and acidity continuously since morning. I live alone so I thought best to come straight here.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Tell me more. Is there any bloating or gas also? Any nausea or vomiting?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, so much gas is there, and my stomach is distended and hard. Also, I read online that these can be signs of heart attack in older women. Is that true?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: That is a fair concern, but let us not worry unnecessarily. Tell me, is the pain in your chest or only in the abdomen? Any pain going to your fingers or arm?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: No, nothing going to my fingers. The pain is mostly in my upper abdomen, burning type. But doctor, I also read that gas can press on the heart — is that possible?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: There is some truth to that but let us examine first. Did you eat anything unusual? Any contaminated food or street food recently?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Umm, I did eat some leftover rice from two days back yesterday night. Could that be contaminated food doctor? I am thinking that is the reason.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Very possible. And any sick contact — someone around you with vomiting or loose motion recently?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: No, nobody. I stay alone only. Doctor, I have high blood pressure and some gallbladder issue from 2020. Can this stomach problem be related to my gallbladder issue?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Yes, the gallbladder issue can definitely contribute to such pain. Are you currently on any medicines — pain medications, montelukast, or iron supplements?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, I take iron supplements for anaemia and I was also given montelukast for my cough. I take pain medications whenever my knee is paining.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Those pain medications can irritate the stomach lining a lot. Now tell me — do you smoke or take cannabis?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Ahh, cannabis — never doctor, not once in my life. And smoking also never. I only take maybe 2 drinks a week, just a small peg in the evening since my husband passed.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Understood. Do you take alcohol every day or just occasionally? Also, any heartburn or sour belching?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: No, not every day, just 2 drinks a week. And yes, so much heartburn and sour belching is there. Doctor, I read online about something called GERD — do I have that?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Based on what you are telling me — the burning pain in the upper abdomen, heartburn, sour belching, and the regular use of pain medications — this is a case of acute gastritis with GERD. Your gallbladder issue is also a contributing factor.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, I want to know — could this cause something serious to my heart? Online it said something about needing a heart rate check and even a bronchoscopy. Do I need all these tests?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: A bronchoscopy is for the lungs — that is completely not needed for you. We will check your heart rate now with an ECG to rule out cardiac issue, and I will also order electrolytes since you are having significant vomiting and may be dehydrated. Please do not trust everything you read online.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Okay doctor. So what medicines should I take for this gastritis? Can I continue my iron supplements and montelukast?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I am prescribing pantoprazole 40 mg before breakfast every morning for the acidity, and domperidone for the nausea and bloating. You may continue montelukast, but please stop the pain medications for now — those are worsening your gastritis. Continue your iron supplements after food only.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, I am also reading that acidity can cause ulcers in the stomach. Should I be worried? And what precautions for my high blood pressure?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: If you take medicines properly and avoid pain medications without food, ulcers can be prevented. For your high blood pressure, avoid stress, excess alcohol, and salty food. If you get chest pain or giddiness at home, come immediately — do not wait.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Understood doctor. Should I also do some electrolytes test at home from a lab? And is there any diet I should follow for the gas and acidity?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Yes, get the electrolytes done today itself from our lab downstairs. Avoid spicy, oily, and fermented food for now. Eat small meals every 3 to 4 hours, avoid lying down right after eating, and drink plenty of water. Come back after 5 days or sooner if pain is not improving.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Come in, come in. Please sit down. You are looking quite pale today.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, I suddenly had a fainting episode last week right at my stall. Everything went black, I just fell down on the road itself.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Alright, let us start from the beginning. Any dizziness or weakness before the fainting?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, I feel weakness almost never on rest days, but on working days it is once a day at least. Also doctor, one more thing — I have this feeling like there is a rock in stomach, mainly in the epigastric area.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Okay, let us come to the epigastric complaint in a moment. Tell me first — any hearing loss or ringing in the ears?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Umm, yes doctor, I have noticed some hearing loss also. It started last summer. I thought it was just from standing near the frying pan all day.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: How long have you been doing street food vending? And are you working near any lead pipes or old painted surfaces at your cooking spot?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, I have been doing this for a long time, almost fifteen years now. And yes, the area where I set up my stall has very old painted walls and there are old pipes also, lead ones I think my neighbour told me.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Now tell me about this rock in stomach feeling. Is the heaviness more on the right side or center of your abdomen?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: It is more on the right side doctor, and sometimes I feel it deep inside, like in the intestine. And doctor, I also get loose stool — it is very watery — after every meal.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Are you taking any medicines currently? Any iron deficiency treatment or multivitamin tablets?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, I was on ferrous sulphate tablets given by another doctor, but I stopped them on my own and started taking some ayurvedic tonic I bought from the market last week itself. I thought it would be better.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: You should not have stopped ferrous sulphate on your own. Did you have any old injury or surgery before — anything to the abdomen or intestine?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, I had a old injury to my right side of the abdomen years ago, a road accident. They did some small procedure but I do not remember what exactly.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Do you eat proper meals? Any non-vegetarian food?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, I eat at my stall only — fried items every day. Very little dal or green vegetables. I taste my own street food mostly, nothing balanced.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any pale skin, breathlessness, or palpitations? Any yellowing of eyes?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Ahh, yes doctor, my wife has been saying my skin is looking dull and pale. I do get breathlessness when climbing stairs. No yellowing of the eyes as far as I know.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Based on your fainting, weakness, pale skin, hearing loss, epigastric discomfort, and your prolonged lead exposure, I believe you have iron deficiency anaemia along with possible lead toxicity. The loose stool and watery motions are also part of this picture.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, can the lead near my stall cause all this? Even the hearing loss and the rock in stomach feeling in the intestine?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Currently your chronic lead exposure combined with nutritional deficiency is hitting multiple organs — your intestine, your ears, and your epigastric region all at once. The old injury may also be contributing to the right side discomfort.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: We need to run a complete blood count, serum ferritin, blood lead level, and a peripheral blood smear today itself. Also we will do liver function test given that right side complaint.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I am restarting ferrous sulphate 200 mg twice daily with meals, and adding folic acid 5 mg once daily. Please stop that ayurvedic tonic immediately — it may be interfering. If lead levels are high, we will start chelation therapy after specialist review.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, should I stop working at the stall? And those watery loose stool after every meal — will that also go away?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: You must shift your stall away from those old lead pipes urgently. Eat iron-rich food — green leafy vegetables, eggs, dal — every day. The loose stool should reduce once lead toxicity is treated, but if fainting happens again, go to emergency straightaway and do not take any medicine on your own without asking me first.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Welcome back. How are you feeling after the hospitalisation? What brings you in today?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, I am not fully okay. For two weeks I am having cramps in my abdomen and also this GERD problem is troubling me. I read on internet that after hernia surgery this can happen.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Okay. Are these cramps worse at night or throughout the day? And how often — is it weekly or more frequent?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Mostly worse at night doctor, and yes it comes weekly, sometimes more. It feels squeezing inside. I also saw online that GERD after surgery can be serious, so I am worried.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Tell me about the piles and abscess — are those wounds healing properly? Any bleeding or discharge from that area?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: The abscess wound is slowly healing doctor. No discharge now. But the piles area is still a little paining when I sit for long time. Being a fisherman I have to sit in the boat for hours, so it is very difficult.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I understand. Any history of chickenpox or stone in the GB or hip replacement? These can sometimes complicate recovery.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, I had chickenpox long back as a child, and stone in the GB was found some years ago but no surgery was done for that. Hip replacement was done for my father — not me. I read about all these on internet and got confused if they are related.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: At the fishing site, are you getting insect bites or tick bite exposure? And any exposure to animal hair from cats or dogs at home?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Ahh, yes doctor, insect bites are very common at the waterside. I also got a tick bite for two weeks back around the same time the cramps started. And we have a dog at home so animal hair exposure is there also.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Is there any headache near the temple area or fever? Any rash on the skin?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, headache near the temple is there on and off. No fever as such but I am feeling fatigue all the time. I read on internet that tick bite can cause some serious infection — is that what is happening to me doctor?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Do you stress a lot because of financial situation? And are you eating junk food — is that once in a while or regularly?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, stress is very high right now. The hospitalisation cost so much, I am really struggling. Junk food I eat once in a while only — mostly whatever is available at the fishing site. Money is very tight so we eat simply.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I understand your situation. We will try to keep investigations minimal and affordable.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, the hospital had given me steroids during admission. I was also told to take atorvastatin but I am not taking it because I cannot afford it right now. I read online that stopping atorvastatin suddenly can be dangerous — is that true?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Yes, stopping atorvastatin abruptly is not advisable. The stress and poor diet combined with your GERD and cramps in the abdomen also need to be properly addressed. The tick bite concerns me as a possible trigger for the fatigue and headache.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Based on all your symptoms — the cramps that are squeezing and worse at night, the GERD, and the fatigue after tick bite — I suspect a tick-borne infection compounding your post-surgical recovery, along with gastroesophageal reflux and post-operative irritable bowel.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, I was reading about tick-borne infection online and it said allergy test and nasal swab should be done — do I need all that?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: The nasal swab is not necessary in your case. What I will order is a kidney function test since you were on steroids, and an allergy test to rule out reaction to animal hair and insect bites. These are important and I will see what can be done at government rates.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Okay doctor. And for the GERD and cramps, what medicine should I take? I cannot buy expensive medicines.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I am prescribing pantoprazole tablet once daily before breakfast for the GERD, and mebeverine for the abdomen cramps. Also restart atorvastatin — I am giving you the generic version which is much cheaper. A short course of doxycycline is also needed for the suspected tick-borne infection.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Please avoid junk food and spicy items as they will worsen the GERD. At the fishing site, wear full-sleeve clothes to prevent insect bites and tick bite. Stress management is very important — the abdomen cramps that feel squeezing can be made much worse by stress.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, online it says the kidney function test results take time — should I be worried about my abdomen pain in the meantime? And my stone in the GB — can that be causing the squeezing cramps?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: The stone in the GB can indeed contribute to the cramps in the abdomen, so do not ignore any squeezing pain that becomes very severe. The kidney function test results will come in one day — take the medicines I prescribed and come back in one week. If fever or headache near the temple worsens, come immediately without waiting.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Good morning, come in, come in. Please have a seat.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Good morning doctor. My family is dragging me here, I told them I am perfectly fine.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: What is your main work? And what exactly is the family worried about?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: I am a fisherman, doctor. They say my sugar is out of control and my weight gain is too much, but I read on the internet that these things settle on their own.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Okay. Are you getting any fatigue, excessive thirst, or frequent urination?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Umm, yes doctor, frequent urination is there, happening twice a week at night mostly. And I have fatigue once a day by evening. I thought it was just from fishing work.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any chest pain or breathlessness? Any cough?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Ahh, yes, there is some sharp pain in my chest a week ago. And cough is there, it is productive, happening more often lately. Doctor, I read on internet that sharp pain in chest is just gas trouble.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: That is not always the case. Do you have any history of TB or any lung problem before?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, I had TB last summer. Took treatment for some months. Also had some surgery and after surgery I had this burning pain in my abdomen, but that settled.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any asbestos exposure at the docks or boat repair yards?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Umm, yes doctor, when I work at the old boat yard there is asbestos in those old boats. Many years of that. But on the internet people say one or two years of exposure is nothing.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Do you smoke or drink?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes, I am smoking a pack a day, and I drink on weekends with friends at the dock.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Are you taking any medicines currently for your diabetes, thyroid, or high cholesterol? Are you missing doses?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Ahh, I am missing doses doctor, I will not lie. I read online that entecavir and ribavirin I was given for my liver problem — people say these have too many side effects so I stopped. Also I stopped my eye drops for the eye pressure problem. Doctor said take it once a day but I forget.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: This is concerning. Based on your history of TB, asbestos exposure, smoking a pack a day, and this productive cough with uncontrolled diabetes and hypothyroidism, I am suspecting a combination of metabolic syndrome along with early lung disease.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, I searched online and it said metabolic syndrome is very common in fishermen due to diet — is that why? And is hypothyroidism connected to my weight gain?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Yes, absolutely, hypothyroidism does contribute to weight gain and fatigue. And missing your medicines is making your diabetes and high cholesterol much worse. The internet is not your doctor.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: We need to do a TMT to check your heart given the sharp pain in your chest. We will also do a DEXA scan to check your bone density because long-term diabetes affects bones. And a temperature check today as I suspect low-grade fever with that productive cough.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, the internet says ribavirin should not be combined with certain tablets — should I restart it or not?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Yes, restart ribavirin and entecavir as prescribed, do not stop on your own. Also restart your eye drops once a day without fail. I am additionally prescribing metformin for your diabetes and levothyroxine for your thyroid.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: And please stop smoking immediately — with TB history and asbestos exposure, your lungs are already at very high risk. Reduce drinking also, especially while on ribavirin and entecavir.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, I also forgot to mention — my feet are paining with a burning pain at night more often lately. Is that also the sugar?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Yes, that burning pain in your feet is likely diabetic neuropathy. We will get a HbA1c done and a nerve conduction study. Please come back in two weeks with all your reports — and this time, no internet diagnosis, only what I tell you.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Mr. Ramesh, it has been quite some time. Where did you disappear to?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Sorry doctor, life got busy. I am here now only.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: You were supposed to come back many years of follow-up pending now. What symptoms are troubling you currently?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, I have been having body pain every other day and some kind of churning feeling in my epigastric region. Also time ago I started getting this tremor in my hands.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any fever? Have you had chills or headache also?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, fever is coming daily in the evenings. The season change is making everything worse I think.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any rash on skin? Nausea or vomiting?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: The upper part of my stomach feels very unsettled. No rash as such, but my hands feel numb every other day.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: You have a history of stroke and past surgery, correct? Were you continuing any medicines after that?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Umm, I was on tenofovir doctor, but I stopped time ago. I also had ear drops prescribed for that ear infection but I used it only a few days.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Why did you stop the medications? No one told you to stop, correct?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: I felt better so I stopped. Also the cost was becoming high.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Do you drink alcohol? Be honest with me please.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Ahh, just rarely doctor... maybe a little more during festivals. I also do yoga 1 hour daily so it balances out, no?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: That is not how it works. Any smoke exposure at home or from your own habit?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: No doctor, I do not smoke. My neighbour smokes near the window, some smoke comes in but I cannot help that.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any pain in the pelvis area? Any loose motion or blood in stool?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: There is some ache in the pelvis also, yes. No blood in stool but motion is irregular.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Looking at the fever pattern, body pain, churning in the epigastric region, and seasonal onset, this presentation is suggestive of typhoid. The tremor and numb sensation could be related to your stopped tenofovir and nutritional deficiency.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, is it serious? I was also worried it could be dengue.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: We cannot rule out dengue without tests. I am ordering vitamin B12 levels and bilirubin also since your epigastric region symptoms and alcohol intake worry me for liver involvement.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I am restarting your tenofovir immediately. I am also prescribing a short course of prednisolone for the inflammation and tremor, and the ear drops must be completed as instructed this time.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, can I continue my yoga during this time?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Light yoga is fine but reduce to 1 hour daily only, and strictly no alcohol as it will worsen the liver damage and interact badly with prednisolone. Do not miss follow-up this time.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Okay doctor, I will be regular from now. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Come in, come in. Please sit down. What is your name and what work do you do?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor sahib, my name is Ramesh. I am working in railways, loading and unloading work only.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Okay Ramesh. So what is the main problem bringing you here today? You are looking very unwell.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, umm, my legs are very swollen and there is some pinching feeling in my joints also. I was in hospital and they sent me home three days ago only but now it is becoming more bad.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: You were recently discharged? What was the treatment for? Was there any swelling of your feet or ankles before also?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Ahh, they said my kidney is not working properly doctor. The swelling was there but now it has become very bad. The joints are feeling warm also when I touch.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Are the joints paining intermittently or all the time? And is there any fistula or hole near the skin anywhere?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, pain is coming many times in the day. And yes, one small thing like a fistula is there on my left leg, some fluid is coming from there also.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I see. What tests were done in the hospital? Did they check your uric acid levels?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: They did some blood tests doctor. I don't know the names, I cannot read properly. They did uric acid I think someone said, and also some throat swab test because I had some throat issue at that time. They also started me on calcium supplements.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Was there any coughing or breathing difficulty? Did they do a bronchoscopy in the hospital?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, yes, there was some coughing and they did that pipe test, that bronchoscopy also they are doing. I don't know what they found.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Okay. Any past history of illness when you were young? Any kidney disease in family or did you have any childhood sickness?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, I had measles in childhood, very bad it was. Family also has some kidney problem, my father also had same issue they say.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Do you smoke or take any cocaine or other substances? And how about non-vegetarian food and drinking?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, cocaine I am taking socially only, not regularly. I drink 3 beers a day and eat non-vegetarian food on weekends. Smoking I stopped long back.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: At your railway job, are you exposed to any fumes or do you work near any factory area?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Ahh yes doctor, loading area is near a factory only, lots of fumes are coming there many times. We work there without any mask. I don't think so it is causing problem but maybe it is.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Have you checked your creatinine levels recently? And is there any reduced urine output or foamy urine?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, they said creatinine is very high. Urine is also very less and yes some foam is also coming. I am scared doctor, I cannot understand what is happening.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Ramesh, you are having chronic kidney disease with high creatinine and now the joint swelling with the fistula on your left leg is suggesting gouty arthritis also, likely due to the high uric acid. The fumes from the factory may also be worsening your kidney function.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor what should I do now? I am not understanding much but please help me. Is it very serious?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I am prescribing febuxostat tablet for your uric acid, furosemide for the swelling, and continue your calcium supplements as before. Also I am adding sodium bicarbonate to protect your kidneys. Please stop cocaine completely and reduce your drinking immediately.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: You must avoid non-vegetarian food as much as possible, especially red meat, as it raises uric acid. Wear a mask near the fumes at work. The fistula on your left leg needs dressing many times a week at a clinic — please do not ignore it.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: We will repeat your uric acid and creatinine blood tests after two weeks and check your joints again. If the swelling is not improving or the fistula is getting worse, we will refer you to a kidney specialist. Take rest and drink plenty of water.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Good morning, please come in and sit down comfortably.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Good morning doctor. I am 67 years old and I have come for a second opinion. The other doctor told me some things but my family is very worried and they are saying I should see you also.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Of course, you are most welcome. What are the main complaints that brought you here today?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, my family is observing that I have headache that is squeezing type, like somebody is pressing hard on my scalp. It has been happening non-stop for two weeks now.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Is there any dizziness or numbness also that your family has noticed?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, yes. My daughter is saying I am losing balance when I walk, and there is numbness in my hands and feet both sides. They said it became very severe suddenly, that is why they rushed me here directly.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any back pain or cramps in the belly area?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Ahh, yes doctor. I have back pain in the lower back and my family noticed I am complaining of cramps near the belly also. The cramps are watery feeling inside, very uncomfortable.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Has she had any mercury or lead exposure — any old factory work, painting work, or anything like that?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, my husband is saying I was working in a small battery unit for 30 years. So there was definitely some lead exposure for many years. And once they also used mercury based chemicals in that unit only.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I see. Any past history of hypertension or diabetes?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes, I have hypertension since about 10 years. No diabetes as such. And umm, I had one knee surgery also, the other doctor gave me some instructions that were for the pre-operative period only, but family got confused about those.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: What medicines are you currently taking? And what did the previous doctor prescribe?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: I am taking amlodipine for BP. The other doctor gave betahistine for the dizziness and said to do some tests but we came here first for second opinion only.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any vomiting, blurred vision, or ringing in ears?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Umm, the blurred vision is there on and off. No vomiting as such but feeling of nausea is there. My son said last night my eyes were looking glazed.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I am going to check your blood pressure and do a quick neurological examination now. We will also need a blood lead level test and MRI brain urgently.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, do you think this is all because of that factory work only? That lead exposure?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Most likely this is a case of lead toxicity causing peripheral neuropathy and encephalopathy. The headache, numbness, dizziness, and cramps all fit this picture. The mercury exposure may also have contributed to the neurological symptoms.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Oh my goodness doctor. So what should we do now? My family is very tensed. Is it serious?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: It is serious but treatable if we act quickly. First we confirm with serum lead level and complete blood count. Depending on levels, we may need chelation therapy. Also your kidney function test and liver function test are important because lead can damage those organs.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: For now I am starting her on dimercaptosuccinic acid which is the chelation agent for lead toxicity. Also continuing amlodipine for BP, and I am adding thiamine and pyridoxine supplements for the peripheral neuropathy. For the headache, take paracetamol 500 mg as needed.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, is there anything special we should be doing at home? Any foods or things to avoid?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: She should have complete rest, avoid any further lead or mercury exposure immediately and permanently. Increase iron and calcium rich diet as they help reduce lead absorption. Watch for worsening confusion, seizures, or sudden weakness — if that happens bring her to emergency straight away. We will review all reports in three days and plan further treatment.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Thank you so much doctor. God bless you. We will get all tests done today itself.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Hello, come in, come in. Sit down. How are you feeling after being discharged?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, I still don't feel okay. My chest is paining and my heart is beating in a funny way, like throbbing, for a week now.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I see. Is the palpitations happening three times a week or more frequently than that?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Umm, yes doctor, about three times a week. Sometimes it feels like pressure like pain on my chest, and I don't know what that means.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Okay. Any stomach pain too? Especially near your pancreas area — that is the middle upper part of your stomach?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Ahh, yes doctor, sometimes that area is cramping. I thought it was just gas trouble.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Alright. When you were admitted, they checked many things. Did they mention anything about hepatitis or cholesterol levels being abnormal?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: They said hepatitis was ruled out, doctor. But I don't understand what hepatitis even is. The cholesterol report they gave me I didn't fully understand.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: That is fine, I will explain. Any family history of stroke or heart disease in your parents or grandparents?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: My grandfather had a stroke quite a while ago. And I had a childhood illness — some kind of fever when I was very small, my mother says.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Okay. Were you ever exposed to insect bites or tick bites recently, any outdoor trips?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, we went for a camp trip and I got many insect bites on my legs and arms. I didn't think it was related to this.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: It can be relevant. Do you smoke cigarettes or have you tried?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Umm, only at parties, doctor. I am a social smoker. It started since college orientation last year. Just cigarettes sometimes, nothing else.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I see. Did the hospital run a CRP test for you? That checks for inflammation inside the body.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: They did many blood tests doctor. I think CRP was positive — the discharge paper says elevated, but I didn't know what that meant.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Understood. Any dizziness, nausea, or breathlessness along with the chest paining?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, dizziness comes three times a week also, and sometimes I feel like my stomach is being squeezed, like cramping. Someone said it could be Crohn's disease but I don't know what that is.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Based on your elevated CRP, the palpitations, pressure like pain in the chest, and the insect bites history, I believe this is a case of myocarditis — inflammation of the heart muscle, likely triggered by an infection. Crohn's disease is not what we are seeing here.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Myocarditis? Is that very serious doctor? And will it affect my pancreas also?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: It is manageable if we treat it properly. The pancreas discomfort is likely due to the inflammation spreading, and we will monitor it. You must rest, avoid any exertion, and stop cigarettes completely — even social smoker level is too much for your heart right now.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I am prescribing diazepam at a low dose for the palpitations and anxiety component, along with ibuprofen for the inflammation and pantoprazole to protect your stomach.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, the diazepam — my friend said it makes you sleepy. Should I be worried about taking it? And what about the cholesterol issue?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Yes, diazepam can cause drowsiness so take it only at night. For cholesterol, we will recheck with a lipid profile after two weeks. Also avoid further insect bites — use protection when outdoors. The grandfather's stroke history means you must take chest pain seriously going forward.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Okay doctor, thank you so much. I will follow everything you said.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Come in, come in. Please sit down. Welcome.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Thank you doctor. Actually my family forced me to come, I was not really wanting to.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: That is okay. What is going on? Tell me what brought you here today.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Umm, I have been having vertigo nonstop for the past few days, and body pain also. I looked it up online and I think it is just some vitamin deficiency.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Online research is fine, but let us do a proper check. Can you describe the vertigo? Is there any spinning sensation or just lightheadedness?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: It is like the whole room is spinning, doctor. And the body pain is very sharp, especially around the knee. The internet said it could be inner ear problem or thyroid issue.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Interesting. Any burning pain in the knee or anywhere else on the leg?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, there is burning pain near the knee also. It is very sharp when I climb stairs at the railway station.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: You work in railways — what exactly do you do there? Any exposure to heat or fumes on the job?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: I am a track maintenance worker. Yes, lot of heat exposure, we work outdoors in strong sun for hours. Also, near the yard there are birds and sometimes cats roaming around — I never thought that was relevant.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: It can be relevant. The birds and cats can sometimes carry infections. Did you have any similar complaints as a teenager?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: No, I was perfectly fine as a teenager. No vertigo, nothing like that. Only I had one small cyst on my neck which was removed, but that was minor.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Okay, noted. Do you drink alcohol or have any other habits?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Ahh, doctor, I do alcohol socially sometimes. And I have been doing vaping — half a pack a day equivalent. I read online it is safer than cigarettes so I switched.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: That is a common misconception. Vaping is not safe — it still affects the lungs, balance, and circulation, and can worsen vertigo. Please do not rely on that comparison.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: But doctor, the website I read said vaping has less chemicals. Also it said vertigo and body pain together could mean some autoimmune thing — could that be it?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Let us not jump to conclusions. Have you done any tests recently? Any thyroid test or electrolytes checked before?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: No doctor, no tests at all. I have no prior medical history. But the internet said TSH should be checked first for vertigo. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Your instinct is partially correct — TSH is important, and I will order a thyroid test along with electrolytes and a complete blood count. The prolonged heat exposure and birds and cats contact also make me want to rule out infection.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Okay doctor. One more thing — on my knee, there is also a small cyst kind of swelling that appeared recently. It is very sharp when I press it.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I am examining you now. Looking at all your symptoms — the vertigo, body pain, burning pain in the knee, the cyst on the knee, and your occupational heat exposure — this is most likely a case of heat exhaustion combined with a ganglion cyst at the knee. The vertigo running nonstop is also suggestive of benign positional vertigo.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Ahh, so it is not something I read about — not autoimmune disease? And this ganglion cyst on knee will go on its own?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: We will wait for the reports, but for now I am prescribing betahistine for the vertigo, diclofenac gel to apply on the knee for the burning pain, and ORS sachets daily given the heat exposure. Also start vitamin D3 tablets since deficiency is common in your occupation.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Okay doctor. Should I stop the vaping and alcohol completely? And what about the knee cyst?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Yes, absolutely stop vaping and reduce alcohol — both will worsen vertigo and slow healing. The cyst on the knee we will reassess after the electrolytes and thyroid test reports come back. Avoid prolonged heat and direct birds and cats contact at the yard until we rule out infection.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Ah, Mr. Sharma! Long time no see. Please sit down.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, sorry for coming so late. Life got very busy.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: No problem. So tell me, how has your diabetes been? You have stopped coming for follow-up for several months now. Any giddiness or fatigue?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, I am having heartburn after every meal since last three months. Also, there is some piles problem since six months, it is very uncomfortable.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Okay, let me understand more. Is the heartburn coming up to your upper part of the sternum? Any aching sensation there?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, it is aching right here at the sternum and just now I noticed it is also going up to my jaw area sometimes.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Hmm, that is concerning. Any chest tightness or shortness of breath along with this jaw pain?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Umm, not much doctor, but sometimes I do feel a little breathlessness when I climb stairs. Also, I was diagnosed with typhoid two months back in another clinic.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I see. Any family history of heart disease? And any history of tuberculosis or blood transfusion in the past?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, my father had a heart attack at age fifty. I had tuberculosis almost fifteen years back and I also had a blood transfusion after an accident five years ago.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any chewing tobacco habit? And are you still on your insulin?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Ahh doctor, I do chewing tobacco 1 hour daily, I know it is bad. And I have stopped taking insulin for past two months because I thought my sugar was fine.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: That is very dangerous, Mr. Sharma. Any recent tick bite or travel to forest areas? And have you been self-medicating, taking Tylenol or any pain relievers on your own?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, yes — there was a tick bite on my leg last month when I went to visit my village farm. And I was taking Tylenol for the body ache, maybe twice or three times a week.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Alright, let me now summarise what I am finding. You have uncontrolled diabetes after self-stopping insulin, heartburn radiating to the sternum and jaw, active piles, a past tuberculosis history, a tick bite last month, and a strong family history of heart attack. This picture needs urgent evaluation.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, is everything serious? I am a little worried about the jaw and sternum pain now.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Yes, you are right to be concerned. Given the aching pain radiating to the jaw, your diabetes, the family history, and your chewing tobacco use, I strongly suspect this is cardiac ischaemia. Also, the tick bite raises concern for tick-borne fever.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Oh my god doctor. And what about the piles and heartburn? Should I worry about those also?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Those we will manage too, but the cardiac issue is the priority right now. I want you to do an ESR to check for infection, a spirometry because of your breathlessness, and a PT INR since you had a blood transfusion earlier and are on irregular medication.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Okay doctor. And what about my insulin? Should I restart it?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Absolutely. I am restarting your insulin immediately — please do not stop it again on your own. I am also prescribing pantoprazole for the heartburn, ispaghula husk sachets for the piles and constipation, and a low-dose aspirin until your cardiac workup is complete. Stop the Tylenol as it is stressing your stomach.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Understood doctor. One more thing — I also have swelling on the leg near the tick bite site, it is warm to touch.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: That swelling with warm to touch sensation around the tick bite is worrying. The ESR will help, and I will also order a Weil-Felix test to rule out rickettsial infection.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Most importantly, please stop all chewing tobacco immediately — it is directly worsening your cardiac risk and also the heartburn. Do not miss follow-ups again, and if the jaw or sternum pain worsens suddenly, go to emergency right away.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, I promise I will be more careful from now on. Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Ah, Priya! Come in, come in. How are your board exam preparations going? Your mother was telling me you have been studying very hard.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Haha, yes doctor, it is going okay I think. But honestly I am more worried about my heart right now than the exams.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Of course, that is why you are here. So tell me, how are you feeling after the discharge? Any chest pain or palpitations still bothering you?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, chest pain is there twice a day still. And palpitations are coming intermittently, not all the time.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: And the breathlessness? Is that still there? Any dizziness or fainting episodes?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Umm, breathlessness is there once a week only, not everyday. But since yesterday I am feeling a bit more dizziness when I stand up suddenly.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Okay. And the palpitations — do they start and stop suddenly? Any feeling of racing in the chest?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes, they start suddenly and then go away on their own. The chest feels like it is fluttering sometimes. It is quite scary, doctor.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I understand it is frightening. Now I must ask — do you chew tobacco or take any wine or alcohol at all? Some teenagers do at parties, no judgment here.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Ahh doctor, honestly I tried wine social smoker type gatherings a couple of times only. And chewing tobacco — confirmed, I did try it from childhood because my grandfather used to give it to us, we did not know it was harmful.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: That is important information, thank you for being honest. Any fumes at home — like cooking fire smoke or anything like that? You live in a rural area, correct?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes, we are from a rural area and there is a lot of cooking smoke at home. Also doctor, family member was sick with fever and throat infection a few months back, and I was the one caring for them.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Good that you mentioned that. Now, when you were admitted, we did your ECG, echocardiogram, and blood pressure monitoring. Were those reports explained to you properly at discharge?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Only partially doctor. They told me ECG showed some changes but I did not fully understand. And my blood pressure monitoring was showing high readings after delivery — wait no, that is my mother's report, sorry! Mine was showing low blood pressure episodes.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: No worries, happens when you are anxious. Did you have any joint pain or skin rash around the same time as the fever? Think carefully.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, my knees and ankles were paining quite badly. It shifted from knee to ankle and back again. And there was a rash on my chest for a few days also.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Priya, based on your history of fever after family member was sick, the joint pain shifting between knees and ankles, the rash, and now these palpitations and ECG changes — this is a case of rheumatic heart disease following rheumatic fever.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Oh doctor, that is so scary. Is it because of that infection? My grandmother also had some heart problem — is it coming from childhood in our family?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: The rheumatic fever itself comes from a throat infection called streptococcal infection — not directly hereditary, but living in a rural area with exposure to fumes and crowded conditions increases risk. The heart valve damage can happen if untreated.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: So what medicines will I need to take doctor? Will I have to take them for a long time? I am worried about side effects.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Yes, I am starting you on blood thinners to prevent any clot formation given your valve involvement. I am also adding probiotics to protect your stomach lining since we will be giving long-term antibiotics. And antihistamines for the rash episodes — take these twice a day after food.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Okay doctor. And the chewing tobacco — I should stop completely? And the wine also? Anything else I should be careful about with the blood thinners?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Absolutely stop both chewing tobacco and wine immediately — these are very harmful for heart and will interfere with your blood thinners. Avoid fumes and smoke at home as much as possible. If there is any bleeding from gums or bruising, come to me immediately — those are side effects to watch for.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I want you to do a repeat ECG and complete blood count next week. Your blood pressure must be checked regularly — at least once a week for now. The palpitations that are coming intermittently should reduce once we stabilize you.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, can I go to school or should I rest? And what about sports — I used to play during from childhood, I mean since childhood, can I still do that?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Welcome back. It has been quite some time since your last visit. How are you and the baby doing?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, sorry for not coming sooner. Baby is fine, but I have not been feeling well myself.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Tell me, what symptoms are you experiencing now? Any yellowing of skin still, or puffy eyes?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, the puffy eyes are still there, for three months now. And my abdomen feels mildly uncomfortable after every meal.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any nausea or vomiting? What about itching on the skin?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Umm, yes, there is some itching. The skin near my abdomen feels slightly painful and sometimes wet with moisture, I do not know why.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Now, I recall we had discussed your fatty liver and jaundice detected in 2025. Have you been taking the medicines I prescribed?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Ahh, doctor, I changed some medicines on my own. I was taking antihistamines for the itching, and I also started antibiotics from the medical shop time ago thinking there was an infection.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: That is concerning. Self-medicating with antibiotics and antihistamines without guidance can worsen liver disease, especially post-delivery when your body is already under stress.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: I did not know that doctor, I am sorry. The puffy eyes are bothering me every other day and I get fatigue very easily.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Are you cycling or doing any sports activity currently? Sometimes physical overexertion matters in your condition.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes, I started light cycling and some sports at the community ground, about 3 times a week, to lose the post-delivery weight.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I have to ask you directly — are you consuming alcohol? Please be honest, it is important for your liver.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Umm... yes doctor, I have been having 3 beers a day. I thought small amounts would not matter.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: That is definitely making your fatty liver worse. Even small amounts of alcohol are harmful when you already have liver disease. Are you also a chain smoker?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Ahh, doctor, I was a chain smoker before pregnancy but I had stopped. I have started again a little after delivery.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any cats or other pets at home? Sometimes animal exposure causes eye swelling and itching.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes, we have two cats at home. I spend a lot of time with them. Could that be causing the puffy eyes?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: It is possible there is an allergic component also. Have you done your liver function test or ultrasound abdomen recently? We need to check the status of your GB as well.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: No doctor, I have not done any tests. The last liver function test was done in 2025 only.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Based on your history, you have alcoholic fatty liver disease with ongoing jaundice, and there is likely an allergic reaction from cats causing the puffy eyes. The GB may also be inflamed given the mildly uncomfortable feeling you described.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I am stopping the self-prescribed antibiotics immediately. I am prescribing ursodeoxycholic acid for the fatty liver, a safer antihistamine called cetirizine for the allergic symptoms, and vitamin E supplements. Take these after every meal.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, is it safe for me while I am breastfeeding? And should I stop the cycling?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: These medicines are safe with breastfeeding but completely stop alcohol and smoking. Light cycling 3 times a week is fine but no heavy sports. Also, keep the cats away from your sleeping area to reduce eye puffiness.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Please get a liver function test, ultrasound abdomen including GB, and total bilirubin done this week. Come back with reports and do not miss your follow-up this time.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Come in, come in. Please sit down. What is your name?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Suresh, doctor. I came running from the gym only, I was not knowing what to do.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Okay Suresh, calm down. What happened? What is bothering you?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, since morning my throat is swelling up like something, and I am having nausea also many times. I am not understanding what is happening.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Is there any rash on your skin? Any itching or swelling around your lips or eyes?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, my lips are feeling very big-big, and there is itching on my arms also. I ate some new protein powder at gym only before this started.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any breathlessness or wheezing in your chest? Are you feeling dizzy?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Umm, little-little breathlessness is there doctor. Chest is feeling tight only. No dizziness doctor.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Suresh, this is looking like an acute allergic reaction, what we call anaphylaxis. The protein powder you took has triggered it. We need to act fast.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, what is this anaphylaxis? Is it dangerous? My mother is also sick at home, I need to go soon.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: It is a severe allergic reaction that can affect your throat and chest very quickly. We will treat you right now, do not worry.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I am giving you an injection of adrenaline right now, and also hydrocortisone intravenously. After that I will prescribe cetirizine tablet and cough syrup for the throat irritation.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Okay doctor. Also doctor, I have acid reflux problem every night in my epigastric area. Can you check that also?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Yes, we will address that also. This acid reflux in the epigastric area — does it go up to the throat? Any burning sensation?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, burning is coming up to here — pointing to throat. Also doctor, I had a stone problem a year ago, kidney stone they said.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I see. Do you work near any factory or mine? Any exposure to chemicals like mercury?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: My father works in a mine, doctor, but me I am not at all going there. I am only doing gym work.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Good. Do you smoke or drink alcohol?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Smoking I was doing doctor, half a pack a day, but now not anymore. Drinking also stopped. I am focusing on fitness only.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Good decision. Were you taking any antacid for your acid reflux? Any endoscopy or ultrasound done?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Ahh, only some antacid tablet I was taking from medical shop. Ultrasound was done a year ago for the stone problem. No endoscopy done doctor.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Okay. Once this allergic reaction settles, we will do a allergy skin prick test and a serum IgE blood test to find out exactly what triggered this. For your acid reflux, we will do an endoscopy also.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
