utterances.text: Doctor: Stop that protein powder completely until we identify the allergen. Avoid all new factory or chemical mercury exposure. If throat swelling comes again, come to emergency immediately — not at all delay.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, my mother at home has fever and cough since morning. Can she take this same cough syrup I am getting?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Do not self-medicate for your mother. Bring her here tomorrow for proper check up. This cough syrup I prescribed is specific for your throat irritation after the allergic reaction, not suitable for general fever and cough. Take care, okay?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Come in, come in. Good to see you again. How are things on the farm?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Managing somehow doctor, crops have not been good this season.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Alright. So this is your quarterly review. Tell me, what new complaints are you having?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, almost a month now there is this itching and rash all over my skin. It is nonstop, no relief at all.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Is the rash anywhere specific — on your arms, legs, or between the fingers? Any swelling also?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Mostly on legs and groin area doctor. And yes, there is swelling near the ankles also. The itching becomes very bad at night.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any muscle pain or weakness in the legs? And have you had any episode of seizures or fits?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Umm, the muscle pain is there every morning when I wake up. But no, nothing like seizures doctor, thank god for that.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Were you exposed to cold weather recently? Or any contaminated food or water? Any travel outside your village?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: There was cold weather two days ago, we slept in the open field. No big travel, but I did eat roadside food last week — maybe contaminated food, I cannot say.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Tell me honestly — do you exercise at all? Or do any cycling?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Ahh, I used to do cycling every day to the market and some exercise also, but now with this muscle pain and swelling I have stopped mostly.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I see. Now, your old reports — the T3, vitamin B12, and AST that were done — did you collect them before the tests last time or after?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: I collected them before the tests were explained to me doctor, so I do not fully understand what they showed. I have the papers here.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Let me see — your vitamin B12 is quite low, T3 is borderline, and AST is mildly elevated. That explains the muscle pain and the fatigue you are feeling. Also, you have a past history of stone problem, correct?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, kidney stone it was. Also my wife — she had cysts on her ovaries, she was also asking if her problem can affect me in any way. No one in my family has this rash though.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I understand. Now this rash — is there any bloody discharge or oozing from the affected area on the skin?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Sometimes there is a bloody scratch mark because the itching is so bad at night. The rash on groin area has circular patches also doctor.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Based on the circular patches on the groin and legs with itching — this is fungal infection, what we call tinea. The low vitamin B12 is worsening your muscle pain and swelling. And the elevated AST means we must watch the liver carefully.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, I am very worried about cost. I cannot afford too many medicines. What should I do for this fungal infection and the swelling?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I understand your situation. I am prescribing gabapentin for the muscle pain — it is available in generic form so cost is less. Also entecavir since your liver enzymes are up and we must be cautious. And I am adding sertraline at a low dose because the nonstop itching and disrupted sleep is affecting your mood also.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Ahh, will these medicines cause any dizziness or make my itching worse? I have to do farm work every morning.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Gabapentin can cause some dizziness initially — take it at night only first. Avoid cold weather exposure directly on skin, keep the groin area dry and clean, and do not scratch. Also restart gentle cycling or exercise — at least every day a short walk — once the swelling reduces.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: We will repeat vitamin B12 and AST after six weeks. The rash should show improvement almost a month into treatment. If seizures or any bloody discharge from skin appears, come immediately — do not wait for quarterly review.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Thank you doctor. I will try my best to follow your advice.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Hello beta, come in, come in. And you must be his father, please sit down.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Good morning doctor. He is my son, he is twelve years old. He is complaining of headache and dizziness for three months now. He did not want to come but I forced him.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Alright, beta tell me yourself — where exactly is the headache? Is it at the forehead or back of the head?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Umm, mostly at the back of my head doctor. And sometimes it is very sharp, like it shoots up suddenly.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Is there any numbness in your hands or feet? Or any tingling?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, almost never is it in the feet, but the hands do get numb sometimes, especially in the morning.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any sore throat, fever, or vomiting along with this?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: He had sore throat about a week back, doctor, but that went away on its own. No vomiting as such.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Father, does anyone at home smoke? Is the child getting exposed to secondhand smoke?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Ahh, yes doctor, I smoke myself. Two packs a day I have been doing for 10 years. I try not to smoke inside but sometimes I do.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I see. And father, you mentioned you work somewhere — what is your occupation? Have you been taking the child near any mine area or factory site?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: I work in a coal mine doctor, for three months the boy has been coming to drop me on his cycle in the morning. He waits near the entrance sometimes for a bit.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Has he been in contact with any sick person recently — like someone with tuberculosis or respiratory infection?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Not that I know of doctor. One neighbour had some cough problem but we do not visit them much.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Has the child been given any medicines at home? Any paracetamol or other tablets on your own?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, we were giving him ibuprofen whenever the sharp pain came. From the medical shop only, no prescription. And he has a history of anxiety disorder — was diagnosed last year.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Okay. Let me check his pulse and blood pressure now. Beta, any pain in the abdomen or liver area, meaning right side below the chest?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: No doctor, nothing in the liver side. Just the headache and sometimes dizziness when I stand up fast.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Father, does anyone in the family have joint pain or rheumatoid arthritis? Any autoimmune conditions in family history?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: My wife's mother had rheumatoid arthritis doctor. But as for the child, we have ruled out that possibility since he was tested last year and reports were normal. Also, does he wine or anything — no, absolutely not, he is twelve only.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Based on all this — the occupational mine dust exposure, the secondhand smoke, the anxiety disorder background, and the very sharp recurrent headache with dizziness and numbness — this looks like a combination of tension headache with possible early peripheral neuropathy triggered by toxic exposure.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, is it serious? What should we do now? Should we stop him from going near the mine?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Yes, immediately stop taking the child near the mine. I am prescribing gabapentin in a low paediatric dose for the numbness and sharp pain episodes, along with vitamin B12 supplements. Stop the ibuprofen on your own — that is not safe.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Father, most importantly, please stop smoking inside the house — the secondhand smoke is worsening his headache and dizziness. We will also do a complete blood count and nerve conduction study to check the numbness properly.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Understood doctor, we will do all the tests. And I will make sure he does not go near the mine anymore. Thank you for explaining everything.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Hello, come in, come in. Please sit down comfortably.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Thank you doctor. Sorry I am a bit late, the traffic was very bad today.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: No problem at all. So, you are here for your quarterly review today, yes? How are you generally feeling?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Uh, mostly okay doctor. Just a little sore throat for a week, nothing too serious I think.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: A little? Tell me more — any swelling in the throat area, or fever along with it?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Umm, the sore throat is actually severe in the morning doctor, and there is some swelling also. And right, I had fever every other day this past week.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any diarrhoea or loose motions? Any child at home with similar fever?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, my younger brother, he is six years old — he had fever and diarrhoea for a week also. We went to a local clinic for him already.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I see. Now, you work in that cement factory, correct? Tell me about your exposure there — any construction site dust or chemicals you are inhaling regularly?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, I work near the construction site area of the factory, and there is a lot of dust. I also take public transport to work around noon shift.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any birds kept at home or nearby? Bird droppings can sometimes trigger respiratory problems.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Ahh, yes, our neighbour keeps many birds on the rooftop, we are very close to them. I never thought that could be a problem.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: It very much can be. Do you have any history of asthma or breathlessness in the past?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: I had asthma as a child but the doctor said it resolved. And I have a past history of jaundice when I was in school, and my family has diabetes — my mother has it.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Okay. Do you smoke cigarettes or use any opioids?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: I used to smoke cigarettes 30 minutes daily but I stopped. And opioids — I used them socially during college but not anymore.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Good that you stopped. You are currently on escitalopram for anxiety — are you taking it regularly?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Right, I am taking escitalopram regularly doctor. No side effects so far. Also, last time you mentioned checking something related to my uterus, I forgot to ask about that.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Yes, I wanted to rule out any infection around the uterus area since you had that severe pelvic pain last quarter. Any discharge or pain now?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: I don't think so, doctor, that pelvic pain near the uterus seems absent now. No discharge either.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Alright. Based on the sore throat, fever every other day, and swelling, this looks like acute tonsillitis with possible viral infection. The construction site dust and birds exposure may be worsening your old asthma tendency as well.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I am prescribing amoxicillin for the throat infection and paracetamol for the fever. Continue your escitalopram as before. I will also add montelukast for the respiratory symptoms given your dust and bird exposure.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: We will send a urine culture to confirm there is no lingering infection near the uterus, and also a throat swab culture to identify the exact organism causing your sore throat.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, should I avoid the public transport during this time? And should I wear a mask at the factory near the construction site?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Absolutely, wear an N95 mask near the construction site and on public transport. Avoid the rooftop with the birds completely until your asthma is reassessed. Stay hydrated, rest well, and come back in two weeks or earlier if the fever becomes severe again.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Hello, please come in and sit down. And you have brought your mother along, good.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Thank you doctor. I was referred here by my family doctor because my periods are very irregular and I have been having some discharge also. I read online it could be PCOS or something worse.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Okay, do not worry too much about what you read online. Tell me, when did these irregular periods start? And what does the discharge look like — is it thin or thick?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: The irregular periods have been there since last week they were supposed to come and did not. And yes, the discharge is thin and whitish. I also had spotting two weeks ago.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I see. How often do you get your periods normally? And is the bleeding heavy or light when they do come?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: They used to be regular every month but now they have been non-stop irregular for about four cycles. When they come, there is a lot of cramping in my lower abdomen and the flow is quite heavy.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any acne on your face or hair thinning on the scalp? Any weight gain recently?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes, I have been getting acne on my chin and jaw a lot. And umm, I have gained maybe three to four kilos in the last few months. I read online that these are all signs of PCOS. Is that what I have, doctor?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: We will come to that shortly. Has there been any pelvic pain or pain in the lower back? How many times have you had the spotting — just the once?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: The spotting happened a few times over the last two months. And yes, there is some pelvic pain too, dull and aching mostly.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any history of vaccination for HPV? And has anyone in the family had hepatitis or liver problems?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Umm, yes, I got the vaccination in school I think, the HPV one. And my uncle had hepatitis B some years back but I was tested and it was ruled out in me.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Good. Are you on any medications currently? Any ibuprofen or Advil for the cramping?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, I take Advil or sometimes ibuprofen when the cramping is very bad. My mother also gave me losartan once when I complained of headache thinking it was her blood pressure tablet that would help, but that was a mistake I think.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Please do not take losartan — that is a blood pressure medication and it is not appropriate for you at all. It can cause dizziness and other problems. Now, does anyone at home smoke? Any exposure to chemicals?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: My father works at a factory and he does smoke at home sometimes, 1 pack per day. I have been around that secondhand smoke since childhood.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Understood. Any ultrasound or blood test done before coming here today?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, my family doctor did a pelvic ultrasound and a hormonal blood test. I have the reports here. The ultrasound showed some small cysts on my ovaries.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: After reviewing these reports and your symptoms — the irregular periods, acne, weight gain, thin discharge, and cysts on the ovaries — this is a case of Polycystic Ovary Syndrome, what we call PCOS.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Oh no, doctor! I read online it can cause infertility and even diabetes later. Is that true? What can I do?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: It is manageable, especially when caught early at your age. PCOS does carry a risk of insulin resistance and diabetes long-term, but with proper treatment, diet, and regular exercise, you can control it very well. We will also monitor your ovaries with repeat ultrasound every six months.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I am prescribing a low-dose oral contraceptive pill to regulate your periods and reduce the acne. Also starting metformin to help with insulin resistance. For the cramping, you may continue ibuprofen but only as needed, not regularly.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, I am a little scared about the oral contraceptive pill. Online it said it can cause blood clots and nausea. Are there any other side effects I should know about?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Some girls do get mild nausea or headache in the first month, but it usually settles. Blood clots are very rare at your age. Do come back immediately if you have chest pain, leg swelling, or sudden vision changes. We will do a fasting blood glucose and lipid profile in three months to keep track.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Okay doctor, thank you so much. I feel better now that I know what is going on. I will follow everything you said.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Yes, come in quickly please, I am running a bit behind today.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, very recently my skin all over my abdomen has broken out badly — rash and itching is too much. Multiple times a day I am scratching only.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Okay. Is there any rash on the lips or ankle also?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Umm, yes doctor, ankle also is having some patches and my lips feel dull ache inside, like swollen feeling. Couple of days only it started there.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any itching that is wet or oozing — like liquid coming out from the patches?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, the abdomen area patches are wet, some fluid is coming. It is also stabbing type pain sometimes when I press on it.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: What work do you do? Any chemicals or cleaning agents contact?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: I am doing domestic help work in four houses. Lots of chemicals — floor cleaners, toilet cleaners, dish soap — my hands are always in it.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any other complaints like loose stools or joint problem?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Ahh, yes doctor, loose stools is there every night for past week. And my knee and ankle joints — there is joint problem also, dull ache type.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: You said you are on multiple medicines — which ones are you currently using?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: One doctor gave clotrimazole cream for the skin. Another gave cetirizine tablet for itching. And I am also taking ibuprofen for the joint pain — all three are ongoing.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Are you taking any alcohol or smoking?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: I smoke 5 cigarettes only sometimes, and drink 2 drinks a week only — occasionally, not regularly doctor.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any history of heart disease or diabetes in the family?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: My mother had some heart problem. Doctor had done a stress test and angiography on her. I myself had appendix operation — doctor did laparoscopy three years back.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: The abdomen rash — is it near your previous laparoscopy scar site?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Uh, yes doctor, exactly near that area only. And the itching there is stabbing when I bend or lift.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Okay, looking at the wet patches on your abdomen and ankle, combined with your chemicals exposure at work and prolonged antibiotic or cream use — this is a fungal infection with contact dermatitis. The lips swelling and loose stools suggest the ibuprofen is causing a reaction — we need to stop that immediately.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor so what should I do about the joint problem then if I stop ibuprofen?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I am prescribing fluconazole tablet once a week for the fungal infection, hydrocortisone cream for the abdomen and ankle rash, and paracetamol for joint pain instead of ibuprofen. Also continue cetirizine at night for the itching. Stop clotrimazole cream — it is not enough for this type.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Most important — avoid all chemicals direct contact, wear thick rubber gloves at work. No alcohol while on fluconazole, it will cause bad reaction. Also cut the smoking — it slows skin healing.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, the loose stools every night — should I do any stool test?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Yes, get a stool routine examination done from the lab today itself. If the loose stools continue beyond a week even after stopping ibuprofen, we may need a colonoscopy also. Come back after ten days for review.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Okay doctor, thank you so much. I will follow everything you said.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Good morning, please have a seat. How can I help you today?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Good morning doctor. Actually I am a police constable, and my department has sent me for a routine health screening. But I also wanted to ask about my son — he has been having fever and diarrhoea three days ago and it is still continuing.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Okay, we will address both. First, for your son — is the diarrhoea non-stop or does it come in episodes?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: It is non-stop doctor. And the fever comes and goes throughout the day. I read on the internet that it could be because of contaminated food.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: That is possible. Has the child been eating outside food or drinking unfiltered water? Any exposure to contaminated food recently?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Uh-huh, he had some street food three days ago, same day the symptoms started. Doctor, the internet said oral rehydration salts are enough — is that right?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: ORS is important yes, but depending on the severity we may need to add more treatment. We will come to that. Now let us do your own screening. Any chest pain or breathlessness?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, actually I have been having a pressure like pain in my back and sometimes a radiating feeling down my spine. Also my hand shakes sometimes. And I have been having a lot of anxiety lately.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: The anxiety — is it new or ongoing? And the back and spine pain — does it come and go or is it constant?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: The anxiety has been there when I was younger also but it got worse recently. The back pain comes and goes, and the hand trembling is non-stop these days.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Do you drink beer or consume any other substance? I need to ask for the screening form.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Umm, I do have beer every day doctor. And — I will be honest — I have been using heroin daily for 10 years. I know the internet says it causes withdrawal and tremors.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: That is very important information. The anxiety, tremors in your hand, and the pressure like pain in your back could all be related to this. Any past history of clotting disorder or any childhood illness I should know about?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yep, I had a clotting disorder detected a few years back, and I had some childhood illness — I think it was related to the spine, the doctor at the time called it an infection. I was never fully treated.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Are you on any medications currently? Any diazepam or other sedatives for the anxiety? And have you ever taken tenofovir or been tested for viral infections?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: I was given diazepam once before for anxiety but I stopped taking it. No one has given me tenofovir. The doctor mentioned something about fumes at my workplace too — we deal with traffic and chemical fumes daily.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Based on what you have told me — heroin use for 10 years, the tremors, anxiety, and history of clotting disorder — I am concerned you have opioid dependence with possible hepatitis co-infection given the heroin use. Your son's condition looks like acute gastroenteritis from contaminated food.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, I read that hepatitis needs very expensive medicines. We are not in a position to afford too much. Is there any cheaper option? And for acute gastroenteritis in children, the internet says antibiotics are not always needed — is that right?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: You are correct about the acute gastroenteritis — for most viral cases antibiotics are not needed. We will run a CRP for your son to check for bacterial involvement. For you, I need to do an Echo of your spine region and CRP to assess the inflammation, plus liver function tests given the heroin and beer history.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, what medicines will you give for my son's fever and diarrhoea? And something for my anxiety and back pain too?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: For your son, I am prescribing oral rehydration salts and zinc syrup for the diarrhoea, and paracetamol suspension for the fever. For you, I am restarting diazepam at a low dose for anxiety and withdrawal, and if the tests confirm hepatitis, we will enrol you in a government programme where tenofovir is available free of cost.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Ahh, that is a relief about the free medicines. But doctor, the pressure like pain in my spine is quite bad. Should I be worried about the clotting disorder making things worse?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Yes, the clotting disorder combined with heroin use for 10 years and exposure to chemical fumes does raise the risk. Please do not ignore the tremors or any sudden numbness in your hand or spine area. Avoid all beer and heroin completely — it will worsen the anxiety and liver damage.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: I understand doctor. The Echo and CRP — can those be done at the government hospital at low cost? We really cannot afford private lab fees.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Absolutely, I will write the referral to the government facility. The CRP and Echo are covered under the CGHS scheme since you are a government employee. Make sure your son finishes the zinc syrup course fully, and follow up in one week for both of you.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Yes, come in quickly please, I am running a bit behind today. What brings you in?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, I am pregnant and I saw another doctor but I wanted a second opinion. I have been feeling very lethargic all the time and there is a skin infection on my chest that is not going away.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Okay. How far along is your pregnancy, and when did this skin infection start?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: I am six months pregnant. The infection started last summer and the skin has turned yellow in patches near the chest. The tiredness is nonstop.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any seizures, fainting, or breathlessness during this time?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Umm, no seizures thank God, but I do get breathlessness twice a day, especially in the evening. And I had one episode of seizures last summer which really scared me.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: You mentioned a prior episode of seizures. Any history of stroke or neurological problems in the family?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: My mother had a stroke some years back. As for me, nobody diagnosed me with anything like that so far.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: What about cigarettes or alcohol? Are you taking any of these?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: I used to have cigarettes every morning before pregnancy, but I have stopped now. Alcohol I never touched, doctor.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Good that you stopped. Any smoke exposure at home or work? Was any sick person around you recently?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes, my coworker was sick a few months back with some cough and fever. And there is smoke from the kitchen stove at home.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: What medicines are you currently on? Did the previous doctor prescribe anything?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Ahh, the other doctor gave me acetaminophen for the body ache and iron supplements for my blood. I also have a thyroid problem so I take levothyroxine twice a day.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Did you consult anyone else — any local health provider before coming here?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, I went to a local informal provider near my area first. He gave me some herbal mixture but it did not help at all with the skin infection or the lethargic feeling.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Okay. Is there any cough or chest pain? I want to check your lung function as well.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: There is some chest pain on the left side of the chest. The lung area feels tight sometimes, especially at night.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Based on what you are telling me, I suspect this is a case of pulmonary infection along with hypothyroidism that is not well controlled, which is causing the lethargic feeling and the skin infection. The prior seizures episode also needs proper evaluation given your family history of stroke.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: We will need a X-ray of the chest — it is safe to do in pregnancy with shielding — and a stress test to rule out any cardiac involvement given your breathlessness and chest pain.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, is the stress test safe in pregnancy? I am worried. Also should I continue the levothyroxine?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Yes, continue your levothyroxine as before — do not skip it. We will do a modified stress test suitable for pregnancy. Your iron supplements should also continue twice a day as your blood levels are low.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: For the skin infection, I am prescribing a topical antibiotic cream — safe in pregnancy. Continue acetaminophen for pain but do not exceed the dose. I am also adding a pregnancy-safe iron supplements with higher dose given the lethargic state.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Please avoid any more herbal mixtures from informal providers — they can be harmful in pregnancy. Also reduce smoke exposure from the kitchen as much as possible. Avoid contact with any sick person to prevent further infection.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Thank you so much doctor, I will follow everything you said.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Oh, it is you! Long time no see — where have you been hiding? I was wondering what happened.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: I know, I know, doctor! I am so sorry. Work at the stall was too hectic and then I was fasting for the religious season, so I kept missing appointments.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Alright, no scolding today, but you must be regular. Now tell me, how are the periods these days?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, that is the main problem. In January they had almost stopped, and then this morning I noticed some discharge, which is why I finally came in.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Okay. Is the discharge happening multiple times a day, or just occasionally?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Umm, multiple times a day doctor. It is yellowish and there is some itching also in the belly area, lower side.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any pain near the uterus region, like lower belly cramping?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, dull ache is there monthly around period time, but it gets better after two or three days on its own.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: When we last met back in 2023, your ultrasound had shown cysts. Have you been doing any exercise as I had recommended?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Ahh, nope doctor, honestly no time. Standing at the stall daily is all the moving I do. Exercise properly — don't think so I have managed even once.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: What about your food and habits? Do you drink alcohol or use cannabis?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, I will be honest — I do take alcohol, around 3 beers a day after stall hours. And cannabis sometimes on weekends to unwind. I know it is not good.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I see. Any pets at home, or do you work near a construction site? I am asking because sometimes environmental exposure can affect hormones.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Ahh, my stall is right next to a construction site, dust is everywhere. And yes, we have two cats at home, so pets are present.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Have you been taking the metformin I had prescribed earlier for the PCOS?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: I stopped after a few months doctor, because I felt better. I also had irregular periods since teenage years but I never followed up properly.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Okay, so based on everything — the irregular cycles, cysts on the previous ultrasound, discharge, and your lifestyle — this is a flare-up of PCOS with a secondary vaginal infection. We need to address both.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, can the alcohol and cannabis be making the PCOS worse?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Absolutely yes — alcohol especially at 3 beers a day can disturb your insulin and hormone levels badly, directly affecting the uterus and worsening the cysts.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I am prescribing metformin 500 mg twice daily again, fluconazole for the vaginal infection, and clindamycin cream to apply locally — please do not skip this time.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: And doctor, what should I do about food while fasting? I do not want the medicines to cause nausea or acidity on an empty stomach.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Take metformin only after you break your fast — never on empty stomach, it will cause nausea. Also please start at least 30 minutes of exercise — walking is enough — daily.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Cut down the alcohol completely while on metformin — combining them can cause dizziness and even hypoglycaemia. And reduce the cannabis too, it is not helping your hormones.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Understood doctor. I will try my best. Should I do that ultrasound again and any blood test?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Yes — get a repeat pelvic ultrasound, fasting insulin, and LH/FSH ratio done this week, and come back to me in two weeks without missing, okay? No more disappearing for months!

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Good morning, please take a seat. You are here for the insurance medical documentation, correct?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, good morning. My company is asking for a full fitness certificate for long-distance driving. They need detailed records.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Alright, I will do a thorough check. Tell me, are you having any cough, breathlessness, or wheezing currently?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, yes, I have been having cough on and off for many months now. Wheezing happens every other day, especially early morning.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Is there any breathlessness while driving or on physical exertion? Any chest tightness or chest pain in the chest area?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Umm, the breathlessness comes periodically doctor, mostly when I am going up a slope or lifting luggage. There is some chest tightness but no severe chest pain.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Are you a cigarettes smoker? If yes, how much are you smoking?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, I have been smoking cigarettes two packs a day since 2023. Before that also I was smoking, but less.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Have you ever used opioids or any other substances? This is for the medico-legal record, please be honest.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Ahh, doctor I must be honest — I have used opioids periodically in the past for staying awake on long night routes, but I have stopped now.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Noted. Any crowded places exposure regularly, like bus depots or busy terminals, which could worsen respiratory symptoms?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, crowded places like bus stands and depots — I am there every other day. Lot of dust and fumes also.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Do you have any past history of high blood pressure, clotting disorder, or jaundice?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, I had jaundice when I was young. And they once told me I have some clotting disorder after a leg swelling episode. High blood pressure — no, not that I know of.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I see. Any bluish discolouration of the lips that you or anyone has noticed? Any swelling in the legs?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: My wife says my lips look slightly bluish sometimes, especially after climbing stairs. Leg swelling I had before but no current swelling.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any bleeding issues or abdominal pain near the colon area? Any loose motions or blood in stool?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: No doctor, nothing like blood in stool. Some abdominal pain near the colon side occasionally, but I thought it was gas trouble. No bleeding.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Have you done any spirometry, chest X-ray, or complete blood count recently? Any treatment going on currently?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Ahh, I did a chest X-ray 2023 only — they said some hyperinflation was there. No spirometry was done. Currently no medicines, nothing.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Based on your heavy smoking of cigarettes at two packs a day, the wheezing, breathlessness, bluish lips, and hyperinflation on chest X-ray, this is a case of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease. The past clotting disorder also makes things complicated.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I am prescribing a short course of steroids to reduce the airway inflammation, and given your clotting disorder history and risk of deep vein thrombosis, we will add heparin under close supervision. I will also order a spirometry, D-dimer test, and liver function test given your jaundice history before finalising the certificate.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, should I be worried about taking steroids with my clotting disorder? And will these tests affect my fitness certificate outcome?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: The steroids dose will be low and short-term, and heparin will protect against clotting risk. You must completely stop cigarettes and opioids — continued use will directly affect your fitness clearance for driving. Avoid crowded places with heavy dust and fumes as much as possible, and report any worsening breathlessness or coughing up blood immediately.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Understood doctor, thank you. I will get all the tests done and come back as soon as possible.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Good afternoon, come in, sit down. How are you doing today?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Fine, doctor.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: This is your annual check-up, yes? How old are you now, and are you having any pain or discomfort anywhere?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: I am 16. Umm, I get pain near my lower abdomen periodically. It is like a pressure like pain.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Lower abdominal pain with a pressure like pain — I see. Any swelling or bulge you notice near your groin area?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Ahh, yes, there is a small bulge there. It comes and goes. It appears three times a week, especially when I lift things.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any nausea, vomiting, or feeling of the bowel being stuck? And any spasms in the area?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Taking nothing for it now. I do get spasms sometimes in my lower abdomen. No vomiting.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any piles or bleeding from rectum? Any abscess or swelling near your bottom?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Denied. Nothing like that, doctor.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: You mentioned you work night shifts — since when? And are you sleeping properly?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Uh, a year ago I started night shift work at a call centre. Sleep is not regular. I take a lot of caffeine to stay awake.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: How much caffeine — how many cups daily? Do you smoke or use anything else?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Around 4 to 5 cups. I was smoking — 5 cigarettes a day for 20 years... wait no, doctor, I mean I have been smoking since age 14. And umm, I used marijuana before but I quit that.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Okay, so you have quit marijuana. Do you use it occasionally still, or fully stopped? And do you do any exercise like running?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Fully stopped. I do running three times a week in the morning. I am from a rural area so I am used to walking a lot.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any family history of hernia? Any history of paralysis or weakness in the legs?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: My mother had hernia during pregnancy. No paralysis in family. I myself feel weakness in legs periodically after the night shifts.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Based on your symptoms — the bulge in the groin, pressure like pain, and spasms — this looks like an inguinal hernia. The weakness in legs may be from sleep deprivation and overexertion.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Is it serious, doctor?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: It needs surgical evaluation. I am ordering an ultrasound abdomen and a complete blood count today. Avoid heavy lifting and straining. Your smoking is also worsening abdominal pressure.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Okay. Also doctor, I sometimes get muscle spasms in my back after running.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Are the back spasms pressure like pain or more of a sharp shooting type? Any numbness in legs?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: More pressure like pain. No numbness.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Alright. I am prescribing dicyclomine for the abdominal spasms, multivitamin B complex for fatigue from night shifts, and ibuprofen gel for the back muscle pain. Reduce caffeine intake, and please follow up after the ultrasound results come.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Good afternoon, please come in and sit down. How are you feeling today?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Ahh, doctor, I am a little better than before but there is still pain on the right side, especially post-op. It is slightly painful most of the time but becomes unbearable worse at night.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Okay, so you were hospitalised two weeks ago for the hernia repair — the laparoscopy was done, correct? And you also had the piles and abscess treated at the same time?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yeah, doctor, all three were done together. The surgeon said the intestine repair went well but the abscess area is still giving me trouble.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Is there any bleeding or discharge from the wound site still? And any fever?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Umm, discharge is there once a day when I clean the wound. Fever is almost never now, doctor, only very mild in evenings sometimes.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Now I need to ask — I see in your file you were on rosuvastatin for cholesterol. Are you still taking it or did you change something on your own?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Ahh, doctor, I stopped the rosuvastatin on my own after surgery because my neighbour said it would interfere with healing. I also started taking antihistamines for the itching on the wound without telling anyone.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: You should never stop rosuvastatin without my advice — this can cause your cholesterol to spike suddenly. And self-medicating with antihistamines is risky especially when you are also on spironolactone for your fluid retention. These can interact badly.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: I did not know that, doctor. I am also on spironolactone for the swelling in my legs that was there before hospitalisation. I thought it was okay to continue it.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Your history mentions rheumatoid arthritis and anxiety disorder. Are those being managed separately? Any joint pain flare-up post-op?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: The rheumatoid arthritis is controlled doctor, I doubt it caused any flare this time. The anxiety disorder is a bit worse since the surgery but I am managing.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: You work in a mine, is that right? Tell me about your occupational exposures — any contact with crowded places, chemicals, or heavy dust underground?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, I work in the mine office but I do go underground sometimes. There is lot of dust and we are always in crowded places during shift changes. I have been doing this for 10 years.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: That is a long time. Any episodes of malaria or anemia in the past given the exposure in that environment?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, I had malaria once about three years back. And they told me I have mild anemia — it was detected at the time of my pre-surgery blood work two weeks ago.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: What about your diet and physical activity? Are you non-vegetarian? That matters for your recovery from anemia.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, I am non-vegetarian, so I eat chicken and eggs regularly. But physical activity I have quit completely after the surgery because of the pain on the right side.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Based on everything, you have post-operative wound infection at the abscess site, anemia that needs correction, and your intestine repair looks adequate but we need to monitor. The swelling in your legs may be related to fluid retention partly worsened by stopping spironolactone irregularly.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: So what should I do now doctor? I am a bit worried about all these medicines together. Should I restart everything?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Yes, restart rosuvastatin tonight itself — do not skip it again. Continue spironolactone as originally prescribed. I am stopping the self-started antihistamines and instead prescribing cetirizine which is safer in your current state. For the anemia I am adding ferrous sulphate tablets once a day with food.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: We will do a complete blood count and wound swab culture today to check the infection and anemia levels. Light physical activity like short walks can be restarted carefully — do not strain the right side.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, should I avoid going back to the mine with all this crowded places and dust? The wound is still open a little.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Absolutely avoid the underground area and crowded places for at least another three to four weeks. Dust exposure can worsen the wound infection and given your history of malaria, crowded damp environments are risky. Wear a mask if you must go to the office level. Come back in one week with the wound swab culture report.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Thank you so much doctor, I will follow everything you said this time properly.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Hello, please come in and have a seat. I can see you have been referred back from the higher centre — no need to worry, we will sort this out together.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Thank you doctor. I am very scared honestly. I am a college student and this has been going on for two weeks now and it is affecting my studies badly.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I understand, that must be quite stressful. Can you tell me exactly what symptoms you are experiencing? Any headache, dizziness, or numbness anywhere?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, all three are there. The headache comes every other day and is very throbbing at the temples. The dizziness comes with it mostly, and I get this numbness on my left hand sometimes.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Does the numbness spread to your arm or face? And is the headache one-sided or on both sides?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Umm, it is mostly one-sided on the left side doctor. The numbness does go up to the forearm sometimes but not really up to the face.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any nausea or vomiting during the headache episodes? Any blurred vision or ringing in the ears?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, nausea is definitely there and once or twice I did vomit. And ahh, there is some blurred vision just before the headache starts — like a flickering light kind of thing in front of my eyes.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: That flickering you describe before the headache is quite important. Any past history of TB, stone in the GB, or blood transfusion in the past?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, never used any hospital before this. No TB, no blood transfusion ever. The stone in the GB — my mother has that but I personally do not have it. I am generally very healthy.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Good to know. Do you smoke or drink alcohol? Any recreational substances?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: I am a social smoker only doctor, not a heavy one. I drink alcohol daily — I mean just a small peg in the evening because of stress from college. Is that a problem?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: It can contribute, yes. Now, where do you stay — hostel or home? Are you exposed to heavy pollution or do you come from a rural area?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: I come from a rural area originally but now staying in the city hostel near the highway, so there is a lot of pollution there. Lots of trucks passing at night and the air quality is really bad.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: What investigations did the higher centre do? Did they do an MRI brain or CT scan? Any EEG?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, they did an MRI brain and CT scan — both came back normal they said. They also did blood tests like CBC and blood sugar. All normal. No EEG was done.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Were you given any medicines over there? Any albuterol or painkillers or anything for the headache?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: They gave me albuterol but I am don't think so it helped — the headache and dizziness came back within two days. They did not explain why they gave it honestly.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: That is understandable. Is there any neck stiffness or sensitivity to light during your episodes? Any weakness in the legs?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes, there is sensitivity to light badly doctor. I have to go into a dark room. No neck stiffness, and the legs are fine — not really any weakness there.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Alright, based on everything — the one-sided headache, the visual aura before the attack, nausea, sensitivity to light, and the numbness — this is a classic case of migraine with aura. The normal MRI brain confirms there is nothing sinister going on.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Oh doctor, I am so relieved. But what is causing this migraine? Is it the pollution or the alcohol or stress from college?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Migraine has multiple triggers — alcohol, pollution, sleep disturbance, and emotional stress are all possible contributors in your case. The drinking alcohol daily is particularly a known migraine trigger and must be reduced.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I am prescribing you sumatriptan to take at the onset of the headache, and propranolol every other day initially as a preventive medicine. Also take domperidone for the nausea. Please maintain a headache diary and come back in two weeks.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Thank you so much doctor, I will follow everything. I will try to reduce the alcohol and move away from that pollution if possible. Should I get an EEG done as well?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Come in, come in. Please sit down. How are you feeling today?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, honestly not good at all. Since last week I am having this body pain all over, and some discharge also is coming from my ear. It is very uncomfortable.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Okay, let me understand. The discharge from your ear — is it foul-smelling? Any pain in the ear?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yeah, it smells bad and the pain is unbearable at times. I thought it would go away on its own, so I did not come earlier.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: This needs attention. Now tell me, you had surgery before — is this your first review after the C-section?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yeah, doctor. The C-section was done two days ago — no wait, two months ago. But two days ago I started noticing redness near my stitches also.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Is there any discharge from the stitch area as well? And any fever or chills?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Small amount of discharge is there from the stitch side, yes. No major fever. But doctor, I also have this irritation near my rectum, sometimes feels like a small ulcer. It is very painful.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: That rectal ulcer is concerning. Have you had any contaminated food recently? Any street food or unclean water?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, I run a shop so I eat outside only. Could be contaminated food, I don't know. But why are you linking my rectum problem with food? That doesn't make sense to me.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: It does make sense — some gut infections after contaminated food can cause ulcer formation in the lower digestive tract near the rectum. Especially after a surgery, immunity is low.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Okay fine. But doctor this body pain is also not going. Is this related to that COVID thing? Someone told me long COVID does this.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Yes, actually I suspect you have post-COVID sequelae — meaning your body is still recovering after the viral infection. The body pain, fatigue, and slow healing of your surgical wound all point to this.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: So what do I do for this? And doctor, the body pain happens rarely some days, but other days it is unbearable. Is that normal?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Yes, that waxing and waning pattern is common in post-viral recovery. We need to check your blood clotting also because after surgery and a viral illness, clot risk is higher. I want to order a coagulation test today.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Coagulation test? Why so many tests, doctor? Is it really necessary? And someone told me I might need a PET scan — is that true?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: The coagulation test is important for your safety after surgery. As for PET scan, that is not needed right now — nobody ordered that for your case. That is for cancer staging, not what you have.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Okay. Also doctor, I should tell you — I smoke, about 10 cigarettes a day. And sometimes I take weed also. Will that cause problem?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Absolutely it will cause problem. Smoking at 10 cigarettes a day slows down wound healing drastically after a C-section. And weed can interfere with your immune system. You must stop both immediately.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor you are saying stop everything — my work stress is so much, how will I manage without smoking?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I understand the stress, but let us start treatment. For your ear discharge, I am prescribing ear drops — use them twice a day. For the wound discharge and the rectal ulcer, I am starting you on metronidazole tablets and povidone-iodine wash for the stitches.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: So many medicines doctor. Will these ear drops work fast? And what about the ulcer near my rectum? It is very unbearable to sit even.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: The ear drops will show improvement within five to seven days. For the ulcer at the rectum, avoid spicy food, avoid straining, and do not use soap directly on that area. The metronidazole will help reduce infection there.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Okay fine, I will try. But doctor, should I come back next week? My body pain is still there even though it happens rarely now.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Yes, come back in one week. Get the coagulation test done tomorrow morning on empty stomach. If the discharge from stitches increases or the body pain becomes unbearable again, come immediately without waiting. Take care of your diet — nobody can heal fast on outside food only.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Come in, come in. Please take a seat. No need to be nervous.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Umm... thank you doctor. I am having weakness in my arms and legs since 2024. It is getting very bad now.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Okay. Tell me, is there any numbness or tingling in the hands or feet?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Ahh... yes doctor. Tingling in both feet is there daily. Hands also sometimes go numb.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any muscle pain or cramps? And are you having fatigue even after rest?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, fatigue is very bad. Even after sleeping full night I feel extremely tired. Muscle pain in legs is there about a week more severely.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: You mentioned these problems started in 2024. Did you have a COVID infection or some severe viral fever around that time?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Umm... yes doctor. I had COVID in early 2024. After that these weakness and tiredness started only.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I see. Any past surgery or other serious illness before this?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Ahh... I had past surgery on my abdomen some years back for a hernia. Otherwise nothing serious doctor.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Okay. You are a manual labourer — any animal hair exposure at your worksite? And do you live in a rural area?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, I work near a farm. Animal hair is always there. I am from a rural area only. Sometimes we eat outside and food quality is not good — contaminated food also possible.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Do you drink alcohol? And are you taking any opioids or any other medicines on your own?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Umm... doctor I take alcohol 2 drinks a week only. About opioids... I was taking some pain tablets for the muscle pain but I stopped.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Alright. I have your lab reports here. Your AST levels are elevated and I had also recommended an EMG. Did you get both done?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor. I got the AST and EMG done last week only. I have the reports here.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Let me review. Your EMG is showing peripheral neuropathy and the elevated AST suggests some liver stress. Combined with your COVID history and exposure, this is a case of post-COVID neuropathy with early hepatic involvement.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Ahh... doctor, this neuropathy — is it very serious? Will I be able to do my work again?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: It is manageable if we treat it properly and early. You must stop the opioids completely and reduce alcohol intake as both are worsening your liver stress and nerve damage.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I am prescribing methylcobalamin for the nerve weakness, pregabalin for the tingling and pain, and silymarin to support your liver.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, any foods I should avoid? And the contaminated food issue — should I be more careful?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Yes, absolutely avoid contaminated food. Eat only properly cooked meals. Avoid heavy lifting that strains your arms and legs until the weakness improves. Also limit animal hair contact and wear a mask at the worksite.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, do I need to come back soon? How will you check if I am improving?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Yes, I want a follow-up in four weeks. We will repeat the AST and also do a nerve conduction study to see how the peripheral neuropathy is responding to treatment.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Thank you so much doctor. I will follow everything properly.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Welcome back. Good to see you up and about after your hospital stay.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Thank you doctor. Still not feeling fully right. I have this stuffy nose every night and a feeling like a rock in stomach after eating.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Okay, let us start from the beginning. Any fatigue, weight gain, or cold intolerance since discharge?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, I am feeling very tired all the time and my hands and feet are always cold. The weight gain also — almost three kilos in one month.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: When you were admitted in 2023, what tests were done? Did they check fasting sugar or thyroid at that time?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: They did fasting sugar doctor and it was high — around 220 they said. And thyroid function test also showed some problem. They also did lumbar puncture because I had severe headache during admission.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I see. Any headache still persisting? Or neck stiffness?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: No doctor, headache has settled. But the stuffy nose is really troubling me every night. I have to breathe through my mouth while sleeping.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: You mentioned you recently travelled to a rural area. Were you exposed to any asbestos, dust, or construction site fumes there?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Actually doctor, I am a teacher by profession but I was visiting my brother who works in a mine. I spent about ten days there. There was definitely asbestos dust around — old building materials, broken sheets lying everywhere.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: That is quite concerning. Any breathlessness, cough, or chest tightness after that trip?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Umm, yes, a little dry cough started after I came back. My chest feels tight in the mornings. I ignored it thinking it was the weather change.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Alright. Now I need to ask — do you smoke, drink alcohol, or use marijuana?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: I used marijuana socially doctor, for 10 years. But I have stopped now. No cigarettes or alcohol.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Good that you stopped. Any bloating, acidity, or nausea related to the rock in stomach feeling? Does it come after specific foods?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: It comes mostly after oily or heavy food doctor. Feeling like something is stuck and not moving in the stomach. Also acidity is there.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Based on your history and earlier reports, you have hypothyroidism, poorly controlled type 2 diabetes, and hypercholesterolaemia. The gastroparesis symptoms — this rock in stomach, bloating — are likely a complication of your diabetes. And the stuffy nose and dry cough after asbestos exposure needs urgent evaluation.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, all this is scaring me. Is the asbestos exposure dangerous for my lungs?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: It can be serious if exposure was prolonged. The dry cough and chest tightness in the chest must not be ignored. Please avoid any further asbestos contact and avoid smoking completely going forward.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: We need to order HRCT chest, lipid profile, HbA1c, and repeat thyroid function test. Are you currently on any medicines?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: They had started metformin 500 mg and levothyroxine during hospitalisation but I stopped both after a month because I felt better. Ahh, I know I should not have done that.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: You must restart immediately. I am prescribing metformin 1000 mg twice daily, levothyroxine 50 mcg every morning on empty stomach, atorvastatin 20 mg at night for your high cholesterol, and domperidone before meals for the gastroparesis. For stuffy nose, start fluticasone nasal spray each night.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, any side effects I should watch out for with metformin? I had loose motion when I took it before.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Loose motion and nausea from metformin are common in the beginning. Take it with food to reduce that. If diarrhoea is severe or persistent, inform me immediately. Also, do not skip levothyroxine — uncontrolled hypothyroidism is worsening your fatigue and weight gain.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Come back in four weeks with your HbA1c, thyroid function test, lipid profile, and HRCT chest reports. We will decide further treatment based on the HRCT chest findings. Stay away from any mines or construction areas until then.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Hello, come in, come in. Please sit down.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, my son he is having swelling on forehead and also whole face. Few days ago it started only.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I see. Is there swelling on the legs or feet also? Any back pain?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, legs also swelling. And he is saying back is paining multiple times a day. He is not telling me but I noticed only.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Is the swelling yellow looking or any colour change in the skin? Any gastritis complaint?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Umm, no skin colour change doctor. But gastritis yes, he is saying stomach is paining and once in a while he is vomiting also.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any family history of diabetes or fracture? Has the child had any surgery before like appendectomy?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: My wife she is having diabetes doctor. And my son, he fell from bicycle — he had fracture in 2020. Appendectomy also he had, two years back.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Was any test done recently? Any urine protein test or creatinine levels checked?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Ahh, creatinine was done last week doctor. Report said it was high. They also did EMG for the back pain complaint. Results are positive doctor, something abnormal is showing.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: The EMG result was positive for abnormality? And what medicines is he currently taking? Has anything been changed recently?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, I have to tell you — previous doctor gave some tablet but I changed it on my own. He was taking fluoxetine but I stopped it few days ago and gave some local medicine. I thought fluoxetine is not suiting him.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: You should not stop fluoxetine on your own without consulting a doctor. Sudden stopping of such medicines can cause mood changes and irritability in children. Please do not change medicines without advice.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Sorry doctor, I did not know. Also our house has mold problem — walls are all damp. Could that be causing swelling?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: The mold can affect lungs and cause allergic reactions, but this swelling pattern is more concerning for kidney involvement. Do you yourself drink coffee — does the child take any?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Uh, I am drinking coffee for 10 years doctor, but child does not take. He only drinks tea once in a while.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Based on the swelling of face, legs, back pain, high creatinine, and the urine protein pattern, this child appears to have nephrotic syndrome with kidney disease. This needs immediate proper treatment.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, but why kidney is affected? He is only 10 years. Is mold in house causing this?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: The mold may have triggered allergic reaction worsening things, but nephrotic syndrome in children often has immune system cause. The fracture treatment in 2020 with strong pain medicines may also have stressed the kidneys.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I am prescribing prednisolone tablets for the nephrotic syndrome, furosemide to reduce the swelling, and omeprazole to control the gastritis. Regarding fluoxetine, I will review whether to restart after consulting the earlier doctor.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, prednisolone is steroid no? Any problem for child? And gastritis will be more with steroid?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Yes, prednisolone is a steroid. It can worsen gastritis so omeprazole is given along with it. Watch for weight gain, mood changes, and high blood pressure. Also, the damp mold in your house must be cleared as infection risk is high while on steroids.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: We need to do kidney biopsy if there is no improvement in four weeks. Also repeat creatinine and urine protein every week. Low sodium diet must be followed to help reduce swelling.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, school is there — can he go? And back pain is there, he cannot sit for long time. Yellow colour urine also coming multiple times a day — is that serious?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Yellow discolouration of urine with multiple times a day frequency is concerning — we will add urine routine examination today. School rest for two weeks is advised. Back pain should reduce once the kidney swelling comes down with furosemide and prednisolone. Come back in one week for review.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Ah, you are finally back! It has been quite some time — how are you doing?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Sorry doctor, life got busy. But now I am here.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Alright, so tell me — what is bothering you currently? And you missed so many follow-ups, that also I want to discuss.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Currently I am having cough which is productive and it is happening non-stop since in January itself. Also my throat is very irritated.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: A productive cough for so long is concerning. Any chest pain? Is it squeezing type or dull?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, sometimes in the lower back also I get severe pain. And the chest feels squeezing when I cough continuously.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
