utterances.text: Doctor: Have you had any history of TB or tuberculosis in the past? Any family member also?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Umm, true doctor, my father had tuberculosis many years back. But I never had it myself, as far as I know.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Okay. Any recent international travel or exposure to heavy pollution? Any workplace exposure to mercury or chemicals?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: I went abroad last year, so yes there was international travel. And my gym near the highway — lots of pollution there. No mercury exposure though, I am not working in any factory.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any burning urination or UTI symptoms? Any pain near the belly button region?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Actually yes, I did have a UTI last month. Pain near the belly button was also there but it came and went once a day. I just ignored it.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: You are on many medicines from different doctors also, correct? Are you taking simvastatin regularly? And have you been self-medicating with any cough syrup?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, I am taking simvastatin from the cardiac doctor. And yes I bought cough syrup from the medical shop myself — it helped a little but the cough came back.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Do you cycle or do any heavy gym work? And are you non-vegetarian? How many cups of tea per day?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: I used to cycle a lot, but not anymore since this cough started. I am non-vegetarian, yes. Tea I take maybe three or four times daily but doctor I don't think that is causing anything.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: We need to check your oxygen saturation right now and also do a weight check — you look like you have lost weight since last visit. Any night sweats or fever?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Ahh, yes doctor, night sweats have been there non-stop for weeks. Fever is low grade only. The oxygen saturation machine at home showed 94 yesterday.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Your weight check shows you are down by 5 kilograms from last visit. The oxygen saturation here is showing 93 percent — that is on the lower side. We need to investigate thoroughly.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Looking at your productive cough, night sweats, significant weight loss, family history of tuberculosis, and pollution exposure — I strongly suspect this is a case of active pulmonary tuberculosis. The UTI may also indicate an underlying immunocompromised state.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, TB? That is very serious no? What should I do now? And the lower back pain and belly button pain — are they related?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: The lower back pain could be related if renal TB is involved — that would also explain your UTI symptoms. We will order a sputum AFB test, chest X-ray, urine culture, and CBC today. You must stop self-medicating with cough syrup immediately.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Until the reports come, I am starting you on isoniazid, rifampicin, pyrazinamide, and ethambutol as first-line anti-TB therapy. We will also continue your simvastatin but at a lower dose as there is drug interaction risk. Take pyridoxine once a day to prevent neuropathy.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Please avoid heavy cycling or gym until your breathlessness improves. Reduce tea as it interferes with iron absorption. Wear a mask always — this is a severe infection and can spread. Come back in two weeks without fail.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Understood doctor. I will follow everything. I just want this cough from the throat downwards to stop — it is making me very tired continuously.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Welcome. This is your workplace health screening, so let us go through everything properly today.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, thank you. Actually I am having itching all over my entire body about a week now, it is very troublesome.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Okay we will address that. Any skin infection or rash visible on your hand or elsewhere?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Umm, yes doctor, there is some redness on my hand. The discharge is clear, not yellow or anything. And doctor, I also wanted to ask about this lump near my groin area.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: That lump near the groin — is it painful? Any swelling that comes and goes?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: It is paining sometimes, especially when I lift heavy things at the factory. The swelling is there all the time now.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: From what you describe, this sounds like an inguinal hernia. We will need to examine it properly. Any history of piles or abscess near the rectal area?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Ahh, yes doctor, when I was younger I had piles, it was treated. But now sometimes there is burning pain — burning pain when passing urine also.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: That burning pain during urination — any UTI diagnosed before? Any fever or discharge along with it?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor actually I think it may be UTI only, I had it before also. No fever now. But doctor, I also have cough — it is productive, coming up with phlegm every morning.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Okay, let us talk about your work. Are you exposed to fumes or chemicals at the factory? Any work near a mine site?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, our unit is close to a mine and there are fumes from the machinery all the time. We do not get proper masks.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Do you drink or use any drugs? Please be honest, it helps me assess your health correctly.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Umm, I take whiskey occasionally on weekends, and 3 beers a day after shift. No drugs, that I denied.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any past history of hypertension or heart problem? Are you on any regular medicines?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, I have hypertension and I was told I have hepatitis B also, so I am on entecavir for that. Blood pressure tablets I stopped taking on my own.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: That is concerning. We will need to check your PT INR and vitamin B12 levels given your alcohol intake and hepatitis B status. I also want to do a lumbar puncture if any neurological signs appear.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, lumbar puncture I will not do — it is very scary and also costly for me. Can we skip that one? The PT INR and vitamin B12 I can manage.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: The lumbar puncture is only if needed later, do not worry for now. But your hepatitis B is active and the liver is at risk especially with 3 beers a day — you must reduce alcohol completely.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: I understand doctor. Also I forgot to mention — there is numbness in my hand sometimes, and my entire body feels very weak by evening.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: That numbness and weakness — any dizziness or headache along with it? Could be related to low vitamin B12.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, headache is there all the time by evening. No dizziness though.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Alright. I am prescribing ciprofloxacin for the UTI, a antifungal cream for the skin infection on your hand, and continue entecavir as before. I am also starting amlodipine for hypertension and methylcobalamin injections for the numbness.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: For the inguinal hernia, avoid heavy lifting at the factory — you must inform your supervisor. The itching across your entire body may be related to liver function, so alcohol must stop completely. Wear proper masks to avoid fumes exposure.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Thank you doctor, I will follow all this. I did not know so many things were connected like this.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Hello, come in, come in. Have a seat, no need to be nervous.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Umm, thank you doctor. I am here for my follow-up after the surgery.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Yes, I have your file here. You had the laparoscopic cholecystectomy six months back, correct? How are you feeling overall?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Ahh, doctor... I am okay mostly, but there is some swelling near my abdomen area for six months now, it is not going down.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any yellowing of your eyes or skin? Any fatigue or nausea?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, yellowing of the eyes started about three weeks back. And I feel very tired all the time. I did not want to say because I thought it would go away on its own.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Did you travel anywhere recently? Any visit to a rural area or congested locality?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Umm, yes doctor, I went to my village last month. It is near a mine area, quite dusty and crowded.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I see. Any cough? If yes, is it productive or heavy?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Ahh, yes there is a cough, it feels heavy and productive. But I get it hardly ever, so I did not think much about it.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any swelling or lumps noticed near your lymph nodes — like in the neck or armpit region?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Umm... nah doctor, I have not noticed any lumps there. But I did feel some soreness near the neck once.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any past history of tuberculosis in yourself or your family?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: My uncle had tuberculosis a few years back. I myself never had it, doctor.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: You are into gym and athletics — do you use opioids or any performance supplements? And how long have you been doing sports?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Ahh, I did use opioids for 10 years for pain management after an old injury, doctor. And I have been doing sports since college. I train 30 minutes daily at least, even now.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Are you under a lot of stress lately? And are you on any current medications — like amlodipine for blood pressure?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, I take amlodipine since college for high blood pressure. And yes, stress is quite bad these days because of training and work both.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Based on everything — the jaundice, swelling, mine area travel history, and long-term opioids use — this looks like a combination of fatty liver disease and likely hepatitis A triggered by the exposure.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, is the fatty liver because of the opioids I was taking?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Yes, long-term opioids use combined with stress and high-intensity sports training puts liver under a lot of strain. The mine area visit likely triggered the acute jaundice episode on top of that.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I will need to order a liver function test, hepatitis A antibody test, ultrasound abdomen, and also a stress test given your cardiac history with blood pressure. Has any of this been done before?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Ahh, nah doctor, none of these tests were done after surgery. Only a basic blood count was checked at that time.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Alright. I am prescribing ursodeoxycholic acid for fatty liver, silymarin to support liver recovery, and continue amlodipine as before. Stop all opioids completely from today.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Reduce stress, avoid heavy sports training for at least four weeks, drink only boiled water, and strictly avoid any further exposure to mine dust or crowded rural areas until the jaundice and swelling fully resolve.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Good morning, please come in and have a seat. So you are here for the school health screening, yes?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Good morning doctor. Yes, the school management sent all of us teachers for this follow-up screening. I was not planning to come actually, but they made it mandatory.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: That is fine, it is a good opportunity. So tell me, are you having any complaints currently? Any body aches or feeling lethargic?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, nothing specific I thought to mention, but now that you ask — I have been feeling very lethargic and body aches are there just now also, like from this morning itself.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I see. And what about your periods? Any irregularity, heavy bleeding, or discharge?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Ahh, the periods are very irregular doctor. Sometimes gap of two to three months. And there is discharge also — it is clear type, not smelly, but it is there often.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any abdominal pain? Especially, is it worse after eating? And is there any bloating or weight gain?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: The abdominal pain is there, yes. It is very sharp and worse after eating once in a while. Weight gain is also there, I have put on about five kilos in one year.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Do you have any history of high blood pressure or stone problem — kidney or gallbladder?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, I had a stone in the kidney two years back. And high blood pressure is there, running in the family. I had a broken bone in my prostate— sorry, I mean in my wrist, from a fall long back.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Alright. Are you currently on any medicines? For example, hydrochlorothiazide for blood pressure or warfarin for anything?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Umm, yes doctor, I am taking hydrochlorothiazide for the blood pressure. No warfarin or anything like that. But I also went to a local health provider nearby — not a proper doctor — he gave me some herbal tablets for the period problem.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I see — I will note that. Junior, please observe — patients consulting informal providers often delay proper diagnosis. Now madam, do you have any pet dander exposure at home or school? Any rash or sneezing issues?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes, we have a cat at home, so pet dander is there. I do get sneezing often, I thought it was just dust from the classroom.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Understood. Do you coffee drink — how much? And what about physical activity? Any cocaine or other substance use?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: I have coffee every morning, two big cups. Physical activity — I used to walk daily but stopped after the knee problem started. Cocaine — no no doctor, nothing like that at all.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Okay, good. Any acne, hair fall, or excess facial hair growth? These things matter for understanding the period irregularity.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, acne is there on my chin and jaw. And some hair fall also. I thought it was because of stress from teaching.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Junior, notice the cluster — irregular periods, weight gain, acne, hair fall, and lethargic feeling. This presentation is classic PCOS — Polycystic Ovarian Syndrome. We should also check for insulin resistance.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, what is this PCOS exactly? The local health person I went to said it is just hormonal imbalance and gave me some powders. Is it serious?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Yes, PCOS is a hormonal imbalance but it needs proper medical management — not from informal providers. We need to run an ultrasound pelvis, fasting insulin, testosterone levels, and a lipid profile given your high blood pressure history.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Okay doctor. Will you give me some medicine to regularize the periods? And what about the discharge — the clear one?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Yes. I am starting you on metformin for insulin regulation and oral contraceptive pills to regulate the cycles. For the discharge — since it is clear and not offensive, I will add fluconazole as a precaution and clindamycin vaginal cream. Continue hydrochlorothiazide as before.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Now, regarding the pet dander — do manage the cat exposure at home. Also, resume physical activity — even thirty minutes of walking helps with PCOS enormously. Please stop the herbal tablets from the informal provider — they can interact with your hydrochlorothiazide and affect the stone risk again.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Thank you so much doctor. I will follow everything properly. I did not realise it was so important. I will come back for the tests soon.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Hello, come in, come in. Please sit down.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Thank you doctor. I am here because my grandmother is not doing well at all. She sent me to get her medicines refilled and also she has new complaints since morning.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Okay, tell me everything. What are her main problems right now? Any back pain, confusion, or anything else new?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, she has been having back pain for a week now, and since morning she is having confusion also. She is not recognising people properly.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Is there any bleeding from the nose or any rash on the skin? And is her skin feeling warm?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Umm, yes, the skin is feeling warm to touch, and once in a while there is some bleeding from the nose also. Nothing too heavy though.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any stomach pain or discomfort that is worse after eating? And any weakness or anemia complaints?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: She has been having stomach pain that is worse after eating, doctor. And the anemia was detected before the tests she had done last month. She looks very pale.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: What is her past medical history? Any high blood pressure or cancer history?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, she has high blood pressure for many years. And ahh, she was treated for cancer also, around two years back. We are very worried about that.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: What medicines is she currently taking? Was she on enalapril and clopidogrel?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, she was on enalapril for the high blood pressure and clopidogrel also. But doctor honestly we cannot afford all these medicines. That is the problem. She has been skipping them.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I see. Now, has she had any sick contact recently? Any sun exposure or pesticides exposure, since she was complaining of skin problems?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: She works in the farm often, so there is definitely pesticides exposure. And sun exposure also is there a lot. Regarding sick contact, my cousin was sick last week and visited her.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Now I want to ask you something directly — does your grandmother drink alcohol or use any substances like weed?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Ahh, doctor... she will scold me for saying this, but yes she does use weed, once in a while. She has been doing it for 10 years. And she drinks alcohol also, twice a day she takes it.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Has she had any tooth pain or problems with her teeth? And the back pain — is it in the upper or lower back?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: She has been having tooth pain and her teeth are very bad condition. The back pain is in the lower back, doctor. It is never this bad before, she says.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Has she had any recent tests done? We may need BUN and ALT levels checked, and depending on the confusion, possibly a spinal tap also.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, she had some blood tests done before the tests last month but not BUN or ALT. The doctor there did not do those. And spinal tap — she is very scared of that.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Based on what you are telling me, the confusion, back pain, anemia, and her history of cancer, I am suspecting this could be metastatic disease with possible liver dysfunction given the alcohol use. The anemia and bleeding also need urgent attention.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, is it very serious? What should we do now? And about the medicines — we really cannot afford much. Is there any cheaper option for the enalapril and clopidogrel?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I understand the financial concern. I will continue enalapril for her high blood pressure and clopidogrel as before — both are available as generic versions at government hospitals. I am also adding iron supplements for the anemia and B-complex for overall nutrition. Please do not skip these medicines.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Most importantly, she must stop the alcohol and weed completely — these are making her confusion and liver problems much worse. She must avoid pesticides and sun exposure also, and if the back pain or confusion increases, bring her to emergency immediately.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Okay doctor, I will tell grandmother everything. Thank you for explaining. We will get the BUN and ALT done as soon as possible and come back for follow-up.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Come in, come in. Good to see you back. How are you feeling today?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, I came for the follow-up after discharge. I had that episode two months ago but these new complaints are there about a week now. headache is still there, mildly uncomfortable but not going.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Okay. And what about the dizziness? Is that also continuing? Any numbness in the arm or the toes?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, dizziness is there. And the numbness in the toes started three days ago. The arm also feels a little dead sometimes.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: How often is the dizziness coming? Is it weekly or more frequent than that?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Umm, it is coming weekly at least, doctor. Sometimes two, three times in a week also. When I stand up fast, it is very bad.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I see. And tell me about your cigarettes. Are you still smoking?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Ahh, doctor I know you will scold me. I am a chain smoker for many years. I am trying to reduce but it is very difficult.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: You must stop completely, no negotiation on that. What about your sleep habits? Are you sleeping properly at night? And are you doing any swimming or any exercise?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: No doctor, sleep is very poor. I am getting only three, four hours. And swimming I am doing 1 hour daily in the morning but about a week back I stopped because of the dizziness.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Good that you stopped for now. Any sun exposure for long hours? Or any animal hair contact at home?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, I sit outside on the terrace in the afternoon. So sun exposure is there daily. And we have a cat at home, so animal hair is everywhere in the house.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I see. When you were admitted, we did a CT scan brain and a MRI brain. Did you bring those reports today?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, I brought them. See, doctor. But I am a poor man, I cannot afford all these big tests again. Please see what is manageable.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I understand your situation completely. Looking at the reports and your symptoms, this is a case of transient ischemic attack with residual cervical spondylosis changes. The numbness in the toes and arm is from nerve compression, and the dizziness and headache are from reduced blood flow to the brain.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, what does that mean exactly? Is it serious? I am worried because I had a mild stroke two months ago also.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: It means we must be very careful. I am prescribing aspirin 75 mg once daily, atorvastatin 40 mg at night, and amlodipine 5 mg in the morning for your hypertension. Also continue the physiotherapy exercises for the neck and arm.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, these medicines, all are expensive? I am struggling financially. Is there any cheaper option in the government hospital?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Do not worry. Aspirin and atorvastatin are available in generic form at the Jan Aushadhi centre, very cheap. I will write generic names only. Also, please do a blood pressure monitoring every week and a fasting blood sugar test also, since high sugar can worsen your condition.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Now, very important — avoid sun exposure in the afternoon completely. The cigarettes must stop today, because smoking is directly worsening the blood supply to your brain. Also the animal hair from the cat — if you are getting any sneezing or breathing difficulty, please tell me.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Understood doctor. No sneezing or breathing difficulty from the cat. But I will keep the cat outside now only.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Good decision. Also fix your sleep habits — at least seven hours of rest is needed. You can restart swimming after two more weeks, slowly, only 1 hour daily, and check your dizziness before getting in the water. Do not go alone.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Now I want to do a teach-back. Can you tell me — what three medicines did I give you, and when to take them?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Ji doctor. You gave me aspirin in the morning, atorvastatin at night, and amlodipine in the morning also. And I must not go in the sun exposure and must stop cigarettes fully.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Excellent, very good! You remembered everything correctly. Come back in ten days. If numbness in the arm or toes increases, or if vision blurring or speech difficulty comes, go to emergency immediately, do not wait. We will repeat the MRI brain after three months if things are not improving.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Arrey, long time no see! How are you doing, my friend? Still driving your auto?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, same old life. But this time I am here for that insurance paper work only, they are asking for full medical report.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Of course, of course. But tell me also, how is the body feeling? Any new fatigue or pain?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, fatigue is there all the time. Even after sitting in the auto for just one hour, I feel completely drained.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: And that old hernia trouble near the abdomen? Is the bulging still coming when you strain?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Haan doctor, it is there only. Sharp pain is coming several times in the day when I am pushing or lifting anything heavy.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: And those piles — any bleeding from the bottom or pain during motion?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Little bit bleeding is there sometimes, and the abscess near the anal area that was drained last time — that place is still paining doctor.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Okay. Do you have history of high blood pressure, TB, or cancer in the family? For the insurance form I need to document all this.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: No doctor, no cancer in family. High blood pressure my father had. TB I myself had before the tests only, remember? That time you had sent me.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Yes yes, I remember. And are you chewing tobacco still? What about marijuana?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Umm, chewing tobacco I am still doing doctor, I know it is bad. Marijuana I stopped. But cigarettes — I am taking 10 cigarettes a day minimum.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: And food habits? Are you eating properly or still on junk food only?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor what to do, on road the whole day — junk food only is available. Proper food I cannot afford also, financial condition is very tight these days.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I understand. Are you taking any medicines currently? Before the tests did you take anything? What about the iron supplements I had prescribed?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Not taking doctor, iron supplements I stopped because I could not afford buying them every month. No other medicine also I am taking.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: See, based on everything — your hernia, piles, and that abscess history — these are three separate surgical problems. The fatigue is likely from anaemia because of the bleeding and poor diet.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, for insurance they are also asking about my hospital visit history and any ongoing treatment. Can you put all that in the report?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Yes, I will document the hospital visit records, the surgical history of abscess drainage, and current hernia and piles status. We also need to run sonography of the abdomen and LFT for complete documentation.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor the sonography and LFT — how much will it cost? I am telling you honestly, I have very little money right now.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Don't worry, I will write government hospital referral so cost will be very less. And about the cough — is there any productive cough or is it clear discharge only? Given your TB history I want to rule out any recurrence.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Ahh, little cough is there, the sputum is clear and sometimes productive in the morning. Chest is also feeling heavy sometimes.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Alright. I am restarting your iron supplements — please take them regularly. I am also prescribing sitz bath treatment and xylocaine ointment for the anal area pain. For the hernia we need surgical opinion, I will write referral letter.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor the sharp pain in abdomen is really troubling me several times in the day. Can something be done without operation? Operation I cannot afford at all.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I understand your situation completely. But delaying hernia surgery can cause serious complications. Meanwhile, stop chewing tobacco and reduce junk food — these are making the anaemia and abscess healing worse. I will attach all the documentation for your insurance and also write a letter recommending free surgery under government scheme.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Good morning. Please come in and sit down.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Good morning doctor. My son is very recently having fever and diarrhoea both together, it became very bad so we came straight away.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: How long has this fever been going on? Is the diarrhoea also from the same time?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: The loose motions started last month, but the fever came very recently. He is passing stool three times a week sometimes but now it is every day.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Is there any vomiting or stomach pain? Any rash anywhere on the body?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Umm, vomiting is there every day for two weeks now. No rash on the body, but I noticed his toes are looking a little red and swollen.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Redness and swelling on the toes — is that painful to touch? Does he complain of pain in the toes?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, he says it is paining when he walks. The toes are also warm to touch.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Was there any family member was sick at home recently? Any contact with someone having fever or diarrhoea?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, his elder sister had fever about last month. She recovered but then he started getting sick.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: How is his physical activity? He usually does cycling or playing or has he stopped due to the illness?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: He has completely stopped cycling and physical activity because of the weakness. He used to be very active before.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: What about drinking water — is he taking enough fluids? Any family history of kidney problems or autoimmune disease?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: He is not drinking much water these days. No kidney or autoimmune history in family that I know of.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Has he been given any antibiotic or oral rehydration salts before coming here? Any stool test or blood test done?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: We gave him oral rehydration salts at home, no antibiotic was started. No tests done, we came directly here doctor.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I will also ask — does anyone at home drink alcohol? Even as an occasional drinker, say 2 drinks a week? Or is there a chain smoker in the house?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: My husband is an occasional drinker, about 2 drinks a week. He is also a chain smoker — he smokes indoors sometimes.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: That is an family member was sick concern for secondhand smoke exposure as well. Now, is there any blood in stool or mucus in stool?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Ahh, yes doctor, there is some mucus in stool. No blood that I have seen.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Based on the fever, diarrhoea with mucus in stool, vomiting, and the swelling and redness of the toes, I am suspecting reactive arthritis following a gastrointestinal infection. We need to confirm this.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I am ordering a stool culture, complete blood count, C-reactive protein, creatinine, and joint X-ray of the toes to assess for any joint damage.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, will he be okay? Should we be worried about the toes? What will happen if the swelling does not go?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Most children recover well. I am prescribing ibuprofen for the joint pain and swelling, zinc supplements to help with the diarrhoea, and continuing oral rehydration salts every day until the loose motions settle.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Please ensure he starts drinking plenty of fluids, avoids physical activity until the toes swelling reduces, and strictly no smoke exposure indoors — that is worsening his overall immunity. Bring him back in one week with the creatinine and other reports.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Hello, congratulations on your new baby! Please take a seat. How can I help you today?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Thank you doctor. I am a new mother, baby is only two months old. I came for a second opinion actually — another doctor gave me some advice but I was not fully satisfied. I have been having allergy attacks that are non-stop for two years now, and they are getting worse after delivery.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Okay, I understand. Tell me more — are you having sneezing, runny nose, or skin rash also? Any wheezing?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, sneezing and runny nose are always there. But the main problem is this severe cramping pain in my epigastric area and sometimes it goes to my upper back. It is very cramping type of sensation.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Interesting. Is the pain around the pancreas region — I mean the upper middle epigastric area going through to the upper back? Does eating make it worse?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Exactly doctor, yes. And my upper back becomes very severe when the attack comes. Also my skin becomes very dry during seasonal changes — in winters especially.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Does the allergy worsen in any particular season? And are you exposed to any fumes or smoke at home?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes, definitely in winter and spring my symptoms are much worse. My husband smokes, so there is smoke at home. And we live near a factory so there are fumes also sometimes. I asked him to stop many times.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Does your husband smoke? How much does he smoke — do you know?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: He smokes a pack a day doctor. I keep telling him, especially now with the baby. And sometimes the food outside also troubles me — I think it may be contaminated food too, because after eating out my stomach goes very bad.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Do you get nausea or vomiting with the stomach pain? How about diarrhoea?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Umm, nausea is ongoing doctor, almost non-stop these days. Diarrhoea is almost never but the upper epigastric pain is really troubling. I was taking acetaminophen for pain relief but the previous doctor said to stop it.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Good that you stopped acetaminophen — it can irritate the stomach. What tests did the previous doctor advise? Did you do any allergy panel or blood work?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: He advised allergy panel but I did not do it yet. He also mentioned something about vitamin B12 test but did not explain why. That is why I came to you for second opinion.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: The vitamin B12 test is very relevant — post-delivery many mothers become deficient, and low B12 deficiency can cause fatigue and worsen allergy symptoms. The fumes, smoke, and contaminated food exposures are all aggravating your immune response.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Based on your history, I believe you have seasonal allergic rhinitis with food sensitivity, and the epigastric and pancreas area pain suggests possible eosinophilic gastroenteritis triggered by your allergic response — this is an immunological condition.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Ahh, that sounds complicated doctor. So the allergy is affecting my stomach also? And the dry skin in winter — is that also related?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Yes, exactly. The dry skin is atopic dermatitis — all part of the same allergic march. Your immune system is overreacting to seasonal triggers, fumes, and food. Post-partum hormonal changes have made everything severe.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I am prescribing cetirizine once daily for the allergic rhinitis, pantoprazole for the epigastric pain, and vitamin B12 supplement tablets. Please do not take acetaminophen without consulting me — use cold compress for minor pain instead.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, I am breastfeeding — are these medicines safe for the baby? And how long will I need to take them?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Cetirizine is considered safe during breastfeeding but take it just after feeding to minimise transfer. Avoid all smoke and fumes completely — passive exposure is harmful for both you and the baby. Also avoid contaminated food and outside food until your gut inflammation settles.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: We will do vitamin B12 levels, complete blood count, serum IgE, and stool routine examination. Based on results, we may add an inhaled corticosteroid if the wheezing continues. I want to review you in three weeks.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Now let me do teach-back. Can you tell me — which medicine is for your allergy, which is for your stomach pain, and what must you avoid at home?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Okay doctor — cetirizine is for the allergy and sneezing, pantoprazole is for the epigastric and upper back pain, and vitamin B12 supplement for my deficiency. I must avoid smoke, fumes, and contaminated food. And no acetaminophen on my own.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Perfect, you have understood very well. Remember, this allergy has been ongoing for two years and it will take time to control fully. Keep the cramping pain diary and if the severe upper back or pancreas area pain comes again suddenly, come to emergency without waiting. Take care.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Come in, please sit down. Welcome.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Thank you doctor. I am coming here for the first time, I mean to you directly. I have diabetes and I was seeing another doctor before but I stopped going for many months now.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Okay, so you have diabetes. Are you on any medicines currently for that?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Umm, yes doctor, I was taking insulin injections before but after that incident I stopped everything. I cannot afford it now, the medicines are too costly.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I see. What main problem is bringing you here today? Any headache, dizziness, or something else bothering you?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, from long time I am having headache and dizziness. It is coming on and off, like some days it is very bad and some days it is okay.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any numbness or tingling in your hands or feet?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Ahh, yes doctor, that also is there. My feet and hands, I feel like pins and needles type tingling sensation. I did not know how to say this properly.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Did you ever have any episode like convulsions, shaking of the body, or you fell down suddenly?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: None of that doctor, no convulsions or falling. But about a week back I felt very spinning in my head and I had to hold the wall.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Okay. Do you drink alcohol? And do you smoke?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Smoking yes doctor, I am smoking 1 pack per day. And drinking, I used to take alcohol daily before, but now I have reduced it a little only.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any exposure to chemicals or paints at your workplace? Any contact with mercury or heavy metals?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Umm, doctor I work in a small factory. There is some chemical smell but I am not sure what all is there. Someone told me there could be mercury also in some materials we handle.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Alright. Have you done any blood tests recently like blood sugar fasting or HbA1c? Any MRI brain or nerve conduction study done before?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Negative doctor, nothing like that is done. I could not afford. The old doctor had suggested some tests but I never went back.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I see. Looking at everything — your uncontrolled diabetes, long history of smoking, alcohol use, and possible mercury exposure at work — you are showing signs of diabetic peripheral neuropathy affecting your hands and feet, plus your headache and dizziness may be due to hypertensive episodes from poorly managed diabetes.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, this neuropathy, is it very serious? I am worried because I cannot afford big big treatments.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: It is manageable if we control your blood sugar properly. First thing is we must restart your insulin. I will try to keep your medicines as affordable as possible. We will also need a blood sugar fasting, HbA1c, and a blood pressure check regularly.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, for the pain in my feet and the headache, is there any tablet you can give? Something not too costly?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Yes, I am prescribing tramadol for the burning pain in your feet, but only short term. I am also starting multivitamins — specifically B-complex — which will help the nerve tingling and numbness. These are available at government dispensary at low cost.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Please stop the alcohol completely — it is directly worsening your nerve damage. And cut down smoking also. If you have convulsions or sudden severe dizziness at any point, go to emergency immediately, do not wait.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor the alcohol, I will try to stop fully. And for the factory chemical exposure, should I be worried about that mercury?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Yes, that is a concern. I will refer you for a urine mercury level test. If confirmed, we may need to report it and get you shifted from that work area. Meanwhile, wear protective gloves and avoid direct contact. Come back in about a week with your blood test reports.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Thank you so much doctor, I will follow everything you said.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Good morning! Nice to see you again. How are you doing overall?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Good morning doctor. Yes, I am back again as you can see!

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: So tell me, what is troubling you after your C-section recovery? Any specific complaints today?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, yesterday I had this very sharp chest pain which really worried me. It was also throbbing near my sternum.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Okay. Were you also having any palpitations or shortness of breath along with this chest pain?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, I had palpitations also. My heart was just racing. But I should say, episodes like this happen almost never, so I was quite alarmed when it started yesterday.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Is the pain thin and radiating, or more localised to the chest wall? Any radiation to the left arm or jaw?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: It feels thin and throbbing, mostly in my chest. No radiation to the arm or jaw, thankfully. Also my blood pressure reading at home was 150 over 95.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I see. Any history of hypertension or cardiac disease in the family? And remind me, you had chickenpox previously, correct?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes, I had chickenpox a year ago as an adult, which was quite bad. My mother has hypertension. No other cardiac history in the family.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: And any known drug allergy? I want to confirm before I prescribe anything.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, I am allergic to aspirin. I get hives and bronchospasm with it. Also mildly allergic to penicillin.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Good that you mentioned that. Now, are you currently walking for exercise, or using e-cigarettes? And are you exposed to any fumes or pollution regularly?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: I do go for walking daily, about thirty minutes. I also use e-cigarettes daily, I know I should stop. The pollution in our area is quite bad and there is fumes from the traffic near my flat. I rarely get a mosquito bite at home thankfully but the outdoors are terrible.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Have you done any recent investigations? Any ECG or echocardiogram done after the C-section?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: I had a ECG done right after surgery which was normal. No echocardiogram has been done. I also did a complete blood count last month and my lipid profile was slightly elevated, the LDL was borderline.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any dizziness, sweating, or fainting episodes? What about ankle swelling?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: umm, dizziness happens hardly ever, maybe once in a while. No fainting at all. No ankle swelling either. The sweating was there yesterday during the episode only.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Based on all this, I think this is a case of hypertensive episode with associated tachycardia, possibly aggravated by your e-cigarettes use and pollution exposure. We also need to rule out costochondritis given the very sharp chest wall pain you described.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: That makes sense doctor. Should I be worried about any cardiac issue given the elevated blood pressure and my borderline lipid profile result?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: We will get a fresh ECG, a 2D echocardiogram, and a repeat lipid profile done today. I also want a thyroid function test since palpitations and elevated blood pressure can both be linked to thyroid dysfunction post-delivery.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Since you are allergic to aspirin, I am prescribing amlodipine 5 mg once a day for your blood pressure, and metoprolol 25 mg twice daily to control the palpitations and tachycardia. For the chest pain, take ibuprofen 400 mg with food if needed, since you are not allergic to that.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, are there any side effects I should watch out for with amlodipine or metoprolol? And should I stop walking until this settles?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: With amlodipine watch for ankle swelling or flushing. With metoprolol some patients get fatigue or bradycardia so do not stop suddenly. Continue your walking daily — that is actually helpful — but please stop the e-cigarettes completely. Also avoid fumes and heavy pollution as much as possible.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Alright doctor, I will follow all of this. Thank you so much, as always you have been very thorough!

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Welcome back. Please sit down comfortably. How are you feeling after the discharge?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, I am feeling a bit better but still not fully okay. The itching on my skin is still there and sore throat has come up after surgery.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Let me go through everything properly. When did the sore throat start and is there any swelling in the throat?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: It started about 10-15 days ago. There is some swelling I think, and the throat feels raw and scratchy.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Okay. Any rash, hives, or watery eyes? These can be signs of an allergic reaction.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, I do get watery eyes periodically, especially around noon when I am driving long stretches. And there is some rash on my forearms.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: You are a long-distance bus driver, so travel and roadside dust exposure can definitely trigger allergies. Have you noticed any particular pattern?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Ahh, yes doctor. When I am on the highway route with lots of travel through construction zones, the itching and sneezing get much worse.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any hair fall recently? And have you had any piles complaint or bleeding from the rectum?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, hair fall is there quite a lot after surgery. And umm, the piles was there before, some bleeding also, but after surgery it has reduced thankfully.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Good. Now regarding your sugar — your blood glucose was uncontrolled during admission. Are you taking your insulin and metformin regularly as prescribed?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, I try but my schedule is very irregular. Sometimes I eat around noon only after many hours of driving, and I forget to take the metformin. The insulin I skip when I am on the road.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: That is a serious concern. Tell me about your diet — what are you eating on these long trips?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: My diet is very bad doctor, I admit. Highway food mostly — oily, heavy meals. Very little vegetables or home-cooked food. And my eating timing is all over the place.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Do you smoke, use vaping, or take any substances like heroin or alcohol?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, I smoke half a pack a day. I started vaping thinking it was safer. No heroin or anything like that, I am not into that at all.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Have you done your follow-up cystoscopy yet? It was advised before discharge for your urinary complaints.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Umm, no doctor, not yet. I was planning to do the cystoscopy this week. I also do some walking — about 1 hour daily — as the doctor suggested.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Based on everything, you have allergic rhinitis with urticaria triggered mainly by travel-related dust exposure. The uncontrolled diabetes is worsening your immune response and delaying recovery.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: So the sore throat and hair fall are also related to the sugar problem, doctor?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Partly yes. Uncontrolled diabetes reduces immunity and can cause hair fall, slow wound healing, and make throat infections worse. You must fix your diet and medication schedule urgently, even on driving days.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I am prescribing cetirizine 10mg once at night for allergy, betamethasone cream for the rash on your forearms, povidone iodine gargles for the sore throat, and we are adjusting your insulin dose. Please also get a HbA1c and total IgE done this week.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, should I stop vaping completely? And is the allergy going to affect my driving?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Yes, stop vaping and smoking immediately — both are triggering your sore throat and urticaria. The cetirizine can cause drowsiness, so take it only at night and never before driving. And please schedule the cystoscopy without further delay.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Understood doctor, thank you so much. I will follow everything properly this time.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Good morning, please come in and have a seat. Is this your first time at our clinic?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Good morning doctor, yes, my company has sent me for this health check. I am a postman, so they do yearly screening now.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Alright, understood. Any particular complaints bothering you, or is this purely routine?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Actually doctor, every morning I am feeling very nauseous and my eyes look a little yellow sometimes. I thought it was nothing major.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Yellowing of the eyes and nausea — how long has this been going on?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Umm, it comes and goes periodically, doctor. But the yellow tinge I first noticed somewhere in 2024. I did not pay much attention at that time.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any abdominal pain or bloating in the upper abdomen? And any itching on the skin?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes, there is some dull aching discomfort on the right side of my abdomen. Itching is not at all, no such thing.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Have you had any liver disease before, or any old injury to the abdomen?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: There was one old injury to my stomach area two years ago — I was delivering parcels and fell off my cycle. They did some scan at that time but said nothing serious.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I see. Now, do you drink — alcohol, beer, anything like that? Please be honest, it helps with diagnosis.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Ahh, occasionally doctor. Maybe a beer or two after meals in the evening, but nothing heavy. Just to relax after the route.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any recreational drugs use — even occasionally?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Not at all, doctor, nothing like that. I only drink coffee quite regularly, after meals mostly, sometimes three or four cups a day.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any chance of someone at school or close contact having jaundice or hepatitis when you were young?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, I remember there was someone at school who had jaundice, but that was long back. I do take some herbal liver tonic drops I bought from the ayurvedic shop. Been taking that for a while.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Alright. I want to do a liver function test, a hepatitis B surface antigen, and a hepatitis C antibody test. Also, let us do an abdominal ultrasound. Can you give a blood sample today?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, I can do it today. I had a liver ultrasound done two years ago after the fall but I do not have those reports now.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Based on your jaundice, periodic nausea, right upper quadrant discomfort, and the history of alcohol use, I suspect this is a case of fatty liver disease with possible jaundice. We will confirm with the tests, but this is the working diagnosis.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Fatty liver, doctor? But I am only having beer sometimes, not like every day. Can those herbal drops also cause any problem to the liver?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Yes, unfortunately some unregulated herbal liver tonics can themselves cause liver damage — it is called herb-induced hepatotoxicity. Even moderate alcohol intake combined with these can stress the liver significantly.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I am stopping the herbal tonic immediately. I am prescribing ursodeoxycholic acid 300 mg twice daily to protect your liver, and vitamin E 400 IU once a day as an antioxidant. If the liver function test shows infection, we may add antiviral therapy.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Should I completely stop beer and coffee also, doctor? And can I continue working my delivery route?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Yes, alcohol must be stopped completely — even one beer can worsen liver inflammation. Coffee in moderation is actually fine, some research shows benefit for the liver. Avoid heavy abdomen strain and dehydration on your route. Come back in four weeks with all blood reports.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Okay doctor, I will follow all of this. Thank you for explaining so clearly.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Good morning. Please sit. I see you have been referred back from the higher centre. What is your occupation?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Good morning doctor. I am long-distance bus driver only.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Alright. Tell me, what problems are you having now? Any irregular periods or discharge still continuing?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, the discharge is stopped now, but two weeks ago I am getting bleeding from down side also bloody discharge is coming again, comes and goes only.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I see. Any pain in the navel area or lower abdomen? Any fever or weight loss?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Umm, yes doctor, there is dull ache near my navel area occasionally. Fever is also coming, and I am losing weight loss also.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any cough or breathlessness? Any pain in the chest or bones?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, cough is there since 2024. Chest is also paining occasionally. My bones also giving dull ache sometimes.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Do you have any past history of past surgery or hepatitis or any fracture?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, I had fracture in my right leg three years back and past surgery for that only. Hepatitis was also detected in 2024.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any exposure to sick contact at work, or any factory fumes, or mosquito bite related illness recently?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Ahh, doctor, I am driving long routes only, so sometimes sick contact is there in the bus passengers. No factory exposure. Mosquito bite is there but I did not get malaria I think.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Do you smoke? How many cigarettes?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor I am smoking 10 cigarettes a day, every morning I am having first one. Before I was smoking two packs a day but now reduced only.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any recreational drugs or alcohol use?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: No doctor, recreational drugs I never took. Alcohol also I stopped long back.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: What medicines were they giving at the higher centre? Were you taking any for thyroid or blood pressure?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor they gave me levothyroxine for thyroid and lisinopril for blood pressure. LFT was also done there but report I am not having now.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Based on your cough, weight loss, fever, bone pain, gynaecological symptoms, and history of hepatitis, I am suspecting tuberculosis — possibly involving the genital tract as well as the chest.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, tuberculosis? That is dangerous? What tests are needed?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: We need to confirm with proper investigations. I am sending you for sputum culture, CBNAAT, repeat LFT, pelvic ultrasound, and chest X-ray urgently. The bloody discharge also needs endometrial biopsy.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, I have to drive bus also. Can I continue driving? Any problem with lisinopril and levothyroxine I am already taking?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Please avoid long-distance driving until investigation results come. The fatigue and dizziness that may come with tuberculosis treatment and your ongoing weight loss make it risky. Continue your current levothyroxine and lisinopril as before, do not stop them.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: For now, I am adding iron supplements for your anaemia and vitamin D3 for the bone pain. Once tuberculosis is confirmed, we will start the full anti-tubercular therapy course.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Thank you doctor, I will do all tests and come back next week.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Ah, long time no see! Where have you been disappearing to?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Sorry doctor, I was busy with factory work. Missed coming here for many months.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Alright, no problem. Now tell me, what is bothering you today? Any itching or rash still?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, the itching on my skin is still there, and now there is a rash spreading also. It started when I was younger but it has gotten worse since I joined the factory.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Where exactly is the rash? On your back, chest, or any other area?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Mainly on my back and also near my inner thighs. Umm, and there is some area near the rectum also, feels numb sometimes and very itchy.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I see. Any scaling or discharge from the rash area? Does the itching happen very often?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: There is some flaky scaling yes. The bad itching is almost never in daytime but gets bad at night.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Are there any dogs or other animals at home or in your workplace?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes, there are stray dogs near the factory gate. I sometimes feed them. My hands touch them regularly.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: What kind of work exactly do you do in the factory? Are you exposed to any chemicals or dust?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: I work near the chemical mixing section. There is lot of chemical fume and metal dust around. No proper mask they give us.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Okay. Do you swim anywhere, like ponds or public pools?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Ahh, I used to do swimming in the local pond when I was a child, but nah, stopped that now. Not going near water bodies anymore.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: What about your diet — are you vegetarian? And I need to ask — are you taking any alcohol?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: I am vegetarian mostly. About alcohol — I was drinking before, but stopped it six months back. The seniors in factory used to give it. I should not have taken.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Good that you stopped. Any back pain near the spine area? Any abdominal pain near the pancreas region — like upper abdomen?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Nah, not much pain in the spine. But yes, sometimes a dull ache in the upper abdomen — I thought it was just gas trouble. The pancreas area I don't know where that is exactly.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Based on the rash, scaling, and itching pattern — especially near the inner thighs and rectum — along with the animal contact and moisture exposure, this looks like a fungal infection. The numbness near the rectum and the spine symptoms need more investigation though.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, any serious tests needed? I am worried about what you said about the spine and the numbness.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: We will do a DEXA scan to check your bone and spine density — given the past alcohol use at a young age. A spinal tap may be needed if the numb feeling worsens. Also I am sending you for bronchoscopy to check your lungs given the chemical fume exposure at work.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: That bronchoscopy — is it painful doctor? And what about the fungal infection on my skin?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: The bronchoscopy is done with mild sedation, you will not feel much. For the fungal infection, I am prescribing clotrimazole cream to apply twice a day on the affected skin areas, and fluconazole tablet once a week for four weeks. For the itching, take cetirizine at night.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Should I avoid anything? Can I continue the factory work doctor?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Avoid contact with stray dogs and keep your skin dry and clean. Use a proper mask at work to reduce chemical fume inhalation. Strictly no alcohol — your age plus past use puts your liver and bones at risk. Come for follow-up after two weeks and we will review the test results including the DEXA scan.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Welcome back. Good to see you up and about. How are you feeling after the hospital discharge?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, I was discharged a week ago but I am still not feeling fully okay. My body is feeling very weak and I keep getting tiredness even when I am just sitting.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I see. Are you having any breathlessness or chest tightness? Any cough remaining?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: The cough is less frequent now doctor, not like before. But sometimes breathlessness comes when I climb stairs, twice a week maybe.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any problem in the mouth? Like sores or dryness? What about your scalp — any itching or hair fall?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, my mouth feels very dry many times, and my scalp is itching a lot since last few weeks. Also some hair fall is there but I thought it is normal.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: These can be post-viral effects. Are you getting sleep disturbance or anxiety at night? You have 12-hour shifts as a security guard, correct?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, the sleep is very bad. I am feeling anxiety type thing at night, my chest feels tight but doctor I do not know the proper name for this feeling. I do night duty also so sleeping in daytime is very difficult.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Are you still smoking? You had told me you were smoking earlier.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Earlier I used to do 10 cigarettes a day, doctor. But after the hospital I have cut down to 5 cigarettes only. Trying to stop fully but it is very hard.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Good that you are reducing. Any heat exposure at your post? You said you stand outside? Any pollution from traffic or dust?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, my post is on the main road so there is a lot of pollution and during daytime the heat is very bad. Also at my home my neighbour has cats and I go there sometimes, my nose starts running immediately.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any known allergy to any medicine? Any medicine that has caused a reaction before?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, some strong allergy to one tablet called tramadol — I took it once for back pain and I got vomiting and rash all over. So I never take it now.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Noted, I have marked tramadol as a clear allergy. Based on your history and the symptoms continuing over a year of repeated infections and now post-COVID recovery, this pattern looks like long COVID with post-viral fatigue, anxiety, and possible allergic rhinitis triggered by cats and pollution.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, this long COVID — is it something very serious? I did not understand fully in hospital also. Will it go away on its own?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: It can take time but with proper rest, reduced smoking, avoiding heat and pollution, and treatment, most patients recover well. Your night shifts are making the fatigue worse — if possible, try to get a daytime posting for a few weeks.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: I will try doctor, my supervisor may allow it. What about the tests you mentioned last time?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I want to run a TSH test to check your thyroid since hair fall and tiredness can come from that. Also a stool test because your stomach upset after discharge is not fully resolved. These two tests are important.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, one more thing — I am getting headache in the head top area almost never — only once in many days — but it is very sharp when it comes. Is that dangerous?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: That sharp headache at the scalp and head top is most likely tension-related because of your sleep disturbance and long shifts. As your anxiety and sleep improve, it should reduce. Watch it for now.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: For the sleep disturbance and anxiety, I am prescribing a low dose of alprazolam — take it only at bedtime, not more than prescribed. For the scalp itching I will give an antifungal dandruff shampoo and also a short course of antihistamine tablet for the allergic rhinitis from the cats.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, this alprazolam — I have heard it is a habit-forming medicine. Should I be worried? And can I take it during my night duty shift?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Very good question. Yes, alprazolam can cause dependence if taken for long. That is why I am giving only a small dose for short time. Do not take it during your shift — only at bedtime when you are at home, as it will cause drowsiness. Also avoid smoking and alcohol while on this tablet. Come back in two weeks after your TSH and stool test reports are ready.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Okay doctor, I will follow everything. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Hello, please come in and sit down. No need to be nervous.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Thank you doctor. I am having irregular periods and discharge from lower abdomen area since last four months. Also feeling restless periodically.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I see. Is the discharge thick or thin? Any pain in the lower abdomen?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, it is thick and hot feeling when coming out. Pain is also there twice a day sometimes. And my head is also paining once in a while.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any history of bleeding disorders or high blood pressure in yourself or family?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: My mother had high blood pressure doctor. Me, I had bleeding disorders from childhood — periods were always heavy and long even as a young girl.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any hoarseness in your voice, or swelling on your lips or head area?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Umm, yes doctor, hoarseness is there since last two weeks. And lips are sometimes swollen. I thought it was from a mosquito bite only.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Are you currently taking any medicines on your own for the pain or discharge?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, I am currently using pantoprazole for gas and stomach burning. I bought it from medical shop only. And I was taking some vitamin tablets but those I am no longer taking since money was finishing.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Do you chew tobacco or use any recreational drugs? And how much screen time do you have in a day?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Ahh, I was doing chewing tobacco before but stopped. Recreational drugs — no doctor, never. Screen time is very high, I watch phone late at night always. I also take 2 drinks a week sometimes at employer's parties.
