utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Has anyone prescribed you sertraline or an inhaler before for your restlessness or breathlessness?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, one doctor gave sertraline six months back for anxiety but I stopped on my own. Inhaler was given last year for wheezing but I am no longer using it.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Based on your symptoms — the irregular periods, discharge, and your history — I suspect you have PCOS and possibly fibroids as well. The hoarseness and lips swelling also need investigation.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, what is this fibroids — I am not understanding. Is it serious?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Fibroids are non-cancerous growths in the lower abdomen area of the uterus. They can cause heavy bleeding and pain. We will confirm with tests. I am ordering a complete blood count, a stool test, and a BUN today.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Okay doctor. What about my restlessness and head paining? Should I continue pantoprazole?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Stop the pantoprazole on your own — I will re-prescribe if needed after tests. For your restlessness and anxiety, I am restarting sertraline at low dose. Also restart the inhaler for wheezing as it was prescribed for a reason.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Please stop chewing tobacco completely — it worsens hoarseness. Reduce your screen time at night as it is making your restlessness worse. And limit the 2 drinks a week also.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, the discharge which is thick and hot — any cream or something for that also?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: We will treat after the complete blood count result comes. Do not self-medicate for that. Now, I want to do teach-back — can you tell me what tests I have ordered for you today?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Ahh, you told complete blood count, stool test, and BUN. And medicines are sertraline and inhaler, and stop pantoprazole on my own.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Very good, that is correct. One more thing — if swelling on your lips increases suddenly or you feel breathlessness after any mosquito bite or food, come to emergency immediately. Allergic swelling can be dangerous.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Thank you so much doctor, I will do all tests and come back. God bless you.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Good morning, please sit down. What brings you here today?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, recently I am having very high fever. It is coming sometimes very strong, sudden onset also.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: How many days has this fever been going on, and is there any headache or body ache?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Five days, doctor. body ache is very bad. And two times I am feeling like fainting, very dizzy also.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any rash on skin or bleeding from nose or gums?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: I doubt it doctor, no rash I see. But stomach is paining, and I am having constipation also since three days.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Have you been going to any crowded places like market or festival recently?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, I am working construction, many people around. And I was also at crowded places for family function last week.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any exposure to pet dander or animals at home? And what about cold weather exposure — any cough or sneezing?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: No pets at home doctor. Cough is little bit there but dry only. I am working outside so cold weather every morning.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Do you smoke or take any marijuana? Any stress or exercise routine?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Smoking I am quit now but before I was chain smoker. Marijuana I take daily doctor, little only. Exercise — no time, stress is very much because my wife also sick at home.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I see. Any past history of stone problem or typhoid before?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, stone in kidney was there two years back. Typhoid I don't know, never tested before.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any nausea or vomiting? And how is the appetite — eating properly?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Vomiting two times happened doctor. Appetite is very less, food not going down properly. Weakness also very much.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Based on the step-ladder pattern fever, constipation, fainting, and weakness with crowded places exposure, this presentation is strongly suggestive of typhoid fever. We must also rule out dengue.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, typhoid serious? My wife also having fever at home, I am caring for her also.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: It is manageable if treated properly. I am ordering blood culture, dengue NS1 antigen test, and Widal test first. Regarding your stone history, I may need cystoscopy later if urinary symptoms appear.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, MRI also needed? Someone told me to do MRI for the fainting.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: MRI is not needed right now — the fainting is most likely from dehydration and high fever. Focus on the infectious workup first and maintain good oral fluids. The marijuana use must stop as it is lowering your immunity.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Okay doctor. One more thing — chest is also little paining sometimes, dull ache only.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: That may be from cough and dehydration. I am prescribing azithromycin 500 mg daily for seven days, paracetamol for fever, and oral rehydration salts to take daily until reports come.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Avoid crowded places completely, maintain hand hygiene, drink only boiled water, and please stop the marijuana. Report immediately if fainting happens again or bleeding starts.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Thank you doctor, I will do all tests today itself.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Come in, come in. Please sit down carefully.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor... uh, it is still paining below the stomach. Since last week it became very sharp.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Okay, let me understand. You had surgery recently for the ectopic pregnancy, correct? Were there any bleeding episodes after discharge?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Umm... nope, no big bleeding. But the paining in the lower abdomen is three times a week, coming and going.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any fever or vomiting also?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Vomiting... no vomiting. But nausea is there every other day. Fever also came once, low-grade.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Now, I see in the notes your case was initially misdiagnosed as a fibroid. Were you taking any medicines at that time?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes, they gave me something... a cough syrup for the cough I had, and some probiotics. But I am not taking those now.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Alright. You are a truck driver, yes? Any tick bite history during your routes, especially forest areas?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Ahh... yes doctor, I think there was a tick bite on my leg for two years back I was having some rash also after that. Nobody checked it properly.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Okay. Do you drink alcohol?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Umm, yes doctor. alcohol I am taking for 20 years. Being a driver, long trips, you know how it is.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any running or physical activity?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: I do running 1 hour daily whenever I am home. But since surgery I stopped.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any ringing in ears or hearing difficulty recently?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes... umm, ringing sound in the ears is there. No contact with any loud machines recently though.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: We need to run a hearing test and also a AST blood test to check your liver given the long alcohol history for 20 years.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, why is the ear ringing coming? Is it related to the surgery?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Based on the tick bite history, the rash two years ago, and now the hearing loss and joint pain pattern, this looks like a case of Lyme disease that was missed earlier. The pelvic pain post-surgery is a separate post-operative complication.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Lyme disease? I never heard of this, doctor. Is it serious?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: It is treatable but needs prompt attention. The AST test will tell us if the liver is affected. Also the hearing test results will guide us. Meanwhile, please take the probiotics after meals to support gut recovery from the surgery.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I am prescribing doxycycline 100 mg twice daily for the Lyme disease, and paracetamol for the pelvic pain as needed. Do not self-medicate with that cough syrup again.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Okay doctor. Can I resume running 1 hour daily? And what about the alcohol?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Absolutely no alcohol while on doxycycline — it will stress the liver further. No running for at least four weeks post-surgery. The post-operative pain in the lower abdomen will worsen with exertion.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Understood doctor. One more thing — my back is also paining constantly since the surgery, maybe from lying in one position.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: That is expected post-operative muscle stiffness. Come back after your AST and hearing test reports are ready, and we will reassess the back pain and overall recovery then.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Good morning. Please sit down comfortably.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Good morning doctor sahib. I am coming for my yearly check-up only. I am working at construction site near the city.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Alright. Any specific complaints today, or is it just a routine check?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, few weeks now I have itching on my skin, intermittently it is happening. And some rash also coming on my arms.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Is the rash spreading to the chest or back area also? Any redness or scaling on the skin?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, some redness is there on the chest also. The itching is very bad in groin area also, I am feeling shy to say.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: No need to feel shy, this is normal in clinic. Any discharge from the skin or blisters forming?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: No doctor, no blisters. But skin is becoming flaky and dry near the groin. Also I am having sneezing several times in the morning.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Are you exposed to any chemicals at the site? Any asbestos handling? Do you have any cats or animals at home?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Umm, yes doctor, at site we are handling old building materials, asbestos also sometimes. At home my neighbour has cats, they are coming inside my room also.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I see. Now tell me, do you alcohol drink regularly? Any other substances you are taking?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, I will be honest. I am taking alcohol every evening. And I am smoking also, two packs a day almost. Previously I had some other substance problems also but now that is stopped.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Good that you are honest with me. Do you get confusion or dizziness sometimes? Any trembling of hands?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Ahh, yes doctor, sometimes confusion is coming in the morning, head is not clear. Hands are also trembling a little.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any past history? I see from your old records there was a stone problem and a cholecystectomy done. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, stone was there in my gallbladder, then cholecystectomy operation was done two years back. After that I am okay only from that side.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Alright. Today your BP reading is showing hypertension. Are you doing any exercise? Any walking regularly?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: No doctor, no walking or exercise. Work is very heavy at site so after coming home I am just resting. The hypertension problem is new, I did not know.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Based on the rash, itching, and flaky skin in the groin and arms, this is a case of fungal infection. The sneezing is likely allergic rhinitis from the cats. And you have early hypertension which needs attention.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, the fungal infection — it is coming because of site work or because of the cats?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Both can be contributing — the sweating and asbestos dust at work weakens the skin barrier, and the cats can carry fungal spores. The alcohol use is also reducing your immunity.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I am prescribing clotrimazole cream to apply on the affected skin twice daily, fluconazole tablet once a week for one month, and cetirizine tablet for the sneezing at night. For your hypertension, I am starting amlodipine 5 mg once daily.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: You must reduce alcohol immediately — it is worsening your hypertension and the confusion you are feeling. Stop keeping the cats inside your room and wear proper gloves when handling asbestos at site. Start walking at least thirty minutes every day.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I am ordering a liver function test, complete blood count, skin scraping KOH test to confirm the fungal infection, and a blood pressure monitoring chart for two weeks. Please come back with the reports.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Thank you doctor, I will do all the tests and come back. I will try to reduce alcohol also slowly.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Come in, come in. Good to see you again. How is the railway job treating you these days?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Ahh, same as always doctor, long shifts and tired feet. But I am managing.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Alright, it has been three months since your last visit. Tell me, how has your cough and breathlessness been?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, the cough is still there. It is dry and sometimes so intense that I cannot even talk. I have had it countless times during the day.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Is the breathlessness also present, or just the cough? Any wheezing sound from the chest?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Umm, yes doctor, wheezing is also coming. The breathlessness is unbearable when I climb even one flight of stairs. My chest feels very tight.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: You used to smoke, correct? Are you still smoking 5 cigarettes a day like before?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Correct doctor, I smoked for many years, but it is not anymore. I stopped three months back after you warned me.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Good. Now, at your workplace, are you exposed to any pesticides or chemical fumes along the railway tracks?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Uh-huh, doctor, actually they do spray pesticides near the tracks regularly. I am standing there daily for duty.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I see. Any exposure to animals like dogs, or was there any exposure at school — like someone at school who had a respiratory illness? I am trying to trace the origin.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Ahh, yes, we had dogs at home when I was a child. And yes, there was someone at school who had coughing fits all the time, we used to sit together.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Are you currently taking any medicines? I remember prescribing pantoprazole and clopidogrel last time. Are you taking those regularly?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Uh-huh, I am taking both doctor. Sometimes I also take painkillers on my own when the back is paining after long shifts.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Please stop those painkillers without prescription — they can irritate the stomach lining badly, especially with clopidogrel on board. Now, what about alcohol? You had a history of heavy use before.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, I have reduced a lot. Earlier it was daily drinking, but now I drink only on weekends. My gastric pain was also coming because of that only.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Based on everything — your many years of smoking history, the dry and intense cough, the wheezing, the breathlessness on exertion, and the ongoing pesticides exposure — I am diagnosing you with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, or COPD. This is also being worsened by your alcohol abuse history reducing your immunity.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, COPD — is it very serious? Can it be cured fully?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: It cannot be fully reversed, but it can be very well controlled. The most important steps are complete avoidance of pesticides, zero smoking, and reducing alcohol to nil. I will also order a lipid profile today since clopidogrel is ongoing, and also an eye exam as unbearable coughing fits can sometimes raise pressure in the eyes.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: So doctor, what medicines should I take now for the wheezing and breathlessness? Should I be using an inhaler?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Yes, I am prescribing a salbutamol inhaler for immediate breathlessness relief, and a budesonide inhaler to be used daily as a maintenance dose. I am also adding montelukast tablets to help with the wheezing. Continue your pantoprazole as it will protect the stomach lining.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Umm, doctor, any special diet or activities I should be avoiding? My work involves standing in open areas near the tracks.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: You must wear a proper dust and chemical mask when near the tracks, especially during pesticides spraying. Avoid cold air directly hitting the chest during night shifts. No alcohol at all — it worsens airway inflammation. Drink plenty of warm water to loosen any secretions.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, should I get the lipid profile and eye exam done today itself or come back separately?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Get the lipid profile blood test done today from our lab before you leave. For the eye exam, I am referring you to the ophthalmology department — take an appointment for next week. Come back to me in six weeks with both reports and we will review your COPD progress at that time.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Arrey, how are you doing? How is the family, everything okay at home?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: All fine doctor, kids are good, wife also. Shop is a bit slow these days but managing.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Good good. And how is your sports going? Still playing on Sundays?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Ahh, not really doctor, for a year now I have not played properly. This stomach pain is giving too much trouble, daily it is bothering me.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Okay, let us get into that. Where exactly is the pain — is it in the lower part of the stomach or more near the ribcage?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Mostly near the ribcage area doctor, and sometimes I feel a tightness going up to my jaw also. Every morning it is bad, especially now with this weather change.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: And are you also feeling weak or any acidity or bloating?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, feeling weak is there. And acidity and gas are very bad, especially in 2024 it got worse. Before surgery also — pre-operative phase — I had similar complaints.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any nausea or vomiting along with this? Any burning sensation in the chest?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Umm, nausea sometimes is there doctor, but vomiting — no. The burning in the chest is there daily, more after eating.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any public transport travel or long sitting hours at the machine? That posture can worsen acidity you know.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, I sit hunched over the sewing machine for hours. And I travel by public transport — standing all the way, very tiring.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: And are you drinking alcohol? If yes, how often?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Only 2 drinks a week doctor, nothing more. And I tried those e-cigarettes for some time but stopped now.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Good that you stopped the e-cigarettes. Now tell me, is there any UTI complaint — burning during urination or anything like that? Sometimes these things come together.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Ahh, no, UTI — no one in my family has mentioned that to me and I myself have no such complaint doctor.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Okay. And this seasonal worsening — is there any sick child at home or someone at school in the family who may have passed something on?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Hmm, could be doctor, my son's teacher — someone at school — was unwell last month. Son had mild cold also.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Alright. Based on everything, this is a clear case of gastroesophageal reflux disease with functional dyspepsia. The jaw tightness you mentioned is referred discomfort from the ribcage area — classic in severe acidity.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, that jaw thing was worrying me. And what about these eye drops that were prescribed during discharge — are they still needed?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: The eye drops were for the minor post-operative dryness — continue them for now, we will review at next visit. But the main focus right now is your gastrointestinal issue and the weakness.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, during the hospital stay they had given me some breathing support also — albuterol nebulization. Should I continue that at home?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: For now, keep albuterol only if you feel breathlessness. For the acidity, I am prescribing pantoprazole 40 mg daily before breakfast, and domperidone for the nausea and bloating. Also take antacid syrup after meals.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Avoid drinking completely for now, reduce spicy food, and do not hunch over the sewing machine without breaks. We will do a upper GI endoscopy and H. pylori breath test next week to rule out deeper issues.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Understood doctor, I will follow everything. The lower part pain — is that also from the same acidity issue? It is dull and continuous most of the time.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Come in, come in. So this is the little one? What is your name, beta?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: His name is Arjun, doctor. I am his mother. We are sorry we did not come for so long.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: That is okay, but it has been many months. What problem is he having now?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, recently he is saying his chest is paining and his heart is going very fast, like dhad-dhad. I got scared so I came.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Okay, the chest pain and the fast heartbeat — is it happening all the time or only sometimes?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: It is happening all the time doctor, almost every few hours. And two days ago he also said his temple was paining very badly, here on the side of his head.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I see. Any dizziness or fainting also? Did he fall down at any point?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Umm, yes doctor, one time he felt like the room was spinning. He did not fall but he had to sit down. And he is sweating a lot also.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Last time we had checked his blood pressure and it was high. Was he taking his medicines regularly?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor honestly no, he was not taking regularly. I used to forget and he also used to say the tablet is bitter. So we skipped many days, I am sorry.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Okay, let me check him now. Arjun, does it pain here on the chest? Does your elbow or arm also pain when the chest is paining?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, he said the elbow also hurts once in a while when the chest pain is bad. I did not know that was related.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any family history of bleeding disorders, jaundice, or rheumatoid arthritis in the family?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Umm, no doctor, nothing like that I know of. His grandfather has sugar problem but that is all.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Does Arjun drink a lot of caffeine — cola drinks, energy drinks, tea?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Ahh, yes doctor, he drinks cold drinks and packaged juice once in a while but at school sometimes more. And he has a very sedentary lifestyle — he sits and plays on tablet all day, no outdoor playing at all.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any recent hospital visit for any infection or illness? And any contact with dogs or other animals?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: We had one hospital visit last month for fever. And yes, our neighbor has dogs, he plays with them all the time.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Okay, looking at everything — the chest pain, palpitations, headache at the temple, and the missed medicines — this child has hypertensive urgency with possible cardiac arrhythmia. His blood pressure right now is very high and needs to be controlled urgently.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, hyper — what is that? Is it dangerous? What does that mean for a child?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: It means the pressure of blood in his body is too high, like a pipe with too much pressure. Because he missed his medicines, it has gone up again and is causing the chest pain, fast heartbeat, and headache at the temple.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I am prescribing amlodipine 2.5 mg once a day and atenolol 25 mg half tablet in the morning. Do not miss even one dose. Also giving aspirin low dose for now.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Stop all caffeine — no cold drinks, no packaged juice. He must not have a sedentary lifestyle anymore. Light walking every day is must. No dogs contact until we rule out any infection trigger.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I am also ordering ECG, echocardiogram, complete blood count, and renal function test today. We need to check why a child this age is having such persistently high blood pressure.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, I promise we will not miss medicines this time. We will do all the tests two days ago itself I was planning to come — I wish I had come sooner. Thank you doctor.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Please come in and have a seat. You have been referred back from the higher centre, correct?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, I am speaking on behalf of my mother-in-law. She is elderly and could not come herself today. The big hospital sent us back saying to continue treatment here.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Alright, tell me — what are the main complaints she is having right now? Any loose stools or fever?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, she has been having loose stools all the time over a year now. And her eyes are also giving trouble — they look wet and watery many times during the day.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I see. Is there any ear discharge or ear pain also? And what about malaria — has she had any such episode recently?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: She did have malaria over a year back, doctor. Regarding the ear discharge, yes, umm, it comes twice a week she says. The higher centre prescribed ear drops but she is not taking them regularly.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Why is she not using the ear drops? Any problem with them?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: She says they cause burning sensation inside the ear, so she stopped. Also doctor, she has a known drug allergy — she reacted badly to antibiotics once before.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Which antibiotics caused the reaction? And does she have any history of anxiety disorder or any psychiatric condition?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, she has had anxiety disorder from childhood. Regarding the antibiotic, no one in the family remembers the exact name — she just breaks into a rash when given any tablet from that group.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Understood. Has she been exposed to any sick contact at home, or any animal hair? We have to rule out allergic cause for the watery eyes.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Ahh, yes doctor — we do have a cat at home. So there is quite a bit of animal hair around. She also works near the kitchen all the time, so there is heat and smoke exposure as well.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Okay. What about her diet and physical activity? Is she vegetarian? And does she take any recreational drugs?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: She is strictly vegetarian for 10 years now, since she became more religious. Physical activity is very little — she barely walks around the house. No recreational drugs at all, doctor.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Has her vitamin D level been checked? Given her vegetarian diet and low physical activity, it may be very low.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Umm, the higher centre did do vitamin D test, doctor. The report says it is severely deficient. They also did some blood count and found anaemia. They gave steroids for a short course but she felt very uneasy after taking them.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Looking at everything — the wet watery eyes, animal hair exposure, heat exposure, and the recurring loose stools with anaemia — this appears to be a case of allergic conjunctivitis combined with irritable bowel syndrome on a background of anxiety disorder and vitamin D deficiency.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, can the anxiety disorder be causing the loose stools? She has been many times to the bathroom before any stressful event also.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Yes, absolutely — anxiety is a well-known trigger for irritable bowel syndrome. The gut and brain are closely connected, and her history from childhood of anxiety disorder is likely making the loose stools worse.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, she reacted to antibiotics before and felt bad on steroids — is it safe to give her new medicines? I am very worried.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Your concern is valid. We will avoid the antibiotic group that caused her rash and we will not repeat steroids. She should also reduce animal hair contact — keep the cat away from her eyes and face area. Avoiding direct heat from the kitchen stove will also help the eyes.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I am prescribing antihistamine eye drops for the allergic conjunctivitis — these are safe and will reduce the wet watery discharge. For the loose stools, she should start probiotics twice a week initially, and I am also prescribing vitamin D3 supplements for her deficiency. For the anaemia, start iron and folic acid tablets daily.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, should she also see someone for the anxiety disorder? And should we do any repeat vitamin D test after some time?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Yes, I will refer her to a psychiatrist for the anxiety. Increasing gentle physical activity like slow walking outdoors will also help both the anxiety and the vitamin D deficiency. Repeat vitamin D and haemoglobin after three months and come back with the reports.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Thank you so much doctor, I will make sure she follows everything properly this time.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Come in, come in. I have a packed schedule today, so let us get straight to it.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Thank you doctor. I went to another doctor and he said some things, so my parents wanted a second opinion.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Alright. What is the main problem you came with? Any weakness, dizziness, something like that?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Umm, yes doctor, weakness is there since a long time. Also lot of hair fall and sometimes I get shortness of breath also.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Is the shortness of breath on walking, on climbing stairs? When exactly does it come?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Mostly on climbing stairs. It comes around noon when I have PE class in school also. My scalp is also looking thin — the hair is becoming very thin and not thick like before.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any pale skin, yellowing of the eyes, or swelling on the legs?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Ahh, my mother says my face looks pale. No yellowing doctor. No swelling on legs.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: How long did you wait before coming? The other doctor saw you recently?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor I saw him only just now — like two days back. But the weakness and hair fall are there for months. We delayed coming for a long time.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: What did the previous doctor say? Did he do any tests?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: He did a complete blood count and said anaemia is there. He also mentioned something about fibroids but I got confused — I am a teenage boy, so my mother got worried and wanted second opinion.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Okay, I understand. Do you exercise regularly? And do you drink coffee or liquor?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: I do exercise sometimes. I drink coffee socially you know, with friends after school. No liquor doctor, I am not drinking that, not anymore — I tried once only.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any sick contact at home or school — anyone with jaundice or fever recently?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: No doctor, no sick contact that I know of. Nobody at home is sick.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: What is your diet like? Are you eating enough iron-rich foods, green vegetables, meat?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Honestly doctor, I am mostly eating junk food. Very less vegetables. My mother says I do not eat properly. I skip breakfast also sometimes.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Alright. Looking at your complete blood count report and your symptoms — hair fall, shortness of breath, weakness, pale skin — this is clearly iron deficiency anaemia with nutritional deficiency. The previous doctor was right. The fibroids mention must have been some confusion in communication — that does not apply here.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: So it is just a blood problem doctor? Nothing serious?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: It is iron deficiency anaemia — very common in teenagers with poor diet, but you must not ignore it. We will repeat serum ferritin and peripheral blood smear to confirm severity. Also cut down on that coffee — it reduces iron absorption.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I am prescribing ferrous sulphate tablet once daily after food, vitamin C tablet with it to help absorption, and a multivitamin syrup at night. Take these for at least three months.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Okay doctor. Should I stop exercise for now? And is there anything else to avoid?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: No, light exercise is fine. But avoid being a chain smoker type — I know you are young but some teenagers start early. Avoid coffee for at least one hour after taking ferrous sulphate. Eat iron-rich foods — spinach, eggs, chicken. Come back after one month with CBC and serum ferritin reports.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Thank you so much doctor. I will follow everything properly.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Good morning, please come in and sit. How can I help you today?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Good morning doctor. Actually it is not for me, my son is sick. He is having fever and diarrhoea since three days.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: How old is your son? Is the fever severe? And how many times loose motions in a day?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: He is seven years old doctor. The fever is quite severe, going up to 104 degrees. And the loose motions — countless times he is running to the toilet.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Is there any vomiting also? Any stomach pain near the lower part of the abdomen?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, vomiting also is there, once a week only but the stomach cramping near the lower part is there every day.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Have you given him any medicine already? Any antibiotics or other tablets on your own?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, I gave him antibiotics from the medical shop without prescription. The fever was there but then it was gone for one day and came back again.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Does your son have any history of urinary infection? Any burning or pain while passing urine?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Umm, yes doctor, he has been having urinary infection from childhood, it keeps coming back again and again.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I see. We will need to do an X-ray of the chest and also a urine culture to rule out any serious infection. Now tell me, what is your own occupation?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: I am a long-distance bus driver doctor. I drive interstate routes, sometimes 12 to 14 hours at a stretch.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Long stretches of sitting — do you have any back pain or leg pain? And I want to ask — do you get exposed to any chemicals or animal hair or dust during your routes?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Ahh, yes doctor, back pain is there every day. And sometimes we carry animal transport loads — so yes, there is animal hair exposure. At the bus depot also there are chemicals and fumes from the cleaning agents.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Do you have any cough? Is it productive? Any breathlessness?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, I have cough, it is productive with some yellowish phlegm. Breathlessness is not there much.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any past history of depression history or any mental health treatment? Do you drink alcohol?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, I had depression history a few years back, took some tablets for it. About alcohol, I take about 3 beers a day — after the long drives to relax only.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I see. Do you do any physical activity? Any cycling or walking regularly?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: I try doctor — cycling I do for 30 minutes daily when I am in town. Also some physical activity like stretching before driving.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Alright. For your son, this looks like a case of acute gastroenteritis with possible recurrent urinary infection complicating things. The productive cough you have along with the chemicals and animal hair exposure suggests occupational bronchitis for you — we will confirm with the X-ray and pulmonary function test.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, for my son — should I stop the antibiotics I was giving? And what about his urinary infection that is there from childhood?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Yes, stop those antibiotics immediately — self-medication is dangerous. For your son I am prescribing oral rehydration salts for the diarrhoea, paracetamol syrup for the fever, and once the urine culture result comes we will start proper targeted antibiotics. For your cough I am prescribing bronchodilator inhaler to use when needed.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Also, please reduce the alcohol — 3 beers a day is too much especially with your depression history. Reduce the chemical fume exposure at the depot by wearing a proper mask. Continue the cycling for 30 minutes daily, it is good for your back pain.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Thank you so much doctor, I will follow everything you said and bring my son for the tests tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Hello, come in, come in. How are you doing today?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Umm, doctor I am okay but not really okay. I am not able to sleep properly and my gums are also bothering me, and oh — I wanted to ask about that ultrasonography report too.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Okay, let us go one by one. First tell me about the not able to sleep problem — since when is this happening?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, since 2024 it has been bad. I wake up in the middle of the night three times a week at least, and then cannot go back to sleep.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I see. And do you remember — you had that bad viral episode. Was it around 2022 when you had that infection?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Ahh yes doctor, I had COVID in 2022 and then again something similar in 2024. That second time my jaundice also came back, you said.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Correct. Now this second episode — were you exposed to anything? Any fumes, chemical exposure, or did someone around you fall ill — like a coworker was sick?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Actually doctor my father works in a factory and he sometimes comes home smelling of fumes. Also one of my classmates was very sick before I got it. Oh wait, I also had a tick bite during a school trekking trip, I forgot to tell you that.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: That tick bite is important — did you notice any rash or fever soon after? And what about your gums — any bleeding there?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: I don't remember a rash but I did have fever doctor. The gums are slightly painful and they swell up intermittently. No major bleeding though.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any nausea or vomiting after every meal? Some post-viral cases show this pattern.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, nausea after every meal I am getting. And my wrist also pains sometimes — that is from an old injury actually.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Let us not mix things — the wrist pain from the old injury, has it changed in character recently or is it the same as before?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: It is the same doctor, no change. Umm, but I wanted to ask — the ultrasonography report that was done last month, what did it show?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: The ultrasonography report showed mild hepatomegaly, which fits with your post-viral picture. We also ran a T4 test to check your thyroid, which came back borderline low. We had arranged a biopsy of that small lump near the gums — that report is pending.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, I also do gym for 30 minutes daily and sometimes yoga also. My friend told me exercise will help my sleep. And I tried beer at a party — just 2 drinks a week these days.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: The gym and yoga are good, please continue. But the beer, even 2 drinks a week, is not acceptable at your age — especially with hepatomegaly showing on your scan. Please stop that completely.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Okay doctor, I will stop. Do you think all this is connected to the jaundice from before?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Yes, I don't think so it is a new separate disease — putting everything together, I believe this is a case of long post-viral sequelae with chronic fatigue, insomnia, and hepatomegaly. The tick bite exposure has been ruled out as a cause since the timing does not match.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: So what do I do for the not able to sleep problem doctor? It is really affecting my studies.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: For the insomnia, I am starting you on a low dose of lorazepam — only short term, you must not take it on your own without my guidance.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Okay. Will the lorazepam make me feel drowsy in the daytime also?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: It can cause some drowsiness initially, so take it only at night. Do not combine it with any beer or alcohol at all — that is very dangerous. We will review after four weeks.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Also I want you to repeat the T4 in six weeks and come back with the biopsy result for those gums. Any pain in the gums that becomes slightly painful more than usual, come immediately.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Okay doctor, thank you so much. I will keep all this in mind.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Arrey, Ramesh ji! Come come, sit down. Good to see you back. How are you feeling after the surgery?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor sahib, I am okay-okay. Slowly managing. Family is also asking about me.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Good good. Now tell me, any heavy bleeding from the wound site or near the pelvis area?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Umm, absent doctor, no bleeding like that. But I am having fatigue and breathlessness since 2024, when I had that COVID infection.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Yes, I remember you had COVID-19 last year. Is the breathlessness there at rest or only on walking?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Mostly on walking, doctor. And I am coughing twice a day, especially in the morning. Dry cough only, no sputum.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any chest pain in the chest or palpitations?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: I think so doctor, sometimes at night I feel heaviness in the chest. I work night shifts in the field so sleep is also very disturbed.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: You mentioned a family member was sick around the same time you had COVID — was it the same illness?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Ahh yes doctor, my wife also got fever. And around that time I was also getting fever from mosquito bite — we suspected dengue also at that time.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I see. Any lead or chemical exposure in your farming work? Pesticides, fertilizers?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: True, doctor, we do use pesticide sprays without proper protection. I have been doing this since I was young. No mask or gloves mostly.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: That is concerning. Do you drink alcohol?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Only on weekends doctor, not too much. And I used to smoke before but I stopped after the surgery.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Good that you stopped smoking. Did you do the pulmonary function test and chest X-ray I had asked last time?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, I got the chest X-ray done. Report says some fibrosis changes. The pulmonary function test was showing mild restriction.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Yes Ramesh ji, looking at your history of COVID-19, the fatigue, breathlessness, and the pulmonary function test findings, this is a case of post-COVID pulmonary fibrosis with long COVID syndrome.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, this long COVID syndrome — will it go away? I need to go back to farm work soon.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: It will take time, but with proper treatment and rest it does improve. The night shift work is making things worse — your sleep disturbance is slowing down recovery. Try to avoid pesticide spray work for now.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I am prescribing N-acetylcysteine tablet twice a day, montelukast at night for the coughing, and multivitamin supplement daily for the fatigue.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Okay doctor. Should I be worried about the pelvis area from the surgery side also?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: The pelvis site is healing well — watch for any heavy bleeding, swelling, or fever. If any of those appear, come immediately without waiting.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: The lead exposure you mentioned — should I do any blood test for that?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Good thinking. Let us do a blood lead level test and also a complete blood count to check for anemia. Long-term pesticide exposure combined with lead can affect your liver and kidneys also, so we will monitor carefully.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Thank you so much doctor. You always explain everything so nicely. I will follow your advice properly this time.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Good morning, Mr. Ramaiah. Please sit down, sit down. How are you feeling today?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Good morning doctor. Ahh, managing only. My grandson had his birthday yesterday, so I am a little tired.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I understand. Now, you have come for pre-operative clearance before your scheduled surgery, correct? Tell me what all complaints you have been having.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, my eyes have been looking very yellow last week, and my skin is also yellowish. itching is there all the time on my arms and stomach.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: That yellowing of eyes and skin is concerning. Any pain in the abdomen or dark urine also?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Umm, yes doctor, dark urine is there on and off. Actually doctor, I also wanted to ask you about my knee pain, it is paining all the time these days.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: We will come to your knee shortly. First tell me — any nausea, vomiting, or loss of appetite also?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, very bad loss of appetite is there. I have not eaten properly two weeks ago itself I stopped eating full meals. nausea is there countless times during the day.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Mr. Ramaiah, I need to ask you directly — do you drink alcohol? How much and how often?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Ahh, doctor, I used to drink 3 beers a day for many years, drinking daily I was. But not anymore, I stopped not too long ago. My wife forced me to stop.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any tick bite recently, or any hospital visit in the recent past? Any chance of mercury exposure through fish or work?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, I doubt it — I doubt it for the tick bite or mercury thing. But there was one hospital visit for my brother last week, I was helping him. Could that have caused something?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Possibly. Now tell me your past history — any previous surgeries or major illnesses?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, I had an appendectomy many years back, and then a hip replacement on my right side also. And I was told I had jaundice before also, maybe ten or twelve years back.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Have you ever taken diazepam or any other sedative medicines on your own — for anxiety or sleep problems?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Umm, doctor, I was taking diazepam on and off for my sleep problems without prescription. I have never fully stopped. I take it on and off.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Mr. Ramaiah, based on everything — the yellowing, dark urine, loss of appetite, and your long alcohol history — this looks like alcoholic fatty liver disease with possible hepatitis. The diazepam use is also damaging the liver.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, is it very serious? My grandson keeps telling me also. True, I have not been taking care at all.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: It is serious enough that we must clear this before your surgery. The liver function must be stable. You must stop alcohol completely — never again — and the diazepam must be tapered carefully under supervision, not stopped suddenly.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, I have had tremors in my hands countless times whenever I try to stop. What to do for that?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: For the tremors and withdrawal symptoms, I am prescribing a supervised taper of diazepam with a dose reduction plan. Also starting thiamine supplements and ursodeoxycholic acid for the liver.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: For pre-operative clearance, we need to run several tests today — HbA1c to check sugar status, creatinine for kidney function, X-ray of the chest, and full liver function panel.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, also my abdomen feels bloated and heavy all the time now. Is that related to the liver only?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Yes, that bloating and heaviness in the abdomen is likely ascites — fluid accumulation due to liver damage. Avoid alcohol entirely — never even one drink — avoid salty and fatty food, reduce strain on the abdomen, and come back once all HbA1c and creatinine results are available.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Thank you doctor. I will follow everything properly this time, I promise.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Welcome back. Good to see you up and about so soon after discharge.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Thank you doctor, but honestly I am still not feeling well. For two weeks now I have had this fatigue that is non-stop, and my joints are paining.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Yes, post-COVID sequelae can linger. Is there any hair loss on the scalp or any skin rash?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Ahh, yes doctor, still having clumps falling from my scalp. And my knees and wrists are giving me a lot of trouble. I am worried this could be a joint problem now.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Have you had any fracture or prior joint problem before this COVID episode?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, I had a fracture of the ankle about three years back, but the joints were fine otherwise. This new joint pain started only two weeks ago.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Understood. Any brain fog, breathlessness, or palpitations still there?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: The breathlessness has reduced, but brain fog is still there, doctor. And I have noticed this itching on my scalp and arms which is quite bothersome.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Was there any known sick contact? Any coworker was sick around you before you fell ill?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, definitely. My coworker was sick with COVID before me. We share a patrol vehicle. Also I do duty in a rural area, so sometimes exposure to dogs and stray animals is also there.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Good to know. Do you smoke or drink alcohol?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Umm, honestly doctor, I drink about 3 beers a day and have been doing so for 10 years. For smoking, roughly 5 cigarettes per day. I know it is bad.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I appreciate your honesty. Any weight gain, cold intolerance, or swelling on the neck? I want to rule out a thyroid problem.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Actually doctor, I have had some weight gain and I feel cold easily. I was reading online and was thinking the same thing — could this be a thyroid problem? I have been worried about it for few weeks now.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Based on what you are telling me — the persistent fatigue, hair loss from the scalp, joint pain, weight gain, and brain fog — this is most likely a case of post-COVID syndrome with possible secondary hypothyroidism.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, is the hypothyroidism caused by COVID itself? I have been reading that it can trigger thyroid problem.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: That is correct. COVID can trigger thyroiditis and worsen autoimmune conditions. The joint problem you are describing is also consistent with reactive arthritis, which we see post-viral.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: So what tests will you be ordering, doctor? Should I be doing a TSH and maybe a ANA panel?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Yes, we will do TSH, Free T4, ANA panel, CBC, ESR, and a CRP to check for inflammation. Also a liver function test given your alcohol intake for two years at this level.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Understood doctor. For the itching and scalp problem, can I take antihistamines on my own?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Yes, I am prescribing antihistamines — specifically cetirizine 10 mg once at night for the itching. Also I am starting you on ibuprofen 400 mg twice daily after food for the joint pain, and vitamin D3 supplement since your levels are likely low post-COVID.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, with my alcohol use, is ibuprofen safe? And should I worry about my liver?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: That is a very valid concern. Ibuprofen and alcohol together are hard on the stomach and liver, so you must cut down your intake significantly. If stomach pain or nausea comes, stop immediately and come back. Also, the smoking will delay your lung recovery post-COVID.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, what about the dogs I am exposed to in the rural area duty — should I be checking for leptospirosis or any other infection?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Good thinking. I will add a leptospira serology to your panel. Meanwhile wear proper footwear on duty and avoid direct contact with stray dogs as much as possible. Come back in ten days with your reports and we will reassess everything.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Hello, come in, come in. Please have a seat. Good to see you again.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Thank you doctor. I am here for my yearly check-up only.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Good. So how are you feeling overall? Any new complaints or paining anywhere?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, actually yesterday I noticed my eyes became a little yellow. And I am feeling fatigue often these days.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Yellowing of eyes — that is important. Any yellowing of skin also? Any nausea or vomiting?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Umm, yes doctor, skin is also slightly yellow I think. And nausea is there often, especially in the morning. No vomiting though.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any abdominal pain or dark urine? Any swelling of lymph nodes around neck or armpits?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, urine is dark colored, yes. And some mild abdominal pain on the right side. I did not notice any swelling of lymph nodes.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Okay. You work in a factory, correct? Tell me about your work — any mercury or chemical exposure there? Any heat stress at the workplace?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Ahh, yes doctor. I work in a mining unit. There is definitely heat exposure all day. And some chemicals also — but I am not sure if mercury is there specifically. They do not tell us workers about these things.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I see. Do you have any pets at home? Any contact with stray animals or contaminated water sources?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: We have pets doctor — two dogs at home. And the water supply in our area is not so clean, honestly.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Now tell me about your habits. Do you exercise or do physical activity regularly? And any recreational drugs or alcohol?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: I go to gym for exercise 3 times a week doctor. For alcohol, I take 2 drinks a week maximum — nothing more. No recreational drugs at all. But I do smoke — 1 pack per day.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any allergies to medications? And do you have any history of stone in the GB or previous operation?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, I had a previous operation for stone in the GB about two years back. And I have allergies to penicillin. I am not on any other medicines currently.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Are you taking any blood thinners or muscle building supplements for the gym? These can affect the liver.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: No doctor, I cannot afford those supplements. Financial situation is very tight — I am managing only basic food itself these days.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Understood. I will order some tests. We need liver function test, ultrasound abdomen, hepatitis B surface antigen, T3, and T4 also since fatigue can be thyroid-related.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, can we do only the most important ones? I am telling you honestly — money is very less right now. Please adjust accordingly.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I understand your situation. Based on the jaundice, dark urine, abdominal pain on the right side, and your work exposure, this looks like fatty liver combined with early hepatitis. We must rule out a serious liver infection.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, is it very serious? What should I do now?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Do not panic. I am prescribing ursodeoxycholic acid tablet twice daily for liver support, and ondansetron for the nausea. Avoid blood thinners and any painkillers without consulting me — they will worsen liver damage.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Most importantly — stop physical activity at the gym completely until liver values normalise. Reduce heat exposure at your workplace as much as possible. Avoid alcohol fully. And keep distance from pets till we rule out leptospirosis.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Okay doctor, I will follow everything. For the hepatitis B surface antigen and ultrasound abdomen — I will try to do it by next week. Thank you for understanding my situation.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Welcome back. Please sit down comfortably. How are you feeling after discharge?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, still not so good. The swelling on my legs and feet is constantly there, not reducing much. Few days ago it was very bad.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Is the swelling tingling or just puffy? Any breathlessness also?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Umm, yes doctor, tingling is there in the feet sometimes. And breathlessness is there nonstop when I climb even two steps.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any cramping in legs at night? And are you passing urine properly?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes, cramping is there at night, sometimes. Urine is less than before, very wet feeling overall, like body is full of water.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I see your creatinine from the hospital was very elevated. Did they do urine albumin and kidney ultrasound also?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, all were done. The kidney ultrasound showed some shrinkage they said. Urine albumin was also positive, heavy leakage they told.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Do you drink alcohol? Please be honest, it is important for your treatment.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Ahh, doctor... little bit only. Ongoing habit for many years, I will not lie. For 10 years I am having this habit. And I smoke also, around 5 cigarettes every day.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any chemicals or mine work exposure in your past job? These things damage kidneys also.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, I worked in a mine for nearly 20 years. Lot of chemicals exposure was there. Now I am retired only.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: You mentioned caring for a sick family member. Is there any stress affecting your sleep habits? Are you resting properly?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: My wife is very sick, doctor. She has tonsillitis and also gastritis constantly. She also has irregular periods. I am managing everything so my sleep habits are very disturbed, not sleeping more than 3 hours.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any cats at home? Some kidney issues can be triggered by animal exposure, especially with compromised immunity.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, we have two cats at home. My grandchildren brought them. Should I be worried?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: We will check that also. Do you do any exercise? Even walking?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: No doctor, no exercise at all. With swelling and breathlessness I cannot even walk to the next room properly.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Based on your creatinine levels, urine albumin result, swelling, and your long history of alcohol, mine chemicals exposure, I am diagnosing you with chronic kidney disease, stage 3 to 4. The proteinuria is significant and the tingling in your feet suggests early peripheral neuropathy also.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, is this very serious? Can it be managed? And what about the cramping?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I am prescribing telmisartan 40 mg once daily to protect the kidneys and control protein leakage. For the cramping in your legs, take calcium carbonate tablets twice a day. Also starting furosemide 40 mg in the morning to reduce the swelling. And vitamin B complex for the peripheral neuropathy.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: You must stop alcohol completely — even one drink can worsen your kidneys rapidly now. Reduce smoking and target full stop. Avoid high-protein and high-salt food.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, understood. I will try my best. But I also wanted to ask, I have had gastritis myself also few days ago with burning in stomach. Is it related?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Yes, gastritis can worsen with kidney disease because toxins build up in the body. I will add pantoprazole 40 mg before breakfast. We need repeat serum creatinine, serum electrolytes, and complete blood count done in one week. Also improve your sleep habits — rest is part of treatment for kidney disease.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Thank you doctor. I will come back next week and bring my wife also for her check-up.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Come in, come in. Please sit down. Take a breath, it is okay.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, I am very scared. Since yesterday my whole body is swelling badly, especially my fingers and joints. I do not know what is happening to me.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Okay, do not worry, we will sort this out. Is the swelling only at the joints and fingers, or also at the calf area?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, the calf also is very puffy. And there is cramping pain also continuously. I am a manual labourer, I cannot afford this kind of thing.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I understand, I understand. Has the urine colour changed at all? Any foamy urine or reduced urine output? And is the swelling yellow tinged on the skin anywhere?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Umm, the urine is dark doctor. And yes, the skin is looking yellow a little bit. I did not notice it before. The swelling is there continuously since last night.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Have you been coughing at all? Any productive cough? And have you been near any sick person recently?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: No doctor, negative for cough. But my neighbour had some infection last week, so yes I was near a sick person. Could that have caused this?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: It is possible. Now tell me honestly, do you have any past history of heart disease or heart attack? Any clotting disorder?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Ahh, yes doctor. I had a heart attack about two years back. And the doctor at that time told me I have a clotting disorder also. I also have heart disease they said. I was on medicines but I stopped taking them.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: You stopped your medicines? Which ones were you on? And have you ever had a stress test done for your heart after that attack?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: I was taking antacids and some eye drops for a separate eye issue. But for the heart medicines I stopped since yesterday only... actually no, I stopped a few weeks ago. The stress test was done once but I do not have the report with me.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Okay. Do you drink alcohol? And what about coffee? Also, what kind of physical activity does your work involve daily?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: I do take alcohol since I was young, doctor. And coffee in the morning. My physical activity is heavy — I carry heavy loads at construction site. And I also smoke, half a pack a day.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Okay. Any pain in the joints that comes occasionally? Any history of something like a fistula near any wound or surgical site? Or any appendicitis like pain in the stomach?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: The joints pain comes occasionally, yes doctor. And uh, I had a small wound on my calf last year, the doctor had said it was forming like a fistula. No appendicitis type pain doctor.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I see. Based on what you are telling me — the swelling, dark urine, yellow tinge, your history of clotting disorder and heart disease, and missing your medicines — I believe you are having acute kidney injury on top of chronic kidney disease. Do not panic, we can manage this.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, is this because I stopped my medicines? Will I be okay? I am very scared.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Missing medicines has definitely worsened the situation. Your heart disease and clotting disorder together reduce blood flow to the kidneys, and the sick person contact may have triggered an infection on top of that.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I am going to start you on furosemide for the swelling, sodium bicarbonate to protect your kidneys, and restart your aspirin and atorvastatin for the heart. Please do not stop any of these.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Okay doctor. And what about the cramping in my calf? Should I stop all physical activity?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Yes, for now complete rest is needed. Stop all heavy physical activity at the construction site until the swelling goes down and your creatinine levels normalise. The cramping in the calf will ease once the fluid reduces.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Also, please stop alcohol completely — it is very damaging to kidneys and the heart together. Cut down coffee also. And do not smoke; half a pack a day is making everything worse.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: I will try doctor. Can I continue my antacids and eye drops also?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Yes, you can continue the antacids and eye drops. I am also ordering a serum creatinine test, urine routine, electrolytes, and a repeat stress test for your heart once you are stable. You will be okay — but please, no more missing doses.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Come in, come in. Please sit down comfortably.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, I am very worried. Since last week my stomach is giving me so much trouble. There is burning and gas all the time.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Okay, do not worry, we will sort this out. Tell me, where exactly is the pain — is it in the upper abdomen or lower?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Mostly upper, doctor. Right here below the chest. The burning sensation is very sharp and the gas is coming up like belching.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Is there any vomiting or nausea also? And how often is this stomach pain happening?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Umm, yes doctor, nausea is there. Earlier the pain used to come monthly, but since last week it has become every day. I feel like I will collapse.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I can see you are in a lot of discomfort. Have you consulted anyone before coming here? Any medicines you took?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, there is one local man near my route, he gives medicines without any prescription. He gave me some antacid powder and some tablet, I do not know the name. It gave clear relief for only one or two hours, then the pain came back worse.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
