utterances.text: Doctor: I understand, those roadside providers sometimes give temporary relief only. Please do not take medicines from them — it can mask the real problem. You have come to the right place now.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, there is also bloating in the stomach and sometimes I see black stool. This scared me a lot, that is why I came running today.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: That is good you came. Black stool is something we must take seriously. Do you smoke or take cannabis? Any alcohol use?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, I smoke about 5 cigarettes per day. And I do take cannabis 3 times a week to manage stress of the job. Alcohol I take daily, just small amount at night.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I see. What about any lead exposure — you are a postman yes? Any area with pollen or heavy pollution on your route? Or contact with any sick person?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, I deliver in the industrial area, so maybe some lead dust also. And pollen is everywhere this season. I did recently meet a sick person at one of my stops, he had some liver problem he told me.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Okay. Any history of hepatitis or liver disease in the past? Any liver function test done before?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Ahh, doctor, a few years back I was told I had some hepatitis B. But I did not take it seriously. No test was done recently, I just ignored it.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Alright, let me examine you. Is there any yellowing of the eyes or skin? Any swelling in the legs?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Now that you say, doctor, my wife told me my eyes look slightly yellow since last week. And my ankles are a bit swollen by evening.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Based on your history of hepatitis B, the jaundice, black stool, and abdominal pain, I believe this is a case of chronic hepatitis B with possible gastritis. Do not be frightened — it is manageable with proper treatment.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, is it very serious? I am only 38 years old. I have a family to support. I do walking all day for my delivery job.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I understand your worry completely. With the right medicines and lifestyle changes, this can be controlled well. We must stop the alcohol and cannabis immediately — these are making the liver situation worse. Reduce smoking also.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I am prescribing entecavir for the hepatitis B, and also pantoprazole for the acidity and gastritis. Take domperidone for nausea and bloating as well.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I am ordering a liver function test, hepatitis B viral load, upper GI endoscopy, and a complete blood count to check for any bleeding internally.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Thank you so much doctor. I was so scared. I will do all tests. The burning in my stomach is very severe right now, can it give relief soon?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Yes, the pantoprazole will give relief from acidity within a day or two. But most importantly, do not go back to that local medicine man. Take only prescribed medicines. Eat light, avoid spicy food, and come back with reports in one week.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Hello, come in, please have a seat. Congratulations on your recent marriage!

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Thank you doctor. I got married just three months back.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: What brings you here today? Are you here for a pre-operative clearance?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, I need clearance for my operation, but since yesterday I am having fever and feeling very weak. I am worried something is wrong.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I see. How high is the fever? Any rash, headache, or body ache?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Fever is very high, doctor. And yes, body ache is there every morning. Also, I had some rash on my skin two days back. A local quack I visited said it could be dengue.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Did you have any vomiting or diarrhea? And any bleeding from the mouth or gums?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes, vomiting happened once a day for two days. But no bleeding from mouth. The quack gave me some tablet but I do not know the name.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Which informal provider did you consult? Did they do any blood test or just gave medicines directly?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Umm, it was a local man near our factory, doctor. He did not do any test. He just said it looks like typhoid or malaria and gave some tablets to take after meals.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: You mentioned a factory. Where exactly do you work? I need to ask about your occupational exposures — do you come in contact with asbestos, chemicals, or dust at work?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: I work in a garment processing unit, doctor, but the building is old. Someone told us there is asbestos in the ceiling panels. We breathe that air every morning when we start work.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: That is concerning. Any cough or breathlessness from that asbestos exposure? Also, have you had COVID in the past?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes, I had COVID a year ago. After that incident, I had some breathlessness on and off, and my heart was also feeling like it was beating very fast sometimes, once a week or so.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: The palpitations in your heart — are they sudden onset and do they go away on their own? Any episode of fainting or seizures?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Ahh, the fast beating in my heart goes away on its own, doctor. And no seizures or fainting thankfully. It happens only once in a while.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Do you smoke, consume alcohol, or take any recreational drugs?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: No doctor, I do not smoke or take drugs at all. I am a newly married woman, nothing like that.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Based on your high grade fever, body ache, rash, and vomiting, this looks like dengue fever. The cardiac symptoms after COVID need separate evaluation before we can clear you for surgery.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, is the operation going to be delayed then? And what about my heart symptoms?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Yes, we need to postpone the operation until the dengue fever resolves and your heart is evaluated. I am ordering a dengue NS1 antigen test, complete blood count, and Widal test to rule out typhoid as well.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: And for the fast heartbeat, doctor? Will that also need some test?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Absolutely. I will refer you for a Holter monitor to record your heart rhythm over 24 hours, since the palpitations are happening once a week. Post-COVID cardiac complications must not be missed.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: For now, I am prescribing paracetamol 500 mg after meals three times a day for the fever, and oral rehydration salts for hydration. Please stop whatever the local quack gave you — it could be harmful.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Okay doctor, I will stop the other tablets. Should I be worried about the asbestos at my workplace too? My colleagues are also coughing a lot.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: That is very important. Please report the asbestos exposure to the factory management and wear a proper mask at work. Once your fever settles and the Holter monitor results are reviewed, we will proceed with pre-operative clearance. Do not take medicines from any informal provider again — always come here first.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Hello, come in, come in. Please sit down. Long time since I saw you last.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, it has been a few months. I was managing on my own but now things have become too much to handle.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Alright, tell me what is troubling you today. Which part of the body is giving you problem?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, there is itching and rash on my buttocks and inner thighs. It is mildly uncomfortable during the day but becomes worse at night. I have been suffering for a week now.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Is the rash spreading? Any discharge or peeling of skin around that area?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: The rash is spreading a little yes. There is some peeling at the edges. No discharge as such, but the itching is very bad periodically throughout the evening.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Do you work in a place with lots of dust or moisture? Any sweating heavily throughout the day because of your work?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, I do domestic work in three houses. There is always dust around me and I sweat heavily while cleaning and mopping. I do not get time to change or bathe in between.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Okay. Now tell me, are you having any hoarseness of your voice, any throat pain, or difficulty swallowing?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Umm, yes actually, for a week I have some hoarseness when I wake up. It settles after some time. I did not think it was connected.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any BP problem symptoms — like giddiness, headache, or blurred vision?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: I get giddiness hardly ever, but no headache. No blurred vision at all. But I do feel some spasms in my legs at night, doctor.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any past history of thyroid disorder, allergies, or kidney stones?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, I have thyroid disorder detected in 2022. And I have allergies to some soaps. I had kidney stones also, that was operated — it was post-op recovery that I missed my follow-up with you.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Were there any issues with your GB — gallbladder — also around that time? Any abdominal pain or nausea?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: The scan had shown some GB sludge doctor but no stone. Nausea I get periodically, mainly after meals.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Are you currently on tenofovir? And do you drink — alcohol I mean?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, tenofovir I am taking regularly. For drinking, I am a social smoker kind of — I mean I drink only at social gatherings, never at home. I also do gym when I get time but these days no time.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Good that you are doing gym when possible. We will need to run your ALT levels today since you are on tenofovir and you mentioned you drink socially. Any previous ALT reports you have brought?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Umm, I have a report from 2022 but I think it is too old now. I did not get any new ALT done recently.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Okay. Looking at the pattern of the rash on your buttocks and thighs, the peeling, the worse at night itching, and your dust and sweat exposure — this is a case of fungal infection, specifically tinea cruris. The hoarseness and spasms in the legs may be related to your thyroid disorder.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I am prescribing clotrimazole cream to apply on the affected area twice a day, and fluconazole tablet once a week for four weeks. For the spasms, we will start magnesium supplement and I will adjust your thyroid medication after checking TSH levels.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Make sure to keep the groin area dry and clean, especially after sweating at work. Never use scented soaps given your allergies. Avoid tight clothing and change after each house you work in if possible. Limit drinking entirely while on fluconazole tablet.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, the BP problem — should I monitor it at home also? Sometimes I feel my heart is beating fast but it is hardly ever.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Yes, do check your BP at your local pharmacy periodically. We will get ALT, TSH, and a kidney function test done today itself. Come back in three weeks with reports, and if rash or hoarseness does not improve, come earlier.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Please come in, sit down. Take a moment.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor... sorry, I am not well at all. All the time I am feeling so bad. itching, swelling on my face... it started this morning very badly.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Okay, okay. Tell me slowly. Is there any rash or hives on your skin? Any breathlessness?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes, rash is there on my arms and neck. And this swelling... it is worse after eating. My muscles are also paining, countless times I have had this sensation but never so severe.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any frequent urination? Nausea or vomiting?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Umm... don't think so on urination. But nausea is there. The discharge from my nose is clear, all the time running.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Have you been exposed to any pesticides or chemicals recently? Do you live in a rural area?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, we are from a village — rural area near Nashik. Husband does farming, lots of pesticides spraying going on near our house. I am exposed all the time.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any known history of asthma or allergy before this?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes, asthma was detected in 2020. And I also have gallstones — they found it last year. Ahh, and some doctor said chronic urticaria also.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Were you taking any medicines for this? Any antihistamines or prednisone?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: I was taking antihistamines on and off, but hardly ever regularly. Someone told me to take prednisone but I stopped because I was scared. I also take metoprolol for my heart — BP problem.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any chest pain or palpitations? Has anyone done an angiogram for you?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: No one has done angiogram. Palpitations I get hardly ever. But chest tightness is there worse after eating sometimes.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Do you smoke? Any caffeine or stress issues?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: I am a social smoker. Tea — too much caffeine, I know it is bad. And stress is too much doctor, taking care of the house, children, everything. I used to do running but stopped now.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any family history of TB or autoimmune diseases? Any exposure to chemicals at home like cleaning agents?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Ahh, my mother had TB long back. And yes, lots of chemicals at home — I clean everything myself. Muscles pain all the time after that.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: We need to check your blood sugar levels today and also run AST to check your liver, given the gallstones history. Have these been checked recently?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: No one has checked blood sugar or AST for a long time. I kept delaying doctor, I thought it will settle on its own.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Based on what you have told me, this looks like allergic urticaria with angioedema, likely triggered by pesticides and chemicals. The asthma and chronic urticaria are contributing. We cannot rule out an autoimmune component.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, is it very serious? The swelling on my face is scaring me, and my muscles are paining so much.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: We are managing it right now. I am prescribing antihistamines to be taken all the time as a regular course, and a short course of prednisone for the swelling and rash. Continue your metoprolol as before but do not skip it.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: You must avoid all pesticides and chemicals completely — even household ones. Reduce caffeine and manage stress. If breathlessness or throat swelling starts, come immediately to emergency.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Okay doctor, I will follow. And the blood sugar and AST test — I will do this morning itself before going home.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Hello, come in, please sit down. How are you doing today?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, I have this rash and itching on my hand. It is bothering me since 2024.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Okay, let me see. Is the rash only on the hand or anywhere else on the body?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Mostly the hand, doctor. Sometimes near the ears also, little bit.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Is the itching constant or does it come and go?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: It comes and goes. Happens a few times in a week. More in the evening.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any coworker was sick recently, or did you share towels or anything like that at office?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Umm, yes doctor, one coworker was sick with some skin infection last month. We did share a common washroom.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any personal history of allergies or eczema before?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: I had some eczema during pregnancy, but that resolved on its own. Quite a while ago that was.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Have you used any creams or medicines for this currently? Any herbal remedies or home treatments?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: I am applying some herbal cream from the local store. 1 hour daily I put it and leave. Never used any prescription cream.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any discharge from the ears? Any productive cough or breathing difficulty?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: No discharge from ears, doctor. No cough also. Just the itching.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any bloating or gas trouble in the intestine area? Fungal overgrowth can sometimes affect the gut also.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Ahh, yes doctor, some bloating in the intestine area a few times in a month. I thought it was just gas.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Do you exercise at all? You have a desk job, correct?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: I used to walk, but not anymore. Very sedentary lifestyle now. Sitting at desk all day.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Your lab reports are here. I want to add an allergy test and also check PT INR given you are using herbal preparations. Had these tests done before?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: No contact with any testing lab before, doctor. Never done allergy test or PT INR. First time.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Based on the rash pattern on your hand and ears, the exposure history, and the bloating, this looks like a fungal infection — likely cutaneous candidiasis with possible gut dysbiosis.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: So the fungal infection is from my coworker, doctor?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Possibly the shared washroom triggered it, yes. The sedentary lifestyle and poor physical activity are also reducing your immunity and allowing the fungal infection to persist.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I am prescribing clotrimazole cream to apply on the hand and ears twice daily, and fluconazole 150 mg tablet once a week for one month. Also start probiotic capsule after food for the gut.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Please stop that herbal cream immediately — it may worsen the rash. Keep the hand and ears dry, avoid sharing personal items, and try to walk at least 30 minutes daily to improve your immunity. We will review allergy test and PT INR results next week.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Hello, please come in and sit down. First time visiting our clinic, is it?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, first time here only. My neighbour referred me, said you are very good.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: No problem, tell me what is bothering you. Take your time.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, umm, I am not sure how to say properly but few weeks now I am feeling very tired, dark circles under my eyes, and my whole body is just... heavy feeling only.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Okay. Any pain anywhere? Any weakness in your arms or legs?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Ahh, yes doctor. There is this stabbing pain in my lower back, it started yesterday but actually the numbness in both legs has been there continuously for some time. Also I have this old injury in the same area from work, doctor.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: What kind of work do you do? Any fumes or chemicals at the workplace?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: I am a manual labourer doctor, working in a factory since I was young. Yes, lot of fumes and dust there, no mask or anything they give us.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I see. Any known medical conditions like diabetes, thyroid problem, or high cholesterol?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, umm, they told me this morning at the blood check camp that my sugar is high and cholesterol also high. I did not know before. Not really any treatment I was taking.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Okay. Any difficulty passing urine, or any pain near the prostate area?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, actually that also is there. Once a week or so I feel like urine is not coming properly, burning sensation is there nonstop sometimes. It is unbearable at night.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Do you smoke or consume marijuana or cannabis?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, I used to take cannabis since I was young but I have stopped now. No smoking at all.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Good. What about physical activity? Any exercise or walking you are doing?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: The work itself is very physical doctor, lifting and carrying all day. But no separate physical activity like exercise or walking. Too tired by evening only.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Alright. Based on what you are telling me, you are showing signs of type 2 diabetes, hypothyroidism, and hypercholesterolaemia. The numbness in your legs and burning sensation near the prostate also needs proper investigation.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, what tests will be needed? I am worried about cost, some tests I may not be able to do.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I understand. I would like to order an EMG for the nerve issue in your legs and an ultrasonography for the prostate and abdomen. Can we do at least these two?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: The ultrasonography I can try doctor, but the EMG sounds expensive. Can we skip that for now? Also I wanted to ask, someone suggested I take fluoxetine for mood — is that okay?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Do not take fluoxetine on your own, it must be prescribed carefully. For the EMG, we can defer but monitor the numbness. Meanwhile we will also check thyroid function test, fasting lipid profile, and HbA1c.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Okay doctor. And for the unbearable breathing difficulty I sometimes get in the factory — the fumes make it very bad — what can I take?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: For the breathlessness due to fume exposure, I am prescribing albuterol inhaler to use when needed. Also I am starting you on calcium supplements because your bone health is at risk with this kind of labour job and low activity. We will begin metformin for your diabetes and atorvastatin for the high cholesterol.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Please avoid further fumes exposure without a proper mask, and do not ignore the numbness in your legs — if it worsens or you have chest pain, come immediately. Reduce heavy physical activity that strains your lower back.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Thank you so much doctor. I will do the ultrasonography and come back next week with the reports.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Good afternoon, please take a seat. Welcome to the clinic.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Thank you doctor. I am a railway employee. I came here because I got a second opinion after another doctor told me some things, but my stomach pain has become very severe now so I just walked in today.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Alright. Tell me, when did this stomach pain start and where exactly is it located in your abdomen?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: It started a month ago doctor. The pain is cramping in nature, mostly in the upper abdomen. I also have acidity and gas every day.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Is the acidity worse at any particular time? Any nausea or vomiting?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, it is worst every morning when I wake up. I have nausea every morning. Vomiting happens once in a while only.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any change in your stool colour? Has it turned yellow or dark at any point?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Umm, yes, doctor. The stool has been yellow every day for the past two weeks. I did not think much of it.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any history of COVID infection? Some patients develop gut issues after that.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, I had COVID last year. After that only my digestion became very bad. Also, I have had some gas trouble from childhood, but this pain is new.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Do you smoke or drink alcohol? Any other substance use like cocaine?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Ahh, I do smoke doctor, half a pack a day currently, but when I was younger I used to smoke 1 pack per day. No cocaine or anything like that. I do take one small drink after meals sometimes.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any travel history recently, especially to a rural area or places with pollution? Sometimes contaminated water can cause these gut issues.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, because of railway duty I had travel to a rural area two months back. There was a lot of pollution and the water was also not clean, I think.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any current medications? Are you on steroids, diazepam, or blood thinners like warfarin?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: The other doctor had given me steroids for something else, and I also take diazepam for sleep problem. No warfarin doctor.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any pelvic pain or issues near your uterus area? Sometimes referred abdominal pain can come from there too.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: No doctor, nothing like that near my uterus. Only the stomach and upper abdomen is paining.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Alright, let me summarise what I am finding. You have cramping abdominal pain, acidity, gas, yellow stools, post-COVID gut dysfunction, travel to a rural area, and long-term steroid use. This is a case of gastritis with possible irritable bowel syndrome and I want to rule out a gastrointestinal infection as well.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, can the steroids that the other doctor gave have caused all this stomach irritation?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Yes, long-term steroids are known to damage the stomach lining and worsen acidity. Also the diazepam can relax the oesophageal sphincter and increase acid reflux. We will need to review both those medications carefully.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I am going to order a stool routine examination, stool culture, upper GI endoscopy, and liver function test to check what is happening given the yellow stools and your travel history.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, can you give me something for the pain and acidity right now? It is really severe today.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I am prescribing pantoprazole 40 mg every day before breakfast, domperidone after meals three times daily for the nausea and gas, and antacid syrup as needed for immediate acidity relief. Please stop the steroids only after discussing with the original prescribing doctor, and we will slowly taper the diazepam as well.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Avoid smoking completely as it worsens gastritis, avoid alcohol especially after meals, and please drink only boiled or filtered water especially during your railway travel to avoid any gut infection again. Come back after the test reports are ready.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Hello, please come in and take a seat. How are you doing today?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Hello doctor, I am a college student, I got referred here by my college clinic doctor. I have been feeling very uncomfortable in my belly since morning but actually this problem is going on since 2024.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I see. Can you point to exactly where the pain is — is it more in the upper belly, the epigastric area, or lower down?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: It is mostly in this upper part, the epigastric area doctor. It is a burning pain that comes multiple times a day, especially after eating.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Is the burning pain unbearable at times, or manageable? And do you notice any nausea or vomiting?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, it becomes unbearable especially in January when the weather is cold. I have had nausea also but vomiting is hardly ever there.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any bloating or gas? And have you noticed any weight loss recently?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Umm, yes doctor, gas is a big problem, a few times every day. And yes there is some weight loss also, about three kilos in two months.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Has there been any abscess or swelling near your abdomen or chest? Any stool changes — like green or tarry stools?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Ahh, no abscess that I have noticed doctor. But present are some changes in stool — green colour sometimes, which is alarming me.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Understood. Any past medical history — any broken bone, surgeries, or gastric ulcer before?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: I had a broken bone in my wrist two years back but that healed fine. No surgeries. Nobody in my family has this stomach problem as far as I know.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Are you taking any medicines currently? Any enalapril or any antacid on your own?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, the college clinic gave me some antacid but I stopped it. I am not on enalapril or any blood pressure tablet. I take painkillers sometimes for headache.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Noted. What is your diet like — are you non-vegetarian? And do you drink alcohol? Any public transport travel with long sitting hours?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes, I am non-vegetarian and my diet is very irregular because of college. I am an occasional drinker, maybe on weekends. And yes, a lot of public transport travel daily, sitting for long stretches with stress eating.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Based on your symptoms — burning pain in the epigastric area, gas, bloating, weight loss, and since 2024 history — this is a chronic case of gastritis with likely peptic ulcer disease. The seasonal worsening in January is also consistent with this.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, is it serious? Will I need any tests done?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: We will do an upper GI endoscopy, a H. pylori breath test, and also a coagulation test given the weight loss and green stool findings. These will confirm the diagnosis.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Meanwhile I am starting you on pantoprazole 40 mg once daily before breakfast, domperidone for the nausea and gas, and sucralfate syrup after meals. Avoid painkillers unless absolutely necessary.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Okay doctor. Should I change my diet as well? And should I stop being non-vegetarian?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: You do not need to stop completely but reduce oily, spicy food. Avoid alcohol entirely for now — even being an occasional drinker is aggravating your gastritis. Also, the public transport stress and irregular meals must be fixed. Eat on time, every day.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Now I want to do a teach-back. Can you tell me — which medicine do you take before breakfast, and what tests are we ordering today?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Uh, doctor — I take pantoprazole before breakfast. And the tests are upper GI endoscopy, H. pylori breath test, and the coagulation test.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Excellent, very good. Also remember — if the burning pain becomes unbearable or if you see any blood in stool, come to emergency immediately. Follow up with me after your endoscopy report is ready.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Good afternoon, please come in and sit comfortably.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Umm... good afternoon, doctor.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: So, what brings you here today? I understand you were recently discharged from hospital?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Ahh... yes doctor, I was discharged 2022 for some issue, but now I am having this pounding heart feeling and peptic ulcer type pain in the epigastric region.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Okay. Is the pounding heart feeling heavy or more like rapid beating? And how long has this been going on?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: It is heavy, doctor... like something pressing inside the chest. This has been there over a year now. I get it occasionally, not all the time.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any rash on skin, itching, or swelling anywhere? Any loose stools or abdominal cramps?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Umm... itching is there occasionally on the arms. And yes, sometimes loose stools also, doctor.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I see. Do you have any history of gallbladder issue or past surgery?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Positive, doctor — I had gallbladder issue and they did past surgery for it some years back. Also I had a stroke once.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Okay. Any contaminated water source at your posting area, or regular smoke exposure on duty?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, at my posting we drink from a borewell — could be contaminated water. And smoke exposure is also there during crowd control duties.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Do you coffee or take any other stimulants regularly?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Ahh... I drink coffee only rarely, doctor. But I have been in this police job for 30 years so irregular diet is always there.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: What medicines were you given at the time of discharge? Are you still taking any paracetamol or other tenofovir or simvastatin?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: They gave me tenofovir and simvastatin after discharge, doctor. Sometimes I take paracetamol also for the epigastric region pain but it does not help much.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any family history of bowel disease or Crohn's disease? Was Crohn's disease ever denied or ruled out in your earlier workup?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Umm... they said denied for Crohn's disease at that time, but the stomach trouble is still there, doctor. I feel embarrassed to talk about these things.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: No need to feel shy — this is just a electrolytes and gut function check. I will also order a complete blood count, stool routine examination, and allergy panel to understand your itching and gut symptoms.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Okay doctor... also I forgot to mention, sometimes I feel nausea after eating and there is bloating in the abdomen.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Based on your peptic ulcer type pain in the epigastric region, pounding heart, itching, over a year history, and your contaminated water exposure, I am suspecting a mixed picture of allergic enteropathy possibly triggered by gut infection along with peptic ulcer disease.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, is this serious? Will the pounding heart go away? I am worried because of my old stroke.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: We will manage it properly. I am prescribing pantoprazole for the epigastric region pain and peptic ulcer, cetirizine for the itching, and please continue your simvastatin and tenofovir as before. Stop taking paracetamol on your own as it can worsen the stomach lining.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Avoid smoke exposure as much as possible on duty, switch to a clean water source, and stop coffee completely even if you have it rarely — it irritates the epigastric region further. Your stroke history means we must keep your pounding heart episodes under close watch too.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Okay doctor, I will follow everything. When should I come back with the electrolytes and other reports?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Welcome back. Good to see you up and about so soon after discharge.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Thanks doctor. I am still noticing blood in urine every morning and I have burning sensation in my throat for two weeks now.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Is the blood in urine frank red or more of a pinkish tinge? And is the throat burning on and off or constant?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: It is frank red doctor, only in the morning stream. The throat thing is on and off, mainly after I wake up or after a session at the gym.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Given your asthma history, do you notice any seasonal pattern? Does it get worse in winter or spring?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, my asthma definitely flares up seasonally. Every morning in winter I am coughing more and I do get wheezing with exertion.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any secondhand smoke exposure at home or gym? And have you been living in or near a rural area?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: The gym is smoke-free but I visit relatives in a rural area sometimes. There is quite a bit of secondhand smoke there as most of the older men smoke indoors.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: And what about your own smoking habit? Are you still a smoker?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Technically I smoke only socially now, but at the party last weekend I went up to almost a pack a day level. My friends call me a chain smoker when I drink.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Speaking of which, how much alcohol are you consuming? Any mercury exposure through diet or supplements?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: I drink alcohol quite heavily on weekends doctor, I will admit. As for mercury, umm, I do eat a lot of large fish like swordfish and tuna post workout. Could that be related?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Possibly. Any flank pain or swelling in the legs? Any fever or chills?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: I doubt it is fever doctor, I have been checking my temperature regularly. No flank pain either. There is mild puffiness around my eyes every morning though.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Right. Were the urine microscopy and kidney function test reports done during your admission available to you?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes, I have them here. The urine microscopy showed red blood cell casts and the kidney function test showed mildly elevated creatinine. The urine culture was negative.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Based on the red blood cell casts, blood in urine, periorbital puffiness, and elevated creatinine, this is IgA nephropathy, also called Berger's disease. The heavy alcohol use and high-mercury fish diet are aggravating factors.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: That is what I suspected. Is the asthma connected? I read it is unlikely but I wanted your opinion.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: You are right that a direct link is unlikely. However, frequent smoking and the secondhand smoke from your rural visits are keeping your asthma active and may be stressing your kidneys indirectly through chronic hypoxia.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I am prescribing omega-3 fatty acids capsules twice daily, ramipril five milligrams once daily to protect the kidneys, and continuing your salbutamol inhaler for asthma. I am also adding prednisolone at a low dose for the inflammatory component.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Should I stop going to the gym completely? And is it safe to keep taking my whey protein supplement?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Light exercise is fine but stop heavy straining and lifting for now as it can worsen blood in urine. Stop the whey protein immediately as excess protein load is harmful to already stressed kidneys. Absolutely no alcohol and avoid large fish to cut down mercury intake.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: We need to repeat urine protein-creatinine ratio, serum IgA levels, and a renal biopsy to confirm grade and plan long-term therapy. Your seasonal asthma management should include a pulmonologist review before winter sets in.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Understood doctor. I will cut down the fish and alcohol. Should I be worried about my kidneys long term given I am only twenty-four?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: With early detection and strict compliance, the prognosis is good. But continued alcohol use, smoking, and mercury exposure can accelerate kidney damage significantly. Follow up in two weeks with the renal function test and urine routine reports.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Welcome back. Good to see you up and about. How are you feeling today?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, I am still not feeling fully okay. Last night I had confusion again, like my head was not clear at all.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I see. Any difficulty swallowing also? And is the confusion happening often?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Confirmed, doctor, the difficulty swallowing is there intermittently, especially in the mornings. And yes, the confusion is troubling me three times a week at least.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any burning sensation or pain when passing urine? Are you suspecting a UTI?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Umm, yes doctor, there is burning pain when I urinate. It started about a week ago. Could be UTI, I am not sure.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Alright. Were any tests done during your hospitalisation? Did they run a COVID test or any blood work?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: That's right, they did a COVID test and full blood work when I was admitted. The COVID result came back positive but they said it was a mild strain.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: You mentioned you were on warfarin before. Are you still taking that, and any other medicines currently?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, I am taking warfarin and atorvastatin as before. I also took some OTC medicine from the medical shop for the UTI symptoms, I did not know what else to do.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: You should not be taking random OTC medicine especially when you are on warfarin. It can interact badly and affect your blood clotting seriously. Please avoid that going forward.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: I understand, doctor. Also, I should mention, there were some insect bites on my arms and legs around the time I fell sick. Could that have triggered something?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: That is worth noting. Any rash or swelling after those insect bites? And did you develop fever soon after?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Ahh, yes, there was fever and mild rash on my chest. That was around 2024 start of the year when everything began.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I need to ask you something directly. Are you drinking alcohol? How long has this been going on?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Umm... doctor, look, I have been drinking alcohol for 20 years. I know I am young but it started early. My father also was drinking for 30 years, so it is in the family I suppose.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Are you doing any physical activity like walking or any exercise at all?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: True, I do walking 3 times a week, but since the hospitalisation I have been resting more. The fatigue is too much after that.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Based on everything — the positive COVID test, the confusion, fatigue, difficulty swallowing, and the timeline — this is a case of post-COVID long-viral sequelae, and additionally you have developed a UTI which needs immediate treatment.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, what does long-viral sequelae mean exactly? Is it serious? And the UTI — can it affect my kidneys if left untreated?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: It means your body is still recovering from the COVID infection. The confusion and fatigue are part of that. Yes, an untreated UTI can travel upward and affect the kidneys, so we act on it right away.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I am prescribing nitrofurantoin for the UTI. Continue your warfarin and atorvastatin as before, but I will monitor the warfarin dosing carefully given the new antibiotic. Stop the self-prescribed OTC medicine immediately.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, should I stop the walking for now? And what about the drinking alcohol — will it make things worse?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Light walking three times a week is fine, but avoid overexerting yourself. As for drinking alcohol, it will absolutely worsen the confusion, interfere with warfarin, and slow your recovery. You must reduce it seriously.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: We will repeat the blood work in two weeks to check your clotting levels and kidney function. If the difficulty swallowing or confusion worsens before then, come back immediately without waiting.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Good morning. Please sit down, let us get started with the documentation for your railway insurance claim.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Good morning doctor. I was discharged from hospital two weeks ago but I am still having chest tightness and wheezing many times during the day.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Alright, so for the medico-legal record — before admission, were you having any cough or breathlessness? What was the pre-operative status?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, the cough was there around two weeks before admission, and breathlessness was happening twice a week at that time.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any stiffness in the chest or wheezing at rest? Is the tightness intermittent or constant?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: It comes and goes doctor, mostly in the early morning. The stiffness is there when I wake up and also sometimes at night rarely.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Now, in his work environment — any dust exposure? Railway yards can be quite problematic for the lungs.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, I am working near the yard for 20 years and there is always dust and diesel fumes. I never wore any mask.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any history of tuberculosis in the past? And any recent hospital visit before this admission that could have triggered something?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, tuberculosis was there about 12 years back, fully treated. And there was an hospital visit before, for a minor procedure.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any insect bites recently? And do you run or do any heavy exercise? Does exertion bring on the wheezing?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Umm, I used to go for running once in a while, but stopped after the breathlessness started. No insect bites that I remember.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Do you take any recreational drugs or have you used to take them? I have to ask for the documentation purposes.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Not at all doctor, I have never taken any recreational drugs. I do not even drink alcohol.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any tonsillitis or throat pain? And is there any burning sensation in the epigastric region after eating?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Ahh, yes doctor, there is burning in the epigastric region, especially at night. The tonsillitis I used to get but not now, two weeks ago it was there.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Based on the clinical picture — intermittent wheezing, chest tightness, occupational dust exposure for 20 years, and the history of tuberculosis — this gentleman has occupational bronchial asthma with possible gastroesophageal reflux contributing to the cough.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Were any tests done during the admission? We will need the results for the insurance file — specifically monospot test and albumin levels — were these checked?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, they did many blood tests. The monospot test was done and report was given to me. I think albumin was also checked but I am not sure about the result.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Was the monospot test positive? I doubt it, but for documentation we need to confirm. Did they tell you anything about infectious mononucleosis?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: They said it was normal doctor, not positive. I did not have fever or lymph node swelling so they were just ruling out things.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Good. Now for treatment — I am prescribing pantoprazole for the reflux and the burning in the epigastric region, antihistamines for the airway reactivity, and iron supplements since your albumin may be borderline low after the hospital stay.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: You must strictly avoid dust at the yard — request your supervisor for a transfer to a covered area. The wheezing and chest tightness can worsen severely with continued exposure.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, can I resume running once in a while? And will this breathlessness which comes and goes become permanent?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Light running is fine once the wheezing settles, but avoid overexertion. With regular antihistamines and pantoprazole, the twice a week episodes should reduce significantly. We will also do a spirometry next visit to formally document the lung function for your railway insurance record.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Hello, welcome. Please sit down comfortably. This is your first visit here, yes?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, thank you. I was a bit nervous to come actually.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: No need to worry at all, I am here to help. So tell me, what has been troubling you?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, umm, since 2024 I have been having so many issues. It started after a bad viral fever — like extreme fatigue, brain fog, and shortness of breath on and off. I went to another doctor and they said it was just anxiety, but I don't think that is correct.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I understand, and I want you to know your concerns are valid. Was that viral fever confirmed as COVID? And are you still having fatigue and brain fog now?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: True, the test confirmed it was COVID. And yes, the fatigue is still there — extremely painful muscle aches too, especially in my legs and arms. Also I am getting headaches many times a week.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Okay, I see. Any nasal discharge? If yes, what colour? And any chest pain or palpitations?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Ahh yes doctor, the nasal discharge is green and heavy — it has been like that for weeks. And some chest tightness also, mostly in the upper chest.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Has anyone around you been unwell recently? Any chance of contaminated food intake, or was a coworker was sick around you?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, actually a coworker was sick with some respiratory thing just before I got worse. And I did eat outside food from a stall — could be contaminated food, I am not sure.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Alright. Now I have to ask you some sensitive questions as part of my assessment — do you vape or use any substances like cocaine?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Umm, I used to vape and I used to try cocaine at college parties, but I have stopped now. I realised it was making things worse.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Thank you for being honest, that is very helpful. Any past history of fracture or clotting disorder? Any surgeries?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, I had a fracture in my right wrist two years back. And they also detected a mild clotting disorder at that time, but I was not given any regular treatment for it.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Were any blood tests or imaging done recently? Any PSA test or other workup done at the previous clinic?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: They only did a basic CBC and chest X-ray. None of the other tests were done — no PSA test, no D-dimer, nothing specific. They just said it was anxiety and sent me home.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I see. Based on everything — the post-COVID timeline, the persistent fatigue, brain fog, green and heavy nasal discharge, and the muscle aches — this is a case of Long COVID syndrome with a secondary sinusitis. The previous diagnosis of anxiety alone was incomplete.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Oh doctor, that actually makes so much sense. So what do we do now? I am also worried about the clotting disorder — could it be making the chest tightness worse?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: That is a very good question. Yes, with a background clotting disorder, the chest tightness needs to be taken seriously. I will order a D-dimer, pulmonary function test, and a full coagulation profile to rule out any thromboembolic issues. We will also do a nasal endoscopy to assess the sinusitis.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: For now I am prescribing amoxicillin-clavulanate 625 mg twice daily for ten days for the sinusitis, montelukast for the chest tightness and post-viral airway inflammation, and paracetamol 500 mg for the headaches and muscle aches. I am also starting vitamin D3 supplements as fatigue in Long COVID is often worsened by deficiency.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Thank you doctor. Is there anything I should be avoiding? Like, can I go back to vaping occasionally? And what about diet?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Absolutely don't think so about returning to vaping — it directly worsens airway inflammation and will undo all the recovery. Cocaine is also strictly off limits given your clotting disorder. Avoid contaminated food and crowded spaces where respiratory infections spread easily.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Understood doctor. One more thing — I also noticed some hair loss since 2024 from my scalp. Is that also related?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Yes, hair loss is a very recognised post-COVID sequela — it is called telogen effluvium. It usually resolves on its own as your body recovers. The vitamin D3 I prescribed and good nutrition will support that process too. Please come back after your tests and we will review everything thoroughly.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Thank you so much doctor, I feel so much better just knowing what is actually going on. I will get the tests done this week itself.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Good afternoon. Please sit down comfortably. How are you doing today?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Good afternoon doctor. I am managing, thank you. My neighbour referred me to you, she said you are very good with lung problems.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Of course. Tell me, what exactly is troubling you? When did all this start?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, since 2022 I am having this cough and wheezing. Then in 2024 the breathlessness also started. I read on the internet it could be asthma or something worse.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Is the breathlessness there all the time or does it come and go? And is the cough moderate or very severe?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: It is happening continuously now, doctor. The cough is there once a day usually in the morning, but the wheezing I have had countless times now. I feel mildly uncomfortable most of the time.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Is the discomfort in your upper part of the chest mainly, or does it spread to your entire body? Any chest tightness?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Mostly it is in the upper part, doctor. But sometimes I feel heaviness on the right side also. I saw online that right side heaviness can mean heart problem also, so I got worried.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any gas or acidity problem? Sometimes these can mimic chest tightness.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Ahh, yes doctor, gas is there. I thought that was separate. The internet said gas and wheezing together could be reflux related, so I was confused.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Let me ask about your past history. Any stone problem — kidney or gallbladder? And did you have chickenpox when you were younger?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, I had chickenpox when I was younger, and there was a stone in my kidney about five years back. Passed on its own they said.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any drug allergies? Have you ever had a reaction to aspirin or any amlodipine type of medicine?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, I actually cannot take aspirin — I get severe rash all over if I do. I never take it now. And amlodipine I was tried once, I stopped it because of ankle swelling.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Good that you told me. Any recent hospital visit, travel, or exposure near a construction site? Dust or chemical exposure can trigger these symptoms.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, there is a construction site right outside my building since 2024. Dust is everywhere. And I had a hospital visit last month for my knee pain. No travel recently, I don't think so anything out of the city.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Do you smoke or have any other habits? Also, how much screen time are you doing? Some patients say late night screen use worsens their breathlessness.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: I never smoked doctor. But screen time is a lot — I watch television for 10 years without any break in habit, maybe four to five hours every evening. I live alone so it is company for me.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Have any tests been done earlier? patch test, stress test, or thyroid test like T4?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, I had T4 done about one year back, that was normal they said. patch test and stress test I never did. The internet said I should ask for a spirometry test also.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Based on everything — the wheezing, breathlessness, cough, construction site dust exposure, and your symptom pattern — this appears to be allergic asthma. The gas and acidity are likely worsening the wheezing through a gastroesophageal reflux component.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Ahh, so the internet was partially right then. Doctor, is this dangerous at my age? I read it can spread to the entire body if not treated.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: It is very manageable, please do not worry. I am prescribing a budesonide inhaler twice a day and montelukast tablet at night. Since you have aspirin allergy, we will avoid all NSAID type medicines. For your acidity, I am adding pantoprazole once a day before breakfast.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Please avoid the construction site dust as much as possible — wear a proper mask when going out. Reduce your evening screen time as late nights can worsen breathlessness. We will also do a spirometry and patch test next week to confirm the allergy triggers.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Thank you so much doctor. You explained much better than the internet did. I will follow everything you said.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Ah, come in, come in. Good to see you again. How are things going at the construction site?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Same as always, doctor. Long days, hard work. You know how it is.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Of course. So today you have come for a refill? Are you still having any pain or new complaints?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Mostly refill only, doctor. But recently I am having loss of appetite and my neck is also giving me very sharp pain occasionally.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I see. Is the neck pain there continuously or does it come and go?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: It comes and goes, doctor. Almost never in the morning but worsens by evening after work. And the appetite loss has been there recently, last few weeks.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: You are currently on hydrochlorothiazide and metoprolol for your blood pressure, correct? Are you taking them regularly?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: I think so, doctor. Most days I take them. Sometimes I forget. And I was also taking ibuprofen for the neck pain on my own.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: That is a concern — taking ibuprofen regularly without consulting can affect your kidneys and interact badly with hydrochlorothiazide. Please do not self-medicate. Now, any history of thyroid disorder? I see it in your old records.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, thyroid disorder was detected some years back. And I also had my cholecystectomy done in 2020. Gallbladder removal, they said.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Good, I have that noted. Now tell me honestly — are you drinking whiskey these days? How frequently?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Ahh, doctor, just a little bit socially. Whiskey 3 times a week only. Nothing too much. I have quit the heavy drinking I was doing before.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Three times a week is not occasional, my friend. And do you consume caffeine — tea, coffee — a lot? What about physical activity?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Tea I drink continuously on site, doctor, lots of caffeine. Physical activity is there because of construction work but no gym or exercise separately. No formal exercise.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: At the construction site, are you exposed to any pesticides or chemicals? Any recent mosquito bite or fever?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: We sometimes spray things on site, so pesticides exposure is possible. And yes, I did get a bad mosquito bite last month but no big fever came after.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Alright. Given your thyroid disorder history, loss of appetite, and regular whiskey intake, I want to run some tests. We will do creatinine to check kidney function since you were on ibuprofen, and also a PSA test and spirometry.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Why spirometry, doctor? That is the breathing test, right? I have no breathing problem.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Yes, it is for lung function. With your occupational pesticide exposure and heavy caffeine and whiskey use, along with the loss of appetite and neck pain, I suspect early alcohol-related liver dysfunction and possible cervical spondylosis causing that very sharp neck pain.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Oh. I did not think it was so serious. The neck pain is occasionally only though, doctor. And the appetite thing — no vomiting or anything, just not feeling hungry.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Understood. For now I am continuing your hydrochlorothiazide and metoprolol for blood pressure. I am stopping ibuprofen — please do not take it anymore. For the neck pain, I will prescribe paracetamol and a muscle relaxant short course. Also starting thiamine supplement given your whiskey intake.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Okay doctor. Any restrictions I should follow? Can I continue my site work?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: You must reduce your whiskey intake significantly — 3 times a week is too much with your liver and kidney history. Cut down caffeine also. Wear proper protective gear at site to avoid pesticide exposure. Come back once creatinine and PSA test results are ready.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: I will try to cut down the whiskey, doctor. I have quit before so I can do it again. I will get the spirometry and blood tests done this week.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Very good. Take the thiamine continuously without gap. Bring all reports next visit and we will re-evaluate your thyroid disorder levels also. Take care of yourself — your body is telling you something.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Hello, welcome. Please sit down comfortably.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Thank you doctor. I got married recently and my office has asked everyone to do a full health screening. So I came here.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Of course, that is a good practice. So tell me, are you having any fever, diarrhea, or any other complaints these days?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Umm, yeah doctor, I have been feeling a bit of fever and loose motions for few weeks now. Also I feel like everything is spinning sometimes.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: That spinning feeling — you mean like vertigo? Does it feel like the room is going round and round?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: I think so, yes doctor. It happens twice a week at least, especially when I get up quickly from bed.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any pain near your umbilical region — that means near the belly button area — or near your lower back?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, there is some paining near the belly button side, once a week roughly. And the lower back also troubles me many times.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any burning or pressure feeling near your bladder — that is the area down where urine comes from? Any burning urination?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Umm, there is some burning when I pass urine, yes. I did not know that is the bladder area only.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I see. Have you had any surgery in the past?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yeah, I had a small surgery quite a while ago for some stone in the kidney, but I do not remember the full details doctor.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Okay. Have you been exposed to someone at school or work who was sick recently? And do you feel pollution around your workplace is affecting you?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, time ago there was a colleague at office who had some stomach infection, and our area does have a lot of pollution with the construction going on nearby.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Understood. Now I have to ask you some personal questions for the screening. Do you do any physical activity regularly? And do you use any substances — like alcohol or drugs?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: I used to do physical activity like yoga before marriage but stopped since then. And I have 3 beers a day habit since college, doctor. Also I tried heroin a couple of times quite a while ago but I have fully stopped that.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I appreciate your honesty. Any headache, nausea, or vomiting along with the diarrhea?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, some nausea is there, especially in the mornings. And the loose motions — I did not know that word diarrhea — that comes twice a week also.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Alright. Based on what you have told me, I believe you have a urinary tract infection causing the burning urination and lower back pain, and the vertigo along with diarrhea and fever suggests a possible gastrointestinal infection. The alcohol intake and past heroin use are also concerning.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, what is this urinary tract infection? Is it serious? I am scared.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Do not worry, it is common and very treatable. It means there is some infection in your urine pipe and bladder area. We will confirm with some tests.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I will order a urine culture, complete blood count, stool examination, and a liver function test given your alcohol intake. Also a kidney function test considering your past kidney stone surgery.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Okay doctor. Will you give me some medicine now? Is there anything for the fever and diarrhea also?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Yes, I am prescribing nitrofurantoin for the urine infection, oral rehydration salts for the diarrhea, and paracetamol for the fever. For the vertigo, I am starting betahistine tablets.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Most importantly, please cut down on the alcohol — 3 beers a day is too much and will worsen the diarrhea and lower back troubles. Also restart your physical activity like yoga, and drink plenty of water to help the bladder infection clear faster.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Hello, come in. Please have a seat. What is your name and how old are you?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Arjun. Sixteen years old.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Alright Arjun, you have come for pre-operative clearance today, correct? What surgery is planned?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes, doctor. Today. Some kidney procedure. My parents arranged it.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Okay. Are you having any swelling — on your face, legs, or feet?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes, on my legs mainly. Once in a while my face also gets puffy in the morning.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any bruising on your skin without any injury? Or spasms in your legs or arms?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Umm, bruising happens hardly ever. Spasms in my legs happen once a week or so.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any cough? Is the cough producing any sputum — is it thick or mucus-like?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: A little cough. It is dull and mucus is there sometimes. Not much.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any past history of jaundice, pneumonia, or any gallbladder issue?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Ahh, jaundice when I was small, doctor. No pneumonia or gallbladder issue that I know of.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: What about exposure to pollen or animal hair — any allergic reactions or breathing difficulty?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: No, nothing like that. We do not have pets at home.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Are you taking any medicines currently — any OTC medicine like painkillers, or do you use an albuterol inhaler for breathing?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: I took some OTC medicine for headache last month. No albuterol. I was told to stop everything before surgery.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Good that you stopped. Also, I heard you are fasting for religious reasons right now. How long have you been fasting? Any dizziness or weakness?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Fasting today only, since morning. Some weakness, but it is okay.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Does anyone in your family drink alcohol? I ask because kidney disease can sometimes run in families with certain habits. What about you — do you ever drink?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Uh, only socially. Maybe 2 drinks a week, after meals sometimes. Not regularly.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Understood. We need to check your blood sugar given the fasting and your creatinine levels. Has any doctor mentioned TB at any point?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: No, never. No one mentioned TB.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Alright Arjun. Based on the swelling, creatinine elevation, and your symptoms, this is consistent with chronic kidney disease. We will proceed with pre-operative workup.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I am prescribing furosemide for the swelling, and calcium carbonate tablets for the spasms. Please take them once a week review as instructed after surgery.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
