utterances.text: Doctor: Also, avoid all pollen and animal hair exposure, stop alcohol completely, and do not take any OTC medicine without asking us first. The blood sugar result must come before we clear you for surgery.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Come in, come in. Please have a seat. Long drive today?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, came straight from the highway. Been on the road since morning.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Alright, so you are here for a refill, but tell me — how are you feeling overall? Any new tiredness or weakness?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, the tiredness is there continuously now. And my thigh is cramping badly, especially after long drives. Also feeling numb there sometimes.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Both thighs, or only one side? And does the thigh feel heavy as well?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Mostly the left side doctor. And yes, it feels heavy after sitting for a long time. The cramping is on and off but the numb feeling is continuously there.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: You have a history of hip replacement, correct? Quite a while ago, if I recall?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: True doctor, the hip replacement was done quite a while ago. Right side. No big problem after that but now this left thigh business is troubling me.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: And your high blood pressure — are you taking your medicines regularly for that?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Umm, nah doctor, I skip sometimes on route. No medical shop near the highway stops. That is actually why I came — refill only.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: That is not good. Now, you recently travelled to a rural area, yes? Any tick bite or sick contact while you were there?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, yes I was parked near a forest area for two nights. I did notice something like a tick bite on my ankle. And the other drivers were all coughing badly — so there was sick contact also.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any exposure to lead — old paint, battery work, any such thing at the yard?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Ahh, actually yes. We load old batteries sometimes at the depot. So lead exposure is possible, I did not think about it.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Do you drink alcohol? And how much physical activity — do you walk or exercise?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: I drink alcohol only socially, not daily. Exercise is just walking at truck stops, maybe 1 hour daily at best.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Okay, let me summarise what I am seeing. You have fatigue, thigh cramping and numbness, uncontrolled high blood pressure due to missed doses, possible lead exposure, a tick bite, and pallor on examination — your conjunctival pallor is quite marked.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, I also noticed my appetite has gone down since last month. And I get breathlessness even walking short distances now.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Based on all this — the pallor, fatigue, breathlessness, possible lead exposure, and your dietary pattern on the road — this looks like iron deficiency anaemia, possibly with a component of lead toxicity. The thigh numbness and cramping may be due to peripheral neuropathy from nutritional deficiency or lead.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: True doctor, I eat very badly on route — roadside food only. No proper vegetables or anything. Also I get a skin rash on and off on my arms — could that be related?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: That skin rash needs investigation too — given the tick bite and sick contact, I want to rule out a reaction. I am going to order a patch test for the skin reaction, and a bronchoscopy if the breathlessness does not improve. Also complete blood count, serum iron, blood lead level, and a peripheral blood smear.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: So for now doctor, what medicines? Can I get my high blood pressure refill and something for this anaemia also?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Yes. I am prescribing amlodipine 5 mg once daily for your high blood pressure — do not skip it on route. For the anaemia, start ferrous sulphate twice daily with meals, and vitamin B12 tablets once daily. I am also adding vitamin C to help iron absorption.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Avoid any further lead contact — wear gloves at the depot. Do not skip your amlodipine 5 mg. Come back in two weeks with all blood test reports, and if that breathlessness worsens, go to casualty immediately — do not wait for the bronchoscopy appointment.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Understood doctor, thank you. I will carry the medicines in my truck from now on itself.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Come in, come in. Please sit down comfortably. You look a little stressed today.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, I am very worried. After the surgery, I am still feeling pain in my whole abdomen and I don't understand what is happening to me.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Please don't worry, we will sort this out together. Tell me, is the pain in your whole abdomen constant or is it coming and going?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: It is coming every other day doctor, and when it comes it is very sharp. I also have yellowish tinge in my eyes, which was not there before.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I see. Any fever or chills? And what about the forehead — are you getting headaches?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: The headaches on the forehead are there once a day, usually in the morning. Fever is low grade only.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Were you given any pain relief medicines after the surgery, and are you still taking them?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, they gave me pain relief tablets but I am taking them almost never now because I am scared of side effects. I was also told to continue simvastatin for my cholesterol problem.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Alright. Now, before the operation — the pre-operative period — did the doctors mention anything about your whole abdomen findings? Were there any ultrasound or CT scan results?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, the previous hospital said it was just gastric ulcer. But then the surgeon said no, it was something in the whole abdomen area. I feel they misdiagnosed me and that is why I am so upset.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I completely understand your frustration. Can you tell me your occupation? You mentioned you are a bus driver — long-distance routes?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, I drive long-distance buses. I am sitting for very long hours, eating outside food. Also, there was someone at school my grandchild goes to who had jaundice, so I am worried about infection.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: That is good you mentioned. Do you smoke or drink alcohol? And do you do any exercise?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: I walk 30 minutes daily when I am not on duty. I don't think so I have any drinking habit — very rarely only, maybe at festivals.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any history of hypertension, diabetes, or liver disease in the family?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: My father had diabetes and hypertension. I myself have been told my blood pressure is borderline high. The cholesterol problem is chronic for me, that is why they started simvastatin.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Based on your yellowish tinge in the eyes, the pain in your whole abdomen, and the post-surgical picture, I believe you have developed post-operative bile leak with secondary cholangitis. The earlier diagnosis of gastric ulcer was indeed incorrect.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Oh doctor, I was so scared. Is the jaundice completely gone now or is it still there? And what about the infection?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: The jaundice is improving but not fully resolved yet. We need to do a liver function test and a MRCP urgently to assess the whole abdomen and bile duct status. Please do not panic — this is very treatable.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, being a bus driver, can I go back to driving? And should I stop the simvastatin because of the liver issue?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Please do not drive long-distance until we get the liver function test results. Also, yes, please hold the simvastatin for now as it can worsen liver inflammation. Avoid all alcohol completely during this period.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I am prescribing ciprofloxacin for the infection — take it once a day for ten days. Continue the pain relief tablet as instructed — do not skip it every other day, take it regularly so the pain does not escalate.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, for the headaches on my forehead, can I take any tablet or should I avoid self-medication?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Avoid self-medicating for the headaches right now. The ciprofloxacin and treating the underlying cholangitis should reduce the headaches as the infection clears. I will review in one week after the MRCP and liver function test reports come.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Thank you so much doctor. I feel much better after talking to you. I will follow everything you said.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Hello, come in, come in. Please sit down. How are you doing today?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, I am very worried. I am having fever over a year on and off, and now body pain also has started. It is dry heat coming from inside, not like normal fever. Both sides of my body are aching so badly.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Okay, do not worry, we will sort this out together. Tell me, is there any rash or skin problem along with the fever?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, there is some skin problem on my arms — small spots. And several times I have noticed the bleeding also, it is becoming bloody when I scratch. I am so scared.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I understand your concern. Have you recently been to a rural area or made any hospital visit for any other reason?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, I went to my native village — a rural area — two months back. And I had one hospital visit for my child also last month. I do night shift work so my sleep is very irregular also.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Okay. Any nausea or vomiting? And are you having loose motions or abdominal pain?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, nausea is coming after every meal. No vomiting as such, but my stomach feels very uneasy always. Headache is also there several times during the day.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Do you have any history of high blood pressure or jaundice before?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, I had jaundice many years back, and high blood pressure is also there — I was given some tablet for it but I stopped taking. I worry so much, doctor. That is why I am also on sertraline and diazepam for my tension and sleep.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Okay, that is fine. I am glad you told me. Are you currently taking the sertraline and diazepam regularly? That is why you came for refill also, correct?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, both are finishing. The diazepam helps me sleep during day hours after my night shift. Without it I cannot rest at all. The sertraline I take in the morning. Both I need refill please.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Understood. Now tell me honestly — do you smoke or use any tobacco? And what about cocaine or any other substance?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, cocaine — never, I would not touch such a thing. But I do use tobacco, I smoke 10 cigarettes a day. And I eat junk food 1 hour daily during my night break — that is all I get to eat at that time.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I see. That junk food habit at night is not helping your stomach at all. Tell me — any weight loss or fatigue also you are noticing?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, very much fatigue. I feel so tired always. My legs — both sides — they feel heavy. I thought maybe it is weakness from poor eating only.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Have you done any blood tests recently? I want to know if vitamin B12 was checked, and also dengue NS1 antigen, Widal test, or complete blood count?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: No doctor, no tests done. I could not afford or find time. But my employer said I should check vitamin B12 because my numbness in fingers is there also. I did not know what to do so I just came here.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Alright, based on your symptoms — the fever, body pain, headache, nausea after every meal, and the rural area visit — I suspect typhoid. Dengue is also possible but ruled out without the classic platelet drop pattern. I also I doubt it is simple viral fever given how long it has been.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, typhoid? How did I get it? Is it serious? I am very scared. And what about my skin problem and those bloody spots on my arms?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Please do not panic. Typhoid usually comes from contaminated food or water, very common in rural area visits. The skin problem and bloody spots — these can be rose spots seen in typhoid, or could be related to dengue rash. That is why the Widal test and dengue NS1 antigen are important to confirm.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I am prescribing azithromycin for the typhoid, paracetamol for fever and body pain, and also pantoprazole for your stomach discomfort and nausea. I am also refilling your sertraline and diazepam as you requested.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: One important thing — please reduce your tobacco use, those 10 cigarettes a day are worsening your immunity. Also cut the junk food at night — it is aggravating your nausea after every meal. Your high blood pressure also needs to be restarted on medication soon.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, and the vitamin B12 test — should I do it now? My fatigue and numbness in both sides of my hands — is it connected to all this fever also?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Yes, please do the vitamin B12, Widal test, dengue NS1 antigen, and complete blood count all together to save your time and cost. The fatigue and numbness may well be vitamin B12 deficiency on top of the infection — with your dry skin and night shift lifestyle, this is very common. Come back in five days with reports and we will adjust treatment accordingly.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Come in, please sit down. You look a bit worried today.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, I work in the railway department and three days ago suddenly I started feeling palpitations and chest pain. It was very very sharp, right in the middle of my chest. I got scared and searched online.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Okay, let us go step by step. Is the chest pain still there now, or has it settled a bit?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: It has reduced doctor, but I am still getting palpitations a few times a day. Also, since about a week I have this strange feeling like a rock in stomach, very uncomfortable.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any shortness of breath, sweating, or dizziness along with the palpitations?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, sweating was there that night, but dizziness is rarely only. I read online it could be a heart attack or maybe anxiety. I am very confused.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I see. Has your BP ever been checked? Any headache or blurred vision?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: I never checked BP before, doctor. No major headache. But doctor, I also noticed something on my tongue and lips — some patches that look green and are slightly painful. I saw online that this can also be serious.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Okay, I will examine those patches carefully. Now tell me — do you chew tobacco? Any smoking or drinking?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, I have been doing chewing tobacco for three months now, I know it is bad. I am a social smoker — social smoker only, not regular. And I take about 3 beers a day after work. I am vegetarian otherwise, very healthy diet.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: And this chewing tobacco — how long has that habit been going on in total? You said three months for the current brand, but any prior tobacco use?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Ahh, actually doctor, I have been using some form of tobacco for 30 years. I switched to chewing type recently. I read online chewing is safer than smoking — is that true?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: That is absolutely not true. Now tell me — any family history of cancer or heart disease? And any recent tick bite or insect bite, any travel to forest areas?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: My father had cancer, doctor — oral cancer. And yes, actually I did have a tick bite on my arm when I was doing railway track inspection in the forest area. That was also three days ago, same day the chest pain started.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: That is very important information. Did you take any painkillers or any medicine on your own after the chest pain started?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: I took one aspirin because the internet said it helps during heart attack. Nothing else, doctor.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Alright. I am checking your BP now — it is elevated. Looking at the patches on your tongue and lips, combined with for three months of chewing tobacco and for 30 years of total tobacco use, these look like early leukoplakia lesions which can be pre-cancerous. The palpitations and chest pain along with the tick bite suggest we are possibly dealing with hypertensive episode alongside early Lyme-type cardiac involvement — we must rule that out urgently.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, the internet said leukoplakia always becomes cancer — is that true? I am very scared.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: No, not always, but we must not ignore it — especially with your long history of tobacco. The most important thing right now is we do the investigations urgently, and you must stop chewing tobacco and drinking completely. The 3 beers a day and smoking are all making your BP worse.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I am prescribing amlodipine 5 mg once daily for your BP, pantoprazole for the rock in stomach feeling, and doxycycline 100 mg twice daily for the possible tick-borne infection following the tick bite. Also, clonazepam 0.25 mg at night if palpitations are disturbing your sleep.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, the doxycycline — I read online it has many side effects. Should I be worried? And can I continue being vegetarian on this medicine?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Being vegetarian is actually helpful. Just take doxycycline with plenty of water and do not lie down immediately after taking it, as it can cause throat irritation. Avoid drinking completely while on this course. Do not take it with dairy.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I am ordering an ECG right now, a Lyme disease serology blood test, lipid profile, fasting blood glucose, and a biopsy referral for those tongue and lips patches. We will also do a 24-hour Holter monitor to capture the palpitations.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, one more thing — the patches on my tongue, they have been there for three months itself, same time I started chewing tobacco. I ignored it thinking it will go away. They are slightly painful when I eat spicy food.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: That confirms my suspicion — the tobacco is directly irritating the tongue and lips lining. Please do not rely on internet only — come for follow-up in one week after the ECG and Lyme disease serology reports are ready. With railway duty and stress, your BP needs close monitoring. Take care.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Ahh, Ramanna-ji! Good to see you up and about. How is the family? Your son was visiting from Pune, no?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, he came last month. Wife is also fine now, thank god. Everyone sends regards.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Good, good. Now tell me, how are you feeling after the hospitalisation? Any new complaints since discharge?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, last week I was feeling quite weak. The breathlessness is still there, a few times in the day, especially in the morning.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: And the cough? Is it still bringing up phlegm? Any wheezing from the chest?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Umm, yes doctor, cough is there once a day at least. And the chest feels tight sometimes. Wheezing also happened for a week after I came home.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: You work in the fields still, na? Any heavy dust exposure recently? The harvesting season is on right now.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, I went back to the field 10-15 days after discharge only. There was lots of dust during threshing. My wife said not to go but what to do.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I see. And at home — do you have any animals? Any pet dander exposure? Also, did anyone in the house fall sick lately? Any family member was sick with cold or infection?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: We have two goats at home, so pet dander is always there. And ahh, my grandson had fever and cold — family member was sick — he was staying with us for one week.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: That explains a lot. Now, I also want to ask — are you having any piles complaints again? Any bleeding or dull ache near the rectum?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Ahh, yes doctor, that dull ache is coming back with the piles. No bleeding yet but the paining is there after passing motion.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Are you taking much coffee? Too much coffee will make the piles worse, you know. And what about screen time — your son got you that smartphone, sitting for hours, no?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor I am taking coffee since college, cannot stop. And the screen time yes, I watch videos, for 10 years my son is telling me to reduce but I do not listen.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Okay. Before I forget — I see in your file there is a note of drug allergy. Which medicine caused that reaction? We must be careful.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, I had a bad drug allergy to aspirin — rash all over the body. Hospital noted it. Also I have been using drugs — those pain tablet things — on my own sometimes for the joint pain.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Ramanna-ji, looking at your history and the worsening after dust exposure and infection contact, this is a case of COPD exacerbation triggered by seasonal factors. The piles are also flaring due to constipation and your coffee intake.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, this COPD — will it keep coming back every season like this? This is the second time I am admitted in one year.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Yes, with ongoing dust exposure and pet dander at home, exacerbations will recur. You must reduce field work during harvest. We will also do a spirometry today to check how much lung function has gone down since last time.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Okay doctor. Also I forgot to mention, ankle swelling is there on the left leg since last week. Dull ache in the ankle also.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Hmm, ankle swelling on the left leg is concerning. Any chest pain or palpitations? We need to rule out right heart failure given your COPD history.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: No doctor, no chest pain. But the left leg feels heavy when I walk in the fields.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Alright. I am prescribing tiotropium inhaler once daily, budesonide-formoterol inhaler twice a day, and sitz bath with lignocaine ointment for the piles. For the ankle swelling start furosemide five milligrams. No aspirin or NSAIDs given your drug allergy.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Also — stop using drugs on your own without asking me. Reduce coffee to one cup only. Limit screen time and sitting for long — that is making your piles worse. Wear a mask in the fields and tie the goats outside the sleeping area to reduce pet dander.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, I will try my best. When should I come back after the spirometry results?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Come back in one week. We will review the spirometry report and also do a ECG and chest X-ray to assess the ankle swelling cause. Take rest, eat high fibre food, and call me immediately if breathlessness worsens.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Good afternoon. Please sit down. What brings you here today?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor... umm, my legs and feet are very swollen. Around two weeks now. It is warm to touch also.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I see. Any pain in the legs? And is the swelling severe on both sides?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Ahh, that's right, both sides doctor. The ankles feel very wet and heavy. I am a tailor, standing after every meal at the machine becomes very difficult.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Have you noticed any change in urine output or foamy urine? Any weight gain recently?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Umm... yes, urine is less. And weight gain is there — around three kilos in two weeks. I am fasting for religious reasons so I thought maybe that was causing it.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Fasting can sometimes worsen kidney stress. Do you have any past history of asthma or any anxiety disorder?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: That's right, doctor. Asthma I have had from childhood. And anxiety disorder was diagnosed maybe five years back. Also I had appendectomy done — after that incident I have been more careful.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Understood. Any shoulder pain or joint complaints? Garment workers often get osteoarthritis with prolonged work.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Ahh yes doctor, shoulder pain is there twice a day, especially in the morning and evening. And my knees also crack sometimes. Someone told me it could be osteoarthritis.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Do you smoke or drink?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Smoking I do, doctor — 1 pack per day. Alcohol only on weekends. I know it is bad but work stress is too much.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any cats or other animals at home? Sometimes animal dander can worsen asthma and affect overall lung health.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: I doubt it doctor — we have two cats at home but I never thought they were causing problem. My breathlessness is there several times a week now also.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Have you done any blood tests or imaging recently? Like a fluoroscopy or mammogram or any kidney function test?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Umm, I had a kidney function test done at the local clinic. Doctor there said my creatinine was very high — that is why they referred me here. Fluoroscopy was done too but I do not fully understand the report.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Is there any nausea or vomiting? And any headache especially in the back of the head?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Nausea is there doctor, after every meal. Headache also comes twice a day. My back also aches but I thought it was from sitting at the tailoring machine.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Based on the high creatinine, swelling, reduced urine output, and weight gain, you are having chronic kidney disease with fluid retention. The shoulder pain and joint changes may also be related to osteoarthritis worsened by your work posture.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Oh god doctor... I was not expecting this. I have a family to support.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I understand. First, I am prescribing furosemide tablet for the swelling and losartan to protect your kidneys. For the shoulder pain and osteoarthritis, I am starting paracetamol — avoid strong pain-killers as they can further damage the kidneys.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Please stop smoking immediately — it worsens both asthma and kidney disease. Also reduce alcohol. Keep the cats away from your sleeping area to help with breathlessness.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, the fasting — can I continue? I do not want to break my religious fast.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: With chronic kidney disease and current fluid retention, prolonged fasting can be dangerous. You must eat small meals and stay well hydrated. We will also do a mammogram and full urine protein test next week to check the extent of kidney damage.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Okay doctor, I will follow. Umm, one last thing — my chest also feels warm and tight several times a day. Is that connected?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Good morning, please come in and take a seat.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Good morning doctor. Actually it is not for me — my son is having some problem 10-15 days now. He is seven years old.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Alright. What are the main complaints your son is having? Any fever or diarrhoea?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, yes — he has fever every night and loose motion three times a week. Also he is not eating properly.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Is the fever very high, or low grade? Any vomiting or rash on the skin?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: The fever is low grade mostly, but at nights it goes up. No rash on skin. He says his stomach is paining also.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Did you take him to any other doctor before? Any treatment given already?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, one local doctor said it is only viral fever and gave some paracetamol syrup. But no improvement at all after one week.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: That is a common error — viral fever with loose motion persisting beyond one week and recurring every night should make us think of enteric fever, not just a simple viral illness. Was there any coworker was sick in your family's surroundings recently?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Umm, yes doctor — my neighbour's child had similar fever and loose motion around the same time. And in my colony the water supply has been irregular.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Understood. Any headache or body ache in the child? Is his abdomen distended or tender to touch?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes, he complains of headache in the evenings. And when I press his stomach area he says it is tender. He looks very weak also.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Based on the history — every night fever for 10-15 days, abdominal pain, loose motion, and tender abdomen — this child is most likely having typhoid fever, also called enteric fever. The earlier diagnosis was missed.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: We need to confirm with a Widal test and blood culture today. I am also ordering a complete blood count to check for anaemia or high lymphocytosis.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, is it serious? And the doctor also mentioned something about doing a genetic test — is that needed? Also they had suggested an EKG — I did not understand why.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: A genetic test is not needed here at all, and an EKG is for heart rhythm — that is not relevant for this child's presentation. Sounds like unnecessary tests were being suggested. Let us focus on the right workup.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I am starting the child on azithromycin syrup for ten days, and continue paracetamol only if the fever crosses 38.5 degrees. Keep him well hydrated with oral rehydration solution — ORS sachets every few hours.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, anything about his food? He has bad junk food habits — he is always asking for outside food and spicy things.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Strictly avoid all junk food for now — no outside food, no oily or spicy items. Give only home-cooked soft diet like khichdi and boiled vegetables. Also his sleep habits must be regular — he should rest 30 minutes daily in the afternoon as well.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Ahh, I see doctor. His sleep habits are quite irregular because I do night shifts as a long-distance bus driver and the house schedule gets disturbed.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I understand. And what about yourself — do you smoke? Any other health issues, like previous fracture or gallstones?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, I am a social smoker — maybe 10 cigarettes a day on a working day, but on off days I smoke less, so I call myself a social smoker. I had a fracture in my leg two years back and yes, gallstones were found last year.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: 10 cigarettes a day is not social smoking — that is regular smoking. With your gallstones, smoking and irregular diet will make things worse. And avoid any atenolol or similar cardiac medicines without cardiologist advice given your occupation — bus driving requires full alertness.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Noted doctor. I was prescribed atenolol once by someone for palpitations but I stopped on my own. I did not know it could affect driving.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Good that you stopped — atenolol can cause dizziness and fatigue, which is dangerous for a long-distance driver. Bring the child back in five days for review. If fever is not settling or he develops vomiting or rash on abdomen, bring him immediately. Blood test reports do call us same day.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Come in, come in. Please sit down. What is your name and what work do you do?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor sahib, my name is Ramesh. I am doing long-distance bus driving, Bangalore to Chennai route.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Okay Ramesh, what is the main problem you are having these days? Tell me in your own words, slowly.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, something is happening inside, like my body is not okay. I am having muscle pain all over and my stomach is also giving trouble many times.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: When you say stomach trouble, is there any blood in stool? Any change in the colour of your motion?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Ahh, yes doctor, monthly sometimes I am seeing something red, and the motion is watery also. I got scared so I went to one local man near our depot.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Local man meaning? A proper doctor, or some other person? Did he give you any herbal medicine or something?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Umm, not a real doctor sahib. He gives herbal medicine only, some leaf powder mixed in water. He said it is just heat problem. No test was done.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I see. Now for this documentation, I need to ask about your job. You said you drive long routes — are you exposed to chemicals like diesel fumes or engine exhaust regularly?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, chemicals smell is always there. Diesel, paint fumes from workshops — whole day sitting and inhaling. And the bus is full of people, so public transport crowd also is there always.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: How many years you have been doing this job? And do you smoke or chew tobacco?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Driving I am doing for twelve years doctor. And yes, I am smoking cigarettes, a pack a day, for 10 years. I tried stopping but could not.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Okay. Any cough or breathlessness? Any fatigue or weakness in your arms and legs?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, cough is there many times in the day. And my legs are feeling very heavy and muscle pain is also coming. Two years ago also this pain started but I ignored.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Did you have any hospital visit before for this complaint? Any test done anywhere?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Denied doctor, I never went to proper hospital before. Only that local man's place I went. No blood test, nothing.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any fever, night sweats, or weight loss? Any swollen glands in your neck area?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Umm, doctor I cannot tell exactly. Sometimes body feels hot at night. Weight loss I think is there, my clothes are loose now. I did not notice neck swelling.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Ramesh, looking at everything — long exposure to chemicals, heavy smoking, muscle pain, blood in stool, and weight loss — I am suspecting occupational lung disease with possible anaemia. I also want to rule out a viral infection. We need proper tests done urgently.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, what tests are you saying? I have not done any test before, I do not understand all this.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Don't worry, I will explain. I am sending you for a bronchoscopy to check your lungs inside, a vitamin B12 level test for the muscle pain and weakness, and a monospot test to check for viral infection. This is all for your insurance documentation also.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Okay doctor. But that local man said not to eat outside food and to take rest only. Is that correct? What should I do now?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: That local man's advice is not enough, Ramesh. You must stop taking that herbal medicine immediately — it can harm your stomach lining more. Stop smoking completely, and avoid direct chemicals exposure at work. Ask your depot to give you a mask.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: For now I am prescribing pantoprazole for your stomach and blood in stool, vitamin B12 injections weekly for the muscle pain and weakness, and salbutamol inhaler for your cough and breathlessness. Come back after your tests are done.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Thank you doctor sahib. I will bring my wife also next time so she can remember all these medicine names for me.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Come in, come in. Please sit down. So, you have come for a second opinion today?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, another doctor saw me last week and prescribed some medicines, but I am not feeling confident. I drive auto-rickshaw whole day and I am having many problems for six months.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Alright, let us go through everything carefully. Now, I want to note for my student here — this gentleman is elderly, multi-morbidity case. Tell me, what is your main complaint? Any cough?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, cough is there constantly. It is a productive cough, lots of phlegm coming.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Good, noted. Any chest pain also? Or burning in the chest?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Ahh yes, burning in chest is there on and off. And once in a while I also get breathlessness while driving.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Notice, students — he has both respiratory and gastric symptoms overlapping. Is there any dry throat irritation or hoarseness of voice as well?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, throat irritation also is there. Voice also becomes hoarse on and off. Very bothering it is.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Do you smoke? How much?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, two packs a day I am smoking for six months... actually no, for many years. I am also occasional drinker, only on weekends.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: And your work — you are driving all day. Any exposure to construction site dust or fumes in your area? Any insect bites recently?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, I park my auto near a construction site constantly. Dust is too much there. And yes, insect bites — last month I had some on my legs.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Interesting. Now tell me — you are sitting in auto all day, any walking or exercise? This is important regarding his sedentary lifestyle, students.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: No doctor, I have a very sedentary lifestyle only. No walking, no exercise. Sitting constantly in auto from morning to night.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any past history of diabetes or hypertension? And what medicines did that other doctor prescribed for you?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, diabetes is there for six months, detected only. He gave me metformin and some antacid syrup for the burning. Also one cough syrup but no relief.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any chest X-ray done? Or blood sugar test, HbA1c?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Umm, chest X-ray was done doctor. He said unlikely anything serious. blood sugar also checked — it was high only.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Very good. Now students, let me explain — this patient has chronic obstructive pulmonary disease secondary to heavy smoking and construction site dust exposure, combined with gastroesophageal reflux disease causing the burning and dry throat irritation. diabetes is an added comorbidity. The hoarseness is unlikely sinister given the reflux picture.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, in simple language — what is happening to me? I am not understanding all these big words.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Simple words — your lungs are damaged from smoking and dust, so cough and breathlessness are there. Also your food pipe is irritated causing burning in chest. And sugar problem is also there.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I am prescribing salbutamol inhaler two puffs for the breathlessness, pantoprazole tablet every morning empty stomach for the gastric reflux, and continue your metformin as it is. Also I am adding mucolytic syrup for productive cough.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: You must stop smoking immediately — two packs a day is very dangerous for your lungs. Also, parking near the construction site — wear a mask. Your sedentary lifestyle is making diabetes worse, so please walk at least thirty minutes.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, should I do any more tests? And the insect bites on my legs — any problem from that?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Yes, we will do a spirometry to check lung function and repeat HbA1c after three months. Regarding the insect bites, no swelling or fever now, so unlikely any infection — but watch for redness or fever and come back immediately if that happens.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Come in, come in. It has been a long time since I have seen you. How are you doing?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, sorry doctor. I was not coming because, umm, family was busy and money was less.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: That is alright. Now tell me, what is troubling you these days? Any new problem?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, my shoulder side is paining, and also something in the chest area is burning burning type feeling.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: When you say burning in the chest, do you also have cough? Is it productive, meaning are you bringing out something when you cough?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Umm, yes doctor, some yellow stuff is coming out when I cough. The cough is coming frequently, especially at morning time.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any fever or weight loss? How is your sleep, any night sweats?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Ahh, some fever is coming, doctor. My sleep habits are also not good, I wake up at night with sweating.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Tell me, is there family history of this type of problem? Did anyone at home have TB or diabetes?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, my grandmother had diabetes and she also had lung problem as a teenager they said. My mother also has sugar problem.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Are you working anywhere? Any construction site or factory work? Any exposure to animals or pet dander?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, I go with my uncle sometimes to construction site for small work. And we have a cat at home, so pet dander is there. No factory work.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Do you smoke or is anyone at home smoking near you?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Umm, doctor I also smoke a little. 5 cigarettes, mostly after meals. My uncle also smokes in the house.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Were any tests done before? In 2023, did you get a X-ray or any blood test done?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, I think one X-ray was done somewhere, but the paper is lost. No other test was done. I could not understand what they said.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Is there any irregular periods or discharge from the lower abdomen area also? Any pain in shoulder when you lift your arm?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Ahh, doctor yes the shoulder is very burning when I lift. Periods are also not regular, coming late frequently.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Looking at everything — the productive cough, night sweats, fever, and the exposure history — I am suspecting pulmonary tuberculosis. Also your shoulder pain and thyroid symptoms need checking, so we need T3 blood test and a Pap smear as well.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, what is Pap smear? I am not understanding. Is it painful?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: It is a simple test to check for any infection or changes in the cervix. It is not very painful, just a little uncomfortable. Given your irregular periods and family history, we must not skip this.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: For now, I am starting you on Isoniazid, Rifampicin, and Pyrazinamide as the anti-TB course. Also take Paracetamol 500 mg for the fever and pain.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, so many medicines. Can I take them on empty stomach? And what about the smoking?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: You must stop smoking completely — 5 cigarettes after meals is making your cough and chest very bad. Take medicines after food only, not on empty stomach. Also avoid the construction site and keep distance from the cat to reduce pet dander exposure. Fix your sleep habits — proper rest is very important.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Okay doctor, I will try. Thank you for explaining properly. I will come for follow-up this time, I promise.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Good morning, please sit. How are you feeling today?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, I am not doing well at all. Today morning also I had fever and I feel so weak, I cannot even stand properly.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I understand, do not worry. Is the fever nonstop or does it come and go?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: It was nonstop during the hospital stay, doctor, but now it comes a few times in a day. My whole body is aching and my teeth are also hurting, I do not know why.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: That tooth sensitivity can happen with high fever. Is there any rash on your arm or body still?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Nah, the rash on my arm has reduced doctor, but the joint pain is still very bad, especially in the knee.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Okay. You live in a rural area, yes? And was there any mold or dampness in your house during the rains?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, we live in a rural area only, and the walls of our house have mold everywhere after the flooding. Also, there is a weekly market and I go to crowded places like that weekly for vegetables and all.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I see. Based on your hospital reports and these symptoms, you have had dengue fever and there is also evidence of typhoid co-infection. That is why recovery is taking longer.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Ahh, both together doctor? My God, that is why I was so bad. And what about my kidney? The hospital doctor said something about that, I got scared.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Yes, with severe dengue, the kidney can get a little affected. That is why we had checked your creatinine levels. The creatinine was slightly elevated during admission, but we need to recheck it now.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor I am very scared, we have no money for big tests. My husband lost his work also. I feel nausea a few times in the day and I cannot eat properly.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Please do not panic, I understand your situation. The creatinine retest is very important and I will mark it as urgent so it is done at a reduced cost. The nausea is expected after typhoid, it will settle with medicines.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: The medicines they gave in hospital, am I supposed to continue all of them? I have some left but I am not sure.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: The IV fluids and ceftriaxone injections from the ward are no longer needed since you are discharged. But you must continue the oral medicines that were prescribed at discharge.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: I was walking to the hospital every day for about 1 hour daily before I got sick, doctor, for my morning walk. Can I start again?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Not yet, please rest fully for at least one more week. Avoid crowded places completely, and make sure your house mold is cleaned with proper ventilation. Your kidney needs time to recover and exertion will stress it further.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Okay doctor. Also, today morning I noticed my urine is dark yellow, almost like tea color. Is that normal?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: That dark urine suggests you are still dehydrated. You must drink at least three liters of water or oral rehydration solution throughout the day. This also affects kidney recovery.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, for the fever and joint pain, what should I take? The pain is so bad, I cannot sleep at night.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I am prescribing paracetamol 500 mg for the fever and pain, to be taken three times a day. Also continue the azithromycin course for the typhoid for five more days. Do not take any ibuprofen or aspirin — that is dangerous with dengue.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Thank you so much doctor, you are explaining everything so nicely. I was very worried.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: That is alright, I am here to help. One more thing — any bleeding from teeth or bleeding from nose or in the urine?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Nah, nothing like that doctor, no bleeding at all. Only the weakness and joint pain is troubling me.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Good, that is reassuring. Come back after three days with your creatinine report and also get a complete blood count done. If fever crosses 102 degrees or you have any vomiting, come immediately, do not wait. You will be fine, just follow these instructions carefully.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Arrey, Ramesh bhai! Long time no see. How are you keeping? Come, sit, sit.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor sahib, I am fine, fine. Just came for my yearly check-up as you told me last time.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Good man, very good. Now tell me, any feeling weak or tiredness recently? How is the body overall?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Ahh, yes doctor, feeling weak every morning when I wake up. And sometimes there is like a rock in stomach feeling in the abdomen area. Very uncomfortable.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Rock in stomach? Okay. Is the aching or burning pain there also? Or more of a heaviness?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Umm, mostly burning pain doctor. And the abdomen feels aching also, intermittently. Not all the time.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any jaundice — yellowing of the eyes or skin? Any nausea or vomiting?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: No yellowing doctor, but recently I noticed my eyes look a bit dull. Nausea is there every morning also.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Okay Ramesh bhai, let me ask you honestly like always — the drinking habit, how is it going? Are you still having alcohol?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, I have cut down a lot, I promise. Nobody in my house allows it now. I was drinking heavily for 10 years before, but now I have really reduced.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: That is good to hear. What about recreational drugs? And are you still smoking?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Recreational drugs — never, doctor, never in my life. Smoking yes, I do 10 cigarettes a day. I have been doing it for 10 years now.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any past history of hepatitis? And that stone problem you had — is it still troubling you?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, I had hepatitis long back. The stone was removed, so that is fine. But doctor, I found a cyst mentioned in my old reports — what is that?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: We will look into the cyst also. Any pain in the spine or head? Sometimes long sitting at the sewing machine causes spine problems in tailors.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Ahh yes doctor, the spine is aching after long hours of work. And head pain comes intermittently. I thought it was just the stress.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: One more thing — at the tailor shop, any pet dander exposure? Some customers bring in clothes with animal hair, yes? Any sneezing or coughing?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor! Many times customers bring pet dander on their clothes. I do get sneezing fits every morning actually. I thought it was thin air in the shop.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Ramesh bhai, looking at everything — the weakness, nausea, your alcohol history, and past hepatitis — this is a case of fatty liver with early chronic liver disease. The cyst on the old report is chronic and needs monitoring.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Ohh doctor, that sounds serious. What should I do now? Will I be okay?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Don't worry, we caught it at the right time. We need a DEXA scan for your spine because of the aching and your smoking, and a cystoscopy to evaluate that cyst properly. Also liver function blood tests I will order.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Okay doctor. Will I need any medicines? And for the sneezing and chest tightness from the pet dander?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Yes. I am prescribing fluticasone nasal spray for the pet dander allergy. For your mood and energy — you seemed low last visit also — I am starting you on fluoxetine at a low dose. And for the spine and bone health, start calcium supplements daily.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Thank you doctor. Umm, actually yes, mood has been low recently. I did not want to say but the burning pain in the abdomen and the feeling weak makes everything harder.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I understand completely. Now Ramesh bhai, strictly no alcohol — even small amount will worsen the fatty liver. Reduce the smoking gradually, and when you have pet dander exposure at the shop, use a mask. Come back after the DEXA scan and cystoscopy results, okay?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Good morning, please come in and sit down. How are you doing today?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Good morning doctor. I am here for the follow-up after my wife's discharge from hospital. She is at home, still feeling weak, so I have come on her behalf to explain everything.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Alright, I understand. Tell me, what symptoms is she having very recently after the discharge?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, she is having seizures — two, three episodes since she came home. She is also not sleeping at all, full insomnia happening three times a week at night she is just lying awake.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: These seizures — how are they? Are they extremely painful for her, any body stiffening or shaking of limbs?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, she says it is extremely painful and after each episode her joint pain over the whole body also increases a lot. She is crying with the pain.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any breathing difficulty or chest tightness? Is there any cough or wet sounds when she breathes?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Umm, yes doctor, she has some wet breathing, like mucus sound coming. Also she mentioned intense headache on and off since discharge.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Has she been given albuterol inhaler or any pain medications at home? What medicines was she sent home with?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, they gave albuterol inhaler and furosemide tablet from the hospital. She is taking those. They also gave some pain medications but she is not taking them regularly because of fear of side effects during pregnancy.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I see. Does she have any past history of TB, any lung problem, or any previous surgery?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, she had TB treatment completed about four years back, and she also underwent cholecystectomy for her gallstone problem two years ago. And during that surgery she required a blood transfusion also.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Okay. Now, you mentioned you both very recently travelled to a rural area — was there any tick bite or insect bites she noticed? Any contact with animals, any animal hair exposure?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Ahh yes doctor, we went to my village last month for a function. She did get some insect bites on her arms and legs. And there were many cattle there — she was sitting close, so animal hair exposure was definitely there. Regarding tick bite, she denied noticing any specific tick.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Does she e-cigarettes use or any tobacco habit? Any smoking?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: She uses e-cigarettes, doctor, 10 cigarettes a day. I have told her to stop but she is not listening. She denied any alcohol or other habit.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Do you have any reports from the hospital? Was any endoscopy or pulmonary function test done during admission? Any BUN blood test report available?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, I have brought all reports. They did endoscopy because of her vomiting problem, and BUN was done also — the report shows some elevation. But pulmonary function test they said was active and scheduled for tomorrow's outpatient.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any swelling or paining near the lower prostate region or urinary complaints? Any bleeding or discharge noted?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: She did complain of some paining in the lower area, near the prostate side she described it. Umm, urinary frequency has increased. No bleeding she has mentioned, nothing like that.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Based on everything — the seizures, joint pain across the whole body, the wet breathing, the insect bites, her history of TB, and the elevated BUN — this appears to be a case of eclampsia with secondary pulmonary oedema and possible tick-borne infection complication. She needs urgent review.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, is this serious? What should I do, should I bring her here immediately or continue the same medicines that are active right now?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: You must bring her in today itself — do not delay. Continue the furosemide and albuterol as prescribed. I am also adding magnesium sulphate injection to control the seizures, and doxycycline for the possible tick-borne illness. The pain medications she should take regularly — stopping them is worsening her joint pain.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Also, she must stop the e-cigarettes completely — during pregnancy this is extremely dangerous, it is worsening the wet breathing difficulty and the pulmonary function test results will be badly affected. No more animal hair or crowded rural area exposure till delivery.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Understood doctor, I will bring her in right away. Thank you so much for explaining everything clearly.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Hello, come in, come in. What is your son's name? How old is he?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, his name is Rohan. He is eight years old. But today I am here for my husband's documentation — insurance company is asking for his medical papers.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I see. So you are here for medico-legal documentation. Tell me what main complaints your husband has been having.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, my husband has been having weight loss and abdominal pain nonstop for several months now. He is just not eating properly.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Is there any cough or fever? Any suspicion of TB?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, the other doctor at the government hospital told us it could be TB. He has had cough countless times in the last few months, especially at night.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Does your husband have any past history of serious illness? Any COVID?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes, he had COVID in 2022. He was hospitalised for almost two weeks that time. After that his health has never been the same.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I see. And what about his drinking habits? Insurance company will ask this directly — does he consume alcohol?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, honestly speaking, he drinks alcohol very heavily. And he smokes also — a pack a day for many years. Two years ago he also used drugs, but he stopped that now.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Has he had any swelling in the abdomen or yellowing of the eyes?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes, the abdomen is quite swollen doctor. And his eyes were yellow last month. Also he has a rash on the wrist that is not going away.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: This rash on the wrist — did it start after any mosquito bite or sun exposure?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: He does go out a lot in the afternoon for his work, so maybe sun exposure is a reason. Also there is lot of mosquito bite problem in our area. I am not sure which one caused it.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Has any biopsy or liver function test been done? Any sputum test for the TB?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: The sputum test was done at government hospital but result was not confirmed. Biopsy was recommended but we have not done it yet because of money problem. Liver function test was done and values were very high, they said.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Is he currently on any medicines at all? Any diazepam or other medicines for anxiety?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, some psychiatrist gave him diazepam two years ago for sleep and anxiety, but he is taking it on his own now without prescription. He takes it nonstop with alcohol also, which I keep telling him is dangerous.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Based on what you are telling me, your husband appears to have alcohol-related liver disease with possible ascites. The weight loss and cough make TB a strong possibility as well, and there is a history of substance abuse that is compounding everything.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, what should we do now? The insurance company needs a proper diagnosis letter. And can something be done for the abdominal pain and swelling?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: For the swelling in the abdomen, I am prescribing furosemide to help drain the fluid. Also, diazepam should be stopped or properly tapered under supervision — he must not continue it on his own, especially with alcohol.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: He must get the biopsy done urgently and repeat the liver function test and chest X-ray. For the insurance documentation I will write a detailed letter mentioning the COVID hospitalisation, the TB suspicion, and current alcohol-related liver disease.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Please tell your husband — alcohol and diazepam together are extremely dangerous, they can cause respiratory failure. He must also avoid sun exposure because of the rash on his wrist.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Thank you doctor. I will try my best to bring him here. He does not listen to me. He has complained of chest pain also some days but no vomiting of blood so far.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: The chest pain must not be ignored — if that comes again, take him to emergency immediately. I am giving you referral for biopsy, ultrasound abdomen, and sputum culture. Please do not delay these.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Good morning, please have a seat. How are you feeling after the discharge?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, honestly not much better. The itching is still there and the rash in the umbilical region looks worse to me. Why was I even discharged so early?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I understand your concern. Can you describe the itching — is it throbbing kind of sensation or more like a burn?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: It is more like stabbing and worse at night. During the day when I am busy at my stall it is okay, but at night it drives me crazy.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Is the rash spreading beyond the umbilical region? Any redness or discharge from the area?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: It has spread a little to the abdomen sides also. There is no discharge but the redness is definitely there. And this itching is happening weekly since before my admission also.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any family member was sick with similar skin rash or fungal infection recently?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes, my wife had similar itching last month. And I visit crowded places like the market daily for my work, so how can I even avoid these things?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: That is important information. Do you work night shifts at your food stall? How are your sleep habits?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: I work from afternoon till midnight doctor. My sleep habits are very irregular — I sleep maybe four hours, sometimes less. You are going to tell me to sleep more, right? I cannot afford that.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Poor sleep does reduce immunity and worsen skin infections. Also, do you drink alcohol at all?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: I am an occasional drinker, just socially. And I drink a lot of tea to stay awake at night — around five to six cups. Is that a problem?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Based on your symptoms and examination, this is a case of dermatophyte fungal infection — commonly called ringworm — aggravated by sweating, heat exposure at the food stall, and low immunity from poor sleep.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: But doctor, I had this even before. Why did the hospital not treat it properly the first time? Was there something missed?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: The hospital treated your acute skin flare post-op. This underlying fungal infection was chronic and needs outpatient follow-up treatment. It was not missed — it needs a longer course.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I am prescribing terbinafine cream to apply twice on the umbilical region and abdomen daily, and fluconazole 150mg tablet once a week for four weeks. Also, cetirizine 10mg at night for the itching.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: That is three medicines! Will the fluconazole not affect my stomach? I have a sensitive system. And can I take it with tea?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Fluconazole can occasionally cause nausea or stomach upset, so take it after food. Excessive tea with cetirizine may reduce its effectiveness — try to reduce to two cups at night.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Also doctor, I am having some pain in the teeth since last week — is that related to all this or separate?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: The tooth pain in the teeth is likely separate — is it throbbing or constant?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: It is throbbing doctor, especially when I drink hot tea. It has been there post-op from my hospital stay, I think stress worsened it.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: For the tooth pain I would advise you to see a dentist separately. Meanwhile do a KOH scraping test and complete blood count today so we can confirm the fungal infection type and check your immunity levels.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: More tests — more money, doctor. Can these not wait? I already spent so much during the admission.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I understand, but if the KOH scraping test is skipped and you have a different fungal strain, the medicines may not work. Also, your night shift exposure at crowded places and contact with your wife's illness means reinfection risk is high — we must confirm the diagnosis properly.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Alright doctor, fine. I will get it done. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Welcome back. How are you feeling after the hospitalisation?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Honestly doctor, not that great. The stomach pain is ongoing and the gas trouble is still there in my upper abdomen. I thought after all those days in hospital things would improve.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I see. Is the acidity still bothering you? Any burning sensation or nausea?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: The burning is there, yes. And umm, I also noticed bloody stools monthly for the past few months. I told the previous doctor but he said it was just piles and dismissed me.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Bloody stools monthly is not something to ignore at all. Is there any pain in the upper abdomen today as well?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes, it is mildly uncomfortable today but earlier this week it was quite sharp. I am telling you, the previous doctor completely misread my case.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I understand your frustration. Let me ask — have you had any contaminated water exposure recently, or has any family member was sick with a stomach infection?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Actually yes, we had a water supply issue in our colony last month. And my son also had loose motion and vomiting around the same time. Could that be related? But why would the hospital not have figured this out?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: That is a very valid point. What tests were done during hospitalisation? Was a stool culture or endoscopy done?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: They did some blood test and ultrasound abdomen, that is all. No endoscopy, nothing. I kept asking but they said it was not necessary. Very irresponsible, I feel.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Was a thyroid test ever done? Sometimes bloating and constipation are linked to thyroid dysfunction.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: No, they never did a thyroid test. See, this is exactly what I mean — nobody was thorough. Now you are telling me thyroid could be involved? Should I not have been told earlier?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I hear you. Do you drink alcohol? And are you smoking at all?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: I have maybe 2 drinks a week, nothing heavy. I do not smoke at all. And I do exercise — I walk 30 minutes daily. So it is not a lifestyle issue, doctor.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Were you prescribed any antacids or proton pump inhibitors during or after the hospitalisation?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: They gave me pantoprazole but I am not taking it regularly because I read online it causes bone loss with long-term use. So I stopped on my own after a week.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I understand your concern but stopping pantoprazole suddenly without medical guidance is not advisable. The gastric erosion needs to heal and skipping medication will only delay recovery. Now, given the bloody stools and upper abdominal pain, we also need to rule out any issue in the lung or systemic cause through proper workup.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Wait, why are you mentioning lung? What does my lung have to do with my stomach pain? Now I am more worried.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
