utterances.text: Doctor: It is a precaution only. Based on the history — the contaminated water, the bloody stools occurring monthly, the acidity, and the prior mismanagement — I believe this is a case of peptic ulcer disease with possible H. pylori infection.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: H. pylori? I have heard of it but is that not something you get only from unhygienic food? I am very careful about what I eat, doctor.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Contaminated water is a very common source of H. pylori infection in India. Given that a family member was sick at the same time, the exposure is highly likely. This is not about personal hygiene habits only.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I am prescribing a standard triple therapy — pantoprazole 40 mg twice daily, amoxicillin 1 gram twice daily, and clarithromycin 500 mg twice daily for 14 days. Please do not stop these on your own this time.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Okay but all three together? That seems like a lot. Will there be any side effects? And what about the thyroid test you mentioned?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Mild nausea or metallic taste can occur but these will pass. We will order the thyroid test, H. pylori stool antigen test, and upper GI endoscopy today itself. Please avoid alcohol completely during the 14-day course.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Alright doctor, fine. I will try to follow properly this time. Thank you for at least listening and explaining everything.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Come in, come in. Please sit down. You look quite worried today.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor saab, I am very tensed. My son, he is only six years old, he is having loose stools daily and also fever few weeks now. I took him to a local health man in our village first but nothing is improving.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I understand, please do not worry, we will sort this out. How many times daily is this loose stools happening? Is there any blood in stool or vomiting?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: About four to five times in the day doctor. No contact with blood in the stool, but vomiting is there occasionally. He is also very weak and not eating properly.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Has the child been exposed to any dirty water or outside food? And you said you work as a farmer — any factory area nearby where water supply could be contaminated?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, there is one factory near our fields. The children sometimes play near that side. We use borewell water mostly. I am very scared, this insurance paper also I need to get done today.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Do not worry, we will handle all paperwork also. What did that local health man give to the child? Any medicines?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: He gave some tablets, I do not know the name. He also said to do a COVID test because of the fever. That came confirmed negative only doctor. And he did one blood test, I think he said T3 also, but I do not understand why.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Okay that is good the COVID test was negative. Now tell me, is the child having any abdominal pain? Any pressure like pain in the stomach area?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, he keeps holding his stomach and saying it is extremely painful. Sometimes he cries also. And the fever goes up daily in the evening especially.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Now for the insurance documentation, I need to ask a few questions about your own family health history also. Any heart disease or heart attack in the family?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: My father had a heart attack few weeks now back, around two months ago. He had heart disease for long time. And my wife, she had some thyroid problem during pregnancy. She was on synthroid at that time.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Okay noted. Is your wife still on synthroid? And does anyone in the family take atenolol or any blood pressure medicines?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: My father takes atenolol for his blood pressure. My wife stopped synthroid after delivery. And doctor, the insurance paper is also asking about PSA test — I do not know what that is.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: The PSA test is a prostate screening test, usually done for older men. For your documentation purposes, we will note that as none done currently. Now, do you yourself smoke or have any habits I should record?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: I am a social smoker doctor, only at gatherings or events. I play sports — kabaddi and cricket — occasionally in the village. No drinking.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Good. Now for the insurance form, I need to check — any pain or swelling in your hand or fingers? Any lumps near breast area for your wife that needs documenting?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: My hand and fingers have some numbness occasionally doctor — I think from farming work. My wife had a lump near her breast but she checked it just now last month, the doctor there said it is benign.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: That is reassuring. Any pressure like pain in your own chest? Any anxiety or depression — any medicines like fluoxetine being taken?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Ahh, doctor, yes, I was having some anxiety and depression after my father's heart attack. City doctor gave fluoxetine for a short time but I stopped it. The chest pressure like pain I feel occasionally only, not too bad.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Okay. Regarding your son, based on what you have described — the loose stools, fever, abdominal pain, and possible contaminated water exposure near that factory — this looks like acute gastroenteritis with possible bacterial infection. We need to confirm with a stool culture.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, will he be okay? I am so worried. What should I give him? The local health man gave so many wrong things already.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: He will be fine, do not worry. I am prescribing oral rehydration salts to give frequently, zinc syrup once daily for ten days, and a mild antibiotic syrup — we will confirm exact one after stool culture result. Also continue paracetamol syrup for fever.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Please make sure the child drinks only boiled or filtered water. No contact with that factory side water at all. And please do not go back to that local health man — some treatments can cause more harm, especially in children.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Umm, yes doctor, I understand. And for the T3 test that was done — should I be worried about that result? The local man said something about thyroid.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: The T3 test is for thyroid function — in a child with diarrhoea and fever, it was not really necessary, but we will review the report. For your insurance documentation, everything is now recorded properly. Bring the child for follow-up after three days and we will reassess. You are doing the right thing by coming here today.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Come in, come in. Please sit down. What has brought you here today?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, my wife is saying I am looking very bad since last three days. She said my fever is very very sharp and I am having body ache all over.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Okay. Is the fever coming occasionally or is it there often throughout the day?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, wife is saying it is coming twice a day. Morning and evening it shoots up badly. Also I have headache in my head and I feel like vomiting often.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Are you having any cough? If cough is there, is it productive — meaning, is anything coming out with it?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Ahh, yes doctor, there is some cough, it is productive, some yellow thing is coming. Also my stomach is paining very sharp inside.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any loose motion or rash on skin? And any bleeding from gums or nose?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Umm, yes doctor, some loose motion is there since yesterday. And wife noticed small rash on my chest and arms. No bleeding from anywhere.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Where do you work? Are you going to any construction site or any dirty water area for your delivery job?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, I am a postman. construction site area is on my route, every day I go there. Water is also standing near that area. I drink whatever water is available sometimes.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I see. Do you have any old illness? Any old injury or anxiety disorder or any sugar or BP problem?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, I had a old injury on my leg in January from a bicycle fall. And yes, doctor had told me I have anxiety disorder in January itself. No sugar, no BP problem.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Did you take any medicine at home? Like ibuprofen or any inhaler or anything else?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Ahh, I took ibuprofen occasionally for the fever and body ache, doctor. No inhaler or anything else. Wife said the fever is not going down even after tablet.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Okay listen, stop ibuprofen immediately. If this is dengue, ibuprofen can cause bleeding inside. It is not safe for you right now.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, what is this dengue? My wife also asked me to ask you. We do not understand these things properly.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Dengue is a sickness that spreads through mosquito bite. Your fever, rash, body ache, and headache all match this. Typhoid is also possible because of the bad water. We need to do some blood tests to confirm.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I am sending you for bone marrow biopsy if platelet count drops very low, but first we do blood count and dengue antigen test. Also, just for our record since you are a male patient over forty, we keep Pap smear and laparoscopy in mind if any abdomen finding comes in female family members who come with similar complaints in future.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, one more thing — my stomach pain is very very sharp after eating. Should I be worried?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Yes, looking at all your symptoms together — the fever coming twice a day, loose motion, rash, headache, and your exposure near construction site with dirty water — this is most likely a case of typhoid fever with possible dengue co-infection.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: So doctor, what should I do now? How long will this last? I cannot miss work, I deliver letters every day.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: You must rest completely for at least one week. I am prescribing paracetamol for the fever, oral rehydration salts for dehydration, and azithromycin antibiotic course for the typhoid fever. Do not take ibuprofen at all.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, anything I should not eat or do? Wife will cook whatever you say.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Eat only soft food — rice, dal, plain things. Drink only boiled or filtered water. Do not go near that construction site water area. Watch out for any bleeding from gums, nose, or in stool — that is a danger sign, come back immediately. Also, your anxiety disorder medicines continue as before, do not stop those.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Thank you doctor, you explained very clearly. I will tell my wife also. We will come back in three days.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Ah, Mrs. Sharma! How are the children? Your son must have finished his board exams by now, no?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, he passed well, thank God. And your family is well?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: All fine, all fine. Now tell me, what is bringing you in today? I heard from the surgeon you need clearance before the operation.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, but I have been having fever for three months now, every morning it comes and goes. I am also having difficulty swallowing sometimes.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Hmm, fever every morning is not good before any surgery. Is there any rash on the skin or joint pain?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: No rash doctor, but there is a pressure-like feeling in my head and sometimes a stabbing pain in the abdomen. Also an aching feeling in my legs.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any insect bites recently? We have had many dengue cases in this area.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, correct, I was bitten many times last summer when we went to the village. I did not think much of it at the time.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: And any vomiting, diarrhoea, or pain near the intestine area?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Ahh, yes doctor, some loose motions on and off, and there is discomfort near the intestine side. Appetite loss is also there.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I see. Any history of blood pressure or sugar problem in the past? Any old illness I should know about?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, I was told I had anxiety disorder during pregnancy. They had given me sertraline for some time but I stopped it on my own. No blood pressure or sugar problem as such.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Did you take any other medicines? Some doctors give multivitamins or simvastatin sometimes for cholesterol — any of those?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Umm, I am taking multivitamins only, doctor. Nothing else regularly. No simvastatin or anything like that.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Alright. Do you smoke or drink wine? Any other habits I should know?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor I am a social smoker only, very rarely. I do have a glass of wine at parties sometimes. I have to be honest, I tried cocaine once or twice at a friend's gathering, but that is all.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Mrs. Sharma, looking at everything — the every morning fever, insect bites history, appetite loss, pain near the intestine, the pattern is suggesting typhoid or possibly dengue. We need to confirm before we can clear you for surgery.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Oh God doctor, typhoid means? Will it delay my operation?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Yes, it will delay things a little, but your safety comes first. We cannot give anaesthesia when there is active infection and fever. We must treat this fully first.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Have you done any blood tests recently? I want to do a coagulation test, Widal test, and dengue NS1 antigen test today.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: No doctor, no tests were done. The surgeon just asked me to come to you for clearance. I did not know all this was needed.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: No worries, we will sort it out. I am starting you on azithromycin for the suspected typhoid, and also continue your multivitamins. If the dengue NS1 antigen test comes positive, we will adjust treatment accordingly.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Please avoid any wine or cocaine completely — they will interfere with the medicines and your liver is already under stress from the infection. Also watch for any bleeding tendencies since your coagulation test is still pending.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, about my anxiety disorder — should I restart sertraline? I have been feeling low and stressed with all this.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Let us wait for the test results first, Mrs. Sharma. Once the fever settles and the infection is treated, we can revisit the sertraline. For now focus on rest, plenty of fluids, light food, and report back in three days with your reports. We will get you cleared for the surgery soon, do not worry.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Hello, come in, please sit down. So you are a college student, yes? And you have brought your younger sibling's reports today?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, my little sister, she is seven years old. She had fever and diarrhoea few days ago and we did some tests.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Okay, let me look at these reports. Before that, tell me — is she still having fever or loose motion now?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: The loose motion is less frequent now, but she still complains of stomach pain after every meal.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any vomiting or burning sensation in the chest or throat area? Sometimes children this age get acidity along with stomach infection.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Umm, yes doctor, she does say something is burning inside her chest, after that incident she started saying this. I did not understand what it was.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I see. Now let me ask — does she have any allergies? Any past history of pneumonia or breathing problems?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, she had pneumonia once when she was four. And she has some dust allergies, the doctor had told us then. Also she has epilepsy, doctor — she is on medicines for that over a year now.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Okay, that is important. Does she have any pets at home, or is there any mold or dampness in the house? Sometimes that can trigger her allergies.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Ahh, we had a cat but we gave it away. And yes, one corner of our room has some dampness, maybe mold also, we have been meaning to fix it.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: That needs to be fixed soon. Now, tell me — do you or anyone at home smoke? Because smoke is very bad for a child with her kind of history.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: My father used to smoke but not anymore. I myself started drinking since college, but only rarely, nothing major doctor.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Okay, I am not judging you, but do take care of your own health too. Now let me summarise what I see in the reports — the AST level is mildly elevated, which means her liver is a little stressed, possibly from the infection.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, AST — what is that? I am not understanding these numbers at all.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: No worries — AST is a simple blood test that tells us how the liver is functioning. When it is high, it means the liver has some irritation. In her case, the diarrhoea and fever from the infection may have caused this. I also want to do a thyroid test because her fatigue and stomach pain can sometimes be linked to thyroid as well.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Okay doctor. And what about this burning she says in the chest? Is that serious?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Yes, that burning sensation combined with her stomach pain after every meal — I think she has developed esophagitis. That means the inner lining of her food pipe is inflamed and irritated. It is not dangerous if we treat it now.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Esophagitis — so that means the food pipe is having swelling inside? Because of the acidity?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Exactly, you understood correctly. The acidity from the infection and also her allergies may have irritated the food pipe lining, causing esophagitis and this burning sensation.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: So what medicines should we give her, doctor? She is also on epilepsy medicines already, so I want to make sure nothing clashes.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Good that you mentioned that. I am prescribing syrup omeprazole once in the morning before food — that will reduce the acidity and help heal the esophagitis. I am also adding ORS sachets to be given whenever she has loose motion, to prevent dehydration. Continue her existing anti-epileptic medicine as before — do not stop that.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Anything we should avoid giving her to eat, doctor? And should she go to school?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Avoid spicy food and fried food completely for at least two weeks — they will make the esophagitis worse. Give her small meals, not large ones. And keep her away from the damp area at home because of her allergies — the mold can trigger coughing and more chest irritation. She can go to school once the fever is completely gone for two days.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: And the thyroid test — should we do that today itself or later?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Do the thyroid test and repeat AST after two weeks. Come back with those reports and we will see if her liver levels have normalised and whether thyroid needs any attention. Take care, and fix that damp wall soon — it is important for her health.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Come in, please sit. How are you feeling today?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor... today very bad. stomach is paining so much, I can barely sit straight.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Tell me, where exactly is the pain? Is it in the upper abdomen or lower?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Upper side, doctor. And gas also is there frequently. Acidity also coming up, burning in the chest.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any vomiting or nausea? Any loose motion or constipation?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Umm... not really vomiting, but feeling like vomiting. Motion is not proper, constipation is there frequently after surgery.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: This is a post-surgery review. Which surgery did you have, and did anyone run a T4 test for you recently?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Operation was for stone, doctor, kidney stone. That T4 test I am not sure, some test was done but I did not understand the report.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I see. Did any local healer or someone from your rural area give you any medicine before you came to us?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, one man in our village gave some powder and told to mix in water. I was taking that for stomach pain. He said it is herbal only.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: These unverified powders can cause a lot of stomach irritation. Do you have any history of mental health problems, like depression or anxiety?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Ahh... yes, some years back there was tension problem, doctor. They said it is mental health only. I was taking tablet at that time.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Are you currently taking any opioids or strong pain medicines prescribed by anyone?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, some pain tablet they gave after operation, I am still taking opioids. The pain is too much so I continued.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Opioids can cause constipation and gas trouble, that is likely worsening your stomach symptoms. Are you non-vegetarian? Heavy oily food?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, non-vegetarian we are. And I am also smoking — two packs a day for many years. My son keeps scolding me.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I see. Based on everything, this is a case of post-operative gastritis with acid reflux and opioid-induced constipation. The smoking and oily food and the quack powder are all making the stomach lining very irritated.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor the burning in my chest is very severe especially after eating. I cannot sleep also.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Is the pain worse after meals? Any bloating or belching also?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, bloating is there and belching also frequently. After eating it becomes worse.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I am prescribing pantoprazole tablet once in the morning empty stomach, domperidone before meals for the nausea and gas, and lactulose syrup for the constipation. Stop that powder from the village man immediately.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor the opioids also I should stop? But pain is too much in the abdomen side.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: We will taper the opioids slowly, not stop suddenly. I will give you tramadol at a lower dose and see how the pain is managed. Also we will repeat the T4 and do a abdominal ultrasound to check for any remaining stone issue.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Please stop smoking completely — two packs a day is very harmful for your stomach lining and healing. Avoid non-vegetarian oily food for at least one month, and do not consult any local quack in your rural area again.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Okay doctor, I will try. Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Hello there, come in, come in. No need to be scared, just relax.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Umm, okay doctor. My grandmother asked me to come. I have been having hoarseness in my throat since last two weeks.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Alright. Is it painful? Any fever or cough also?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: It is slightly painful, doctor. No fever as such. Also I get loose stools, it is happening more often lately.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any burning sensation in your stomach or chest?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Ahh, yes doctor, there is a burning feeling in the stomach more often lately. My wrist also pains sometimes, but that is minor.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Tell me, did you have any health problems as a teenager — any fits or heart problem?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Umm, my grandmother says I had epilepsy when I was small. And my grandfather in the family has heart disease, but I do not have that myself, I think.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any problem with your ovaries or any hormonal issue? And are you currently on blood thinners or any other regular medicine?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: They did a USG last month and found some cyst near the ovaries. I am not on blood thinners or anything regularly. They gave me Advil once for pain but it made my stomach very bad.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Oh, Advil caused a reaction — that is a known allergy then, we will note that. Any crowded places exposure recently, like school events or public transport?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yup, doctor, lots of crowded places — school annual function was there last week, all packed. Maybe that is why the throat got bad.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Do you smoke or use cocaine or any substances? I ask because some teenagers do experiment.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Never doctor, I promise. I do not use cocaine or anything like that. I only drink tea, quite a lot though, for 20 years — oh wait, I am only 16, my grandmother says that, she has been giving me tea since I was small.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Ha, understood. No alcohol either? Sometimes boys say 2 drinks a week casually.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yup, honestly never doctor. I am too scared of all that.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Okay. Based on everything — the hoarseness, loose stools, burning in the stomach, and the recent crowded places contact — this looks like a throat infection with associated gastritis. The ovaries cyst we will address separately.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Umm, so the hoarseness will go away, doctor? And what about the wrist pain?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Yes, the hoarseness should resolve with treatment. For the wrist pain, since it is mild, we will monitor. Avoid Advil completely given the allergy — use safer options only.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: What medicine are you giving, doctor? I am a bit scared of medicines.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: No worries. I am prescribing azithromycin for the throat infection — it is safe and easy to take. For the gastritis and burning, I will add a proton pump inhibitor tablet, and ORS sachets for the loose stools.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Should I avoid anything, doctor? Anything about the ovaries cyst also?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Avoid crowded places for a few days, drink plenty of fluids, and reduce tea intake as it worsens gastritis. Since you have history of epilepsy, continue regular follow up for that. For the ovaries cyst, repeat USG in three months.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Okay doctor. What about my wrist pain? It is slightly painful especially in the morning.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: That morning stiffness with wrist pain is something to watch — since we cannot give Advil due to your allergy, do warm compress for now and if it does not improve in two weeks come back, we will do an X-ray and check for inflammation.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Good to see you back. How are you feeling after the discharge?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Umm, still some discomfort doctor, mainly in the lower part. The paining is there once a week.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Is the paining near the buttocks area also, or only lower part?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Mostly buttocks, doctor. It is cramping type, worse at night.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Right. Your bone marrow biopsy results came back. Did you check the temperature chart I asked you to maintain?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes, doctor. Before the tests, temperature was a bit high, around 99 to 100 degrees.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any history of surgery before this hospitalisation, or blood transfusion at any point?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes, I had blood transfusion after that old surgery for piles. Also had a broken bone in my upper part of the lower part leg 6-7 months back.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any pesticides or chemical exposure? Do you work near a construction site?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Ahh, yes doctor, I work on a construction site. There was some mercury handling also at previous job, and pesticides from childhood as we had farm land.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Do you e-cigarettes use?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, a pack a day roughly. Also I do exercise 30 minutes daily.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any weight gain noticed recently? Any fatigue or joint pain?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes, weight gain is there doctor, around 5 kilos. fatigue also, especially at upper part of the body after evening.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: We had ordered a DEXA scan as well. Have you done it?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes, I got it done before the tests at your pathology centre only. Report is here.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Looking at the bone marrow biopsy, DEXA scan, and your history of exposures, this is consistent with bone marrow suppression secondary to toxic mercury and pesticides exposure, along with osteopenia. The piles and hernia complications from before have added stress on the body.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, is the weight gain related to this also?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: The weight gain is partly from reduced activity post-surgery and partly from fatigue limiting your movement. The cramping worse at night is related to bone marrow suppression and low haemoglobin.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I am prescribing atorvastatin for lipid management given the weight gain, pantoprazole for gastric irritation from all the medicines, and azithromycin short course for the low-grade fever.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, should I continue e-cigarettes?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Absolutely no. e-cigarettes are worsening your bone marrow suppression. Stop immediately. Also avoid construction site dust and any pesticides contact.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Am I  the medicines correctly? I am taking pantoprazole before food only.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Yes, pantoprazole should be taken before food, that is correct. atorvastatin take at night. Come back after 6-7 months for repeat bone marrow biopsy and DEXA scan to track progress.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Okay doctor, thank you.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: So you were referred back from the higher centre. Tell me, what all has been going on?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, honestly my stomach has been giving me trouble three times a week, and also I wanted to ask about my wife's pregnancy — she is having bleeding too.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Let us first focus on you. You are saying your stomach is troubling you — is it more of a cramping pain or a burning kind of pain?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Umm, it is mildly uncomfortable mostly, not too severe, but sometimes there is bloating also. Doctor, can I also ask about pet dander — my neighbour has cats and I am sneezing a lot.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: We will get to the pet dander allergy in a moment. First, any loose motion or blood in stool?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Ahh, yes doctor, loose motion is there since three days ago, and once or twice there was some blood also. My intestine area feels very uncomfortable.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any history of previous operation on your abdomen or intestine?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes, I had a previous operation for a stomach ulcer about four years back. They said there was some ulcer problem in the stomach.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: And are you drinking alcohol currently? How much?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Uh, doctor, I will be honest — I am drinking regularly. Also I smoke about 10 cigarettes a day. I also drink a lot of tea, maybe five cups.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: That is quite a lot. Any family history of Crohn's disease or bowel problems?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: No doctor, nothing like that in family. But doctor, my wife is also not doing well — she had vomiting and dizziness in the pregnancy. Can I ask about that?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I understand your concern for your wife, but let me finish your assessment first. We have ordered a AST test because with your alcohol history, liver damage is a concern. Did the higher centre do any blood work?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: They did some tests but I do not remember the names. They gave me some antibiotics for three days and said to come back here. I also took some antihistamines on my own for the sneezing from the cats.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Taking antihistamines on your own is not advisable. Now, the sneezing and runny nose — did they start after contact with the cats or were they there before?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Only after the cats came, doctor. And the itching in my eyes also started then. That pet dander is really troubling me.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Alright, so based on everything — the blood in stool, three times a week bowel disturbance, and your history of stomach ulcer — this looks like possible Crohn's disease or a recurrence of stomach ulcer. A new ulcer in the intestine is unlikely but cannot be ruled out without further testing.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, what is this Crohn's disease? I have not heard of it before.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Crohn's disease is a condition where the intestine becomes inflamed and causes cramping, loose motion, and bleeding. The drinking and smoking are making it much worse, I must tell you.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Ahh, I see. I will try my best doctor, it is not easy with the work pressure.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I understand. Now I am prescribing you antibiotics to continue for the infection, and I am also adding antihistamines properly for the pet dander allergy — but at the correct dose.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, is there anything I should avoid eating? And what about my tea — can I still drink it?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Reduce the tea to one or two cups, as it irritates the stomach lining. Completely stop the drinking — the AST result will tell us how much liver damage has happened already. Avoid spicy and oily food.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: And for my wife's bleeding in the pregnancy — she is also feeling breathlessness and mildly uncomfortable at night. Should she come here separately?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Yes, she must come separately as soon as possible — bleeding and breathlessness in pregnancy need immediate evaluation. For you, come back once the AST result is ready so we can plan the next step for your intestine properly.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Please come in, sit down. What has brought you here today?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, I am having very severe pain in my lower abdomen since two weeks ago. It is becoming too much to bear now.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: How many months pregnant are you, and is this pain in the lower abdomen constant or does it come and go?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: I am seven months along doctor. The pain is there sometimes, not all the time. It gets better when I lie on my left side.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any bleeding from down below? Any discharge or leaking of water?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Umm, no bleeding doctor, but I did notice some discharge that was slightly yellowish quite a while ago. Now it has mostly stopped.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any headache, blurring of vision, or swelling in the hands and feet?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: My feet are swollen doctor, yes. And sometimes I get headache also, but I thought it was just weakness.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Have you had any antenatal checkups since the pregnancy started? Any blood pressure monitoring done?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Ahh, doctor we are very poor, we cannot afford too many visits. I had one checkup since 2024 when the pregnancy was confirmed, that is all. No money for more tests.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I understand. Any kidney problem, hypertension, or diabetes before this pregnancy?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: No doctor, nothing like that. No such history in family also.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Do you drink alcohol? I need you to be honest with me, it is important for your baby's health.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Umm... doctor I used to drink, but never heavily. I stopped after I found out about the pregnancy. I did not want to harm the baby.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any birds at home or nearby? Or any other animal contact that you can recall?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: We have pigeons on our terrace, yes doctor. There are many birds there. Why are you asking about that?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I will explain shortly. Is the pain also near the intestine area? Any nausea or vomiting?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, sometimes it feels like it is deep inside near the intestine. I have had nausea also but I thought that is normal in pregnancy only.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Looking at your swelling, your headache, and this lower abdomen pain, I believe this is a case of preeclampsia. I have ruled out a simple urinary tract infection for now, but we need urgent tests.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Preeclampsia? Doctor, what is that? Is my baby okay? Please tell me, I am very worried.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: It is a dangerous blood pressure complication in pregnancy. We need to do urine protein test, CBC, liver function test, and an obstetric ultrasound right away. We must monitor the baby closely.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I am starting you on labetalol for controlling your blood pressure and magnesium sulphate injection to prevent any seizures. You will also need calcium supplements and low dose aspirin as well.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, these medicines — are they available in the government hospital? I truly cannot afford private pharmacy rates. We have no money at all.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Do not worry, these are all available free at the government hospital. I am referring you there immediately. You must not delay or the preeclampsia can progress to eclampsia with fits, which is very dangerous for both you and the baby. Also, absolutely never take any alcohol again, not even a little.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Okay doctor, I understand. Thank you so much. I will go right away with my husband.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Hello, welcome. Please sit down comfortably.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Thank you doctor. I am a shopkeeper. I have come for a second opinion because the other doctor's advice is not giving me confidence. I am very restless and worried from long time.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I understand. Please don't worry, we will sort this out together. Tell me, what exact stomach pain or acidity complaint are you having?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, I am having stabbing pain in my lower part of the stomach. Also gas trouble and bloating are there nonstop. Uh, and acidity is coming up twice a week at least.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Is there any nausea or vomiting also? Any pain going up to the chest or head?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yup, doctor, sometimes my head is also paining along with this. And mild nausea is there intermittently. I got scared thinking it may be something serious in my stomach.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Did these complaints start after surgery or was it before only? And did you bring any previous reports?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, many of these problems started after surgery — I had a small operation last year. I brought the ultrasonography report also with me. The other doctor said nothing major but I am still not satisfied.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Okay, let me see the ultrasonography report. Also, do you have any past history of heart attack or stroke? Any anxiety disorder?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, I had a heart attack some years back, and yes, I have been diagnosed with anxiety disorder also. No stroke thankfully. Umm, because of anxiety disorder I am already taking fluoxetine daily.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Are you on any other medicines? Like prednisone or hydrochlorothiazide? These can sometimes aggravate acidity.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, I am taking prednisone for some inflammation and hydrochlorothiazide for my blood pressure. Could these be causing my stomach pain?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Yes, prednisone especially is known to irritate the stomach lining and worsen acidity and gas trouble. This is most likely a contributing factor. Please do not worry — this is manageable.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Do you have any exposure to fumes or chemicals in your shop environment? Sometimes that triggers gastric irritation.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Umm, yes doctor, there are some paint fumes in the area near my shop. I sit there for 1 hour daily at least. Also I think I had a mild viral infection recently which made everything worse.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I see. Do you take your food on time or do you skip meals? And are you eating anything spicy after meals often?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, I skip meals many times. And I do have tea and snacks after meals also. I take a lot of stress because of the shop — customer problems, financial worries, it is daily. I cannot stop this stress.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Based on everything — your acidity, stabbing pain in the lower part, gas trouble, prednisone use, exposure to fumes, and the stress — this is a case of gastritis with irritable bowel syndrome. Your anxiety disorder is also making the stomach symptoms worse. Please do not panic — this is very treatable.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, I was so scared it was something like another heart attack again. What should I do now? Should I stop prednisone? And what about the viral infection?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Do not stop prednisone on your own — we will speak to your other doctor about reducing the dose gradually. The viral infection has settled most likely, but it has left your gut a little sensitive. Take small, light meals on time, avoid spicy food, reduce tea intake, and please try to manage your stress.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I am prescribing pantoprazole tablet in the morning on empty stomach, domperidone after meals three times, and antacid syrup as needed for immediate acidity relief. Continue your fluoxetine as before.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Thank you so much doctor. Any side effects I should watch for? And the head pain — will that go also?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: The headache in your head is mostly tension-related from stress and the acidity — it should settle as gut improves. Watch for any blood in stool or very severe chest pain — if those happen, come immediately. Avoid the fumes area as much as possible.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Should I repeat the ultrasonography report or do any other test doctor?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: The current ultrasonography report looks fine. Let us do a stool routine examination and H. pylori breath test this week. If pain persists or worsens, we will do an upper GI endoscopy also. Come back in two weeks — I am sure you will feel much better by then. No need to be restless about this.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Hello, come in, please sit. How are you feeling today?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Umm... doctor, not so good. I am feeling fatigue all the time and brain fog also is there after surgery.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Okay, can you tell me more? Is there any chest pain or shortness of breath?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Ahh... chest pain is there doctor, stabbing type, severe. Shortness of breath also happens but rarely.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: You had COVID before your surgery, correct? And when exactly was the surgery?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, the surgery was six months ago. COVID I got very recently, maybe two months back only.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Are you having any headache, tinnitus, or hearing difficulty? Some post-COVID patients report ear problems.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Umm... ringing in the ear is there almost never, but hearing difficulty I am noticing very recently doctor. I am very shy to say but memory issues also.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any known allergies to medicines or food that I should know?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Currently I have allergies to penicillin, doctor. I got rash last time.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Good you told me. Now, were you exposed to anyone sick at work or home? Any coworker was sick or family member was sick situation?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, both actually. Coworker was sick first, then at home also family member was sick. I do night shifts so my immunity must be low also.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I see. What about workplace environment? Any asbestos or chemical exposure in your office building?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Ahh... asbestos, I am not sure doctor. The building is old, they did some renovation very recently. I sit near that area.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Are you taking your post-surgery medicines regularly? And are you doing any physical activity like gym?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Honestly doctor, I am missing doses sometimes. Gym I was doing 30 minutes daily before, but after surgery I have stopped completely.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Based on everything — the chest symptoms, fatigue, brain fog, and your COVID history — this looks like long COVID syndrome, also called post-acute sequelae of COVID. Pulmonary fibrosis has been ruled out for now based on your earlier chest X-ray reports.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, is this serious? Will the fatigue and chest pain go away?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: It is manageable but you must not miss doses and you should get proper sleep. Night shifts are making things worse for your fatigue and brain fog. We need to check your heart rate and blood sugar today, and also refer you for a hearing test for the ear complaints.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Okay doctor. Should I also worry about the asbestos exposure from that renovation?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Yes, we should keep an eye on it. If breathlessness or dry cough worsens, come immediately. Avoid sitting near that renovation area and wear a dust mask at work.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I am prescribing Vitamin C tablets once daily, coenzyme Q10 supplements, and low-dose aspirin for the chest discomfort. Since you have allergies to penicillin, I am avoiding all beta-lactam group medicines.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, can I restart gym now? I want to do at least 30 minutes daily again.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Start slowly, only light walking for now. Do not push yourself. Palpitations or dizziness during exercise — stop immediately and come back. Once your heart rate and blood sugar results are reviewed, we will decide on full gym resumption.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Thank you so much doctor. I will follow properly this time, I promise.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Good morning, please sit. How are you feeling after the surgery?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, umm, I am feeling better than before but still having some pain in my upper abdomen twice a day, especially after meals.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Is the pain worse after eating? Which foods seem to trigger it?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, it is worse after eating oily food. Sometimes it also comes on and off even without eating much.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any nausea or vomiting also? Any bloating in the stomach?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: The nausea is there multiple times a day, doctor. And yes, there is bloating also, especially in the evening.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: You had a complicated delivery last time, correct? Any family history of gallbladder issue or liver disease?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, my mother had a gallbladder issue and she had surgery for it also. My elder sister also has some gallstone problem.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I see. And you yourself were diagnosed with gestational diabetes during this pregnancy, right? When was that detected?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: That was detected a year ago only, during my seventh month checkup. Before that I had no sugar problem at all.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Okay. Do you smoke or drink alcohol? Please be honest, it helps in your treatment.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Ahh, doctor, I quit drinking completely when I got pregnant. Before that I used to drink socially only, very rarely, at family occasions.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Good that you stopped. Were you smoking at any point, even as a teenager?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Umm, yes, I had tried smoking as a teenager but I quit long before marriage. I am currently not doing any of that.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Good. Have you had any yellowing of your eyes or skin? Any itching anywhere?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: No, no yellowing doctor. But there is some itching on the skin on and off. I thought it was due to pollen because the season changed.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Possible, yes. The pollen can cause skin rash or itching. Any fever or chills after the surgery?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: No fever doctor, but I had some constipation issue for the first few days. That is better now thankfully.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Based on your symptoms, the family history, and your post-operative condition, this looks like post-cholecystectomy syndrome combined with residual bile duct irritation. The gestational diabetes also needs continued monitoring.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, this post-surgery pain — will it go away on its own or do I need more treatment?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: It should settle with proper diet and medicines. We will also order a liver function test, ultrasound abdomen, and a fasting blood glucose to keep track of your diabetes.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Okay doctor, thank you. My husband is also there outside, he is very worried.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Tell him not to worry. I am prescribing pantoprazole for the bloating and nausea, domperidone for digestion, and ursodeoxycholic acid to help the bile flow properly. Take all medicines twice a day after food.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Avoid all oily and fried foods strictly. The worse after eating pattern will improve once you follow the diet. Also avoid any pollen exposure if the itching is bothering you.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: I will follow everything doctor. I just want the pain in my upper abdomen to fully go away before I start caring for the baby properly.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Hello, please sit down. How are you feeling today?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: I am okay doctor, just came for the review after the operation.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Right, this is your post-surgery review. Tell me, any pain or discomfort in the abdomen area since we did the procedure?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Umm, for six months I had a lot of pain in the lower abdomen, but not anymore doctor, it has settled down mostly.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Good. Any bleeding or discharge from the wound site? Any swelling?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: denied, nothing like that doctor. The wound is fine. But sometimes I get sharp pain in the lower abdomen, every other day, especially at night.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: That sharp pain — is it worse at night or also in the daytime?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Mostly worse at night doctor. During the day I am doing my labour work so I am not noticing, but at night it troubles me frequently.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Okay. Any nausea, vomiting, or loose motion? How is your bowel?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Ahh, loose motion is there on and off doctor. And my abdomen feels crampy sometimes. They had told me I have some colitis also, I think.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Yes, the ultrasonography report did show some inflammation. Any history of pneumonia or any lung problem before?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: true doctor, I had pneumonia 6-7 months back, around the same time as the pregnancy complication. I was given some antibiotics at that time.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any cough or breathlessness now? Any fever?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: denied doctor, no fever, no cough. But I am having knee pain on and off, especially in the calf area also it is paining.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: The knee pain — any swelling or redness near the calf? Any history of insect bites recently?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Umm, yes doctor, I work outside a lot. There is some insect bites happening. One of the children also had some rash — someone at school had spread an infection, they said.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Alright. Do you smoke or take liquor?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, I take liquor on weekends only. And I smoke 10 cigarettes a day. I also do some physical exercise, 1 hour daily, as part of my labour work only.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: We should do a BUN test to check your kidney function, and also schedule a follow-up ultrasonography report for the abdomen. Have you been taking any medicines currently?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: I was taking some antihistamines for the skin rash from the insect bites, doctor. Otherwise nothing else.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Looking at all your symptoms — the colitis, the sharp pain in the lower abdomen, and the post-operative history — this appears to be a case of post-surgical colitis with secondary bowel inflammation. The knee pain and calf discomfort may be related to the insect bites causing a reactive response.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, what should I do about this? Will the colitis go away? I am worried because the sharp pain in abdomen is very troubling at night.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I am prescribing amoxicillin for the infection component, and continue antihistamines for the rash and allergic reaction from the bites. Avoid liquor completely till the colitis settles.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Also, please reduce smoking — it is affecting your recovery. No heavy lifting in your labour work for now. Come back after the BUN result and the follow-up scan for proper reassessment of the abdomen.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Okay doctor, I will do the BUN test and come back for the follow-up. I will try to manage the smoking also. Thank you doctor.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Hello, come in, come in. No need to be nervous, I will not bite!

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Umm... doctor, my family brought me here. I have been having puffy eyes over a year now and also some rash on my elbow.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Okay, tell me more. Is the rash on your elbow clear or is it scaly and crusted?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Ahh... it is, umm, clear mostly doctor. Not too dirty looking. And the puffy eyes are nonstop, like all the time.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any itching or burning sensation around the elbow area? Any watering from eyes?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: I think so, yes, some itching is there. And the watering from eyes has become less frequent now compared to before.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any known heat or pollution exposure? Like travelling in open vehicles or working near fire?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Umm, yes doctor. I play sports outside on weekends and the area near my house has a lot of pollution.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any family history of epilepsy or allergy conditions? And does anyone at home drink alcohol?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Nah, none of the allergy thing in family. But my grandfather had epilepsy. And my uncle drinks alcohol on weekends, not me doctor, I promise.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Good, good. Now has anyone in the family had a hip replacement or any previous operation related to allergy issues or skin?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Uh, my grandmother had a hip replacement and also one previous operation on her knee I think. Not related to skin, doctor.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Have you done any skin test or COVID test recently? Any tests done before coming here?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: We did a COVID test last month — it was negative. None of the skin test has been done, doctor.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Are you taking any medicines currently? Any herbal or home remedy for this rash or puffy eyes?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: My family is giving me some herbal leaf paste on the elbow. And doctor, someone told to take omeprazole for the stomach upset, so I took it two times.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Okay, and is there any shortness of breath or sneezing that comes along with the puffy eyes? Does it get worse with heat?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Umm, I think so doctor, when it is very hot outside the puffy eyes becomes more. And some sneezing also comes all the time during that period.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Looking at all this — the puffy eyes, itching, rash on elbow, and worsening with pollution and heat — this is a case of allergic dermatitis combined with allergic conjunctivitis.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Ahh, doctor, is it something serious? My family was very worried about these puffy eyes going on over a year.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: It is manageable, no need to panic. We will do a proper skin test to identify the exact allergen. Please stop the herbal leaf paste as it may worsen the rash on your elbow.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Okay doctor, I will tell my family to stop that.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I am prescribing cetirizine tablet once at night for the itching and puffy eyes, and a mild hydrocortisone cream to apply on the elbow rash twice daily. Also continue the omeprazole only if you have stomach upset, otherwise stop it.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Avoid playing sports in peak afternoon heat, wear full sleeves to protect your elbow, and use a mask when going out in pollution. No alcohol ever at your age, and never self-medicate.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Thank you doctor, I will follow all this carefully.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Come in, come in. Please sit. How are you doing today?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Managing only doctor, life is like that only.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: This is your annual check-up, correct? Any specific complaints you want to tell me about?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, I am feeling very tired and weak for two years now. Also there is cough on and off.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: This tiredness — is it constant or coming and going? Any dizziness or shortness of breath?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, dizziness is there multiple times a day. And when I climb stairs or run to catch my auto, breathlessness is coming more often lately. Very disturbing doctor.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any pale skin or yellowing of your eyes? Any palpitations or headache?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: My wife said my face is looking pale doctor. Headache is also there sometimes. No yellowing I think.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Tell me, do you eat properly? Vegetables, dal, all that? Any loss of appetite?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Honestly doctor, eating is not proper. I skip meals many times. My wife is sick so cooking is also not happening properly at home. And umm, loss of appetite is there for two years itself.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I see. You are also caring for your sick family member — that is a lot of stress. Do you drink alcohol? And do you smoke?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Ahh, doctor... little bit only drinking. Daily it is happening but not too much. Smoking also — two packs a day I am doing, since many years.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Two packs a day is quite heavy. Any recreational drugs usage? And how much screen time are you spending — sometimes people complain of eye strain or sleep disturbance because of mobile.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: No doctor, no recreational drugs. Screen time is there after meals only, watching some videos to relax. Driving all day is very tiring.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any hospital visit recently for your wife's care? Any cats or other pets at home?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, hospital visit is happening regularly, taking wife for her treatment. And we have two cats at home, my children's pets.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Okay. Any past medical history? Any major surgeries or childhood illnesses like chickenpox?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, I had chickenpox when I was young. And my father had bypass surgery — does that matter? For me nothing major surgery happened.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Family history is also important, yes. Now regarding this cough and tiredness — have you done any tests before? Any endoscopy done ever, given that you are a regular drinker?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: No doctor, no endoscopy I did. Only blood test once, two years back, but I lost the report. Nothing was told to me seriously at that time.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Based on your tiredness, dizziness, pale skin, poor diet, and heavy alcohol use, you are showing signs of anaemia with likely nutritional deficiency — iron deficiency and vitamin B12 deficiency. The alcohol is damaging your stomach lining also.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, is it serious? My family is depending on me. What should I do?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: We will manage this. I am prescribing ferrous sulphate tablets — one tablet after meals twice daily, and methylcobalamin supplement daily for the B12 deficiency. Also, multivitamin syrup in the morning. For the cough I am giving ambroxol syrup.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Now most importantly — the alcohol must stop or reduce drastically. It is blocking iron absorption and causing gastric irritation. We need to do complete blood count, serum ferritin, vitamin B12 levels, and endoscopy given your drinking history. Reduce smoking also — two packs a day is very harmful for your lungs and heart.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Okay doctor, I will try my best. Can you also check my chest for the cough? It is dry type and happening multiple times a day, more in the morning.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Come in, come in. Please sit down. You look tired today.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, it is very difficult. I drive auto all day, no energy left.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Okay, what is the main problem you are coming for today? We need to check you before your operation.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, itching is there all over, my entire body is paining and redness also coming on eyes sometimes.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: How long is this itching going on? And is there any swelling on the skin?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Umm, it started a year ago doctor. Swelling also comes, gets worse when I am outside in the heat. Rash is also there on my arms.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Does the itching happen often or only sometimes? Any breathlessness or throat tightness when it happens?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Ahh, hardly ever there is breathlessness doctor. But throat tightness I felt quite a while ago, once only.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Do you stay in a rural area? Any exposure to plants, animals, or chemicals while driving?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, I stay in rural area only. There is lots of dust and sometimes pesticide smell near the farms on my route.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any known allergy to medicines or food items? Do you drink alcohol?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, I drink 3 beers a day. Medicine allergy I do not know. Food allergy also I am not sure.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Do you take caffeine — meaning tea or coffee — how much regularly?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Tea I take, but caffeine like strong coffee I take rarely only doctor. Just normal chai two times.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Okay. Did you do any blood test or skin prick allergy test before?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: No doctor, nothing like that. I went to one local doctor who gave some tablet but I do not remember the name. Itching came down for some days then returned.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I see. Based on what you are telling — the itching, redness of eyes, rash on arms, and swelling — this looks like chronic allergic urticaria. It is a kind of allergy reaction happening in your body.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, allergy only? Then operation can happen or not?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Yes, we can clear you for operation, but first we need your allergy to be controlled. We will do a complete blood count, IgE level test, and liver function test because of your alcohol intake. These results must be okay before surgery.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Okay doctor. Also sometimes my eyes are watering a lot and burning sensation is there in my chest also.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: That burning in the chest — is it regularly or only after eating? Any vomiting?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: After eating sometimes doctor. Vomiting is no. Just acid reflux feeling coming.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Alright. I am prescribing cetirizine 10 mg once daily for the itching and rash, pantoprazole for the acid reflux, and eye drops for the eye redness and watering. Take these for ten days.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Also, you must stop or reduce your alcohol drinking — 3 beers a day is too much before operation. It can worsen allergic reaction and affect your liver function test results. Avoid dust and pesticide exposure as much as possible.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Okay doctor, I will try. Thank you for explaining properly, I understand now.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Good morning, Mr. Rajan. Please sit, sit. How are you keeping these days?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Good morning doctor. Managing only, you know how it is at this age.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Yes yes, understood. Now you were just discharged last week, so tell me — what new complaints are you having? Any chest pain or palpitations?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, uh-huh, that chest pain is still there. It is sharp pain near my chest, and I am getting palpitations also more often lately.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Is the pain throbbing or does it feel heavy on the chest? Any breathlessness along with it?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Mostly it is heavy feeling doctor, like someone is pressing. Breathlessness also comes twice a day sometimes. And the palpitations started coming from long time but now it is worse after discharge.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Now tell me, are you having any stiffness in the joints, especially in the morning? And any swelling in hands or feet?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Ahh, yes doctor, that stiffness is there for two years. My whole body feels stiff in the morning. My daughter was saying it might be some bone problem only.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Okay, and do you have any known history of osteoporosis or epilepsy? Any past diagnosis your previous doctor gave?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, osteoporosis they said something about bones being weak, that was told before the tests were done last year. Epilepsy I had it when I was younger but it is controlled now, no fits for two years.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Good. Now regarding your habits — are you doing any exercise? Were you into any sports before? And are you still smoking?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, exercise and sports I was very regular, since I was young I used to play cricket and walk also. But smoking I did for many years, stopped only after my heart problem came.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Good that you stopped. Any pets at home or sick contact recently — anyone in family having fever or cough?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: No doctor, no pets we are keeping. And no sick contact also — everyone at home is fine only.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Alright. Any burning in the throat or chest after eating — like esophagitis type of feeling, acid coming up?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Umm, yes doctor, that burning also is there after meals. I thought it was gastric only. It is coming more often lately, especially at night when I lie down.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Currently what medicines are you taking? Are you on amlodipine for your blood pressure? And anything for the gastric?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, amlodipine I am taking twice a day as you prescribed last time. For gastric they gave omeprazole during hospital admission, but I stopped it after discharge.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
