utterances.text: Doctor: Okay, now I want to order some tests. We need a kidney function test because of your long-term medicines, a DEXA scan for the bone density, and also a genetic test to see if there is any inherited tendency for your joint and bone issues.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, why genetic test? Is there something serious? And what about the stiffness — is it related to my chest pain?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Mr. Rajan, I will be straightforward with you. The stiffness in whole body, the joint swelling, and the pattern over for two years — this is consistent with rheumatoid arthritis. The chest pain and palpitations we must investigate further for cardiac cause, and the burning is esophagitis from acid reflux.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Ahh, rheumatoid arthritis — I have heard of it but never thought it would affect the whole body like this. Doctor, what about the ovaries problem my wife was mentioning — she said same type of stiffness can come from there also?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: In males the ovaries are not applicable of course, but hormonal causes we will keep in mind. For now the DEXA scan and kidney function test results will guide us. The sharp pain in chest needs an ECG and 2D echocardiogram also — I will add those orders.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Now for medicines — please restart omeprazole twice a day before meals for the esophagitis. Continue amlodipine as before for blood pressure. I am also adding a low-dose aspirin and referring you to a rheumatologist for the rheumatoid arthritis management.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Okay doctor, I will follow properly. Should I avoid any food or exercise for now? I am a bit worried about the palpitations coming when I walk.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Hello, come in, come in. Please sit down comfortably.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Thank you doctor. Umm, I came because my legs are having swelling again and I am feeling very tired also.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I see. When did this swelling come back? And is it only in the legs or somewhere else also?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: It came back very recently doctor. Both legs only, from ankle going upward. It is happening twice a week that I notice it really bad.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any breathlessness when walking, or puffiness on your face in the morning?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Ahh, not at all on the face doctor. But yes, breathlessness is there a little when I climb stairs. Also nausea is there sometimes.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Do you have any sugar problem? I mean, diabetes?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, I have diabetes time ago it was found. I am taking tablets for that only.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Are you currently on any beta blockers or any antacids? Any cough syrup you are taking on your own?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: My previous doctor gave me some beta blockers for my BP problem. And yes, I was taking antacids for gas trouble, and cough syrup I bought from medical shop myself very recently because of cough.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Okay, I will note all that down. Have you been around anyone who was unwell? Any coworker was sick or anything like that?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, one coworker was sick at office last month with some infection. Also I have cats at home, and I got a mosquito bite on my arm that was very red and swollen for two days.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any gym or sports activity you are doing? How much water are you drinking?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: I do gym 30 minutes daily doctor, light exercise only. No sports. Water I am drinking less, only two or three glasses maybe.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: We need to check your kidney function. When did you last do a blood test or creatinine test?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, that creatinine — I do not know what that is exactly — I did it time ago and the doctor said some number was high. After that the report is gone, I cannot find it.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: No problem, we will redo it. I want to do a serum creatinine, urine protein test, and blood pressure monitoring today itself.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Umm, doctor the urine protein test — is it costly? My husband is saying do not spend too much this time. Can we skip one test?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I understand, but these tests are very important. The swelling in your legs and the high creatinine together tell me your kidney is under stress. Without the urine protein test I cannot know how serious the leaking from kidney is. It is not very expensive, please do it.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Based on your history of diabetes, high BP, the swelling, and previous high creatinine, this looks like chronic kidney disease — in 2025 we have good ways to manage it if you follow properly.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Chronic kidney disease — doctor, does that mean my kidney will stop working? I am very scared.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Please do not panic. If you control your diabetes and blood pressure, avoid heavy gym work that dehydrates, drink more water, and avoid self-buying cough syrup or antacids without asking me — those can harm the kidney.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I am continuing your beta blockers for BP. I am also adding telmisartan once at night to protect the kidney, and furosemide tablet in the morning for the swelling. Take furosemide after meals only, do not take empty stomach.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, my cats at home — should I remove them? And that mosquito bite area on my arm still has a small rash.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: The cats are okay as long as you maintain hygiene, wash hands well. For the rash on your arm, I will give calamine lotion for local application. Come back in two weeks with all test reports — the serum creatinine, urine protein test, and HbA1c for your sugar check also.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Hello, please come in and sit. Congratulations on your new baby. How are you feeling today?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Thank you doctor. It is my first baby so everything is new for me, I am a little confused only.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: That is okay, take your time. You were referred back from the higher centre — can you tell me what main problem they saw there?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, umm, they said something about my hypertension not settling after delivery. I also get these headache episodes, like very bad, throbbing, happening every few days.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Okay. Any dizziness or numbness also you are feeling?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, dizziness is there nonstop sometimes. And that numbness feeling — it is coming every few days, mainly on my skin and sometimes near my mouth area.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Does the numbness reach your tongue also? Or only around the mouth?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Ahh, yes doctor, the tongue also feels a little strange sometimes, like a tingling. I do not know how to explain it properly.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: No worries, you are explaining well. Any body pain or weakness in the arms or legs?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: There is body pain doctor, for six months now — even during the pregnancy it was there. The higher centre doctor said to mention this here. I get it every few days, not always.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Understood. Do you have any history of kidney stones or kidney problems?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, I had kidney stones few days ago — they found it during one scan at the higher centre. They said it is small only but noted it.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I see. Do you smoke or drink? And before your pregnancy, were you going to gym or doing swimming regularly?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: I used to drink, about 2 drinks a week, but that I have stopped now since pregnancy. My husband is a chain smoker but I myself never smoked. I used to do gym and swimming before, but with delivery and all, that also stopped. Lot of stress nowadays, doctor.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Are you from a rural area? Any exposure to pesticides or chemicals at home or in your surroundings?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, we are from a rural area only, near the fields. My in-laws use some sprays for the crops, so that exposure is there sometimes.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Okay. The higher centre — did they do any MRI or ultrasound for you? And any echocardiogram?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: They did an MRI of my head and one ultrasound for the kidney stones. The echocardiogram they said to do here only, they could not arrange it there. They gave me a referral letter also.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any allergy to any medicine? Did they prescribe anything before sending you here?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, I have allergy to sulpha drugs, I get rash on the skin. They had given me one antihypertensive tablet but I am hardly ever taking it regularly because I am breastfeeding and I was scared.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I understand your concern. Based on your post-partum hypertension, the persistent headache, dizziness, and numbness around your mouth and tongue, along with your MRI findings, this is looking like post-partum hypertensive encephalopathy. The kidney stones are a separate concern we must watch.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, is this dangerous for me? I am breastfeeding also, so I am worried about what medicines are safe.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: It is manageable, do not panic. I am prescribing labetalol tablet for the hypertension — it is safe for breastfeeding. For the headache and body pain, take paracetamol as needed. We will avoid all sulpha-based drugs given your allergy.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Please avoid stress as much as possible, it is making your hypertension worse. No gym or heavy exercise for now. We need to do the echocardiogram today and one repeat ultrasound for the kidney for six months follow-up. Take the labetalol every few days is not okay — it must be taken regularly every day without skipping.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Okay doctor, I will do as you say. Thank you so much for explaining everything clearly.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Hello, welcome. Please sit down comfortably.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Thank you doctor. I am an IT person, doing night shifts, so my schedule is completely off. I came for a refill and also to show this rash on my chest area near the sternum.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Okay, let me have a look. How long has this rash been there, and is there any itching also?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: It started a couple of months back, doctor. There is itching happening more often lately, and the rash is spreading a little on my lower back also now.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Did you travel anywhere recently, like a rural or congested area? Any exposure to contaminated food or unhygienic surroundings?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, I went to a village stay program a couple of months ago. The food and water there were not so clean, definitely some contaminated food must have been taken. And the area had a lot of heat and humidity, which I am not used to.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I see. Any discharge from the rash, or any scaling or ring-shaped patches on the skin?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Umm, yes doctor, there are ring-shaped patches, and a bit of scaling. Also my lower back is red and flaky near the edges.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Based on what I am seeing, this looks like a clear case of fungal infection — specifically tinea corporis. The heat and moisture from your travel, combined with night shift sweating, have made things worse.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Ahh, so it is a fungal infection only? Is that why the itching on my sternum is so bad after every meal especially when I sweat?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Exactly. Sweating after eating and sitting long hours at your desk is worsening the fungal infection. Also, cold weather in your air-conditioned office can cause dryness that makes the rash crack and itch more. You need to keep the area dry and clean.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I am prescribing you clotrimazole cream to apply on the chest and lower back patches twice a day, and fluconazole tablet once a week for four weeks. Also continuing your ranitidine refill as before for your gastric trouble.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, the ranitidine — I have been on it since 2021. My previous doctor started it. Is it still okay to continue?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Yes, ranitidine is fine for now for your acidity. But since you have been on it since 2021, we should monitor. Are you still having heartburn or acidity after every meal?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, the acidity is after every meal, and I drink a lot of coffee also during night shift to stay awake. I have been drinking coffee since I was young, so it is a habit.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Understood. Do you exercise at all? And do you drink alcohol — how many drinks per day roughly?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Ahh, exercise is almost zero doctor with these night shifts. And I take around 3 beers a day to wind down after shift. I know it is not good.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: That 3 beers a day combined with coffee is directly worsening your acidity and also suppressing your immunity, which is making the fungal infection persist. You must cut down alcohol and coffee, and start some exercise even if short walks.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, you mentioned PSA test last time in 2022 — should I repeat it now? I had some urinary frequency also off and on.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Good that you remembered. Since the last PSA test was done in 2022 and you are now reporting urinary frequency, yes we should repeat it. I will also add a urine routine examination and KFT to the order.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Okay doctor. Also sometimes I get lower back pain on my lower back region, which comes more often lately, and I thought it may be from sitting long hours.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Yes, long hours of sitting at the desk causes lower back pain. The cold weather from air conditioning also stiffens the lower back muscles. Start exercise and take short breaks every hour from your desk.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Now let me do a quick teach-back — can you tell me how you will use the clotrimazole cream and the fluconazole tablet that I just prescribed?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Sure doctor — clotrimazole cream I will apply on the chest near the sternum and on the lower back rash twice a day, and fluconazole I will take once a week for four weeks. I will also reduce coffee and alcohol, try to exercise a little, and come back if the itching does not reduce.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Perfect, you have got it right. Also make sure to do the PSA test, urine routine examination, and KFT this week, and come back in three weeks. If the rash spreads further or the itching becomes unbearable, come earlier.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Good afternoon, please sit. What brings you to the chest specialist today?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, I have been having this wheezing and breathlessness since a couple of months now. Also some cough that is comes and goes. My general doctor just sent me here without explaining anything.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I see. Is the wheezing happening every night or only during certain activities?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Mostly every night it disturbs my sleep, and a few times during the day also. But honestly I feel the previous doctor was just guessing, so I am not sure this is even a lung problem.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I understand your concern. Have you recently travelled to any rural or congested area? Any mold or pet dander exposure?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes, I visited a relative's old house in a village last month — very damp walls, so maybe mold was there. And they had two cats, so pet dander also. But I doubt this alone caused everything.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any occupational lead exposure or living near industrial areas?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Not anymore, doctor. I used to work near a battery manufacturing unit about five years back, but I left that job. Why are you asking all this? Is this really necessary?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: It is very much necessary, madam. Do you also have joint pain or any cramping sensation anywhere?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Actually yes, there is joint pain in my upper part — shoulders mostly. And sometimes this cramping feeling in the intestine area. I have been taking painkillers on my own for that.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any issue near the gallbladder area — like pain after eating or bloating?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Umm, almost never doctor. Only occasionally. But what does my gallbladder have to do with my breathing? You are checking too many things at once.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Everything is connected, madam. Do you have any history of stroke or elevated blood pressure?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: I had a stroke about three years ago — minor one they said. And still my blood pressure reading comes high sometimes. I take my tablet for it but not regularly, I admit.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Do you drink wine or use tobacco? Any screen time habits that affect your sleep?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: I have wine every day — just one glass, nothing wrong with that. I am vegetarian so my diet is fine. And yes, my screen time is also quite high at night, but what does that have to do with wheezing?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any smoking history?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Ahh, I used to smoke half a pack a day for about ten years but quit two years ago. I doubt my old smoking is still causing this after so long.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Madam, based on your mold, pet dander, and prior smoking history combined with every night wheezing and breathlessness, this is a case of allergic asthma with possible chronic obstructive pulmonary disease overlap. The joint pain and lead exposure history also need evaluation for systemic inflammation.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: I doubt it doctor, I really feel it could be something else entirely. Are you sure you are not jumping to conclusions?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I understand your scepticism, but we need tests to confirm. I am ordering a PET scan for the systemic inflammation concern and an angiogram given your stroke history and uncontrolled blood pressure. We will also do spirometry and allergy skin testing for the wheezing.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Fine. But what will you give me for now? I cannot keep suffering with this breathlessness every night and this joint pain.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I am starting you on prednisolone for five days to reduce the airway inflammation, along with a bronchodilator inhaler to use when the wheezing gets worse at night. Please stop self-medicating with painkillers as they can worsen asthma.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Also, please avoid going near damp areas or pet dander exposure again, reduce your wine intake as alcohol can trigger wheezing, and cut down on screen time at night to allow proper sleep and let your blood pressure stabilise.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Okay doctor, but for the joint pain and the cramping near my intestine — will the prednisolone handle that also, or do I need to see some other specialist?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Come in, please sit. I am Doctor Mehta, the specialist. Your family doctor has referred your child here?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor. My son, he is seven years old. He has been unwell since yesterday.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Alright. What exactly is happening? Any fever or diarrhoea?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes, both doctor. Fever came suddenly and he is having loose motions every day, about four to five times.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Is he complaining of any pain in his joints or soreness in the throat?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: He is saying his throat is paining. The joints — umm, I am not sure, he does not say much but he is limping a little.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Limping, okay. Is the joint pain extremely painful when you press or touch the area?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, he cried when I pressed on his knee. He is not letting anyone touch it.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any complaint of pain in his ears? Any ear discharge or hearing difficulty?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Ahh, yes doctor, he was pulling at his ears often last night. No discharge I think.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Has he been exposed to any pet dander at home, or has any family member was sick recently?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: My wife had cold and sore throat last week. And we have a cat at home, so yes, pet dander is there.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Has the child been to any garden or park recently? Any chance of a tick bite?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Uh, we went to the park two days back. I did not see any tick bite but I cannot say for certain.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Does he have any food allergy or any known drug reaction history I should know about?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, he has a food allergy to shellfish. And the family doctor told us he reacted badly to penicillin once, so that is avoided.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Good that you mentioned that. Now tell me — you work in garments? Do you smoke at all?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, I am a tailor. I do smoke daily, for 10 years. But not inside the house near the child.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Understood. Looking at the fever, joint pain that is extremely painful, sore throat, and ears involvement — this is presenting like reactive arthritis following a streptococcal infection. We need to rule out rheumatic fever as well.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, is it very serious? What tests will you do?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: We will do a throat swab culture, ASO titre, CRP, and complete blood count. Also an X-ray of the knee. In some cases we consider laparoscopy if there is abdominal involvement, but that is not needed now.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Okay doctor. He also has stomach pain often, so I was worried about that.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: We will monitor that. For now, I am prescribing azithromycin for the throat infection — since he is allergic to penicillin — along with ibuprofen for the joint pain and fever, and oral rehydration salts for the diarrhoea.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Keep him away from the cat to reduce pet dander exposure, give plenty of fluids, and if the fever crosses 103 degrees or the joints become more extremely painful, bring him immediately to emergency.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Thank you doctor. I will follow everything you said.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Welcome back. How are you feeling after discharge?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Umm, somewhat better doctor, but the yellowish tinge on my skin and eyes is still there. Also getting palpitations every few days.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any nausea or vomiting? Any heaviness in the lower part of your abdomen?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: The nausea is there after every meal doctor. And there is a dull ache in the lower part of my belly, yes.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any swelling or tenderness near the calf area or around the lymph nodes?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Ahh, actually yes, the calf is feeling intense pain when I walk and I noticed some swelling near the lymph nodes in my neck.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: We got your AST and HbA1c reports. Your AST levels are very elevated and HbA1c is still poorly controlled. Were you taking the medicines given at discharge regularly?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Uh, I was taking omeprazole regularly doctor, but I missed the other tablets a couple of times because of night shift work.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Are you still consuming beer or any alcohol? Please be honest with me.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, I stopped after admission only. But before that I used to have beer once in a while... okay maybe more than that on weekends.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Have you ever been exposed to lead or any industrial chemicals at your workplace?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Right, actually in my earlier job I worked in a hardware assembly unit and there was some lead exposure for about two years. That was from childhood days, small scale factory work before IT.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Do you have any drug allergy that we should be aware of before adjusting your medications?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, I have a drug allergy to sulfa drugs, it was noted from childhood itself. I used to get rashes all over.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: What about running or any physical exercise? Are you maintaining any routine?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: I do running once in a while only doctor, because night shifts are very tiring. No proper routine.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Based on everything — your reports, symptoms, and alcohol history — you have alcoholic fatty liver disease with jaundice, and your diabetes is uncontrolled. The palpitations and calf swelling also need further evaluation, so I am ordering an angiogram.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, the angiogram — is it because of my heart also? Should I be worried?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: The palpitations and calf swelling together are concerning for possible deep vein thrombosis or cardiac involvement, so the angiogram is necessary to rule that out. Also your lymph nodes will be monitored closely.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I am prescribing synthroid as your thyroid levels are also off, continue omeprazole twice a day, and I am adding metformin for the sugar control. Avoid sulfa drugs completely given your allergy history.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, the metformin — will it cause any problem with my liver since it is already not well?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: That is a valid concern. At lower doses metformin is generally safe, but we will recheck your AST in two weeks. Strictly stopped alcohol — even a small amount will worsen the fatty liver and jaundice significantly.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Understood doctor. One more thing — there is a dull ache in my chest also, every few days, especially during night shifts.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: That dull ache in the chest combined with palpitations is why the angiogram must not be delayed. Also try to reduce night shifts if possible — sleep disruption is worsening your blood sugar and overall fatigue.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Thank you doctor, I will follow everything properly this time.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Good morning, please come in and sit down comfortably.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Good morning doctor. They sent me from the society health camp, said I should get properly checked because my BP was coming high there.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Right, so let us go through everything carefully. Are you having any chest pain or palpitations — meaning your heart feels like it is beating fast or fluttering?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, for a month I am feeling this beating sensation in my chest, and occasionally there is some chest pain also, but mild only.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any vomiting or nausea along with the chest pain?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Umm, nausea is there sometimes doctor, but vomiting — nope, nothing like that has happened.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Good. Now, how long has the BP been high? Has anyone told you before?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, over a year they are saying my pressure is on the higher side. I was not taking it seriously, thinking it is just tiredness.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any past history of TB or any serious illness before? Any blood transfusion taken at any time?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Ahh, yes doctor — I had TB 2-3 years back, took full course of medicines. And blood transfusion was given after my second delivery, some heavy bleeding had happened.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Understood. Do you cycle or do any physical activity regularly? And do you smoke or take liquor?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, I do some cycling every day in the morning, only small rounds. Liquor I take after meals sometimes, my husband also does. But I am not a chain smoker — I confirmed to my husband also, I have never touched cigarettes.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Good. Now, are you living in a city area or rural area? Any pets at home or smoke exposure from kitchen or surroundings?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: We are originally from rural area doctor, shifted here three years back. We have pets — two cats at home. And earlier in village there was always cooking smoke, wood fire only we were using.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any itching or rash on the scalp or skin? Any breathlessness on climbing stairs?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: There is some itching on my scalp over a year, I thought it is just dryness. And yes doctor, breathlessness comes when I climb to the second floor.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Have you done any heart test before — like an Echo or ECG? Any medicines you are currently taking?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Umm, ECG was done at the camp but Echo — I doubt it doctor, I don't think I ever did that one. For anxiety they had given some tablet — I think it was lorazepam — but I stopped on my own.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Based on everything — the palpitations, mild chest pain, elevated BP, and breathlessness — this looks like hypertension with possible early cardiac involvement. The anxiety is also contributing to her palpitations.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I am prescribing atenolol for the BP and palpitations — take it every day in the morning. For anxiety, I am giving a very small dose of lorazepam, only when symptoms are bad, not regularly.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, this atenolol — will it cause any side effects? I have heard dizziness comes.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Some patients do get dizziness initially, especially if you get up too fast. Also, the liquor you take after meals — please stop that completely, it pushes the BP up further and reacts badly with atenolol.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Continue your cycling — that is good. But we must do an Echo and a lipid profile to check the heart properly. Also a chest X-ray given the old TB history.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, the itching on my scalp — should I be worried? And the pets at home, should I remove them?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: The scalp itching may be related to the pets or just dryness — let us do a skin allergy test to be sure. You don't need to remove them immediately, but keep the scalp clean and we will review after results.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Come in, please sit down. So you have come for a second opinion today, is it?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, the other doctor gave some advice but I was not fully satisfied. My son is for two weeks having fever and diarrhoea. He is seven years old only.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Okay. Is the fever intermittent or is it there all the time?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: It is intermittent, doctor. It comes every other day, then goes down with medicine, then comes back again.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any body pain also? Is the child complaining of his stomach or legs hurting?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Uh, yes doctor. He says body pain is there, mostly in the legs and stomach. He is also having vomiting every other day along with the loose motions.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Tell me, did you recently travel anywhere? Any heat exposure or congested area?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, we went to my wife's village before the tests were done. Very crowded area, and there was a lot of heat also. We stayed in a small house with many people.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any pets in that house? Or any factory or chemical smell nearby?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes, there were pets — two dogs and some goats also. No factory nearby as such, but the water supply was not clean I think.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: And yourself — do you drink alcohol or use e-cigarettes? Do you go to the gym? I ask because stress and lifestyle affect immunity in the whole family.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: I used to drink occasionally but stopped. I used to go to the gym also, but no time now with my food stall work. E-cigarettes I never tried.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: What did the previous doctor say? What medicines were given?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: They gave some paracetamol syrup and oral rehydration solution. They said it might be viral but I was not sure because the fever keeps returning.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Let me summarise what I am seeing — intermittent fever coming every other day, diarrhoea, vomiting, body pain, travel to a congested rural area, contaminated water, and pets exposure. A simple viral illness is ruled out in my mind — this picture is more consistent with enteric fever, possibly typhoid.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Uh-huh, uh-huh. So doctor, is it serious? Is it a chronic problem or will it go?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: It is not chronic if treated properly. We need to act quickly. We will do a Widal test, a blood culture, complete blood count, and stool culture to confirm.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, can the dirty water alone cause all this? Or is it also because of the pets?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Contaminated water is the main cause for typhoid. The pets could have added some risk of other infections like leptospirosis also, so we must check. Heat exposure worsens dehydration from the diarrhoea.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Okay doctor. What medicines should he take now? The previous doctor's medicines are finishing today.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I am prescribing azithromycin syrup for the infection, continue paracetamol for fever, and keep giving oral rehydration solution frequently. If his legs or face swell up at any point, I will add furosemide — but right now that is not needed.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, any food restrictions? He loves eating outside food from my stall only.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Strictly no outside food right now — only home-cooked soft food like rice and dal. Make sure all water is boiled. Avoid any heat and crowded areas for now. Watch for rash on the chest or abdomen, high fever above 103 degrees, or bleeding — bring him immediately if any of those happen.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: And doctor, the Widal test and other reports — how soon should I come back with them?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Come back in two days with all reports. If the fever or diarrhoea is worsening before the tests are done, do not wait — go to the hospital emergency directly. He should be fine with proper treatment, do not worry.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Good morning, please have a seat. What brings you in today?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Good morning doctor. I am a street food vendor and I need some papers done for my insurance claim, but also I have been feeling very unwell a week ago it started, and I am very worried about everything.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I understand, do not worry, we will sort everything out. Tell me, what exact symptoms are you having? Any body aches, fatigue, or breathlessness?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, body aches are there countless times throughout the day, and my upper abdomen is also paining, it is intense sometimes, especially in the mornings when I start my stall.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Okay, and any asthma or cough or wheezing also? Any swelling in your arm?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yeah doctor, the asthma is there on and off since years, and umm, my left arm has been paining also, especially in this cold season. The wheezing gets worse when the weather changes.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I see. Has your sugar or thyroid problem been checked recently? And any family history of diabetes or thyroid disease?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, in January I had all the tests done. My sugar was borderline they said, and my thyroid was also slightly off. My mother had diabetes and high cholesterol. I was taking metformin before the tests but I stopped on my own.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: You should not stop medicines without asking us. Now, have you been exposed to any heat at your stall for long hours? And is anyone at home sick — any family member was sick recently?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yeah, doctor, I stand near the frying stall in heat for almost eight to ten hours. And yes, my wife had fever and cold last week, so family member was sick at home. Also I travel by public transport every day, so who knows where I catch these things.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: That is quite a lot of exposure. Do you cycle to work or do any yoga? And how much caffeine are you taking in a day?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor I used to do cycling in the mornings and some yoga also, but now with this pain I have stopped. And caffeine — ahh, I drink at least five to six cups of tea per day because standing at the stall requires it. I also smoke 1 pack per day, I know it is bad but stress is too much.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Smoking 1 pack per day combined with your borderline diabetes and asthma is very risky, especially with seasonal changes. The heat and fumes from your stall are also aggravating everything. You must try to reduce this.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: True doctor, I know. Also I get acidity in my upper abdomen countless times after eating oily food. And dizziness also comes on and off. My cholesterol was also high in the last report, they said.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Do you have those reports with you? And were any thyroid function tests or fasting blood sugar or lipid profile done in January?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, I have brought the papers. The fasting blood sugar was 118, lipid profile showed high triglycerides, and the thyroid function test showed slightly raised TSH. I was given levothyroxine but I stopped that also a week ago.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Okay, looking at all this — you have type 2 diabetes in early stage, hypothyroidism, dyslipidemia, and your asthma is getting seasonal worsening. The body aches and upper abdomen pain are all connected to these conditions.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Oh doctor, so many things at once! I am so scared. What should I do now? Will the insurance cover all this? And will I be okay to keep running my stall?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Do not worry, we will manage everything step by step. I will document everything needed for your insurance. You need to restart your medicines, maintain a proper diet, reduce caffeine, and try to resume light yoga once the body aches settle. Avoiding prolonged heat exposure at your stall is also important.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor please tell me exactly what medicines to take. I get confused countless times with so many tablets. And for the asthma also, I need something because the wheezing in my arm and breathlessness are bothering me badly.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I am prescribing metformin 500 mg twice daily for sugar, levothyroxine 50 mcg in the morning on empty stomach for hypothyroidism, atorvastatin 10 mg at night for cholesterol, and salbutamol inhaler for asthma attacks. For acidity take pantoprazole 40 mg before breakfast.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: True, doctor. Umm, one more thing — the pain in my upper abdomen is sometimes so intense that I feel like vomiting also, especially after travelling by public transport in the heat.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: That nausea and vomiting sensation near the upper abdomen may be gastritis triggered by caffeine and oily food. I will order a fresh HbA1c, complete blood count, and abdominal ultrasound to rule out other causes.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, also I want to mention that my body aches and joint pain are definitely more in winter, like every year in January it peaks. Is that seasonal? Because I used to do cycling but now even that seems difficult.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Yes, seasonal worsening is very common with hypothyroidism and asthma in winter months. Keep yourself warm, do not skip levothyroxine, use the salbutamol inhaler if wheezing starts, cut down smoking to protect your upper abdomen lining and asthma, and please travel by public transport with a mask to avoid infections. Come back in four weeks with all test reports.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Hello, please come in and sit down. So you have come for your annual check-up today, yes?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, my husband told me to come. I am a homemaker only, I also do night shift packing work in the factory, so I am not getting proper sleep at all.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Okay, okay. Tell me, are you having any swelling anywhere on the body? Like on the legs or face?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, the legs are getting like... big, big, heavy. And the face also, in the morning it looks like... puffed up, I don't know how to say properly.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Alright. Any problem near the bladder side? Like burning when passing urine, or urine is less than usual?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Umm, yes doctor, the urine is coming very less in amount, and sporadically there is some burning also near the bladder side I feel.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Is there any joint problem? Like pain in the knees or fingers?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Ahh, yes, there was a joint problem in the knees last month, but that is gone now. Now only the swelling of the legs is troubling me.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any fatigue or loss of appetite? Are you feeling nausea at all?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, I get very tired fast fast. Eating also I don't feel like much. Nausea is there sporadically, some mornings only.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Do you have any history of diabetes or blood pressure? Or any kidney problem before?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: My blood pressure is a bit high, doctor, they told me before. But I never took regular medicines. Diabetes I don't know, never checked properly.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Okay. Have you taken any steroids or pain medicines on your own? Sometimes people take without prescription.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, my neighbour gave me steroids tablets last month for the joint problem. I took for maybe ten days. No one told me it is harmful.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I see. Do you drink alcohol? And do you smoke at all?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Uh, doctor, I sometimes take small drink only, like 2 drinks a week maximum. My husband and I go out 3 times a week in the evening, that time only. Smoking I never do.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any recent travel? Like going to another city or any international travel?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: No international travel, but some travel to my village side was there last month. Doctor, why are you asking all this?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I will explain. Looking at your swelling, reduced urine output, high blood pressure history, and with the steroids you took, I am suspecting chronic kidney disease. We need to confirm with tests.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I am ordering a serum creatinine, blood urea nitrogen, urine routine microscopy, and a kidney ultrasound. Also a fasting blood glucose and blood pressure monitoring.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, the swelling is moderate only right now, not too big. Will it become very bad? What should I do?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: For now I am starting you on amlodipine five milligrams once daily for the blood pressure, and furosemide for the swelling. Do not take any more steroids or painkillers on your own, please.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: You must reduce salt in your food, drink water in moderate amounts only, not too much not too less. Also stop the alcohol completely, even 2 drinks a week is too much for a kidney problem patient.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, my night shift work, can I continue? My sleep is very less, only three four hours. Will it affect the kidneys?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Yes, sleep deprivation does affect kidney health and blood pressure badly. I strongly advise you to shift away from night shifts if possible. Come back after one week with all the test reports, then we will review and adjust the plan accordingly.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Welcome, congratulations on your new baby. Please have a seat and make yourself comfortable.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Thank you doctor. Umm, I am here for the surgery clearance but I also keep getting tightness in my chest once in a while and my hand feels stiffness in the mornings.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Okay, let us go step by step. When did the chest tightness and stiffness first start?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: The tightness started after I had COVID in 2022. The stiffness in the hand I am also noticing today it is worse than before.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Are you also having any memory loss, fatigue, or brain fog since the COVID episode?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yeah, doctor, the memory loss is quite bad. I forget things weekly like names, where I kept things. My throat also feels dry most of the time. Oh, and doctor, I also wanted to ask about my baby's feeding schedule—

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: We will come to baby feeding separately. Right now tell me — are the lymph nodes anywhere swollen? Under the arms or neck?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Umm, yeah, the lymph nodes in my neck were swollen last month but now they are a little better. I have body ache three times a week also.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Have you done any imaging or a PET scan for the swollen lymph nodes?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: No, doctor, nothing like that has been done. I was told to wait since I was pregnant. The doctor gave me an inhaler for the chest tightness but I use it only once in a while.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any history of osteoporosis or jaundice in the past?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yeah, I had jaundice when I was a teenager, and my mother has osteoporosis so doctor told me I am at risk. I have been taking rosuvastatin for my cholesterol since last year.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any exposure to mercury or chemicals at home or at work?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Ahh, I used to work in a small lab before my delivery, so there was some chemicals exposure, and I think mercury also at that time. I left the job three months ago.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Are you a vegetarian? And I also need to ask — any history of substance use like heroin or alcohol?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: I am vegetarian, yes. Ahh, doctor, I will be honest — I did use heroin a few years back but I have been clean since 2022. I also used to smoke 10 cigarettes a day but I stopped when I got pregnant.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Good that you stopped. Are you doing any physical activity or exercise currently?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Just light walking for 30 minutes daily, doctor. But I also get breathlessness when I walk fast, and my joints feel stiffness after walking. Doctor, also, is it safe for the baby — I mean no contact issue with the medicines?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Your symptoms point to long COVID sequelae — specifically post-viral fatigue, memory loss, and joint stiffness. The dry throat and chest tightness also fit this picture. The lymph node swelling needs further evaluation before we clear you for surgery.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: So doctor, the surgery can be done or not? And will the memory loss get better on its own?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: We will need the PET scan report and also a pulmonary function test and bone density scan given your family history of osteoporosis. Surgery clearance will depend on these results. The memory loss does improve with time in most long COVID patients but it may take six to twelve months.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Continue your inhaler use as prescribed — three times a week or as needed for tightness. I am adding vitamin D3 supplements for your bone health and omega-3 capsules to support joint stiffness and brain fog. Continue rosuvastatin as before.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, are these medicines safe while I am breastfeeding? The baby is only two months old.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Vitamin D3 and omega-3 capsules are safe during breastfeeding. However, rosuvastatin should be monitored carefully — I will check your liver function test since you had past jaundice, and given prior chemicals and mercury exposure, we must watch liver health closely. Avoid smoking completely — no contact with secondhand smoke near the baby either.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Thank you so much doctor, I feel much better knowing there is a proper plan now.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Ah, Ramnath ji! Good to see you again. How are the fields this season?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor sahib, the rains have been good this year. But I myself am not so good, that is why I came.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Yes yes, it is your quarterly review time. Tell me, how is the swelling in your legs and feet?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, the swelling is coming back every few days. Not too long ago it was manageable but now it is puffing up again by evening.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: And any breathlessness or fatigue along with it? Any trouble passing urine?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Ahh, yes doctor, I feel tired periodically, especially in the afternoon. Urine is also less than before, very concentrated and dark.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Your last serum creatinine was borderline. Did you get the repeat kidney function test done that I asked for a month ago?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, I did get the kidney function test done. The report showed creatinine has gone up to 3.2. I also did urine protein as you said.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Good that you got it done. Tell me, are you still taking opioids for your back pain? Some farmers use those pain tablets regularly, I know.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: No doctor, I stopped those. Not anymore. You had scolded me last time itself, so I stopped completely.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Very good, Ramnath ji. Any smoke exposure in the fields — burning crop stubble or anything like that?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, there is always some stubble burning nearby, so smoke is there in the air. I cannot always avoid it.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I see. Any international travel recently? And did you ever do a COVID test when you had that fever last quarter?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: No international travel for me, doctor, I have never gone outside India. The COVID test I did a month ago when fever came — it was negative.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: How about coffee? You used to drink a lot, I remember you telling me.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Umm, I have cut down doctor. Not anymore like before — maybe one small cup in morning only. And I started doing light exercise also, as you told me.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Good efforts, Ramnath ji. Based on your rising creatinine, the swelling, and proteinuria, this is chronic kidney disease, Stage 3 progressing. We also noticed a small fistula at the access site from your earlier procedure, and I want to check that with a fluoroscopy.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, this fistula — is it dangerous? Should I be worried? And what is fluoroscopy?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: The fistula is a small abnormal connection, and the fluoroscopy is an X-ray based imaging test to see inside and check it properly. We need it done for a week from now, do not delay.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, also I had some wheezing for a week last month. My neighbor gave me his albuterol inhaler and I used it — it helped a little.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Ramnath ji, please do not use anyone else's albuterol without prescription. Your kidneys are already under stress, and taking medicines not prescribed for you can worsen the creatinine levels further.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Understood doctor, sorry for that. Can you tell me what medicines I should be taking properly now? Also, I had a small infection near my foot — do I need antibiotics?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Yes, for the infection on your foot, I am prescribing antibiotics — specifically amoxicillin-clavulanate twice daily for five days. For your kidneys, continue telmisartan and I am adding furosemide for the swelling.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Also, please do a urine culture before starting the antibiotics, restrict salty food, keep doing that light exercise, and come back in one month with your serum creatinine and fluoroscopy reports.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Thank you so much doctor. You always take such good care. I will follow everything properly this time, promise.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Good afternoon. Please take a seat. What brings you here today?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, actually I went to another doctor for a week before coming here, and he told me something about my kidney being affected, but I also have swelling in my legs that is constant and my blood sugar is not getting controlled even with medicines.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Okay, let us go through things properly. First, tell me about the swelling — is it only in your legs or also in the face or hands?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: It is mainly in the legs and feet, doctor, and it becomes worse at night. Also sometimes the face is a little puffy in the morning. And oh — I also get headache that is extremely painful, happening nonstop.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any foamy urine or reduced urine output? Any breathlessness?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, the urine has been foamy — I noticed that for a week now. Breathlessness, hardly ever, only if I climb stairs fast.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: What medicines are you currently taking for the sugar problem? And has any doctor checked your serum creatinine or urine protein?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: The other doctor prescribed metformin and glipizide, but my sugar is still shooting up. He did do a serum creatinine — it came back high, he said something like 2.4, and there was protein in the urine routine also.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any family history of heart disease or anemia? Any personal history of pneumonia or major illness before this?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Umm, my father had heart disease, yes. I myself had pneumonia about two years back, and I was told I had mild anemia after that. I recovered, but they gave me iron tablets for some months.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Do you drink alcohol? And any smoking?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: No smoking at all doctor, never. Alcohol — only socially, maybe 2 drinks a week. I have been doing this for 20 years — well, since college basically.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Alright. Any contaminated water source at home, or do you travel regularly by public transport? Any contact with dogs or other animals?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Oh yes, we had a water supply issue last month so we may have had contaminated water. I do take public transport nonstop for my office commute. And we do have two dogs at home — is that a problem, doctor?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: It can be relevant, we will keep that in mind. Do you do any physical activity? I want to understand your overall lifestyle.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, I do swimming — I go to a community pool. But lately because of the swelling and fatigue I have reduced it a lot.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Based on the elevated serum creatinine, proteinuria, swelling in the legs, constant foamy urine, and uncontrolled blood sugar, this is a case of diabetic nephropathy — your kidneys are getting damaged due to the sugar problem.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Oh my god doctor — is it serious? And can the headache also be related? It is extremely painful and nonstop some days.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Yes, the headache is likely related to high blood pressure which often accompanies kidney disease. We need to control your blood sugar much more aggressively and also protect the kidneys.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I am stopping metformin immediately since your serum creatinine is high — it is not safe now. I am prescribing insulin instead for sugar control, and adding losartan to protect the kidneys and manage the blood pressure. Also start furosemide for the swelling.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, the swimming — can I continue? And should I stop the drinking alcohol?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Yes, you must stop alcohol completely — even 2 drinks a week is too much when your kidneys are compromised. Swimming in a public pool is fine for light exercise, but avoid any community pool that uses contaminated water or has poor hygiene — your immunity is lower right now.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I also want you to do a stool test to rule out any infection given the contaminated water and dogs exposure. We will also check a complete HbA1c and kidney function test panel.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Okay doctor. One more thing — I sometimes feel nausea especially in the morning. Could that also be related to the kidney problem?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Yes, nausea can be a sign of uremia when kidney function is declining. Please follow the diet plan I am giving you — low contaminated water risk, reduced protein and salt, no alcohol, and come back in two weeks with all the reports including the stool test, HbA1c, and kidney function test.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Hello, come in, come in. How are you feeling today? Take a seat.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, I am feeling so worried. From long time I am having this stomach pain and after the surgery also it has not fully gone. My left side is still paining a few times every day.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Okay, let us not worry too much. Tell me, is the stomach pain coming at any particular time, like around noon or after eating?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, it comes more around noon and also every night when I lie down. And doctor, I am fasting for religious reasons these days, so I am eating only once and I think that is making it worse.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I see. Fasting can put extra stress on the stomach. Now tell me, is there any yellowing of your eyes or skin still remaining?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Umm, the yellowing in the eyes has reduced doctor, but sometimes I am getting a headache in my head also, a few times in the week. And I feel very fatigue all the time.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Good that the jaundice is improving. Now I want to ask you some questions your parents told me about. Do you have any dust or pet dander exposure at home or school?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Ahh, yes doctor, we have a cat at home so pet dander is definitely there. And my school is near a construction site so dust is also a lot. Also sometimes I have to go to crowded places for festivals and I feel breathless there.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Alright. I must ask you honestly — have you ever tried drinking or any substances like whiskey or cocaine? I will not judge you, I just need to know for your treatment.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: No doctor, never, I promise. I know about drinking and whiskey and cocaine from friends but I have not done any of that. But I do smoke — only 5 cigarettes a day, I started just a few months back.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: At your age, even 5 cigarettes a day is very harmful, especially with a fatty liver diagnosis. You must stop smoking completely. Any cocaine or alcohol use will destroy your liver recovery, please be very careful.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: I understand doctor, I will stop. My uncle had knee replacement last year and he was also told the same thing about smoking. But doctor, can this liver problem also cause tuberculosis? Someone told me it can.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Tuberculosis is a separate infection, it does not come directly from liver disease. But if your immunity is low due to fatty liver or jaundice, you may be more vulnerable in crowded places. We will check for it separately if needed.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Okay doctor. Also, I am on lisinopril — my previous doctor had started it. Is that still okay with the liver surgery recovery?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Lisinopril needs to be monitored carefully now because your liver is still recovering. I will review the dosage after we see today's blood reports. Do not stop it on your own.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Tell me, is there any nausea or vomiting also? And any itching on the skin?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes, the nausea is there every night doctor. And the left side stomach pain becomes sharp and stabbing sometimes. No itching thankfully.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Based on the surgery history and all your current symptoms, you are recovering from acute jaundice with underlying fatty liver disease. The left side pain and nausea are part of the post-operative recovery phase.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, will this fatty liver go away fully? I am very scared. And what about the fasting I am doing — is it damaging my liver?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: With proper diet and no smoking, fatty liver can reverse fully at your age. The fasting is putting extra load on your liver right now, so I recommend you eat small meals every few hours instead of one big meal during this recovery period.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Have you done your liver function test and ultrasound abdomen after surgery? Did the previous hospital give you any reports?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Ahh yes doctor, I have the reports. They did liver function test and bilirubin test — the bilirubin was still a little high they said. They also did ultrasound abdomen and said there is still some fatty changes in the liver.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Okay, I am prescribing ursodeoxycholic acid tablet twice daily for liver support, pantoprazole to help with the stomach pain and nausea, and vitamin E supplement once daily. Continue the lisinopril as before until I review the new reports.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, anything I should be especially avoiding? Like certain foods or going to crowded places? And is the headache in my head related to all this?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Avoid all oily and fried food, stop smoking completely, and reduce exposure to dust and pet dander as much as possible. The headache may be from fatigue and low nutrition due to fasting — once you eat properly it should reduce. Come back in two weeks with fresh liver function test reports and we will review everything.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Good morning, please come in and sit down. No need to feel nervous.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Umm, good morning doctor. 10-15 days from now my skin and eyes are becoming yellow, so my daughter brought me here.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I see. Any itching on the skin, or pain near your abdomen?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Ahh, yes doctor, right side of my stomach is giving squeezing type pain every morning. And some itching also is there.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any nausea, vomiting, or loss of appetite?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Umm, yes doctor. Eating is very less now. Nausea is there every morning also. I am not able to take even tea properly.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Is your urine colour dark? Any pale stools?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, urine is very dark yellow colour. Stools also are very light coloured, I noticed.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any family member with liver disease or jaundice? Any family member was sick with similar condition?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Ahh, yes doctor. My elder brother had fatty liver and my mother also had jaundice last summer only. She was hospitalised.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Do you chew tobacco or smoke at all?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Umm... I am currently using chewing tobacco doctor, two packs a day. And my son-in-law says I am a social smoker also, on gatherings only.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Are you taking any medicines currently? Any Advil or pain-killers regularly?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, I take Advil when headache comes, sometimes every morning. And for high blood pressure I am on beta blockers also, my other doctor gave.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: What about heparin or any blood thinners? Any history of clotting disorder?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: That one doctor denied. Nothing like that I have taken. No clotting problem also that I know of.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Based on your symptoms — yellow eyes and skin, squeezing pain on the right side, dark urine, family history — this looks like jaundice with underlying fatty liver disease. The regular Advil is not helping your liver at all.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, is it very serious? I am little scared only.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: We will run some tests first. I am ordering liver function tests, ultrasound abdomen, and bilirubin levels. Also, since you have been on beta blockers, we need to check ECG as well.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, my daughter was asking — is bone marrow biopsy also needed? She read somewhere online about this.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: A bone marrow biopsy is not required at this stage. We will go step by step. First the liver function tests results, then we decide further.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: For now, I am prescribing ursodeoxycholic acid tablets for your liver, ondansetron for the nausea, and small dose of heparin injection to prevent any blood clotting risk given your liver inflammation. Please stop Advil completely.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Okay doctor. That fatigue and weakness in legs is also there, I forgot to tell. 10-15 days same time it started.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: That weakness is also related to your liver disease. You must stop the chewing tobacco completely — it is making your liver condition much worse. Avoid oily and fatty food also. Come back with reports in three days.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Thank you doctor, I will try my best. My daughter will help me.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Please come in and sit down. I understand you are here for documentation purposes today?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, my insurance company is asking for a proper medical certificate. I am an elderly lady living alone, so I need everything properly written down.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Of course, we will take care of that. First tell me, what main complaints are you having? Any stomach pain or acidity?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, for three months I am having stomach pain and cramps in my abdomen, and so much gas trouble also. It is happening many times in the day.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Are these cramps sharp or dull and aching? And any bloating after eating?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Umm, mostly dull and aching doctor, but several times it becomes sharp. Yes, bloating is also there after every meal. And two days ago I had very severe acidity with burning in my chest.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any nausea or vomiting? And any menstrual bleeding or abnormal bleeding from anywhere?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, I am past that age, so no contact with menstrual bleeding for many years now. But nausea is there, true, especially in the mornings.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Do you drink wine or any alcohol? And are you non-vegetarian?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Ahh, yes doctor, I take wine maybe 2 drinks a week only. And yes I am non-vegetarian, I eat chicken and fish regularly. Could that be causing this?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: It can contribute, yes. Now, do you smoke at all?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: I am a social smoker doctor, not a regular one. But my son when he visits, he smokes a pack a day inside the house.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: That is passive smoke exposure, which is harmful. Now, any mold in your house? You mentioned you live alone in an old building.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor now that you mention it, there is mold on the walls in my bathroom and kitchen. I have been complaining to the building people but nothing is done.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: And what about screen time? Are you spending long hours on mobile or tablet late at night?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes, correct doctor, I do a lot of screen time at night because I cannot sleep. I watch shows until very late, then my stomach starts paining badly.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Have you done any upper GI endoscopy or H. pylori breath test before? Any past history of peptic ulcer disease?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: I had a endoscopy done about five years back, they said mild gastritis at that time. Since then I was taking some antacid syrup but I stopped it on my own.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Based on your symptoms of cramps, bloating, acidity, and the history of gastritis, along with your lifestyle factors, I am diagnosing you with gastroesophageal reflux disease with underlying irritable bowel syndrome. The mold and late-night screen time are making it worse.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, so what exactly is happening in my stomach? Should I be worried?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: The acid from your stomach is going back up into your food pipe, causing the burning and cramps. The gas trouble and bloating are from the bowel sensitivity.
