We need to do a stool H. pylori antigen test and a repeat upper GI endoscopy to confirm. Also a complete blood count to check for any anemia.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, I must tell you honestly, I am on pension only, my budget is very tight. I cannot afford expensive medicines.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I understand completely. I am prescribing affordable generic medicines for you. Take pantoprazole 40 mg once daily before breakfast, domperidone 10 mg before meals for the nausea and bloating, and simethicone drops for the gas trouble. These are all available at government dispensary at low cost.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Also please reduce your wine intake, stop eating spicy and heavy non-vegetarian food at night, and reduce late-night screen time as it disturbs your digestion and sleep cycle. The mold must be removed — it can worsen your gastric irritation and cause respiratory symptoms too.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Thank you doctor. Correct, I will follow everything. Please make the certificate also for the insurance people mentioning my gastroesophageal reflux disease and the tests you have advised.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Good morning, please come in and sit down.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Good morning doctor. I am coming for insurance paper work, they are asking full medical check up report.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Alright, I will document everything properly. Tell me, do you have any current complaints or are you just here for the documentation?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, actually for three months I am feeling irritable frequently and also memory loss is there, I am forgetting small small things many times.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Okay, any trembling or numbness in the hand?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Umm, yes doctor, intermittently the hand is feeling numbness, few days ago it was more. My wife also saying my hand is shaking sometimes.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: You mentioned diabetes. Are you on any medication currently?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, I am taking insulin injection, daily I am taking. Also metformin tablet was there but doctor stopped that few days ago.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Have you ever been exposed to any chemicals or mercury in your work environment?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Ahh, yes doctor, I was working in paint factory for long time, mercury and chemical exposure was there. But now I am quit that job.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: How long were you working there and were you smoking or drinking alcohol during that period?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor I was smoking for 10 years, half a pack a day I was doing. But now not anymore, I stopped. Alcohol also I quit two years back.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Good. Now I also notice in your file there is mention of your wife having irregular periods and PCOS. Did she come along today?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: No doctor, she is not coming. But she is also having white discharge frequently, she asked me to mention. She is doing fasting for religious reason, for three months she is keeping fast.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: For your wife, is there any pelvic pain or itching in the lower abdomen area also?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, she said itching is there intermittently and lower abdomen also paining sometimes. She is also feeling fatigue because of the fasting only.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Has she done any pelvic ultrasound or hormone profile tests for the PCOS?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Umm, she did ultrasound six months back only, doctor said PCOS is confirmed. Blood sugar test also she did, it was normal.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Based on your symptoms — the irritability, memory loss, and numbness in the hand — combined with your past mercury exposure, this looks like peripheral neuropathy likely worsened by your diabetes. We will need to confirm.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I will order a nerve conduction study, HbA1c, and serum mercury level for you today. Is that okay?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, whatever you say. Insurance company also asking for blood sugar fasting and ECG report also.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I will add those as well. Now for your numbness and irritability, I am prescribing methylcobalamin tablet once daily, alpha lipoic acid capsule once daily, and please continue your insulin as scheduled.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: And please tell your wife to see a gynaecologist soon for the white discharge and irregular periods. During fasting periods, make sure her insulin dose is adjusted — hypoglycemia risk is high otherwise.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, she is not diabetic, fasting is only religious. But I will tell her to go to gynaecologist. My memory loss will go away with medicines or it will stay?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: With proper insulin control, methylcobalamin supplementation, and avoiding any further mercury exposure, your memory loss and irritability should improve over three months. Come back after tests are done and we will review everything.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Come in, come in. Good to see you again. Please sit.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Thank you doctor. Long time, yes.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: So how have you been managing? Any new complaints since your last visit two months ago?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Ahh, doctor, I have been having headache intermittently, and also some dizziness. It started properly three days ago.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Where exactly is this headache? Is it in the forehead, temples, or back of the head?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Mostly the back of the head, doctor. And it is worse after eating in the afternoon. Also there is numbness in my hands sometimes.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any stiffness in your neck or shoulders? Any vomiting or blurring of vision?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Umm, yes doctor, there is stiffness in the neck. No vomiting, but yes the vision is slightly blurred sometimes.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Are you taking your regular aspirin as I prescribed? And what about the other tablets?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Uh, doctor honestly I stopped the aspirin two days ago because I read online it is bad for the stomach. I am taking some OTC pain tablets from the medical shop only.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: That is not good. Do you also have asthma? I see it in your record. Are you using any inhaler or are you on montelukast?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes, doctor, I have asthma since childhood. I was on montelukast but I stopped that also. I thought I was feeling fine.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: You are a fisherman, so you must be going to crowded places like fish market, using public transport? And is there any chance of contaminated water exposure on the boat?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, yes, fish market is very crowded. And the water on the boat, honestly we do not always check. Sometimes we use whatever water is available. I know, I know, you will scold me.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I am not scolding, I am concerned. Do you still smoke? Last time you were at two packs a day.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Not anymore, doctor. I have cut it down a lot. Maybe one or two cigarettes only, very rarely. My chest was troubling me too much.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Good, that is an improvement at least. Any swelling in the legs or ankles? Any shortness of breath at rest?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Umm, there is some swelling in the ankles doctor, two months ago it was not there. And shortness of breath comes intermittently when I climb stairs.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Looking at all this — the headache, dizziness, numbness, and ankle swelling — I believe you have uncontrolled hypertension with early fluid retention. Your asthma is also not under control.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, is this serious? I have been taking those OTC tablets for headache — is that causing any problem?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Those OTC pain tablets — if they are ibuprofen type — they will raise your blood pressure and worsen the fluid retention. Stop them immediately. We need to do a blood pressure monitoring, serum creatinine, and ECG today itself.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I am restarting your aspirin — do not stop it on your own. I am also adding furosemide for the ankle swelling, and I want you back on montelukast for your asthma.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, this furosemide — any side effects I should know? And can I still go to work on the boat?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Furosemide will make you pass more urine, so stay well hydrated. Strictly avoid contaminated water on the boat — with your blood pressure and asthma situation, any infection will make things worse fast. Also try to avoid crowded places and public transport during peak hours because dust and pollutants will trigger your asthma.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, I will follow properly this time. I will not stop tablets on my own. Please do those tests now.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Ah, Rajendra ji! Good to see you. How is the family? Your son's wedding preparations going on well?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: All good doctor saab, very hectic days. The wedding is next month. But today I have come for my quarterly check and also my grandson is not well.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Oh, the little one is unwell? What is happening with him?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: He has been having fever and diarrhoea — the stools are watery — couple of days now. He is only four years old.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Is there any vomiting also? And is the fever continuous or going up and down?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yep, some vomiting also started two days ago. The fever is often coming back, not settling fully. A family member was sick last week with similar complaints, so I think the child caught it from there.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any history of asthma or allergies in the child? And has he been given anything at home for the fever?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: No asthma, but he does have some allergies — some food items. We gave him ibuprofen syrup last night, periodically as needed.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Okay, based on the watery diarrhoea, fever, and the family member was sick history, this looks like a viral gastroenteritis. We will manage it with oral rehydration and continue ibuprofen for fever control.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: For the child, I am prescribing ribavirin in syrup form for the viral load, and continue ibuprofen after meals only. Make sure he is getting plenty of fluids.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Thank you doctor. Now for myself — I have been feeling uneasy on my right side periodically. Also there is some gas trouble often these days.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: The uneasiness on the right side — is it on the back also, or only front? Any tingling sensation on the skin around that area?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Ahh, yes doctor — it is going from the right side to the back also. And yes, there is this tingling on the skin there. It is ongoing for a week or so.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Has any rash appeared on the skin in that area? And is there a cyst or swelling you can feel?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Umm, yes a small cyst kind of thing I noticed on the skin near the back. No full rash as such yet.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any asbestos exposure during your government service years? You were in public works, correct?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Active exposure for many years yes — there was plenty of asbestos in the old buildings we worked in. But that was long back doctor.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Alright. Any cocaine or substance use? I have to ask formally. And how about physical activity these days?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Never doctor, no cocaine or anything like that. Physical activity is less these days — wedding planning is tiring. Earlier I used to smoke two packs a day but I stopped five years back.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: The tingling on the skin, the cyst, and the right side to back radiation — this pattern is suggesting early herpes zoster. The stress from wedding preparations may have triggered it.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, should we do some test? And what about my blood pressure review — is that ongoing as before?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Yes, BP review is ongoing. We will check your blood pressure reading today and also do a lumbar puncture to rule out any nerve involvement given the tingling pattern. Strong family history of nerve conditions means we should not take chances.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: For you, I am prescribing ribavirin antiviral course for the herpes zoster, and continuing losartan for your hypertension. Take losartan after meals as usual.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Any precautions for the gas problem doctor? It is becoming quite troublesome.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Avoid heavy oily food for now, the gas and uneasy feeling on the right side should settle once the herpes zoster is treated. Keep physical activity light — short walks are fine. Come back in two weeks or sooner if the rash spreads on the skin.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Come in, come in. Sorry for the wait, we are running a bit late today.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: No problem doctor. Actually my son needs this today for his school health screening. He is 8 years old.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Alright. Any complaints currently? pain, swelling, anything bothering him near the belly button area?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, time ago he had a small bulge near the belly button, it was slightly painful. He also gets gas frequently.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any past surgeries? Any history of hernia repair?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Active concern there actually — he had a small hernia repair done two years back. The surgeon said it went well.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Okay. Any discharge or redness near the belly button now? Any abscess or pus?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Not aware of any discharge doctor. But he does complain of a shooting pain near that area once a week or so.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any history of jaundice? Any liver problems?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, he had jaundice when he was around 3 years old. Fully recovered though. No yellowing of eyes since then.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any mosquito bite recently or any illness from someone nearby — like a coworker was sick at school or home?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Umm, yes there was a mosquito bite on his arm last week. And his classmate had fever recently. Also, we noticed some mold in our bathroom at home.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Is he having any breathlessness or cough? Does he use any inhaler?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, he has a inhaler for wheezing. The wheezing comes frequently when there is mold or dust around.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any family history of anxiety disorder? The child seems quite anxious even now sitting here.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Ahh yes, I myself have anxiety disorder. He has also been showing restlessness and tingling in his hands when he gets nervous.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Does anyone at home cannabis use or smoke? Like socially or occasionally? Secondhand exposure can affect children.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: My husband does cannabis occasionally and smokes about 10 cigarettes a day. He does it outside but yes, sometimes inside also.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Based on the history and the shooting pain near the belly button with prior hernia repair, this looks like a possible recurrent hernia. The tingling in hands and gas could be related to nutritional deficiency. We should check vitamin B12 levels.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, should we worry about the recurrent hernia? And the vitamin B12 — when should we do it?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Get the vitamin B12 done this week itself. For the belly button pain, I want a surgical review. The gas and bloating can be managed with diet changes also.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Any medicines for now doctor? Also, is tenofovir safe — someone told me to give it for immunity?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Please do not give tenofovir on your own — that is an antiviral, not for children like this. I am prescribing a multivitamin syrup and continue the inhaler as before. If wheezing worsens, come immediately.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Most importantly, ask your husband to stop smoking indoors. Secondhand smoke worsens wheezing and the mold at home must be cleaned — these are serious mold exposure risks for the child.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Thank you so much doctor, we will follow everything you said.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Come in, come in, please have a seat. You look quite tired today.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, I am very worried. From long time my legs and feet are very swollen, and I have been ignoring it but now it is getting worse. I am doing domestic work in three houses and I cannot miss work, so I tried to manage at home only.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I understand, please don't worry, we will sort this out together. Can you tell me, is the swelling on both legs or only one side?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Both sides, doctor. And my face also puffing up in the morning. The swelling is there more often lately, it used to come and go periodically but now it is not going at all.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Okay, and are you having any breathlessness, nausea, or decreased urine?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Urine has reduced a lot, doctor. And I feel nausea sometimes in the morning. Also fatigue is so much, I cannot even climb the stairs without getting breathlessness.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Have you taken any medicines on your own for this swelling or for any pain? Any mild pain killer or anything like that?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, I was taking ibuprofen for my back pain. I was buying from the medical shop without prescription. I took it for almost one month thinking it will help.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I see. And do you have any history of allergies or clotting disorder or any other past illness?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, I had some allergies when I was young, some skin rash type. And one doctor had told me something about clotting disorder also but I never followed up, we had no money at that time.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Okay. Any previous viral infection or dengue episode? Sometimes kidney problems can start after these infections.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor! Two years back I had dengue. I was admitted also for a few days. And after that I had one episode of viral infection also with very high fever. After that my swelling started slowly slowly.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I see, that is very helpful information. Do you smoke or use e-cigarettes? And do you drink alcohol?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: I used to use e-cigarettes but not anymore, I stopped after I started feeling sick. No alcohol at all. I do swimming sometimes in the colony tank and I drink a lot of tea, maybe five to six cups a day.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Alright. Do you go to crowded places often for work? And any pain or discomfort near your ovaries or lower abdomen?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, I travel by bus every day and markets are very crowded, so crowded places yes. And sometimes there is mild ache near my ovaries area, lower abdomen side. But I thought it is just tiredness.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I am quite concerned. Looking at your swelling, decreased urine output, and this history of dengue and long-term ibuprofen use, this looks like chronic kidney disease. The pain killer you were taking has damaged the kidneys further. We need to confirm with tests.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, please do not tell me something very serious. I have small children at home, I am the only one earning. I am feeling very scared.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Please don't panic, we will manage this together step by step. Have you done any check-up before for this? Any blood test or EMG or urine test done previously?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: No doctor, no proper check-up done. I had EMG done two years back for my hand tingling but nothing else after that. I was always thinking it will get better on its own.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: We need to do serum creatinine, urine routine, complete blood count, and kidney ultrasound today. Please stop ibuprofen immediately — it is making your kidneys worse. I know you have money constraints, we will find a way.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor I will stop it. But what about my back pain? The pain is there more often lately also and I need to do physical work every day.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: For pain I will prescribe enalapril for your high blood pressure which is also causing swelling, and for the back pain I will give you paracetamol which is safer for your kidneys. No more ibuprofen or any other pain killer from the shop, please.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, the medicines you are giving, enalapril and others, are they very costly? And should I stop tea also? And anything else I should avoid?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: These medicines are available as generics and are affordable. Please reduce tea to one cup a day, avoid crowded places where you may catch a viral infection as your immunity is low, avoid swimming in colony tanks as water can carry infection, keep your legs elevated when resting to reduce swelling, and please come back once the reports are done — we will take this one step at a time, you are not alone in this.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Alright, come in. You are here for your post-surgery follow-up, yes?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, the surgery was done in 2023 for a appendix removal. I came because I am not feeling well again.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: What is bothering you now? Any fever?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yeah, doctor. Fever is coming many times in the day. And stomach pain is also there after surgery.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: How bad is the stomach pain? Any cramping sensation?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: It is cramping doctor, very unbearable. It is paining non-stop near the abdomen.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any headache, body ache, or rash on the skin?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Umm, yes doctor. Body ache is there three times a week. No rash that I noticed.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any vomiting, loose motion, or chills?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Chills are there when fever comes. No vomiting yet. Loose motion also sometimes.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: You work in construction, correct? Any chemicals or fumes exposure at the site?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, chemicals and fumes are non-stop on site. No one wears protection there.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any herbal or alternative medicine you have been taking for this fever?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Ahh, yes doctor. I have been taking neem leaf extract and giloy juice. When I was younger also these worked for me.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: What about painkillers? Any self-medication for the stomach pain?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, I took painkillers from the chemist shop. It gave some relief but the cramping came back.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Do you smoke? How much?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, I am a chain smoker. I know it is bad.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Based on your symptoms, I suspect this is a case of typhoid fever possibly combined with dengue. The cramping and loose motion with high-grade fever are classic signs. Those herbal remedies are not enough here.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: We need to do a Widal test, dengue NS1 antigen test, and a complete blood count immediately. Also a platelet count to rule out dengue severity.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, will these tests show something? I hope it is not serious.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: We will start you on azithromycin 500 mg once daily for the typhoid, paracetamol 650 mg for the fever and body ache, and oral rehydration salts for the loose motion. Stop the herbal remedies and those painkillers immediately.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Avoid all fumes and chemicals at site until you recover. Take complete rest. No smoking as it will worsen the infection. Drink only boiled water.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Okay doctor, I will try. My work is giving me tension but I will manage.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Come back in five days with the Widal test and dengue NS1 antigen test reports. If fever goes above 103 degrees or bleeding starts from nose or gums, go to emergency straight away.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Good morning, please sit down. How are you feeling today?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, I had my heart operation and I was sent home three days ago, but now my chest is giving me some trouble again, it is paining on and off.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I see. Can you tell me more — is the pain in your chest sharp or more like a pressure feeling? And is there any warmth or warm feeling near the operation area?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Umm, yes doctor, the chest near where they cut is feeling warm to touch, and the paining comes on and off, not always.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Are you having any palpitations — I mean like your heart is beating very fast or jumping around in your chest?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Ahh, yes doctor, that jumping feeling — it is happening once a week or so. I did not know what it was called. I thought maybe gas trouble only.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Okay. Any breathlessness or dizziness along with that jumping feeling?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, no breathlessness, but sometimes my head goes a little dizzy. And my blood pressure reading at home was showing high, neighbour checked with her machine.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Did the hospital give you any medicines when they discharged you? Are you taking them regularly?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: They gave me some tablets. I was taking paracetamol for the pain, and they also gave steroids for some swelling they said, but I stopped the steroids on my own after two days because I was scared of side effects.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I understand your worry, but stopping medicines on your own can be dangerous. Were you also given acetaminophen or any blood thinner tablet?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, one more tablet was there, maybe that acetaminophen only — same as paracetamol they said. I am still taking that one.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Good. Now tell me about your daily routine. Do you smoke or drink? Any history of diabetes or high blood pressure before the surgery?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, I used to smoke — I was a social smoker only, but I have no longer smoked 10-15 days now since surgery. I had hypertension for long time — I was on tablets for 10 years.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: That is good you stopped smoking. What about your activity — are you doing any walking or sports, or just resting at home?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Ahh, I am just lying down mostly doctor, very sedentary lifestyle right now. And I am on phone and TV always — lot of screen time daily because nothing else to do at home.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Understood. Have you been going out at all — to the market or hospital visit for follow-up? Any pollution exposure, like vehicle smoke or construction dust near your house?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, only hospital visit I did — came here today. Near my house there is road digging work so lot of pollution and dust also, yes.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I see. Was there any fever at home, or redness or discharge from the operation cut on your chest?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Never any discharge doctor, the cut looks okay from outside. But the area around it is warm and a little swollen feeling. No fever I think.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Okay, after examining you and looking at your history, I believe you are having post-operative pericarditis — that means the lining around your heart has become irritated after the surgery — along with wound site inflammation near your chest. This is why you are having the palpitations and chest pain.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I am prescribing you back on steroids at the right dose — please do not stop them on your own this time. Continue paracetamol for pain, and I am adding a tablet called ibuprofen to reduce the inflammation around the heart lining.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, I am scared of taking so many medicines. Will the steroids not cause more problems? And should I do any blood test or scanning?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: The steroids are safe at this dose for short time — stopping them suddenly is more dangerous. I am ordering a ECG, echocardiogram, and CBC blood test to check your heart and rule out infection. Also please avoid pollution, reduce your screen time, and do no longer sit idle — short walks inside the house are fine. Come back in 10-15 days for review.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Okay doctor, thank you so much. I will follow everything you said properly this time.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Good afternoon, please have a seat. What brings you here today?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, I came for second opinion only. Another doctor was telling me something about operation but I am not sure. I have been having swelling near my groin area for a year now.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I see. Is the swelling soft or hard to touch? And does it come out when you strain or cough?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, it comes out when I am straining or lifting. It goes back in when I lie down. The pain is there all the time near my groin.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any bleeding from bottom or piles complaint also? Some patients have both together.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Umm, actually yes, doctor. There is some bleeding from bottom also, once a week or so. I did not want to mention. And the stool is thin sometimes.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Good you told me. Any abscess or discharge near the anal area? Any fever?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: No, nothing like fever or discharge. Just the bleeding and pain in the bottom area.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any other health conditions? What about sugar problem or knee pain or anything like that?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Ahh, doctor yes, I have sugar problem for a year only, and knee pain is also there. And I have epilepsy since many years and also depression history. I am on medicines for those.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I see. Any prostate problem or urine difficulty? And what medicines are you currently taking?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor they checked my prostate before, was some mild enlargement they said. For gas trouble I was on pantoprazole but I stopped it on my own last month and started some other tablet from medical shop. I am also taking antiepileptic tablets and antidepressant.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: You should not stop pantoprazole on your own without consulting. Now, do you drink alcohol? I want you to be honest with me.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Uh, doctor, yes, I do take alcohol for 30 years. Only 2 drinks a week now though, doctor. Not much.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: What about smoking? And any exposure to pet dander at home? Sometimes we see allergic reactions causing skin rash or breathing problems in elderly patients.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: No doctor, no smoking. No pets at home. But my grandson was saying someone at school had some infection recently. I do visit him every morning.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Alright. Did the first doctor do any tests like T3 or KFT? Or any colonoscopy?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: He had asked for KFT and T3 but I have not done them yet doctor. I came here first to take your opinion. He also mentioned ultrasound abdomen for checking.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Based on what you are telling me, you have an inguinal hernia on the groin side, and the bleeding with thin stool suggests internal piles, possibly grade two. The prostate enlargement should also be monitored carefully.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, is operation necessary? I am scared because of my epilepsy and all. Can it be managed with medicines only?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: The inguinal hernia will need surgical repair eventually, but we can plan it properly after your KFT, T3, and ECG are done. For the piles, we will first try conservative management. Your epilepsy medicines need to be coordinated with the surgeon before any anaesthesia.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I am restarting pantoprazole every morning before food. Also prescribing sitz bath and micronized purified flavonoid fraction tablets for the piles, and glucosamine for your knee pain.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: What should I avoid doctor? Any food restrictions? And what about my alcohol intake?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: You must stop alcohol completely, especially because of your depression history and prostate issue. Avoid constipation — take high fibre diet, drink plenty of water. Do not lift heavy weights as it will worsen the inguinal hernia. And never stop your antiepileptic tablets on your own.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Thank you doctor, I will follow your advice and do the tests soon.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Good morning, please come in and sit down comfortably.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Good morning doctor. I am newly married, just recently shifted to this area. I have been having fever and my husband and mother-in-law both noticed I am looking very unwell.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I see. Tell me more — when did this fever start, and did you notice any other symptoms along with it?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, my mother-in-law says since last ten days I have been having high-grade fever that comes and goes often, along with severe headache and body ache. She also noticed a rash on my arms.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Is there any vomiting, loose motion, or abdominal pain?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, yes, there is vomiting often and the stomach pain is quite crampy and constant. My husband says I barely ate anything for four days.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Is there any bleeding from gums or nose, or any joint pain?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Umm, my mother-in-law did mention she saw some bleeding from gums two days ago. And the joint pain in my knees and ankles is very severe.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Have you been exposed to dust or any construction site nearby? Or do you keep cats at home?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, actually our new house is right next to a construction site. There is a lot of dust all the time. And yes, we do have cats at home — two of them.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Did you visit any other doctor before coming here? Any medicines already given?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, we went to a local clinic a week ago. They said it was viral fever only and gave some paracetamol. But the symptoms became more severe, so we came here. Also, they had put me on losartan saying my blood pressure was slightly high, but that seems unrelated.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Do you smoke or consume alcohol?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Ahh, I am a social smoker doctor, not regularly. For alcohol, I take 2 drinks a week maximum. And I do take caffeine — every day, about three to four cups of tea.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any chills or sweating episodes? Any weight loss noticed recently?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, the chills are very bad at night. My mother-in-law says she found me shivering badly last night. And I think I have lost some weight recently, my clothes feel loose.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I will be examining you now. I need to check for lymph node enlargement and assess your abdomen for any tenderness or splenomegaly.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, my abdomen is very tender to touch on the right side. Even my husband noticed it looks a bit swollen.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Based on what you are telling me and the clinical findings — the high-grade fever, rash, bleeding from gums, joint pain, and thrombocytopenia features — this is most likely dengue fever. However, given the abdomen involvement and step-ladder pattern of fever, I cannot rule out typhoid co-infection. The earlier diagnosis of simple viral fever was incorrect.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, this is worrying. What tests will you do to confirm?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I am ordering a complete blood count urgently to check platelet levels, along with a dengue NS1 antigen test, Widal test for typhoid, and blood culture. I am also sending for a biopsy of the rash area to rule out other causes. A TMT is on hold for now given the losartan use — we will reassess blood pressure separately.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, should I stop the losartan that the previous doctor gave? And is the caffeine intake making things worse?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Please stop the losartan immediately — it can drop your blood pressure dangerously in dengue. Reduce caffeine intake as it causes dehydration. Avoid the dust from the construction site as much as possible, and keep the cats away from your room during recovery. Also avoid no alcohol completely right now.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I am prescribing oral rehydration salts to be taken frequently throughout the day, paracetamol 500 mg for fever — no ibuprofen or aspirin as they worsen bleeding. I am also starting azithromycin 500 mg once daily for seven days to cover the possible typhoid infection. You need platelet transfusion standby if levels fall further.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, do I need to get admitted? My husband is very worried and my mother-in-law is also asking.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Yes, I strongly recommend admission. Your platelet count may be dropping and the bleeding from gums is a warning sign. We need to monitor the complete blood count every twelve hours. Rest is very important — no exertion whatsoever. We will reassess in forty-eight hours once dengue NS1 antigen and Widal test results come.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Hello, welcome back. Please sit down comfortably.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Thank you doctor. Actually, umm, I am a bit nervous. I missed my last few appointments, I apologize for that. I was not feeling too well and work was very hectic.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: That is alright. Just tell me what is troubling you now. What are your main complaints?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, I have been having fever continuously since a few days now and also body ache all over. Yesterday it became very bad.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Is the fever mild or high grade? Any headache or rash on the body?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Uhh, it is mild in the morning but high at night. And yes, headache is there nonstop, radiating from my forehead to the back of my neck. No big rash that I noticed.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any vomiting or nausea? What about stomach pain — is it worse after eating?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yep, the nausea is there most of the time. And the stomach pain does become worse after eating, especially at night after my shift meal. I do night shifts so I eat very late.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I see. Do you work around any chemicals or pollution in your workplace? Any exposure to cold weather outside?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Nah, not chemicals exactly. But the hospital corridor where I work has a lot of pollution from outside air coming in, and I do walk out in the cold weather at odd hours. Night shifts are quite cold.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any history of childhood illness like typhoid or dengue before? Do you have high blood pressure or thyroid disorder?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, I had some childhood illness — my mother told me it was typhoid when I was around seven. And I was also detected with thyroid disorder two years back. I also have high blood pressure but that is somewhat controlled now.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Are you on any medications currently for thyroid disorder or high blood pressure?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: I was on levothyroxine and amlodipine but I am no longer taking them regularly. I kept skipping doses because of the night shift schedule.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I see, that is a concern. Do you smoke or drink wine? Any regular exercise or sports?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Umm, I used to play sports — football — but not anymore. I drink wine occasionally on weekends. And about smoking — yes, I am a chain smoker, easily a pack a day. I know it is bad.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any joint pain or eye redness? Any bleeding from the gums or blood in urine?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Nah, nothing like bleeding at all. But joint pain is there in my knees and wrists. I thought it was from long standing during night duty. No eye redness that I noticed.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: We need to run some tests urgently. I am ordering a dengue NS1 antigen test, Widal test for typhoid, complete blood count, and thyroid function test. Also a blood pressure reading right now.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Okay doctor. Will the dengue NS1 antigen test confirm whether I have dengue? I am a bit scared about that.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Based on your symptoms — the continuous fever, headache, joint pain, and nausea — this looks like a probable case of dengue fever. We cannot rule out typhoid either, given your history. Tests will confirm.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yep, please tell me what I should do now, doctor. Can I continue going to night shifts? I do not want to lose pay.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Absolutely not. You must take complete rest, no night shifts for at least one week. The cold weather exposure at night and irregular sleep are making the fever worse. Drink plenty of fluids, especially water and coconut water. Avoid wine and smoking completely during this illness.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I am prescribing paracetamol 500 mg three times a day for fever and body ache, ondansetron for the nausea, and ORS sachets to stay hydrated. Also restart your levothyroxine and amlodipine from today itself — skipping those is not acceptable.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Understood doctor. I will take the medicines properly this time and come back once the test results are ready. Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Good afternoon, please come in and sit down. What brings you here today?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, my stomach is giving trouble for three months. Also skin is little yellow colour only. I thought it will go by itself.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Yellowing of the skin and eyes is not something to ignore, madam. Any nausea or vomiting also?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes, doctor, vomiting happened several times last week. And fatigue is too much, I cannot even do walking now.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any pain in the chest or abdomen? Any fear of heart attack?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Umm, little dull aching pain is there in upper abdomen. No chest pain doctor. I was more worried it is heart attack only so I came.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Good that you came. Any frequent urination or dark coloured urine?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, urine is very dark, like tea colour. And frequent urination is also there, several times in the night also.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Have you had any illness recently, like COVID or any surgery?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Ahh, I had COVID 10-15 days before only. And my gallbladder removal surgery was done, problems started after surgery itself.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I see. Are you keeping any pets at home? Sometimes animal exposure can cause liver problems.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, we have two dogs. They are indoor dogs only. Is that causing this problem?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: It can sometimes contribute. Now, tell me about your diet. Are you eating junk food regularly?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Ahh, junk food I eat occasionally only. But my daughter says my oil intake is too much. I also eat outside food occasionally.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Are you on any medications currently? Like clopidogrel or inhaler or anything else?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, I am taking clopidogrel for my heart since long time. And doctor gave azithromycin when I had COVID. I finished that course. I also use inhaler occasionally for breathlessness.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: That is helpful. Clopidogrel can sometimes affect the liver. We need to do some blood tests and imaging. I am ordering a liver function test, ultrasound abdomen, and hepatitis B and C serology.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, all this testing is needed? What is happening to me? Is it something serious?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Madam, based on your symptoms — jaundice, dark urine, liver area pain, and your history of gallbladder surgery and COVID — this appears to be a case of fatty liver disease with acute jaundice. The tests will confirm.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, what I should do now? I am scared. Any serious problem will come?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Do not worry, we will manage this well. I am prescribing ursodeoxycholic acid tablets for liver support, pantoprazole for stomach protection, and multivitamin syrup. Continue your clopidogrel but we will review the dose after test results.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Completely stop junk food and oily food. Avoid pets close contact until we rule out infection. Gentle walking only — no heavy exercise. Drink plenty of water to manage dark urine.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, one more thing — sometimes itching on skin is also there. I forgot to tell. Is that also related?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Yes, itching on skin is a classic sign of jaundice — bile salts deposit under the skin and cause this. Once the liver function improves, itching will reduce. Come back 10-15 days after tests with reports.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Thank you so much doctor. I will follow everything you said.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Come in, please sit. What has brought you here today on emergency basis?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, hip pain is there. Since yesterday it is very bad.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Just hip, or is there pain in the back also? And how intense is it on a scale of ten?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Both. Back and hip both are paining. It is severe, maybe eight out of ten.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any tingling or numbness going down the leg or into the wrist?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes, tingling in the wrist is there. Happens often.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: What is your occupation? Are you doing any physical labour job?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Construction work, doctor. Lifting heavy materials several times in a day.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any lead or paint chemical exposure at the site? Are you working with old pipes or paint scraping?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes, recently we were breaking old walls. Lead paint dust was everywhere.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: And at home or nearby, any smoke exposure? Or anyone sick — like someone at school with infection, your children?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: My child had fever from someone at school. And yes, smoke is there from the cooking fire at home.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Do you also have hemorrhoids? Any bleeding or discomfort near the bottom?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Umm, yes doctor. Hemorrhoids is there since two weeks ago. Somebody told me it is just gastric problem. I believed them.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: How frequently is the bleeding from bottom happening?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: It happens frequently, doctor. Almost several times in a week.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Are you smoking? How many cigarettes in a day?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Ahh, I smoke 5 cigarettes daily, doctor. My friend smokes half a pack a day but I am less only. I go to the gym 3 times a week also.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Were you on any medicines before? Any blood test or X-ray done for this hip pain?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: No tests done. But I have thyroid problem and I take synthroid for that. For the hip pain they gave me ribavirin by mistake at another clinic. It did nothing.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: That was a wrong prescription — ribavirin is an antiviral, it should not have been given. Looking at your hip pain, tingling in the wrist, back pain, and the lead dust exposure, this looks like lead toxicity compounded by lumbar radiculopathy. The hemorrhoids is a separate issue aggravated by heavy lifting.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Continue your synthroid as before. I am prescribing diclofenac for the intense hip pain and calcium dobesilate for the hemorrhoids. We will also start chelation workup.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Most importantly, stop working near lead paint dust immediately. Wear a proper mask if you must go to the site. No heavy lifting at all — it is worsening your back and hemorrhoids both.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Okay doctor. And the tingling in wrist — will that go away?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Yes, once we get your blood lead level and nerve conduction study done, we will know the exact nerve damage. The tingling should reduce with treatment. Come back in three days with the reports.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Welcome back. Good to see you out of the hospital. How are you feeling today?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, I am still having cough and breathlessness. It is happening continuously now, not going at all.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Is the wheezing also still there? Any chest tightness when you go to the fields?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, the wheezing is still coming on and off. And my lower part of the chest is giving a dull ache, slightly painful when I breathe deep.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Is the cough constant throughout the day or more at certain times? Any sputum coming out?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: It is constant doctor, the whole day it is troubling. Some sputum is there, yellowish colour. At night it is getting worse.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Now tell me, you were admitted because of a severe asthma attack. Were you exposed to any mold in your house or storage area on the farm?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Ahh, yes doctor. after that incident only I was thinking — my grain storage room has lot of dampness and there is definitely mold growing on the walls there.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: That is a very important clue. Now, do you have history of anemia? I see it mentioned in the hospital discharge summary.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, the anemia was first found out during pregnancy and it was very low at that time. Then after delivery they gave me iron tablets for some months but I stopped in between.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: And what about your past surgery? The discharge notes mention an operation — what was that for?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: That was a cesarean section only doctor. after that incident I had some wound problem also but it healed. My bones also have been aching doctor, kind of a dull ache in the bones since the anemia started.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I see. Are you walking regularly for exercise? Any physical activity you are managing?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: I try walking in the morning occasionally, but with this breathlessness it has become difficult. Not anymore like before when I used to walk long distances.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I have to ask you directly — the hospital records mentioned something about substance use. Were you using cocaine?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, I will be honest. I did use cocaine occasionally some years back but not anymore. I also used to smoke half a pack a day but I have reduced. The cough comes rarely with blood, just once or twice.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Okay. We did a spirometry and chest X-ray during your hospital stay. Your complete blood count showed low haemoglobin and your peak flow was significantly reduced. Did they explain these reports to you?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: They said something about low blood and lungs not working properly but I could not understand fully doctor. They gave me salbutamol nebulization and IV steroids in the ward.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Let me explain step by step. You have allergic asthma triggered heavily by mold exposure from your farm storage. Combined with untreated anemia and past cocaine use which damages the lungs, your lungs are under severe strain. The dull ache in your bones is from iron deficiency secondary to the anemia. This is a case of uncontrolled asthma with iron deficiency anemia compounding your symptoms.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, so the mold in the storage room is the main reason my breathing trouble keeps coming back? And the bones aching is from the blood problem only?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Exactly right. The mold is a major trigger — you must stop going into that storage room immediately and have it cleaned thoroughly. The bones aching will improve once we treat the anemia properly. We also need to order a serum ferritin and peripheral blood smear to confirm the type of anemia.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I am prescribing fluticasone-salmeterol inhaler twice daily for the asthma, salbutamol inhaler as needed for rescue, ferrous sulphate tablets twice daily for the anemia, and montelukast at night. Continue these without stopping in between.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Okay doctor. Should I continue walking? And is it safe for me to go to the fields for farm work?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Walking occasionally on flat ground is fine, but avoid mold areas and dusty fields completely until the wheezing settles. Stop smoking entirely — even half a pack a day is worsening your lungs. Come back after two weeks with the serum ferritin report and we will review your breathlessness again.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Thank you doctor, I will follow everything you said. God bless you.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Hello, please come in and have a seat. I see you have been referred back from the higher centre.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, I was there for about a week. They did many tests and sent me back with some papers. I am not fully understanding what all they found.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: That is alright, I will go through everything. First tell me, how are you feeling now? Any cough or breathlessness?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Umm, the cough is still there doctor, but it is mild now. Earlier it was very bad. And the breathlessness also feels less frequent now compared to before.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Okay good. What about wheezing — that whistling sound from the chest?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Ahh yes, that sound. It was very scary initially. It is still coming less frequent now, mainly when I climb stairs or walk fast. My chest also feels tight sometimes.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Do you have any known history of anemia or any blood-related problem earlier?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, they told me I had anemia in 2024 itself. I was given iron tablets at that time but I stopped taking them after some time.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I see. And the higher centre records say you were put on tenofovir and sertraline. Are you taking those regularly?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Uh, not always doctor. Sometimes I forget, sometimes I feel okay so I skip. I have been missing doses here and there for the past 6-7 months.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: That is a concern. Do you smoke or have any such habits?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor I do smoke, 10 cigarettes a day. It started since college. I have been trying to cut down but it is very difficult.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: And at home, is there any mold on the walls? Any pet dander from animals, or do you keep birds at home?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Ahh yes doctor, we have two birds at home, parrots. And the bathroom has some mold also. I did not think these could be causing problem.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: They absolutely can. Now tell me, are you having fever, night sweats, or any weight loss also?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Umm, no fever as such. But I have lost some weight, maybe 3 to 4 kilos in the last 6-7 months. And fatigue is there every evening.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: The higher centre — did they do a spirometry or chest X-ray there?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, there are reports here. They did spirometry, chest X-ray, and also some blood test. The wheezing was confirmed they said.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: After going through all the reports and your symptoms, this is a case of bronchial asthma with some airway inflammation. The missed doses of tenofovir and sertraline have not helped your recovery at all.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, can the pet dander and mold really make the asthma worse? I thought it was only from smoking.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Both are triggers. The mold, pet dander, and birds at home can cause airway irritation and worsen wheezing. And smoking 10 cigarettes a day is directly damaging your lungs.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I am prescribing a salbutamol inhaler for immediate breathlessness relief, and a budesonide inhaler as a daily controller. Continue your tenofovir and sertraline without fail.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, will the cough fully go away? And should I remove the birds from home? That will be very difficult for my family.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: The cough will improve significantly if you take medicines properly and avoid triggers. Ideally keep the birds away from your living area, clean the mold from your bathroom, and please reduce smoking gradually. Missing doses again will set you back badly.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I am also ordering a repeat complete blood count to check your anemia status, and a peak flow meter reading every morning. Come back in two weeks and do not skip any dose this time.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Come in, come in. Sorry for the wait, we are running a bit behind today.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: No problem doctor, thank you for seeing us.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: So this is your son? How old is he and what is bringing you here today — is this for documentation or a check-up?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: He is nine years old doctor. We need the medical report for school insurance, but he has also been having cough and wheezing for few weeks now.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Okay, noted. Any breathlessness also? And how often is the wheezing coming?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, breathlessness is there twice a week at least. The wheezing happens every morning when he wakes up. Once in a while it is bad enough that he cannot do his running in school.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Does he become drowsy or very tired after these episodes? Any fever?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: He was very drowsy last night after one bad episode. No fever doctor, thankfully.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Was there any sick contact recently? Any coworker was sick or someone at home or school with similar illness?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Actually, a month ago his class teacher was sick with cough and cold for many days. Many children also got it.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any family history of asthma or allergic rhinitis?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, I myself have allergic rhinitis. His mother has asthma since childhood.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Has he taken any OTC medicine or anything from the medical shop for this cough?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: We gave some OTC medicine cough syrup from the pharmacy, but no relief. Doctor also once gave amoxicillin when he had throat infection, but he had a bad reaction to it.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: What kind of reaction to amoxicillin? Any rash or swelling?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: He got rash all over his chest and back, and swelling on his face. So we are told he is allergic to that medicine.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Understood, allergy to amoxicillin is noted. Does he do any physical activity regularly — like sports or exercise? How many days per week?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: He goes for football practice 3 times a week doctor, but lately he is stopping in between because of the breathlessness.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Okay. Based on the every morning wheezing, breathlessness, strong family history of asthma, and exercise intolerance, this child has bronchial asthma. The recent episode of being drowsy is concerning — it suggests the episode was quite severe.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, for the insurance form they are asking if he needs any special tests like angiography or lumbar puncture. Should we do all these?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Angiography and lumbar puncture are absolutely not needed here — those are for very different conditions. For this child I will order a spirometry and peak flow measurement, and a basic AST as part of the insurance panel. I will document the bronchial asthma diagnosis in his report.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: And for treatment doctor, what should we give him? Also please note he cannot take amoxicillin and we have been told heparin is also to be avoided for him due to some reaction he had after surgery.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Noted — allergy to amoxicillin and heparin both documented. I am prescribing a salbutamol inhaler for acute wheezing episodes and a budesonide inhaler as a daily controller. Please stop all OTC medicine cough syrups — they are not helping and may worsen the drowsiness.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Also keep him away from dust, cold air, and any sick children as much as possible. If he becomes drowsy again or breathlessness does not settle with the salbutamol inhaler, bring him to emergency immediately — do not wait.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Thank you so much doctor. We will follow everything you said.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Come in, please sit down. You look quite unwell today.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, two days ago I am getting chest pain and breathlessness. Very sudden it is coming.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Is the chest pain there right now? Any dizziness or palpitations also?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: No, pain is less now but breathlessness is still there. Heart it is beating fast fast. It is happening several times in the day.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any fever, cough, or leg swelling you noticed?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Umm, fever — no. But legs are a little swollen doctor, both sides. Cough is there almost never now.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Did you have COVID infection in the past? Any hospital admission for that?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Confirmed, doctor. Four months back I had COVID. I was in hospital for one week. Since then tiredness is always there.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I see. Are you smoking or drinking?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Before I was smoking two packs a day doctor, but not anymore. I stopped after COVID. Now 1 pack per day only — ahh, I mean I am trying to reduce still.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any dogs or animals at home? Any chemical fumes at your tailoring work?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: We have dogs at home, two dogs. And in the garment shop, fabric dust is always there doctor, full day.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Have you taken any medicine on your own? Any ibuprofen or paracetamol for the chest pain?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, I took ibuprofen two days ago for the chest pain. Little relief only it gave.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Do you do any exercise or running? Is the breathlessness worse with activity?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Exercise and running — no doctor, I am not doing. Standing and stitching whole day, that itself is tiring. Breathlessness is more when I am walking fast.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Let me examine you now. Your chest sounds are reduced on right side and your oxygen saturation is low at 91 percent. We need to do some tests urgently — EKG, MRI of the chest, and iron studies to check for anaemia.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, all these test — why iron studies? My blood is weak only?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Post COVID, many patients develop anaemia and lung inflammation. The iron studies will tell us if your blood is lacking. The EKG checks your heart rhythm because palpitations are there.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Okay doctor, I understand. I will do whatever you say.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Based on your history and examination, this looks like post-COVID sequelae with possible pleural effusion on the right side and cardiac arrhythmia. The fabric dust and smoking are making the lungs more weak.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, pleural effusion — what is this? Water in lungs only?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Yes, simply put, fluid is collecting around your lungs. That is why breathlessness is there and chest sounds are less. Also please stop taking ibuprofen on your own — it can cause kidney damage and worsen fluid retention.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I am prescribing furosemide to remove the extra fluid, aspirin for your heart, and prednisolone to reduce the lung inflammation. Also starting ferrous sulphate once iron studies confirm anaemia.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: You must stop smoking completely and avoid fabric dust at work — wear a mask every day. If chest pain or breathlessness becomes severe suddenly, come to emergency immediately without waiting.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Good morning! Come, come, sit. How are things going at school?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Busy as always, doctor. Year-end exams and all. I came for my regular refill mostly.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Of course, we will sort out the refill. But first tell me, any new pain or discomfort just started recently?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Umm, actually yes. There is this shooting pain near my wrist just started last week, and I also noticed a tremor in my neck area a few times now.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: A tremor near the neck? Is it happening more often lately or only occasionally? Any stiffness also?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: It is coming more often lately, doctor. And yes, some stiffness in the neck. Also my chest feels heavy sometimes, especially at night.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Okay. What about your periods — any irregularity? You had PCOS diagnosed two years ago, correct?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes, the PCOS is still there. Bleeding is heavy and I am having discharge too, weekly almost. And that frequent urination problem also came back.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: The frequent urination needs investigation. Have you done a urine culture recently? And any burning while passing urine?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Ahh, I did urine culture maybe four months back and it was clear. But now it is coming more often lately, doctor, so maybe we should repeat it.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Yes, we will repeat it. Also, you had a stone in the GB — any pain in the stomach or right side more often lately?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: That stone in the GB is still sitting there only, doctor. Some intense cramping weekly after eating. And I have developed piles also — very uncomfortable.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I see. Any mold at home or in the classroom? Sometimes mold exposure can worsen respiratory and other symptoms.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Actually yes, the old school building has some dampness and I think there is mold near the ceiling of my classroom. I did not connect that to anything.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: That can be a factor. Now, I have to ask — you had some beer drinking history. Are you still drinking?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, I was drinking beer daily for 30 years, I know, but not anymore. I stopped six months back. Please do not make it a big thing.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I appreciate you stopping, truly. Now what about diet — are you non-vegetarian or vegetarian currently?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: I switched to vegetarian two years ago mostly, but I eat non-vegetarian after meals at social functions sometimes. Umm, not very strict.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Based on what you are telling me — the tremor, shooting pain in the wrist, and heavy feeling in the chest — combined with your long beer history, I suspect alcohol withdrawal neuropathy and possible bone density loss.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Bone density loss? That sounds serious, doctor. What do we do?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: We need a DEXA scan to check your bone density properly. Given the prior alcohol use for 30 years, there is real risk. I am also concerned the tremor in the neck may need a spinal tap to rule out any neurological cause.

utterances.speaker: Patient
