utterances.text: Patient: Ahh, that spinal tap sounds scary. And doctor, I forgot to mention — I also have piles with intense pain near the bottom area, happening weekly.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: We will manage the piles conservatively for now. For the PCOS and discharge, I am continuing your current steroids course after meals, and I am prescribing metronidazole for the discharge, calcium supplements for the bone, and sitz bath preparation for the piles.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Regarding the steroids — do not take them on an empty stomach, always after meals. And please stay away from the mold area at school as much as possible — it will worsen the chest symptoms.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Understood, doctor. I will book the DEXA scan and repeat the urine culture this week. And not anymore drinking — I promise that part is done.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Ah, come in, come in. Good to see you again. What brings you in today?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, actually my family pushed me to come. It is just a minor rash on my skin, nothing serious. A bit of itching once in a while, that is all.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Minor rash, you say? Let me have a look. How long has this rash been there on your skin?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Umm, it has been there for a year actually. I thought it would go on its own. The itching is more often lately, I admit.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: A year is quite long. Is the itching happening multiple times a day now? Any discharge or bloody crusting from the skin lesions?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, the itching is multiple times a day now. And uh, there is some bloody scratching when I go too hard. The lesions are mostly on my arms and groin.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any family member was sick with a similar skin issue? Any international travel recently or staying in a rural area?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes, actually one family member was sick with something similar in 2020. No international travel, but I do work in different houses, some in a rural area outside the city.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I see. Any known history of epilepsy or any other chronic conditions I should know about?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, I have epilepsy, it is still active. I am on phenytoin for that. No other major issues.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Good that you are on phenytoin. Now, I have to ask — do you drink alcohol? And what about your sleep habits?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: I am an occasional drinker, doctor, nothing heavy. My sleep habits are not great — I sleep very late because of work schedules and I wake up multiple times a day, I mean night.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Alright. I have to ask you directly — any use of cocaine or heroin? You can be honest with me, it affects treatment decisions.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, I know why you are asking. No, I have not used cocaine or heroin. You know I am straightforward with you.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Good, I appreciate that. Any weakness in the limbs or episodes of paralysis, even temporary?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Ahh, actually yes, I have had one or two episodes of temporary paralysis on my right side after my seizures. Lasted maybe an hour each time. My neurologist said it is post-ictal.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Okay, that is Todd's paralysis related to your epilepsy. Now, coming back to the skin — any scaling, redness, or thickening of the affected patches?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes, there is definite scaling and redness. The patches on my groin are ring-shaped. I was actually suspecting a fungal infection myself, given the pattern.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Your suspicion is correct. This is a classic case of dermatophytosis — what we call ringworm or fungal infection. The groin involvement is tinea cruris and the arm patches are tinea corporis. One year of untreated spread explains the severity.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: I knew it was fungal infection. So what do we do now, doctor? I was also wondering if the phenytoin could be interacting with any antifungal you plan to prescribe?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Very good question. I am prescribing terbinafine cream to apply on the affected patches on your arms and groin twice daily, plus oral itraconazole 200 mg once daily for four weeks. I am avoiding fluconazole because of its interaction with phenytoin.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: That makes sense, doctor. Should I also do a skin scraping test or KOH examination to confirm?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Yes, I am sending you for a KOH examination and a skin scraping culture today just to confirm the fungal species. Also, given your epilepsy and those seizure episodes, I want a EEG and serum phenytoin level checked as well.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Keep the affected skin dry at all times, change your clothes daily, and do not share towels. The itching will reduce in about a week but continue the full course of itraconazole. Also, please regularise your sleep habits as poor sleep can lower your seizure threshold.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Thank you doctor, you always explain everything so clearly. I will follow all of this properly this time, I promise.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Please come in, sit down. No need to be nervous, just take a breath.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, I am sorry to come like this without appointment. I am having headache since this morning and I felt very dizzy also.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: It is okay, you did the right thing coming here. Now tell me, is this headache very severe, or just mild?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Umm, little-little only doctor, nothing much. But my ears are also feeling blocked and I have numbness in my hands every few days.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Every few days numbness is not small thing. Is the dizziness spinning type, like the room is rotating?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Ahh, yes doctor, spinning type only. I have to hold the wall when it happens. Also I feel nausea sometimes after.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any vomiting? And is there any ringing in ears also?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: No vomiting doctor. But ringing in ears is there hardly ever, only sometimes at night. The headache started for six months now, on and off.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: For six months and you are telling me now only? Any blurring of vision or weakness in your legs?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Uh, no doctor, no weakness. I was thinking it is just stress headache from household work. I did not want to bother anyone.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I understand, but these symptoms need checking. Any old history — any fracture or injury to bones earlier?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, I had a fracture in my wrist in January last year. And childhood chickenpox also I had.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Okay. Any history of gallstones or belly operations?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes, gallstones were detected two years back but no operation was done. They said monitor only.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Are you exposed to secondhand smoke or smoke at home — cooking fire, incense, anything like that?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: My husband smokes doctor, so secondhand smoke is there at home 3 times a week at least. And I cook on gas so little smoke from kitchen also.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Let me check your pulse and blood pressure now. Your pulse is 88, little on the higher side. I want to also order a MRI brain and audiometry test for those ears.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, MRI means something serious? I am getting little scared now.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Do not panic. Based on your spinning dizziness, ringing in ears, and headache, this looks like vestibular migraine possibly, or early Meniere's disease affecting your inner ears. MRI is just to rule out other causes.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Okay doctor. Is there medicine for this? It is disturbing my daily work so much.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Yes, I am prescribing betahistine tablet twice daily for the dizziness, and cinnarizine for the nausea. Also, ear drops for the blocked feeling in your ears.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Any things I should avoid doctor? I do yoga 3 times a week, can I continue?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Yoga is fine but avoid sudden head movements and bending forward. Also reduce secondhand smoke exposure as much as possible — ask your husband to smoke outside. Avoid stress triggers too.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Okay doctor. Should I come back if numbness in hands increases or headache becomes very severe?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Absolutely, come immediately if numbness spreads to your face or legs, or if you get loss of balance or blurring of vision. Follow up in two weeks with MRI report and blood pressure monitoring chart.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Good morning, please sit down. I understand you are here for insurance documentation today.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, good morning. Since 2024 I am having so much trouble — headache, dizziness, and sometimes my hands go numb. I have complained countless times to my previous doctor but nothing was done properly.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I see. Is the headache severe, or more of a dull ache? And where exactly — in the temples, forehead, or back of the head?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: It is severe doctor, mostly at the back of the head and spreading to the neck. The dizziness comes whenever I stand up quickly.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any numbness in the teeth area or jaw? Sometimes nerve problems can cause that also. And have you noticed any rash on the skin?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Umm, now that you mention it, there is some tingling near my teeth around two weeks back. And yes, I did get a rash on my arms also around two weeks ago, it came and went.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Alright. Do you have any history of rheumatoid arthritis, osteoporosis, or food allergy? These are important for the documentation.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Correct, doctor. I have osteoporosis diagnosed five years back and rheumatoid arthritis also. Food allergy is there to certain nuts — I was told before the tests were done to avoid them completely.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Have you ever had irregular periods in the past, or were you diagnosed with anemia? Even in earlier years?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, I had irregular periods for many years before menopause, and anemia was detected around that time too. I used to feel very weak, cold hands and feet always.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Do you drink alcohol? And how often — on weekends or more regularly?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Ahh, doctor I will be honest. I used to drink alcohol quite heavily before, but now only once in a while and on weekends at most. My children keep telling me to stop.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I appreciate your honesty. Do you do any exercise — yoga or walking? And are you exposed to pollution regularly, like near traffic or construction?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: I do yoga once in a while, not regularly. The road outside my building has a lot of construction — so yes, pollution is quite bad. Living alone makes it difficult to go elsewhere.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Are you currently on any medications? Has anyone done a MRI or chest X-ray for you recently? And was your temperature checked during the last visit?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: I am taking amlodipine for blood pressure and spironolactone also. The chest X-ray was done before the tests for documentation. MRI has not been done yet. Temperature was normal at the last visit, they told me.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Based on your symptoms — the headache, dizziness, numbness in the teeth and hands, combined with your history of rheumatoid arthritis and previous alcohol use — I believe this is a case of cervicogenic headache with possible peripheral neuropathy. The rash may also be linked to an autoimmune flare.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, could the pollution be making my headache worse? I feel it is always severe on days when the construction is going on.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Correct, pollution and dust particles can definitely trigger headache episodes and worsen dizziness, especially when there is already an underlying cervicogenic component. I doubt it is the primary cause alone, but it is certainly a strong contributing factor.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: And the anemia — could that be coming back? My hands and feet still feel cold so many times, it is happening countless times in a week.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: We need to check your MRI of the cervical spine and a full blood count to see if anemia has returned. Given your osteoporosis, the neck changes could be significant. Also we will repeat the chest X-ray for documentation purposes.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I will continue your amlodipine and spironolactone. Additionally, I am prescribing methylcobalamin for the numbness and peripheral neuropathy, and iron supplements if the blood count confirms anemia.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, any special neck exercises I should do? And should I stop yoga for now because of the dizziness?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Continue gentle yoga but avoid any neck inversion poses as they can worsen dizziness and headache. Most importantly, please reduce alcohol intake fully — even on weekends it is harmful with your current amlodipine dosage. Also stay away from pollution as much as possible and wear a mask near the construction area.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Thank you so much doctor, I will follow everything you said. It is difficult living alone but I will try my best.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Hello, come in, sit down. What brings you here today?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, I am having swelling in my legs and feet since a month ago. Also general body discomfort is there, feeling very tired all the time.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I see. Is there puffiness around your eyes also, especially in the morning? Any reduction in urine output?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, eyes are puffy every morning. Urine is also less, and it looks foamy and dark weekly or so I notice it.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Before coming here, did you try any treatment? Any local doctor or anyone else you consulted?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Umm, yes doctor. I went to a local compounder near our site. He gave me some pain tablets and said it is just body swelling from hard work. I was taking those for one week but no improvement. I also had tonsillitis problem around 2025 January which I treated on my own with some syrup.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: That compounder may have made things worse. Unnecessary pain tablets can damage the kidneys. Do you have any history of high blood pressure or asthma?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, I have high blood pressure for 10 years but I take tablets rarely. No asthma.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Okay. Any exposure at work — like mine dust, chemicals, or heavy metals? Construction workers sometimes get kidney problems from such exposures.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: I work near a mine construction site doctor, lot of dust and chemicals. Also recently a family member was sick at home with some fever, and I also had fever after a mosquito bite about six weeks back.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any pain in your lower back or abdomen? Some patients get pain near the ovaries region or lower abdomen with kidney problems.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Ahh, there is some dull aching in my lower back doctor, constant and dull. No specific pain near ovaries area.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Are you on any other medicines currently? Anything for mood or anxiety — like sertraline or escitalopram?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: No doctor, nothing like sertraline or escitalopram. I only take BP tablet rarely, that too only when my head is paining badly.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Looking at all your symptoms — swelling in legs, foamy urine, puffiness around eyes, uncontrolled high blood pressure, and your exposure history — I suspect you have chronic kidney disease, possibly worsened by the self-medication and overuse of pain tablets.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Kidney disease doctor? That sounds serious. What tests are needed?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: We need to do a serum creatinine, blood urea, urine routine microscopy, urine protein-to-creatinine ratio, and a kidney ultrasound. Also CBC and dengue serology given that mosquito bite history.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Okay doctor, I will get all done. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: For now I am prescribing amlodipine 5 mg once daily for your high blood pressure, and furosemide 20 mg once daily to reduce the swelling. Stop all pain tablets immediately — no ibuprofen or diclofenac at all.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, any food restrictions? And what about my body discomfort — is that related?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Yes, the body discomfort is related to chronic kidney disease. Reduce mine dust and chemical exposure at work immediately. Avoid high-protein foods, reduce salt intake, drink only 1 to 1.5 litres of water per day till kidney ultrasound results come. And please take BP medicines regularly, not rarely.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Also, never go to unqualified compounders again. The pain tablets they gave you have damaged your kidneys further. Your tonsillitis episode in 2025 that went untreated properly may also have triggered some kidney inflammation.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Now let me do a teach-back. Can you tell me — what medicines are you taking and what are you stopping?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, I will take amlodipine once daily and furosemide once daily. I will stop all pain tablets — no ibuprofen or diclofenac. I will reduce salt and chemicals at mine site, and come back after serum creatinine and all tests are done.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Very good, that is exactly correct. One more thing — if swelling in legs or face increases suddenly, or you get breathlessness or chest pain, go to emergency immediately. Follow up with me in one week with all reports.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Hello, please come in and sit. How are you feeling today after the discharge?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Umm, doctor I am still not fully okay. There is lower abdominal pain that is constant and I am having irregular periods non-stop worrying me.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Alright. Tell me about the pain — is it squeezing type or more of a dull ache in the lower abdomen?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: It is more like a squeezing sensation doctor, mainly in the lower abdomen and sometimes radiating to my back. It comes every few days but this time it has been constant.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Have you noticed any vaginal discharge? Is it thin or thick in consistency?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes, there is discharge — it is thin and whitish. I have also had weight gain and acne for a month now.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Okay. You have a history of PCOS I can see from your notes — since when exactly?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Since 2021, doctor. It has been going on for 2-3 years now. It is quite chronic at this point.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Were you on any medication for the PCOS? I see metformin was prescribed at discharge — are you still taking it as directed?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Ahh, doctor I have to be honest — I stopped the metformin on my own after four days because it was causing nausea and loose motion. I am no longer taking it.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I see. And you are working night shifts — any smoke exposure at your workplace or at home? Also, did anyone at home fall sick recently — any family member was sick?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: No smoke at work doctor, but yes, a family member was sick last week with some viral thing. I also feel very fatigued because of the night shifts.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Do you do any physical activity or yoga or sports? Lifestyle plays a big role in managing PCOS.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: I do yoga for 1 hour daily, doctor. I have been into physical activity since I was young. But with these night shifts I have not been able to do sports at all.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Let me summarise what I am seeing — you have PCOS with hormonal imbalance, the constant lower abdominal pain, thin vaginal discharge, and I suspect early secondary insulin resistance compounding the picture. This is a case of PCOS exacerbation.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, can the night shifts really make PCOS worse? I have had headaches daily also.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Yes, disrupted sleep worsens hormonal imbalance and insulin resistance significantly. The headaches are likely from sleep deprivation and hormonal fluctuations. We also need to check your oxygen saturation since you mentioned fatigue — low saturation can happen with disrupted sleep patterns.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, I had also taken albuterol inhaler from a friend once when I was feeling breathless — is that okay to do?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: No, please do not use albuterol on your own without prescription — it can cause palpitations and tremors. Self-medicating is no longer acceptable given your current condition. I also need to do a pelvic ultrasound and check your fasting insulin and LH/FSH ratio.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Understood doctor. Ahh, I also noticed my face has more hair growth and my scalp hair is falling out daily.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: That is hirsutism and hair loss from elevated androgens — very typical in PCOS. The plan is to restart medication at a lower dose, continue your yoga for 1 hour daily, and reduce night shift stress. We will also check a thyroid profile and HbA1c to rule out overlap conditions.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, so what medicines will you give me now for the PCOS and the lower abdominal pain?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I am restarting metformin at half the dose — 500 mg after dinner only — to minimise the nausea. I am also prescribing mefenamic acid for the lower abdominal pain, fluconazole for the vaginal discharge, and a vitamin D3 supplement since PCOS patients are almost always deficient.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Okay doctor. Anything special I should avoid or watch out for?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Avoid stress and irregular meals — both worsen insulin resistance. Keep doing your yoga and if possible add light physical activity even on night shift days. Come back after your pelvic ultrasound and oxygen saturation check are done — ideally within the week. No self-medicating with albuterol or anything else please.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Hello, come in, please sit down. I see you have been referred back from the higher centre.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, they sent us back and said to continue treatment here. My child is very sick, he has had fever and diarrhoea since today morning.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Alright, let me understand. Is the fever continuous or coming and going? And how many times has the diarrhoea occurred?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: The fever is continuous doctor, and loose motions have happened a few times already since morning.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any vomiting or rash? And has he complained of hip pain or pain in the joints at all?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Umm, not at all any rash or vomiting doctor. But yes, he has been saying his joints are hurting, and slight hip pain also is there.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: So to summarise what I am seeing — the child has fever, diarrhoea a few times, hip pain, and joint pain. The higher centre likely ruled out major structural issues. Now I want to check exposure history. Has he been near birds recently?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, we have pigeons on the terrace and he plays there all the time. He also goes to crowded places like the market with me frequently.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: That is important. Exposure to birds and crowded places can explain certain infections. Now, has the child had any cough? Any dry cough especially?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Ahh yes, there is a dry cough for the past two days also doctor. I forgot to mention.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Does anyone in the family have any history of stone problem or cancer? Any serious illness history I should know about?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: His grandfather had a stone problem in the kidney, and one aunt had cancer doctor, but she recovered. The child himself had no surgeries except one small one but that pain started after surgery.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I see. And the mother — were there any complications during pregnancy? Any pain in the lower abdomen or infections reported?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, my wife had pain in the lower abdomen during pregnancy but the doctors said it was normal at that time. No major issues.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Alright. Now I must ask you directly — do you vape or use drugs? I ask because it can affect the child's home environment.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, I will be honest. I do vaping every day, since I was young. And I used drugs for 10 years but I have stopped now mostly.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I appreciate your honesty. The vaping every day at home is likely worsening the child's respiratory symptoms. You must stop immediately. The secondhand exposure is harmful.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: That's right doctor, my wife also keeps saying the same thing. I will try my best to stop.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Based on everything — the fever, dry cough, diarrhoea, joint pain, hip pain, and bird exposure — this looks like a case of reactive arthritis triggered by a bacterial infection, possibly from the environment. I also want to rule out psittacosis given the bird exposure.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, what tests do we need to do now? Is it something serious?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I am ordering a kidney function test because of the family stone history and the joint symptoms. I will also order a complete blood count and a stool culture to identify the infection causing diarrhoea.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, can you give something to bring down the fever and hip pain right now? He is very uncomfortable.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Yes. I am prescribing paracetamol syrup for the fever and pain — give it every six hours as needed. And because of the dry cough and breathing trouble, I am also giving an inhaler for relief. Use it twice a day.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Should we avoid crowded places and keep him away from the birds on the terrace?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Absolutely, keep him away from birds and avoid crowded places until the fever settles. Give paracetamol regularly, use the inhaler as instructed, ensure plenty of fluids for the diarrhoea, and come back with the kidney function test and stool culture reports in three days.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Good morning. Please sit, sit. Your family told me you were not wanting to come today, is it?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Aah, doctor, they are overreacting only. I am fine mostly. These people worry too much.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Alright, let us see. Tell me, what is the main problem you are having? Any stomach pain or gas trouble?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Umm, yes doctor, there is some dull pain near the upper abdomen area, and gas is happening non-stop. Also acidity is there since many years.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Is the pain more near the belly button side or higher up? And does it go anywhere else, like to the bones of your back?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: It is mostly in the upper abdomen, doctor. Sometimes a mild ache goes to the bones in my back side also. But nothing too serious I feel.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: How many times in a day is this pain coming? And is there any vomiting or nausea?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: The pain comes many times throughout the day, doctor. And yes, nausea is there every other day. No proper vomiting as such.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I see. Now tell me, are you on any medicines? Your family said you changed something on your own recently?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Ahh, doctor, I used to take pantoprazole tablet that you gave earlier. But I stopped it and started taking antacid syrup from the medical shop only, on my own. That one seemed to work better I thought.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Hmm, that is not good, you should not change medicines on your own. Now, are you having any diet issues — eating too much spicy or oily food?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, my diet is normal only. I eat whatever is cooked at home. Maybe some spicy items, but that has been many years like that. I am not doing anything new.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: What about chewing tobacco? Are you still taking tobacco in any form?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Umm, doctor, I have been chewing tobacco for 30 years. I am an occasional drinker also, but very less. These things I cannot just stop suddenly, no?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: That chewing tobacco habit is a big problem for your upper abdomen and can seriously worsen your acidity and gastric pain. You must stop it.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Have you had any international travel recently, or been near any sick person with stomach infection? Also, any exposure to heat for long hours?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: No doctor, no international travel. I stay at home only. But yes, my grandson had some stomach infection last month — he is a sick person who was vomiting — and I was near him only. And yes, I sit in the sun many times, so heat exposure is there.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Did you do any tests? Any stool test or ultrasound abdomen done earlier?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: No doctor, nothing like that. No tests at all. I was just managing with the antacid syrup only.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Okay, based on your symptoms — the dull pain in the upper abdomen, acidity non-stop, nausea, and your tobacco habit for 30 years — this looks like chronic gastritis, possibly with peptic ulcer disease. We also need to rule out H. pylori infection given the contact with a sick person.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I am prescribing pantoprazole 40 mg twice daily before food, domperidone for the nausea, and sucralfate suspension at night for the upper abdomen lining. Do not self-change these medicines this time.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, should I do any test also? And what about that mild ache going to my back bones?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Yes, we will do a throat swab to rule out any associated infection, stool antigen test for H. pylori, and ultrasound abdomen to check the upper abdomen organs. The back bones ache may be referred pain from the gastritis, but we will monitor it.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: And strictly avoid chewing tobacco, reduce spicy diet, and avoid sitting in heat for long. Come back after one week with the test reports.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Okay doctor, I will try my best. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Arrey, Suresh! Come come, sit down. How is your wife? And the kids — exams are going on, no?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, all fine. Wife is managing the house. Younger one's school exams are there next week. But I myself am still not hundred percent, that is why I came so soon.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Good that you came early for follow-up. You were discharged not too long ago, so I want to check everything properly. How are you feeling overall?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, the fever has reduced, but I am still feeling moderate weakness. Body is not cooperating fully.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any rash on the body? Or any skin infection anywhere? Sometimes after such fever it can appear.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Umm, yes doctor, there is something near my belly button area — some redness there. I thought it was just irritation from the hospital bed.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Let me see — yes, this looks like a skin infection, possibly secondary to your hospital stay. We need to address this. And your blood pressure reading — let me do a BP check right now.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, the blood pressure was always slightly high, from long time now. Even in hospital they were noting it.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Okay. Now, I heard from the discharge nurse you were on medicines from two or three different doctors. What all are you taking currently?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Ahh, yes doctor. One doctor near our locality gave me clopidogrel for the heart thinning. Another doctor gave acetaminophen for pain and fever. And pregabalin was given for some nerve pain in my legs.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Suresh, this is a problem. Clopidogrel and acetaminophen together can affect your stomach lining, and with dengue history your platelet count was already low. You should not take these without telling me first.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: I am sorry doctor, I did not know. Also, I have diabetes and asthma from long time, so different doctors have been giving different things.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Okay. What about cold weather — does it trigger your breathlessness? And any cats or animals at home?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, cold weather definitely makes my breathlessness worse. And we do have two cats at home, they are with us from long time. You think they are causing problem?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Possibly contributing to your asthma. I want to arrange an allergy test for you — it will show if the cats are a trigger. Also, we had done a PSA test during your admission as routine screening — that report is here, it looks absent for any concern, so no prostate issue right now.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Oh that is a relief doctor. And the dengue and typhoid both together — is that common? I had both confirmed in hospital only.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: It is uncommon but not impossible, especially when the body immunity is weak. Your measles history as a child also may have left some effect on immunity. That is why recovery is slower for you.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, I also do cycling and running for fitness — for 20 years I have been doing this. Should I continue now or stop?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Stop running and heavy cycling for at least two to three weeks. Your body is still recovering. Also, I know you take coffee — do you have it socially or more regularly?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Ahh, I take coffee socially mostly, but occasionally at home also when work stress is there. At the tailor shop, long hours sitting also giving me back pain occasionally.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Okay. Any nausea or vomiting still? And loose motion — is it there or absent now?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: The loose motion is absent now, thankfully. Nausea is also gone mostly. Only the weakness and that belly button area redness is bothering me.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Alright Suresh, I am stopping clopidogrel for now — do not take it until I review. Continue acetaminophen only if fever comes, not otherwise. For the skin infection near belly button, I am prescribing a topical antibiotic cream. Hold pregabalin also — I will re-evaluate that nerve pain.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Also, keep monitoring your blood pressure with home BP check every morning. Note down the readings and bring them when you come next week. We will also recheck your dengue recovery with a blood panel.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Understood doctor. I will note the BP check readings occasionally — I mean morning and evening both. And I will not start cycling or running without asking you. Thank you so much doctor.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Come in, come in. Please sit quickly, I have many patients today.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Sorry doctor. I am feeling very tired and dizzy for a year now. Last few days it became very bad, that is why I came.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any breathlessness or palpitations? Any yellowing of your eyes or skin?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, breathlessness is there nonstop since few days. And yellowing of eyes, my wife noticed last week.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any headache or fainting? How about swelling in legs?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Headache is there every morning, doctor. Swelling in legs is also there intermittently. No fainting but I feel I will fall sometimes.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any history of bleeding disorders or high blood pressure in the family?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Umm, not aware of any such thing in family, doctor. I myself had high blood pressure detected last year only.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any known drug allergy? And are you currently on any blood pressure tablets?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: No allergy doctor. I was on amlodipine but I stopped it on my own and started some ayurvedic tablet from the medical shop last month.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: You changed medicine on your own? That is not correct. Do you drink alcohol or smoke?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Ahh, sorry doctor. Yes I drink alcohol, 3 beers a day, for 10 years. I also smoke every morning with my tea, one cigarette only.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: What work do you do? Any factory exposure or pollution?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: I am daily-wage labourer doctor, I work in a factory near the highway. Lot of pollution and dust there. No mask or anything they give us.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Did you do any tests before coming? Any USG report or Echo done before the tests I will prescribe?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: I did one ultrasound last month doctor, at a small clinic. They said liver is slightly enlarged but I did not understand the report properly.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I see. Looking at your tiredness, yellowing of eyes, swelling, and your alcohol history, this is a case of anaemia with nutritional deficiency and possible liver damage.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Anaemia means what doctor? Is it very serious?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Anaemia means your blood is very low in iron and important nutrients. With your alcohol intake and factory work, your body is not absorbing properly. It can become serious if ignored.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I am prescribing ferrous sulphate tablet every morning after food, folic acid once daily, and restart your amlodipine for high blood pressure. Stop that ayurvedic tablet immediately.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Okay doctor. This tiredness in legs and dizziness will go with these medicines?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: It will improve in four to six weeks if you take medicines properly. You must also eat green vegetables, lentils, and eggs every morning. Your breathlessness and swelling should reduce as anaemia improves.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Reduce your alcohol intake immediately — your liver is already showing enlargement. Smoking also must stop. Never change your blood pressure medication on your own again.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I am ordering a fresh ultrasound, an Echo for your heart given the swelling, and a full blood count with liver function test. Bring all reports next week.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Thank you doctor, I will do all tests and come. I will try to reduce drinking also.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Asha! Come in, come in. How are the kids? Your daughter must be in college now, no?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, she cleared her entrance exam. Thank you for asking.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Good, good. Now tell me — your family brought you today. What is going on with your health?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Honestly doctor, I am fine mostly. But last month this fatigue and brain fog started and it is there all the time now.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: You had COVID some months back, yes? Any breathlessness? Any palpitations? What about pain in the belly or epigastric area?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Umm, the breathlessness is yes, it comes every morning when I climb stairs. And there is intense burning in the epigastric area — it is non-stop since a week ago.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any pressure or cramping around the uterus area? Any irregular bleeding?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Ahh, now that you say — there is a dull ache low down near the uterus side also. No bleeding, nothing like that.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Asha, you had a blood transfusion after your second delivery, correct? And any known allergies I should keep in mind?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, the blood transfusion was quite a while ago. And I have allergies to sulfa drugs — you noted it last time.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Good that you reminded me. Now honestly — are you still drinking? Any recreational drugs or vaping? I know you are a social smoker — still going on?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: The vaping — yes, I do it once in a while. Drinking is social only doctor, nothing heavy. No recreational drugs, I swear.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any sick person contact at home recently? And your husband — he still works near that factory area?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes, my mother-in-law was sick last month — she had fever and cough. And yes, my husband comes from that factory side, there is always dust and fumes on his clothes.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Are you taking the pregabalin I prescribed last time for your nerve pain? And the ear drops for that ear infection?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Uh, doctor — the pregabalin I have been missing doses, I will not lie. The ear drops I finished the course. The ear pain is better now.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Asha, you cannot miss doses like this. Any tingling or numbness in your hands or feet still? Any headache?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: The tingling in the feet is there every morning when I wake up. Headache also comes every morning doctor.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Asha, this is a clear picture of post-COVID syndrome — the fatigue, brain fog, breathlessness, and nerve pain all fit. The epigastric burning is likely gastritis triggered by the viral illness and your irregular eating.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: But why is the uterus area giving pain also, doctor? Is that related?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: The pelvic discomfort near the uterus could be stress-related tension or referred pain from the belly. We need to rule out gynecological causes — I am referring you for a pelvic ultrasound. I also want a CBC, ferritin, and thyroid function test given the fatigue.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, all these tests — okay, I will do. But what about this intense burning in my epigastric area? It is disturbing my sleep also.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I am starting you on pantoprazole 40mg before breakfast for the gastritis, and domperidone if the nausea comes. Please resume your pregabalin — no more skipping. I am also adding vitamin B12 tablets for the tingling and fatigue.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Asha, the vaping must stop completely — it is worsening your breathlessness and irritating your stomach lining. Even once in a while is too much now. Cut the drinking also, especially with pantoprazole going on.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Okay doctor, I understand. I will do the pelvic ultrasound and CBC this week and come back. And I will not miss the pregabalin this time, promise.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Come in, come in. Please sit down. How are you today?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: I am okay doctor, thank you. I am here because my operation is scheduled next week and they are asking for pre-operative clearance.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Yes, noted. And what is your occupation? You look like you work with your hands.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: I am a tailor, doctor. I work in a garment factory for more than fifteen years now.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Alright. Before we proceed to clearance, I can see something on your forehead and arms. Is there any rash or itching bothering you?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Ahh, yes doctor, that is why I was actually a little nervous to come. I have itching and a rash on my forehead and also on my neck. The itching is very intense.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: How long have you had this? And is the rash spreading anywhere else — chest, back, between the fingers?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: It started around three weeks back doctor. And umm, yes, it has spread a little between my fingers also. I was checking online and I thought it might be some fungal infection, so I delayed coming.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Does the itching happen at any particular time? Is there any burning or discharge from the rash?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: The itching is there once a day mainly in the evenings after work. No discharge doctor, but there is some redness and scaling also. I read online it looks exactly like ringworm.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I see. And you work in a factory with many other workers? Any factory chemicals or fabric dyes you are exposed to regularly?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, we use lot of synthetic fabric and the dyes also. Whole day I am sitting and cutting and stitching. It is a closed factory, not much air also.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any history of allergies — to medicines, fabric, or food? And any past surgery we should know about?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Umm, I had a past surgery for appendicitis around eight years back. And I have some allergies to sulpha drugs, doctor — that is documented. Also I have a old injury on my right knee from an accident.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Good that you mentioned the allergies — we will be careful with medicines. Do you smoke or drink? Any such habits?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: I am a social smoker doctor, since college only — not heavy at all. And drinking also since I was young, but very occasional, only at functions and all.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any stomach pain or discomfort in the epigastric area? Any acidity or heartburn?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, actually I do have some acidity problem. The epigastric area is sometimes uncomfortable after surgery — it started after my appendix operation only. I am taking ranitidine on my own sometimes.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any joint pain or aching in the bones? Sometimes with skin infections there can be body ache also.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: No doctor, my bones are fine. No joint pain. Only the skin is bothering me. I was reading online about fungal infection and it said I should apply some antifungal cream — so I tried one from the medical store but no relief.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I have examined the rash on your forehead, neck, and between the fingers. This is a case of dermatophytosis — what you correctly guessed, a fungal infection. The moist closed environment at your factory is likely contributing.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Ah, so I was right doctor! I read about it online. So what do I do now? Will it affect my operation also?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: We need to treat this before the operation. I am prescribing terbinafine tablets once daily and clotrimazole cream to apply on the rash area twice daily. Do not use the over-the-counter cream anymore — it was not the right formulation.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Also, please avoid prolonged exposure in the closed factory without ventilation until this clears. Keep the skin dry and clean. We will also do a KOH smear test and routine blood work for pre-operative clearance — your allergies to sulpha drugs are noted and we will ensure the anaesthesia team is informed.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Thank you so much doctor. I will do as you say. Should I continue the ranitidine also for my epigastric problem?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Good morning, please sit down. Take your time, no need to be nervous.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Good morning doctor. I am a teacher, I have been managing on my own quite a while ago when this all started, but it is getting too much now.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Alright. What are the main problems you are having? Tell me from the beginning.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, umm, I have pain in my whole abdomen, it is worse with movement, and every morning I wake up feeling very stiff and uncomfortable.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any tingling or numbness anywhere, especially in the legs or feet?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Ahh, yes doctor, tingling in both feet is there continuously. Sometimes once in a while it shoots up to my knee also.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any burning or urgency when passing urine? Any bladder problem?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Umm, yes doctor, the bladder is giving trouble also. I feel burning and I cannot hold properly. It is very embarrassing to say this.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I understand, please do not worry. Any history of diabetes or high blood pressure?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, yes, I have diabetes since 2021, and hypertension also is there. I take tablets but not regularly, I admit.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Have you taken any pain medications or prednisolone on your own for this pain?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Ahh doctor, yes, I have been taking pain medications just started taking more this week, and a friend gave me prednisolone also for two days. I did not want to come to hospital, I was scared.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any history of alcohol use? Please be honest, it will help me treat you better.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, I used to drink heavily since I was young, but I have cut down now. Not every day anymore.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any recent international travel? And have you been exposed to cold weather for long periods?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, I had international travel to Canada last year, and there I was in cold weather for nearly three weeks. After that my joint pain and stiffness became much worse.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any swelling in the joints? Any redness or warmth in your hands or wrists?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Umm, yes, my wrists are swollen and warm to touch. The stiffness is worse with movement in the morning especially.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Looking at everything — the joint swelling, every morning stiffness, tingling in feet, and bladder symptoms along with your diabetes — I suspect you have rheumatoid arthritis with diabetic peripheral neuropathy. The self-use of prednisolone without proper guidance has complicated things.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, is the bladder problem also because of the diabetic neuropathy? And is the prednisolone causing any harm?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Yes, the bladder involvement can be from diabetic neuropathy. And unsupervised prednisolone can worsen your blood sugar and cause bone thinning, especially with your history of alcohol use.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I am prescribing methotrexate for the rheumatoid arthritis, methylcobalamin for the tingling and neuropathy, and adjusting your metformin dose. We will stop the unsupervised pain medications and prednisolone immediately.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: You must avoid cold weather exposure, reduce alcohol completely, and never take prednisolone or pain medications without consulting me — they will damage your stomach lining and raise your sugar levels dangerously.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: We need anti-CCP antibody test, HbA1c, urine culture for the bladder infection, nerve conduction study, and liver function test given your alcohol history. Please get these done today.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Thank you so much doctor. I will follow everything properly this time, I promise.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Ah, Mr. Ramesh, you have finally come back. It has been quite some months since your last visit.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Sorry doctor, work pressure was too much. Factory was running double shifts.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: No problem, let us start fresh. Junior, please observe carefully — this gentleman missed follow-up for several months, so we must revisit everything. Mr. Ramesh, what is bothering you most right now?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, main problem is this chest pain in my chest area and palpitations. These are happening daily now.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: And the palpitations — are they coming with the chest pain together, or separately? Any back pain also? Junior, notice how we always look for radiation of pain in the back.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Together sometimes, sporadically they come separately also. Yes, some back pain is there in my lower back, but that I thought was from standing all day in the factory.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Has your blood pressure been checked recently? Any dizziness or shortness of breath?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Umm, dizziness comes on and off, doctor. Shortness of breath started after that incident at the factory last year — there was a gas leak.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Gas leak — that is important. Junior, write that down, possible chemical fume exposure. Mr. Ramesh, any international travel in the past few months? Sometimes travelling can affect the heart and lungs.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: No, no international travel doctor. I have not gone anywhere outside the state even.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Good. Now tell me honestly about your habits. Are you still taking whiskey? And what about stress levels and diet? These three are major contributors in cardiovascular cases, junior — always ask together.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Whiskey I have stopped, doctor. Completely stopped after that incident when my wife gave me a scolding. But stress is very high still. And diet is not good — mostly canteen food, oily and salty.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Good that you stopped alcohol. Now smoking — how many cigarettes are you taking?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Ahh, before I was smoking two packs a day, doctor. Now I have reduced to 10 cigarettes a day on working days and I only smoke on weekends more heavily with my colleagues.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Junior, note this — even 10 cigarettes a day is dangerous with his cardiac risk profile. Mr. Ramesh, any past history? Any pneumonia or broken bone or major illness before?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, I had pneumonia about three years back, was admitted for one week. And there was a broken bone in my left wrist from a factory accident two years ago. Took paracetamol for that pain, nothing else.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Were you given any losartan or any blood pressure medication before you disappeared from follow-up? And any use of albuterol inhaler?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes, losartan was given by you previously, but I ran out and did not buy more. Albuterol inhaler was given after the gas leak episode, I used it for two months and then stopped on my own.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Junior, this is a classic case of uncontrolled hypertension with hypertensive heart disease features — the palpitations, chest pain, and dizziness are all consistent. The pneumonia history plus chemical fume exposure has likely given him some reactive airway disease on top. We must investigate properly.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Mr. Ramesh, I am ordering a ECG, chest X-ray, echocardiogram, lipid profile, and kidney function test today itself. Junior, in hypertensive patients we always check serum creatinine and urine microalbumin for end organ damage.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, is this chest pain going to become a heart attack? I am scared. And will the back pain also go away?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: We will prevent that with proper treatment. I am restarting losartan 50 mg daily for your blood pressure. I am also prescribing albuterol inhaler as needed for the breathlessness, and paracetamol 500 mg for the back pain — do not take any other pain killers without asking me.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Most importantly — fix your diet, reduce salt and oil intake completely. Manage stress with walking or relaxation. And stop smoking fully — even 10 cigarettes a day is damaging your heart and lungs every single day.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Understood doctor. One more thing — sometimes I feel numbness in my left arm, it comes sporadically. I forgot to mention.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: That numbness in the left arm is a very important sign — junior, this could indicate cardiac ischemia radiating to the arm. Mr. Ramesh, do not delay the ECG today, and if you feel severe chest pain or left arm pain together at any time, go to emergency immediately. Come back in two weeks after all tests are done — no missing appointments this time.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Good morning, please sit down. What brings you here today?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Good morning doctor. I am a domestic help, and I am here because my employer is asking for medical documentation for insurance purposes. My family members also noticed some problems with me and told me to get checked properly.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Alright, that is fine. Tell me, what symptoms are you having? Any rash or itching on the body?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, there is itching and some rash on my lower part — my sister noticed it and said the rash looks green in some areas, and it comes and goes. It is happening frequently.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Okay, and how long has this been going on? Any discharge or burning sensation along with the itching?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: It started two months ago doctor. My sister said there is a discharge sometimes also. And the burning sensation is there after every meal in my upper abdomen also — separate problem that is.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I see. Any vertigo or dizziness? Any headache?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Umm, the vertigo was there when I was younger doctor, but nobody told me about it being serious at that time. Now it is not there much.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Okay. Have you been exposed to any contaminated food recently, or any mosquito bite — have you been working in areas where mosquitoes are more?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, we had some issue at the house where I work — the food was not good some time ago, I think I ate some contaminated food. And mosquito bite is always there, we live near a waterlogged area.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any exposure to mercury? Sometimes in certain cleaning products or skin-lightening creams that are used in households — have you applied anything like that?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Ahh, doctor my employer uses some whitening cream, and I also applied it some time ago — I did not know it could be a problem. Could it have mercury in it?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: It is quite possible, we will check that. Now tell me, do you smoke or take any substance? What is your diet like?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: I use e-cigarettes doctor, half a pack a day roughly. I drink non-vegetarian food — I mean I eat non-veg daily. I also do exercise socially, only sometimes with friends.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Have you taken any painkillers or any cream on your own for the rash? Any past surgeries or medical history?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: I took some painkillers for the burning in the upper abdomen, but nothing specific for the rash. I had a cholecystectomy — gallbladder removal — done about three years back.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Looking at the rash on your lower part with the greenish tinge and discharge, along with the mercury exposure history, this looks like a fungal infection combined with possible contact dermatitis. The upper abdomen burning after your cholecystectomy could be post-cholecystectomy syndrome.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, what tests will you be doing? I am a bit worried about the cost — some tests I may not be able to do right now.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I understand. I will advise a patch test to confirm the mercury or chemical contact dermatitis — that is essential. I was also thinking of a DEXA scan given your age and dietary history, but we can defer that if there is a cost issue.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: The patch test is okay doctor, I can do that. But the DEXA scan please let us keep for later — maybe after insurance settles.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: That is fine. For the fungal infection, I am prescribing clotrimazole cream to apply on the affected area daily, and fluconazole tablet once a week for four weeks. For the upper abdomen burning, take pantoprazole daily before breakfast. Stop the painkillers on your own — they are making the gastric irritation worse.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Okay doctor. Anything I should be careful about? The itching is very bad at night especially.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Yes, please stop using any whitening cream immediately — the mercury exposure must be cut off completely. Avoid non-vegetarian oily food after every meal situation — eat light, especially given your cholecystectomy history. Also, the e-cigarettes are irritating your skin and overall immunity, so try to cut down from half a pack a day.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, for the insurance documentation — will you write that this fungal infection and contact dermatitis is work-related because of the chemicals I was exposed to at my employer's home?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I can document that there is a likely occupational mercury exposure contributing to the contact dermatitis — the patch test result will strengthen that case. Once we have the report, I will prepare the formal documentation. Come back in two weeks and we will review the rash, the itching, and the upper abdomen burning also.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Welcome back. Good to see you up and about after the hospital stay.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Thank you doctor, umm, I am feeling a little better now.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: So tell me, how have things been since discharge? Any new complaints or are the old ones frequently returning?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, umm, the gastritis is still there but it is less frequent now. And since morning I am having a bad headache.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: The gastritis — is the feeling burning type, same as before?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, burning in the stomach area, especially after eating. I am also noticing my stools are thin and sometimes green, which is worrying me.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I see. Now regarding your liquor intake — are you still drinking or have you stopped?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, umm, I have never fully stopped, I am being honest. I take it occasionally now, maybe rarely in a week, not like before.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: You must understand that even small amounts of liquor is putting heavy load on your liver, especially with your history. Do you have any fumes exposure at your shop?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, there is some fumes from paint and varnish products we keep in the shop. I have been still going to work despite the hospitalization.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Understood. Now let me review — you had a hepatitis diagnosis in 2021, correct? And your rheumatoid arthritis and hypertension — are those being managed?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Umm, yes doctor. The rheumatoid arthritis medicines I stopped two months ago because of all the hospital visits. The hypertension tablets I am taking sometimes only, not regularly.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Were you given heparin during the hospital stay? And are you currently on sertraline for your mood?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, they gave heparin in the hospital. The sertraline was started two months ago only, I am taking it but very shy to tell anyone at home.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: That is completely fine, no need to be shy about it. I also heard you are caring for a sick family member right now — that must be adding a lot of stress?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, my wife has been unwell, so I am managing the shop and home together. Umm, I think the headache and gastritis are getting worse because of no rest.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: We did a blood test last visit. I am also checking your heart rate now — it seems slightly elevated. Did you take any acetaminophen for the headache today?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, I took two tablets of acetaminophen since morning but the headache is still there only.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Looking at all the findings — the burning in the stomach, thin and green stools, ongoing liquor use, and the background of hepatitis — this is a case of alcoholic gastritis with possible liver involvement and stress-induced headache.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, is the liver in serious danger? Umm, I am scared.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: The liver is under strain right now. We will repeat the blood test including liver function, and monitor your heart rate closely. The most important thing is zero liquor — even occasionally is harmful in your condition.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I am prescribing a proper course — continue sertraline as it is, do never stop it suddenly. For gastritis I am adding a proton pump inhibitor, and for the headache avoid acetaminophen excess since your liver is already stressed — I am writing a safer alternative. Also restart your rheumatoid arthritis medicines as before.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, the fumes at shop — should I be worried about those also for the liver?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Come in, please take a seat. What brings you here today?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, I am a railway employee. My department has asked for full medical documentation for insurance purpose. But honestly I am also here because my symptoms have become very bad now.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Alright, let us go through everything properly. Tell me, what are the main complaints you are experiencing right now?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, I am having depression since the last few months, and also vision problems — my both sides of the field of view have become blurry. And there is pain in the lower part of my abdomen that is simply unbearable.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Tell me more about this lower part pain. What does it feel like, and does it come and go?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, it is a squeezing type of sensation and it comes and goes. It has happened countless times over the past weeks. Sometimes the pain feels like it is coming from around the colon area.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Do you have any known medical history? Any clotting disorder or blood-related problems?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, I was diagnosed with a clotting disorder as a teenager. I was also told I had hypertension and type 2 diabetes about ten years back.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any surgery in the past? And did your symptoms change after surgery?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, I had an operation on my abdomen about five years ago for a bowel obstruction. The pain in my lower part actually became worse after surgery.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Since you work with the railways, I need to ask about occupational exposures. Have you been exposed to smoke, chemical fumes, or dust at your workplace?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, still working in the yard area. There is a lot of smoke from engines and burning materials. I have been exposed to it for many years, ever since I joined.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Do you smoke or drink alcohol?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: I have been smoking since I was young, doctor. At present it is about two packs a day. Alcohol I take occasionally only.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: What about the vision problems — is it affecting both sides equally? Any headache or dizziness along with it?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, both sides are affected equally. And umm, I do get headache on and off. The dizziness is comes and goes type, not constant.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Have you done any tests recently — like CT scan of abdomen, colonoscopy, or ophthalmology review for the vision problems?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: I did a CT scan last month but the report is pending. I had a blood coagulation test done also. No colonoscopy has been done yet doctor.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Based on your history of clotting disorder, the squeezing pain in the colon region, and your smoking history, I believe you are suffering from ischemic colitis with possible peripheral vascular disease. The vision problems may be due to hypertensive retinopathy, given your hypertension.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, this is all very serious. What should I do now? And what about my depression?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I am prescribing aspirin 75 mg once daily for the vascular issue, amlodipine 5 mg for your hypertension, and sertraline 50 mg once daily for your depression. Also continue your metformin for diabetes.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: You must stop smoking immediately — the smoke exposure at work combined with two packs a day is making your ischemic colitis and peripheral vascular disease significantly worse. Please request a transfer away from the engine yard.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: And doctor, for the insurance documentation, which tests will you recommend? They need everything on record.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Come in, come in. Please sit down comfortably.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Thank you doctor. Umm, I have been having some pain and bloating in my stomach area since around six months ago.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
