utterances.text: Doctor: Alright. Is the pain in the lower abdomen or more towards the pelvis area?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Ahh, it is more towards the pelvis area, doctor. It comes every day, especially after eating.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Do you also get loose stools or constipation? Any cramping in the abdomen?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, umm, both are happening periodically. Sometimes loose stools, sometimes constipation. It is quite embarrassing to say.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: No need to feel shy, just tell me everything. Do you also get gas trouble or nausea?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: The gas trouble is there several times a day, doctor. It is very troublesome around noon especially.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I see. Now tell me, you had some hernia and piles surgery before, correct? When was that done?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Ahh yes doctor, the hernia repair was done a year ago and the piles surgery was around six months ago. I also had a small abscess drainage done at that same time.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Okay. Any family member was sick at home recently, or any exposure to pesticides in your work or surroundings?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, my brother had typhoid recently. And umm, I work near agricultural fields so there is some pesticides exposure I think.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Understood. What about your vaccination history? Did you get vaccination for typhoid or hepatitis?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Umm, I am not sure doctor. I don't think I have taken any vaccination in many years. I am sorry.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: That is fine. Are you currently fasting for religious reasons? And do you do any walking or exercise, for how long?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, I am fasting these days for religious purposes. I do some walking for 1 hour daily, that is all.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Does the fasting make your abdominal pain worse? And is there any bleeding from the rectal area still?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, the abdominal pain is a bit worse when fasting. The bleeding from the rectal area has stopped mostly, thank god.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Okay, based on everything you have told me — the bloating, alternating loose stools and constipation, gas trouble, and pelvic discomfort — this is a case of IBS, that is irritable bowel syndrome, likely aggravated by your post-surgical state and fasting.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Good morning, come in, come in. Please sit down and relax.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Good morning doctor, umm, I am a bit nervous. I had my hernia repair done yesterday and I am having this itching all over my skin since this morning.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Okay, no need to worry. Can you show me where the itching is? Is there any rash or redness visible?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, there is a rash here on the calf area and also around the joints. The skin there feels dry and thin.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Is there any discharge from the rash? Is it clear or coloured?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Umm, it is clear discharge doctor, nothing yellow or green. The itching is happening daily and very intermittently at the joints and bones also.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Have you been exposed to any sick person recently, or maybe pesticides or pet dander at home?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Ahh, yes doctor, we have a dog at home so pet dander is definitely there. And I live near a farm, so pesticides exposure is possible. No sick person contact though.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Have you taken anything on your own for this itching or rash? Any creams or tablets from the medical shop?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, I was so worried I went to the pharmacy myself. I bought some prednisolone tablets and applied an antifungal cream. I took it daily for two days without any prescription, I know it is wrong.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I understand, but that is something we must discuss. Now, are you also having any abdominal pain or chest pain since the surgery?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Umm, a mild abdominal pain is there doctor near the operation site, but no chest pain at all. I am scared about jaundice also because my skin looks slightly yellow to me.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any yellowing of the eyes? And is the abdominal pain constant or comes and goes?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: No doctor, the eyes look normal I think. The abdominal pain is coming and going, not constant. It started this morning only.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Do you go to the gym regularly? And do you smoke or drink alcohol?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, I go to the gym 3 times a week. I drink alcohol only socially. I do smoke though, about 1 pack per day. I know it is bad for recovery.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: The smoking at 1 pack per day is a serious concern especially after your hernia repair. It will delay wound healing significantly. You must stop immediately.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: I understand doctor. My trainer also told me the same. Is the rash and itching related to my surgery or is it something else?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Good morning, please come in and sit down. How are you feeling today?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, not so well. I am for a month now having yellowish eyes and my skin has also become yellow. It is there nonstop.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Okay. Any nausea or vomiting? How about fatigue?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, vomiting is happening every morning and I have vomited countless times this week. I am feeling very fatigue all day.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any pain near your abdomen? What does the pain feel like?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Umm, yes doctor. It feels squeezing and heavy on my upper right side. It is paining a lot there.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any dark urine or pale stools? Any itching on the skin?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes, my urine has been very dark coloured and I noticed my stools are quite pale. No itching so far.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Now I need to ask — are you currently vaping or taking wine or any alcohol?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Ahh, doctor I was vaping 30 minutes daily before I knew I was pregnant. I also used to have wine occasionally but I stopped once I found out about the pregnancy.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Have you had any exposure to pets at home or contact with any sick person recently?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, we have pets — two cats at home. And my neighbour was very unwell last month, I did visit her. She may have been a sick person with some infection.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I see. Do you have any prior liver disease, hepatitis, or any other medical history?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: No doctor, nothing like that. This is my first pregnancy and I had no medical problems before. I have not taken any medicines regularly.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Alright. Have you done any tests recently — like liver function test, hepatitis B surface antigen, or thyroid test?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: I did a liver function test last week at a nearby lab. The report shows bilirubin is quite high they said, but I did not do thyroid test or the hepatitis B surface antigen.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Based on your jaundice, the squeezing pain in the right upper abdomen, your past vaping and wine use, and the pet exposure, I believe you have fatty liver disease along with jaundice — most likely intrahepatic cholestasis of pregnancy. We must rule out viral hepatitis as well.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, is it dangerous for my baby? How did this happen?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: The earlier vaping and wine exposure may have stressed the liver. Pregnancy itself puts extra load on the liver, and contact with a sick person or pets could have added infection risk. The fatigue and nonstop nausea are all signs the liver is under strain.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I am prescribing ursodeoxycholic acid tablets for the cholestasis, vitamin K supplement to protect the baby, and ondansetron for the vomiting. Please stop all vaping completely if not already done.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Please come in and have a seat. I understand your family was quite insistent on bringing you today.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, my wife dragged me here honestly. I told her it is nothing serious but she would not listen.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Well, she did the right thing. Now tell me, what has been happening? Any swelling or discomfort you have noticed?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Umm, doctor, since yesterday my legs are looking quite puffy, especially near the ankles. And two days ago I noticed the swelling had also come near my jaw area, which really scared me.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Okay, that puffiness near the jaw and ankles is something we must take seriously. Are you having any breathlessness or chest pain?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Not really, doctor. Breathing is mostly fine. But I do feel very fatigue after even small walking — this is almost never like this for me, I am a constable, I walk all day on duty.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any reduced urine output? Or foamy urine? And any nausea or vomiting?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, now that you ask — urine has been less since yesterday also, and it looks a bit frothy. Nausea was there few days ago but that has gone now.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I see. Do you have any history of diabetes or hypertension? And are you on any medicines currently?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, I have hypothyroidism — it was detected three years back. I am taking medicines for that. And blood pressure also is slightly high, my previous doctor gave me losartan for that. I also sometimes take tramadol for my back pain because duty is very demanding.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: How often are you taking the tramadol? And were you given dexamethasone at any point, maybe for any allergy or inflammation?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Tramadol I take once in a while — not regularly. And yes! Few days ago one colleague gave me dexamethasone saying it will reduce the swelling fast. I took it two or three times only.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Alright. Do you smoke or drink alcohol? And what about your diet — are you eating lot of salty or oily food?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: I am a social smoker doctor, I smoke only socially at gatherings. Alcohol I have once in a while. But diet is not good honestly — canteen food, very oily, salty, whatever is available on duty.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Are you posted near any industrial area or mine? Heavy metals sometimes affect the kidneys.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, I was posted near a mine area for almost two years before this posting. I was not knowing this can cause kidney issues.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Based on what you are telling me — the swelling, foamy urine, reduced urine output, and your history of hypertension plus the mine exposure and irregular use of tramadol and dexamethasone — I am suspecting chronic kidney disease. We need to confirm with tests urgently.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Kidney disease? Doctor, that is serious no? I am only forty two. What tests will you do?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Yes, I understand this is worrying, but we caught it now and that is good. I will order a TSH because of your hypothyroidism, a serum creatinine and urine albumin test for the kidneys, a X-ray chest to check for fluid accumulation, and an echocardiogram to see if the heart is under any strain.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Ahh, so many tests. Doctor, this dexamethasone I took — did it make things worse? And should I stop the losartan also?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Come in, come in. Please sit down. How are you feeling after the surgery?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Ahh, doctor, much better than before, but for six months I am having this yellowish discoloration of my eyes and skin — it is coming and going.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Okay, let us start from the beginning. Any fatigue, nausea, or loss of appetite also?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, tiredness is there more often lately. Also, some pain near the belly button area, especially after eating.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Is the pain near the belly button sharp or dull and aching? And any swelling or hardness there?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Umm, it is more dull and aching, doctor. Sometimes also paining in the joints — knee and wrist both. I wanted to ask you about this constipation problem also—

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: We will come to that. First tell me, any dark urine or pale stools? And how often does the jaundice flare up?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes, dark urine is there doctor. The jaundice flare happens once a week roughly. And itching on skin also, I forgot to mention.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Now let me ask about your history. You had a hernia repair six months ago, correct? Any allergies that were noted before surgery?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, hernia repair was done at district hospital. And yes, I have allergies — to some insect bites, my whole arm swells up whenever that happens.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any exposure to mold at home or fumes at work? As a constable you may be near vehicles or chemicals.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Ahh yes, lots of fumes on traffic duty doctor, almost never can I avoid it. And our old quarters has mold on the walls, especially in rainy season.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Now, I have to ask directly — you had a history of alcohol use. Are you still drinking?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, not anymore the heavy drinking. Now only drinking alcohol on weekends — just one or two. I have cut down a lot, I promise.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: What about smoking or tobacco? And how much tea are you taking in a day?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Smoking I have stopped, never touch it now. Tea I take too much doctor, maybe five to six cups. And I started walking in the morning as doctor advised after surgery.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Good that you are doing walking. Have you done any recent blood tests? We need your ESR and creatinine levels checked, along with liver function test.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: I did liver function test last month doctor — bilirubin was high they said. But ESR and creatinine were not done. Also I was given some liver tonic syrup by the previous doctor but I stopped it.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Based on the jaundice, fatigue, high bilirubin, and your history of alcohol use, this is a case of alcoholic fatty liver disease with cholestatic jaundice. The joint pains may be a related inflammatory reaction.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, is this very serious? Will the liver be damaged permanently? I am worried about my job also.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Ah, welcome back! It has been quite a long time. How are you doing?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, no contact from my side for months, I am sorry. I was recently discharged from hospital and now I have loss of appetite and sometimes confusion also. Very worried I am.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Okay, let us go step by step. When did this loss of appetite start? Any yellowing of skin or eye yellowing?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Since last three weeks, doctor. The eyes were yellow when I was admitted. And there is a dull pain in the abdomen area also.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any confusion episodes — like forgetfulness, disorientation? How often is it happening?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Umm, it happens once a week roughly. My wife says I am not making sense sometimes in the evening. Also there is nausea daily.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I see. Do you drink alcohol? And for how long has this been going on?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: I am an occasional drinker, doctor. But I have been drinking on and off for 20 years. Not heavy, I am telling you.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: What about caffeine — tea, coffee? How much are you taking per day?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Ahh, three to four cups of tea 1 hour daily during my delivery rounds, doctor. I am a postman so I am always on road.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: During your delivery work, any pesticides or chemical exposure? Also any pollen exposure in fields or farmland areas?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yep, doctor. I go through agricultural areas frequently. There is a lot of spraying happening. And family member was sick at home last month — jaundice type only.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any history of liver or past surgery? Any illness in childhood?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Nothing major, doctor. In childhood I had some liver infection they said, but no surgery at that time. Later I had a past surgery for gallstones about eight years back.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any bleeding gums or sores inside the mouth? Any swelling in the legs or abdomen?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, there is some soreness inside the mouth. The abdomen is slightly bloated also, especially after eating.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Based on your symptoms — the jaundice, loss of appetite, dull abdominal pain, confusion, long-standing drinking history, and the pesticides exposure — this is most likely a case of alcoholic fatty liver disease with early signs of hepatic encephalopathy. The fatty liver has now progressed due to neglect.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, what is this hepatic encephalopathy? Is it very serious? I am scared.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Yes, it is serious and needs immediate attention. The confusion you are having is because the liver is not filtering toxins properly, and they are reaching your brain. We must stop all drinking completely, reduce caffeine, and get some tests done urgently.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I am ordering an LFT right away — that is a liver function test. We will also do a TMT to check your heart since you have been on long delivery walks, and a cystoscopy is needed given your earlier urine complaints at the time of discharge.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, at discharge they gave me ranitidine. Should I continue that? And is there anything else I should be taking?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Continue the ranitidine for now for the nausea and stomach irritation. I am also prescribing lactulose syrup to help with the hepatic encephalopathy, and silymarin tablets for liver support. Take multivitamin B complex as well — your levels are low.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Stop all drinking immediately — even one drink can worsen the liver damage. Avoid pesticides and farm chemical areas during delivery. If confusion increases or there is vomiting blood, go to emergency right away.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Good morning. Please sit down comfortably.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Good morning, doctor.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: This visit is for medico-legal documentation, correct? Can you tell me your occupation and what brought you here today?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: I work as a tailor in a factory. I was told to come for insurance paperwork after my delivery complication.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Understood. How are you feeling currently? Any feeling dizzy or itching anywhere?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Umm, confirmed, doctor. Some feeling dizzy is there, and itching on the foot, mildly uncomfortable only.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any churning sensation in the stomach, or nausea? When does the dizziness come on?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: The churning happens after every meal, but it is less frequent now compared to before. Feeling dizzy is almost never now.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: What investigations were done? Was an ultrasonography performed during the pregnancy, and was a PT INR checked?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, ultrasonography was done two weeks ago, and PT INR was checked before the tests for the surgery.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: How was your recovery post-op? Any bleeding or swelling in the joints?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Recovery was okay. Some swelling in the joints was there post-op, but it went down. No bleeding.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any past childhood illness on record, or any major surgery before? I see a note about hip replacement — is that correct?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, hip replacement was done three years back. And some childhood illness was there — fever with rash, they said it affected the lung slightly.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Were you exposed to insect bites or sun exposure during pregnancy? These can affect the skin and sometimes the lung.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: The sun exposure was a lot, I work outdoors sometimes near the factory loading area. Insect bites also, yes.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I need to ask about habits also — do you use opioids or have you in the past? And cigarettes or caffeine?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Umm, opioids I was taking for 10 years, stopped after I found out about pregnancy. Caffeine I take after meals. Cigarettes — no, never.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Based on everything, this appears to be a case of obstetric cholestasis with anaemia post-delivery, compounded by past opioid dependence affecting your recovery. The itching on the foot and the churning are consistent with this.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Okay doctor. Is it serious for the insurance form?
